papers.title: Foundation Models for Event Prediction Across Heterogeneous Event Logs
papers.abstract: Event logs are ubiquitous across real-world domains, including business processes, manufacturing workflows, healthcare, and many other operational systems. Yet event logs can differ substantially in their event semantics, label spaces, interaction patterns, and temporal scales, making it difficult to build a single foundation model that generalizes directly to previously unseen systems. We address this challenge with the Foundation Event Predictor (FEP), a simple and scalable in-context architecture that performs next-event prediction through learned, event-level nonparametric inference. Causal self-attention encodes context and target histories into key and query representations, respectively, while the observed next context events are encoded as values. Cross-attention then performs learned, relevance-weighted aggregation of next-event outcomes over all context transitions, allowing the entire nonparametric prediction procedure to be expressed as standard attention operations and efficiently parallelized with modern kernels such as FlashAttention. To promote cross-system generalization, we introduce permutation-robust embedding learning and random fixed embeddings to decouple event IDs from persistent semantics, together with empirical quantile transforms and robust normalization to handle diverse temporal scales. We pretrain FEP on 696 real-world event datasets spanning heterogeneous event systems and evaluate it on 50 held-out datasets unseen during pretraining. Across these datasets, FEP generalizes effectively to new event systems without parameter adaptation, frequently approaching the performance of strong models trained separately on each target dataset while substantially outperforming existing foundation-model baselines, particularly on challenging prediction tasks.

papers.title: Photoacoustic imaging of human brain function through intact adult skulls
papers.abstract: Blood-oxygen-level-dependent (BOLD) functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) has revolutionized noninvasive imaging of human brain function, but it indirectly senses deoxyhemoglobin through water-proton relaxation and relies on bulky, costly, noisy, enclosed, superconducting-magnet scanners. In contrast, photoacoustic computed tomography (PACT) directly probes hemoglobin absorption using a more compact, lower-cost, quieter, open, magnet-free system. However, functional PACT of the adult human brain has so far been demonstrated only after surgical skull removal, because the skull strongly attenuates optical and acoustic signals. Here, we demonstrate non-invasive transcranial functional PACT (T-fPACT) through the intact adult skull. A densely packed, high-channel-count (3,072-element) hemispherical ultrasonic array provides near-$2π$-steradian simultaneous acquisition, enabling high sensitivity and single-shot three-dimensional imaging at 20 Hz that eliminates motion blurring. Participant-specific stabilization further enables measurement of small task-evoked hemodynamic responses over the entire task duration. In healthy adults, T-fPACT localized responses to expected sensorimotor regions, distinguished task-specific motor representations, and yielded consistent localizations across repeated task runs and visits. Comparison with high-field (7 T) fMRI showed spatially corresponding functional regions, while dual-wavelength imaging revealed distinct hemoglobin-weighted responses. These findings overcome the long-standing skull barrier in human brain PACT and establish non-invasive, rapid volumetric photoacoustic imaging of brain function.

papers.title: A Collision-Aware Predictive Rerouting Framework for Connected and Automated Vehicles
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the problem of mitigating non-recurrent congestion in urban transportation networks through predictive and adaptive routing for connected and automated vehicles (CAVs). We propose a collision-aware predictive rerouting framework that integrates microscopic SUMO simulation, DCRNN-based spatiotemporal traffic-state forecasting, collision-window lookahead, and multi-objective route scoring. The routing controller uses predicted congestion, live emission information, route-length penalties, and incident-window constraints to decide when CAVs deviate from their current routes. The completed simulation campaign across three urban network scenarios, five CAV penetration levels, three random seeds, and multiple benchmark rerouting strategies shows that the proposed full framework does not dominate all baselines in aggregate travel time, distance, or emissions. Instead, its principal advantage is operational stability: it maintains comparable network-level efficiency while substantially reducing rerouting frequency relative to active rerouting baselines. These results demonstrate both the promise and the tradeoffs of embedding graph-based prediction and collision awareness into real-time CAV rerouting, and they motivate further work on forecast calibration, uncertainty-aware prediction, and system-level fairness between CAV and non-CAV traffic.

papers.title: Collective Benefits and Efficiency in Coupled Echo State Networks
papers.abstract: Simple aggregation of independent responses ("wisdom of crowds") generally improves collective performance through statistical facilitation, but interaction among members can sometimes hinder group outcomes. However, under certain circumstances, coordination studies show that interacting groups can outperform their individual members and nominal groups, and interaction can also be more efficient than independence. We present a reservoir computing model to investigate how interaction can enhance joint performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency. Echo state networks were trained independently to identify Japanese speakers from vowel recordings and tested jointly with and without coupled feedback. Model pairs reproduced the dyadic advantage reported by Bahrami et al. (2010) with interaction via pooled-feedback, but not when independent responses were aggregated together. Model dynamics revealed that interaction was beneficial whereas aggregated outputs were prone to diverging from runaway feedback over time. In terms of efficiency, larger groups of smaller interacting models outperformed smaller groups of larger models while equating for total amount of group computation. Our results offer a formal framework for explaining when and why interaction enhances collective intelligence.

papers.title: Merit: Making every modality earn its contribution in multimodal attention decoding
papers.abstract: More than 1.5 billion people have hearing loss. When several people talk at once, hearing aids amplify every voice alike. Auditory attention decoding (AAD) aims to solve this by reading a listener's brain signals to find the attended talker, letting the device amplify only them. A real device will not see the brain alone; smart glasses and earbuds also track eyes, head, and scene. These behavioral signals help, as people often look at who they listen to. However, they show where a listener looks, not whom they hear. A decoder relying heavily on them fails when a listener cannot move their head or listens without looking - exactly when a brain-based device is needed. A multimodal decoder must use these signals without letting them replace the electroencephalogram (EEG). Accuracy alone cannot show whether it does. We present MERIT, a decoder and evaluation method asking: how much accuracy does each input earn? MERIT shuffles each input stream across test examples, measures the accuracy drop, and splits the result across streams using Shapley values. It also blocks two shortcuts: candidate audio is checked before training so it cannot reveal the answer, and the scoring function cannot beat chance if it ignores the brain. On a public dataset with EEG, eye tracking, head motion, and scene video, MERIT improves on the published benchmark, reaching 0.82 four-way accuracy within listeners and 0.74 on unseen listeners (chance is 0.25). The measurement reveals what accuracy hides: adding behavioral streams raises overall accuracy but almost halves the brain's share of it. On two other datasets, the same tests find a label imbalance in a widely used benchmark and flag results that accuracy alone would report as brain decoding.

papers.title: Another Brick in the Wall: A Computationally Assisted Proof of an Improved Upper Bound for Thrackles
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a thrackle, where a thrackle is a graph drawing in which each edge meets every other edge exactly once, either at a vertex or at a crossing. It is conjectured that, for all thrackles, the number of edges is less than or equal to the number of vertices. Fulek and Pach created a program to determine whether or not a graph can be a thrackle. Through a reconstruction and improvement of their algorithm, we computationally prove a key dumbbell to be non-thrackleable. Using this exclusion, we improve Xu's 8-face half-edge bound from five to four. Finally, using this stronger restriction with Xu's framework, together with separate arguments for graphs containing triangles and disconnected graphs, we improve the known upper bound toward this conjecture to $m\le1.385(n-1)$ for $n\ge4$.

papers.title: CÆNL: Collapse-Based Active Neural Learning with Objective-Aligned Representation Control
papers.abstract: Active learning changes the representations used to acquire subsequent labels. We study this interaction through Collapse-Based Active Neural Learning (CÆNL), which separates acquisition, Dynamic Collapse Regularization (DCR), and its coefficient policy. DCR penalizes a normalized within-class to between-class scatter residual above a frozen reference, with a separate class-separation safeguard. Fixed, scheduled, deterministic-feedback, and learned-feedback policies apply this objective. The analysis establishes scatter invariances, conditional local descent, and coefficient bounds, and shows why clean geometry alone cannot guarantee input robustness. Six-seed classification comparisons are complemented by a 104-run study with separate control selection and ten-seed evaluations on each of two backbones. At 60% annotations on ImageNet-100, entropy acquisition with DCR and MACC-Lite reaches 73.420 +/- 0.512% accuracy on ResNet-50 and 73.086 +/- 0.397% on ResNet-18 (mean +/- seed SD), exceeding entropy alone by 1.742 and 1.834 percentage points. Both gains survive Holm correction under paired-t and exact sign-flip tests, with unchanged feedback settings across backbones. Independently tuned constants attain slightly higher mean accuracy; the paired comparisons establish neither adaptive superiority nor equivalence. Separate six-seed spectral studies yield a small fixed-regularization C4 loss reduction, worse CIFAR-10 diffusion FID, and inconclusive AudioCaps captioning effects. Earlier classification studies find near-zero AutoAttack accuracy at L-infinity radius 8/255 and no added benefit from learned control. The results support the evaluated combined classification treatment and identify the task dependence of geometry-informed regularization.

papers.title: Rethinking World Models for Biosignals
papers.abstract: World models promise to learn how systems evolve and respond to actions, enabling simulation, planning and decision-making. Bringing this promise to biosignals requires more than accurate prediction of physiological recordings. We examine existing biosignal world models through two requirements for intervention use: a genuine action and evidence of its causal effect. We identify three fundamental bottlenecks rooted in physiology: Temporal Latency, the variable delay between an action and its observable effect; System Openness, the influence of drivers beyond the modelled intervention; and Endogenous Dynamics, the system's ongoing evolution without that intervention. Drawing on published evidence, we outline corresponding research directions and propose an Intervention-Effect Validation Checklist to guide evaluation. The aim is to help the biosignal community realise the core promise of world models by learning the latent mechanisms that govern physiological evolution and responses to interventions.

papers.title: An Optimal Algorithm for Changing from Longitudinal to Latitudinal Formation of Autonomous Aircraft Squadrons
papers.abstract: This work presents an algorithm for changing from longitudinal to latitudinal formation of autonomous aircraft squadrons. The maneuvers are defined dynamically by using a predefined set of 3D basic maneuvers. This formation change is necessary when the squadron has to perform tasks demanding both formations, such as landing, lift-off, obstacle avoidance and georeferencing. The time complexity analysis of the transformation algorithm reveals that its efficiency is optimal. Simulations show that the formation change is done without collision, and the proof of correctness ensures its latitudinal formation features.

papers.title: Covariance-Rank Rounding and a Sharp Integrality Gap for a Matroid Edge-Coverage Moment Lift
papers.abstract: Selecting vertices covers their incident edges, but a matroid can prevent selecting the combinations that cover the most weight. We study whether pair-selection information improves rounding from a semidefinite relaxation of this problem. A feasible point $(x,Y)$ records individual and paired selection values. Its relaxation objective is $U$, and the matrix $Y-xx^\top$ has rank $d$. We compare the feasible marginal vectors obtained by fixing one element as selected or excluded, then round only the best vector. For $d\ge1$, the resulting basis has value at least $(3/4+1/(4d))U$. The procedure is deterministic and polynomial-time for a supplied exact rational point and an independence oracle. Weighting the covariance spectrum by the objective gives a stronger version of the bound. To show the rank factor is sharp, we construct a rank-$2m$ rational linear matroid and $m$ disjoint four-cycles with integral optimum $3m+1$, relaxation optimum $4m$, and an optimal covariance matrix of rank $m$. Thus the relaxation has limiting reciprocal integrality gap $4/3$, despite its conditional constraints. One valid pair-exclusion inequality makes it exact on this family, as an explicit semidefinite certificate shows. The result concerns rounding and the strength of this relaxation; it does not supply a low-rank optimal point or a fixed universal approximation improvement.

papers.title: CacheSmith: Accurate RAG Serving under Latency SLOs with Adaptive KV Reuse
papers.abstract: This paper presents CacheSmith, a KV cache reuse system for RAG prefill that maximizes quality-gated SLO attainment. While context caching lowers prefill latency by reusing precomputed KV states for retrieved chunks, it misses cross-chunk attention that a full prefill would compute over concatenated inputs. Prior selective recomputation schemes tackle this problem but enforce static, one-size-fits-all configurations that fail to effectively handle request heterogeneity or dynamic latency budgets. CacheSmith decomposes selective recomputation into a three-phase workflow of WarmUp, Probe, and Patch that can be dynamically configured to exploit a wide range of cost-accuracy trade-offs. At serving time, an SLO-aware scheduler in CacheSmith forms batches to mitigate inter-request interference during layer-by-layer prefill, while a budget-aware planner configures recomputation phases across the batch to maximize the number of requests satisfying both generation quality and latency targets. Both components make fast, solver-free decisions over profiled cost-accuracy bands. On four benchmarks across varying arrival rates and burstiness levels, CacheSmith improves quality-gated SLO attainment by up to 27.5%, over four state-of-the-art baselines.

papers.title: Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Scene Reconstruction: Methods, Systems, and Trade-offs
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) allows for high-quality real-time novel-view synthesis. Since its inception in 2023, its explicit and highly configurable scene representation has been extended toward sparse-view generation, dynamic reconstruction, efficiency and compression, streaming, and simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM). Although Gaussian Splatting can provide real-time rendering, rendering an existing representation is distinct from constructing, updating, or maintaining the scene itself. In this survey, we synthesize current literature, categorize them and provide a connection of current approaches and tools towards an end-to-end pipeline. Explicitly, we categorize GS scene reconstruction into five overlapping families: single-shot generation, dynamic representations, efficiency and compression, streaming and immersive systems, and Gaussian Splatting SLAM. We distinguish render-only throughput from task-specific scene generation, update, tracking, mapping, and optimization costs, and combine controlled sparse-view benchmarking with native evaluations to identify cross-family quality, latency, memory, and update-cost trade-offs.

papers.title: Matroid-Aware Spectral Certificates for Multiplicative Coverage Approximation
papers.abstract: We maximize the weight of edges covered by selected vertices, together with nonnegative individual rewards, under an arbitrary matroid constraint. The continuous coverage objective is quadratic and need not be concave. Our method searches projections onto a small set of directions and solves a concave subproblem for each projection center. A coverage-specific inequality converts the subproblem bounds into a multiplicative guarantee, while matroid rounding restores an integral solution. Let $A$ be the weighted adjacency matrix and $D$ the diagonal matrix of singleton values, restricted to positive-value elements after objective-preserving preprocessing. Set $\varrho=λ_{\max}(D^{-1/2}AD^{-1/2})$. For an integer budget $q\ge0$, let $τ_q$ be the smallest nonnegative threshold for which $A+τ_qD$ has at most $q$ negative eigenvalues on the span of differences of matroid bases. We obtain the factor $1-\varrhoτ_q/[2(\varrho+τ_q)]-\varepsilon$ in time $(2+q/\varepsilon)^{O(q+1)}N^{O(1)}$, where $N$ is the binary input length and a zero-over-zero loss is zero. The algorithm returns a rational upper bound on the integral optimum. A separate exact-algebraic construction produces polynomial-bit low-rank rational corrections with positive threshold slack; its proof isolates eigenvalues, keeps eigenspace bases unnormalized, and approximates scalar factors only at the final step. The numerical proposal prototype is not used to justify this complexity statement. Supplied certificates also yield robustness to locally bounded edge additions. These are threshold-dependent coverage guarantees, not a new general spectral-search principle or a universal approximation improvement.

papers.title: Non-contact lens metrology from optical flow and differentiable ray tracing
papers.abstract: Accurate lens surface metrology is essential to determine the manufactured geometry of refractive optical elements and their deviation from the specified design. We demonstrate a transmission metrology method that reconstructs refractive lens surfaces from the displacement of a wavelet-noise-patterned mask. Lens-induced distortion is represented by a dense displacement field. A differentiable ray tracer fits the lens geometry using a calibrated near-telecentric camera model with an effective finite ray origin. We validate the method on commercial lenses. The recovered geometries agree with nominal specifications, and the plano-aspheric reconstruction is compared with chromatic confocal profilometry.

papers.title: Alpern Lemma Independent of a Partition for Aperiodic Systems
papers.abstract: We prove that for every $(X,\mathcal{B},μ,T)$, an aperiodic, probability preserving system and $\mathcal{P}$ a finite measurable partition of $X$, there exists an Alpern Multitower whose base is independent of $\mathcal{P}$. This removes the ergodicity assumption in the original proof of the independent Alpern Lemma of \cite{MR3373823}. As a consequence, we remove ergodicity assumption from recent results on limit theorems in deterministic systems \cite{Kosloff_Volny_2022,kosloffVolnyStableCLT,MR4955410}.

papers.title: Improved Combinatorial Auctions with and without Samples
papers.abstract: We give new mechanisms for combinatorial auctions in the offline, secretary, and prophet-with-samples models. Specifically, we obtain the following guarantees for social welfare maximization with $m$ items and $n$ XOS buyers: * In the prophet-with-samples version, buyers arrive in adversarial order and draw their values from independent distributions. We give a universally truthful, polynomial-time $(2+\eps)$-approximation mechanism using $O(\log\!\log m)$ samples from each distribution. The approximation factor is tight even for a single item and without the incentive constraints, due to the classic prophet inequality. Compared to the previous state-of-the-art with the same guarantees [Dütting--Kesselheim--Lucier--Reiffenhäuser--Singla (FOCS 2024)], our running time is exponentially faster, and our sample complexity is doubly-exponentially lower, resolving two explicit open problems by Dütting et al. * Using the same techniques, we also obtain improved mechanisms in the secretary and offline versions, where the values are worst-case, and buyers are processed in either random order (secretary) or without any timing restrictions (offline). After a long line of works, the state of the art in both models is an $O((\log\!\log m)^2)$-approximation due to [Assadi--Kesselheim--Singla (SODA 2021)], who explicitly ask whether it can be improved to $O(\log\!\log m)$. We indeed obtain an $O(\log\!\log m)$-approximate universally truthful mechanism for the secretary and offline models.

papers.title: Orthogonality of Defect Ideals for Jordan Homomorphisms
papers.abstract: Let $\varphi\colon A\to B$ be a Jordan homomorphism of associative algebras over a field $\mathbb{F}$ of characteristic different from $2$, with defect ideals $V_{\varphi}$ and $W_{\varphi}$. If $A=\operatorname{Alg}([[A,A],[A,A]])$, then $V_{\varphi}W_{\varphi}=W_{\varphi}V_{\varphi}=0$ and $V_{\varphi}\cap W_{\varphi}\subseteq\operatorname{Ann}(\operatorname{Alg}(\varphi(A)))$. Moreover, the induced map modulo $V_{\varphi}\cap W_{\varphi}$ is standard. The annihilator bound is sharp, even in finite dimension. As an application, when $A$ is unital and $A=K(A)$, every Jordan homomorphism defined on $A$ is splittable and standard. In this setting, the corresponding result of Brešar and Zelmanov holds without the surjectivity hypothesis.

papers.title: Recovery of Rough Sources in the Inverse Monge-Ampère Problem
papers.abstract: We prove that every nonnegative $L^1$ source in the Monge-Ampère equation \[ \det D^2u=f\quad\text{in }Ω, \] on a bounded uniformly convex $C^{1,1}$ domain $Ω\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$, is uniquely determined by generalized boundary measurements of Alexandrov solutions. The measurement is the extremal boundary slope, which extends the classical outward normal derivative and may take the value $+\infty$. For each direction $ω\in\mathbb S^{n-1}$, it suffices to know these slopes for cylindrical Dirichlet data $\frac{t_k^ω}{2}|P_ωx|^2$ along any sequence $t_k^ω\to\infty$, where $P_ω$ projects onto $ω^\perp$. The boundary value and extremal slope determine the interior subgradient image up to a Lebesgue null set. An exact change of variables formula then converts equality of these images into integral identities for the source, and a large-amplitude limit recovers its Euclidean X-ray transform. This yields uniqueness without a positive lower bound on the source. For nonnegative $L^\infty$ sources, the extremal slopes are bounded and agree with the interior normal derivatives, giving a Dirichlet-to-interior-Neumann formulation. We also extend the inverse argument to the gradient-weighted equation \[ \vartheta(\nabla u)\det D^2u=f, \] where the known weight $\vartheta$ is locally integrable, Borel measurable, and bounded below by a positive constant. We prove existence of the corresponding Alexandrov solutions and show that the same cylindrical boundary-slope data uniquely determine every nonnegative $L^1$ source.

papers.title: Chromatic Block-Gibbs p-Bit Decoding of QLDPC Codes
papers.abstract: We introduce a parallel decoder for quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes based on probabilistic bits (p-bits), tunable stochastic binary units controlled by local fields. The idea is that predicted error configurations, interpreted as explanations of the observed syndrome, are updated stochastically using local Gibbs conditionals, while a progressively strengthened parity penalty drives the search toward syndrome-valid configurations. A coloring of the decoding graph enables parallel block updates, and independent replicas and restarts provide trajectory diversity. The best candidate encountered during the search is returned, mirroring the candidate-selection strategy of recent ensemble decoders. At the stated update budgets, the resulting logical error rates are on par with leading decoders under both code-capacity and circuit-level noise. While the total number of variable resamplings can be substantially larger than the message-update count of BP-based alternatives, the numerical results establish constraint-annealed p-bit dynamics as a competitive stochastic alternative for QLDPC decoding and motivate further study of hardware-native implementations.

papers.title: YUBI-Real2Sim: 3DGS Scene Verification for Reliable Policy Evaluation
papers.abstract: Evaluating VLA policies on real robots is costly, time-consuming, and difficult to reproduce, making real-to-sim simulation essential for scalable evaluation. While 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables rapid real-to-sim scene generation, the reconstruction quality required for reliable policy evaluation remains unquantified. In particular, policies relying on wrist-mounted fisheye cameras (e.g., YUBI handheld gripper data) are heavily exposed to visual artifacts (holes, floaters) in wide-angle views, directly degrading task performance. To address this, we present YUBI-Real2Sim, a unified framework for 3DGS-based scene reconstruction and real-to-sim policy evaluation under dual fisheye wrist views. We develop an integrated pipeline combining 200-degree fisheye camera capture, 3DGS training, 3D foundation models for object modeling, and MuJoCo-based physical simulation, reproducing the observed real-world policy ordering in eight of nine scene-task comparisons. Using this framework, we construct a benchmark across two bimanual robot platforms, three scenes, three tasks, and dual pi0.5-based policies. This systematically measures real-to-sim rank agreement and evaluates policy sensitivity against counterfactual 3DGS artifacts (ceiling holes, floaters, warping) and capture disturbances. We further analyze whether novel-view quality scores can indicate policy-ranking reliability under a scene-held-out evaluation protocol. The results show task-dependent performance and limitations of quality-based reliability prediction, highlighting the need to assess reconstruction quality when using Real2Sim for policy evaluation. These results do not yet establish a generally reliable scene-acceptance rule. Project Page: https://yubi-real2sim.airoa.io.

papers.title: Schauder estimate in large scale for compressible planar cavity flows with fast-decaying vorticity
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study planar compressible cavity flows fast-decaying vorticity and establish a Schauder estimate in large scale. As an application, we obtain an a priori asymptotic growth rate estimate of the cavity, that $s^{\frac{1}{2}-δ}\lesssim h(s)\lesssim s^{\frac{1}{2}+δ}$. This is by far the most accurate asymptotic estimate for compressible cavity flows and is probably the first paper that takes vorticity into account in the asymptotic analysis.

papers.title: Enhanced Detective: A Dual-Stage Proactive Defense Against Internal Poisoning Attacks in Financial Fraud Detection Using Federated Learning
papers.abstract: With recent developments in Artificial Intelligence (AI), the adoption of distributed learning paradigms such as Federated Learning (FL) has emerged. In simple terms, FL enables multiple entities to collaboratively train AI models without sharing local data. The FL paradigm is particularly valuable in privacy-sensitive settings, such as financial services, because it enables institutions to collaboratively improve fraud-detection models while keeping sensitive transaction data local. However, FL schemes are prone to security vulnerabilities, where malicious clients can poison local data or model updates and degrade the global model, and hence the performance of the resulting model might be affected. Therefore, in this work, we propose Enhanced Detective, a dual-stage robust aggregation strategy that combines Median Absolute Deviation (MAD), distance-based update filtering, and FedMedian aggregation. Experiments on an imbalanced credit card dataset evaluate targeted label-flipping and weight-scaling attacks over 50 communication rounds. With 40% malicious clients, Enhanced Detective achieves an AUPRC of 0.796 and a Recall of 0.847.

papers.title: Fractional Calderón problem with $L^{\infty}$-conductivities
papers.abstract: We study the inverse problem for the fractional conductivity equation with uniformly elliptic conductivities $γ\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$. For every $n\geq1$ and $0<s<1$, we prove that the local exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann map on any nonempty open subset of the exterior of a bounded open domain determines $γ$ uniquely almost everywhere in $\mathbb R^n$. No continuity, Sobolev regularity, or prescribed behavior at infinity is required. The proof works directly with the conductivity bilinear form and avoids the fractional Liouville reduction. It combines exterior determination at Lebesgue points, equality of weighted solutions, and a unique continuation principle for the fractional Laplacian in the weighted class \[ L_s=\left\{ g\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^n): \int_{\mathbb R^n} \frac{|g(x)|}{1+|x|^{n+2s}}\,dx<\infty \right\}. \] Specifically, if $g\in L_s$ and both $g$ and $(-Δ)^s g$ vanish in a nonempty open set, with the latter equality understood distributionally, then $g=0$ almost everywhere. This result requires neither local boundedness nor Sobolev regularity of $g$. Its proof uses the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension and boundary unique continuation for the associated degenerate elliptic equation.

papers.title: Monoidal structure on Rota-Baxter algebras via augmentation, and free cocycle bialgebras
papers.abstract: A tensor product is known for commutative Rota--Baxter algebras through a universal construction, but its underlying algebra need not be the ordinary tensor product $A\otimes B$ and can be substantially larger. We show that, after passing to augmented Rota--Baxter algebras, the ordinary tensor product itself carries a natural Rota--Baxter operator which makes the category monoidal with the usual associator and unit constraints. The resulting structure is intrinsically nonsymmetric: over a field of characteristic zero, this operator and its flip-conjugated counterpart are the only possibilities among linear combinations of five natural terms, while over any field the full category admits no braiding. Its comonoid objects are precisely Rota--Baxter cocycle bialgebras. Moreover, the free Rota--Baxter adjunction yields a bimonad and free cocycle bialgebras on ordinary bialgebras, with compatible Hopf structures for connected filtered inputs, in both the associative and commutative settings.

papers.title: Box-WAM: Box Trajectories as Compact State Representations for World Action Models
papers.abstract: World action models (WAMs) are a category of policy models that ex- plicitly predict both actions and future world states. They have been shown to outperform action-only models across various robotic manipulation tasks. How- ever, representing the future with full-frame video prediction can be computation- ally expensive during both training and inference. This raises a central question: what compact state representation preserves the planning and supervision bene- fits of future prediction? In this paper, we propose BoxWAM, which replaces dense future frames with oriented bounding box trajectories of task-relevant ob- jects. By explicitly imagining object-centric future motion, our method provides a lightweight prediction target that captures the key physical changes induced by robot actions. We show that box trajectory prediction substantially reduces com- putational cost while improving action prediction performance, suggesting that object-centric compact states can serve as an efficient alternative to video-based world action modeling for robotic manipulation. Result videos can be found on https://box-wam.github.io

papers.title: On horn-shaped Reinhardt domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new class of unbounded Reinhardt domains in $\mathbb C^n$ ($n\geq 2$),which we call horn domains. We study the dimensions of the Bergman spaces,the holomorphic sectional curvature of the Bergman metric, and the holomorphic equivalence problem for such horn Reinhardt domains.

papers.title: ATTUNE: Agentic Throughput Tuning for LLM Training
papers.abstract: Training a large language model can occupy thousands of GPUs for weeks, and its speed depends on its recipe: how the model is split across GPUs, how memory is traded for compute, and which kernels and communication overlaps it uses. Finding a good recipe is still manual work for experts. Automated tuners search fixed lists of knobs and check only that a job runs, so they miss large gains and can ship changes that silently alter what the model learns. ATTUNE tunes any working recipe unattended within a GPU-hour budget. A coding agent, guided by lessons from past tuning runs, finds each run's bottleneck and changes one setting at a time, and a correctness gate outside the agent refuses changes known to alter training. ATTUNE is deployed in production at Amazon Ads, a business that reported $19.8 billion in revenue in Q2 2026. Its recipes train the models that power Amazon's Ads Agent. On three of the models it tunes, its recipes raise throughput per GPU by 1.7x on average and up to 3.9x over internal expert-tuned recipes. It also speeds up four of NVIDIA's benchmark recipes by 7-26% and held-out public recipes by up to 2.6x, and beats Bayesian optimization, random search and OptiCo, a recent LLM-agent tuner, at the same GPU-hour budget. We release ATTUNE at github.com/amazon-science/attune and OpenRecipes, a leaderboard of more than 60 verified recipes, at openrecipes.ai.

papers.title: Information transfer as a new indicator of approaching local bifurcations: saddle-node, pitchfork and Hopf bifurcations
papers.abstract: Early warning signals are key tools for anticipating qualitative changes in the dynamics of complex systems. In this work, we investigate whether an information-theoretic measure designed to characterize directional causal dependencies between observables can provide early warning of the approach to bifurcations. The measure considered is the rate of information transfer, which has been successfully applied to characterize directional dependencies in a broad range of fields, from economics to climate science. Three fundamental local bifurcations are considered: saddle-node, pitchfork, and Hopf bifurcations. We first investigate idealized (quasi-)potential stochastic systems for which analytical expressions for the rate of information transfer can be derived. Distinct signatures are found for the three bifurcation types. In particular, the rate of information transfer displays a strong increase and divergence when approaching the saddle-node bifurcation, whereas smoother but systematic changes are found near the pitchfork and Hopf bifurcations. The approach is then tested using low-order climate models exhibiting the same types of bifurcations. The results confirm that changes in the rate of information transfer can precede the corresponding dynamical transitions, suggesting that directional information transfer provides a useful complementary early-warning indicator for detecting the approach to critical transitions in nonlinear stochastic systems.

papers.title: TwinPrune: Density-Aware Two-Phase Token Pruning for Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: We propose a unified spatial-density signal to score token importance for both inference phases: bipartite merge for prefill and KV eviction for decode, yielding measurable gains in each stage. To isolate the two phases, we split benchmarks by scoring logic. Prefill probes (MMBench, POPE, ScienceQA) evaluate only the first decoded token; their accuracy reflects prefill logits argmax before any decode KV eviction. Full-pipeline probes (TextVQA, DocVQA, MM-Vet) assess the complete generated sequence and capture both phases. We identify a critical evaluation pitfall: decode pruning claims validated solely on prefill probes measure prefill quality, not decode performance. Experiments show discarding all visual KV during decode barely affects prefill-probe accuracy but degrades TextVQA and MM-Vet drastically; this insensitivity stems from the scoring rule, not compression intensity. Evaluated on seven model variants (InternVL-3.5, Qwen3-VL, LLaVA-1.5) and three full-pipeline benchmarks, our method achieves a three-way Pareto frontier across compute, memory and accuracy. Density-based prefill compression maintains strong accuracy, scales linearly with visual token count, and delivers 100x faster token selection at high resolution. For decode, density top-k KV eviction consistently outperforms strong baselines H2O, SnapKV and StreamingLLM on TextVQA and MM-Vet across three retention ratios. At 0.125 keep ratio on TextVQA, it surpasses H2O by 9.6 points; InternVL-3.5 models (2B to 38B) maintain a 7 to 10 point advantage. Compression scales favorably with model size: every measured 8B to 38B model transition reduces accuracy loss instead of worsening it. We suggest MM-Vet or DocVQA as mandatory full-pipeline validation for any decode-phase claims. Our code is available at https://github.com/Kai-Liu001/TwinPrune

papers.title: Towards Green AI: Evaluating Energy Efficiency for Quantized LLM Inference
papers.abstract: While it is known that quantization of large language models (LLMs) reduces memory usage via lower-bit weights, studies quantifying the resulting impact on energy usage and carbon intensity are scarce. We present the first unified evaluation of weight-only quantization strategies for LLM inference across varying input/output lengths and GPUs, highlighting differences in energy efficiency in addition to accuracy degradation and runtime. We study quantized inference on Llama 2 7B, Phi 3.5 Mini Instruct, OLMo 1B, Qwen 2.5 7B, and Qwen 2.5 14B across GLUE MNLI, MMLU, HumanEval, and GSM8K datasets, evaluating 10 post-training quantization (PTQ) strategies on NVIDIA H100, A6000, A100, and L4 GPUs. We identify a novel trend showing that quantization techniques tend to exhibit peak energy efficiency relative to full-precision baselines when inputs are sufficiently long and outputs are short. Furthermore, we show that quantization strategies become marginally more energy-efficient relative to full-precision models as batch sizes increase, though gains are modest. Notably, fused-kernel implementations such as EETQ int8 and Bitsandbytes int8 offer the highest energy savings, up to 4x compared to FP32 on short text generation, with negligible accuracy loss. Finally, we observe that energy usage closely tracks runtime on our evaluated benchmarks, indicating that, in practice, latency optimization can serve as a reliable proxy for reducing the environmental footprint of LLM services. We conclude with suggested directions for strategically selecting low-carbon quantization strategies based on specific inference requirements.

papers.title: CrossPortrait: Cross-Species Portrait Animation via Adversarial Motion Alignment
papers.abstract: Cross-species portrait animation, which aims to animate a source portrait of species A using a driving video of species B, is particularly challenging due to substantial anatomical differences in facial structures across species. Previous works typically fine-tune human portrait animation models on animal video datasets but often suffer from driving-species leakage. To address this, we propose CrossPortrait, a novel framework for expressive cross-species portrait animation, supporting diverse scenarios including human-to-animal, animal-to-human and cross-species animal-to-animal (e.g. cat-to-dog) animation. Specifically, we decompose the portrait motion into rigid head poses and expression keypoints. To accommodate species-specific facial structures while facilitating cross-species expression alignment, we introduce a species-routed expression encoder that incorporates species-specific LoRAs into a unified expression encoder. Furthermore, we introduce expression-level adversarial domain adaptation (Ex-ADA) to suppress driving-species-specific information in the expression latents, thereby mitigating species leakage and promoting a shared expression space across species. Extensive experiments show that our method enables expressive and identity-preserving portrait animation across diverse species and outperforms other state-of-the-art approaches.

papers.title: A null model to detect coordinated online behavior integrating evidence from multiple indicators
papers.abstract: Coordinated online accounts can amplify messages and manipulate attention, but detecting such behavior is challenging due to confounding factors like account activity and item popularity. We propose a statistical null-model framework that assesses behavioral similarity between accounts by comparing observed coordination indicators against activity- and popularity-conditioned reference distributions. By combining evidence across multiple indicators and partners, our method can identify suspicious coordination links more accurately. Evaluations on nine labeled information-operation datasets involving over 152 thousand accounts show that aggregating p-values multiplicatively across indicators and partners yields improved detection performance. While results vary across information operations, this approach offers a generalizable and statistically principled tool for uncovering coordinated online behavior.

papers.title: Sim4RAD: A MATLAB Toolkit for Design-Phase Sizing, Actuator Selection and URDF-Model Verification of Serial Robotic Arms
papers.abstract: Actuator sizing is an early and consequential decision: joint torque and velocity specifications fix the motors, gearboxes and brakes before any CAD model exists. Sim4RAD is a MATLAB toolkit for that phase and for the verification that follows it. It builds a rigid-body model from a handful of parameters, and four analyses supply the specification: a static analysis combining lever-arm sampling with a posture search, giving a rated torque at a chosen payload envelope and a reproducible peak torque; a dynamics pipeline that reshapes a trajectory under one of four constraints, including the actuator torque-speed envelope; a stochastic analysis over many random motions, so a specification rests on a class of motions, not one trajectory; and a workspace and dexterity analysis that separates where the arm can reach from how it can reach there. Replacing the synthesized model by a URDF file turns the same analyses to verification. A 7-DOF anthropomorphic arm is compared in three layouts differing in the shoulder axis order and in whether the last wrist joint is coaxial with the payload. The static demand at half arm length is nearly the same in all three, and it sizes the joints rather than the sampled motion; reordering the shoulder axes leaves the worst-case torque unchanged at 55 N m and the reachable volume within 8 percent. A last wrist joint coaxial with the payload removes its gravity torque, reduces the adjacent wrist joint by almost a third and cuts the last joint demand tenfold in a 5 m/s scan, at the price of dexterity (mean 0.570 to 0.348). The same arm needs 20 to 37 times more torque for a 5 m/s target than for a 2 s motion: the scenario, not the trajectory, must be fixed first. Verification should use the URDF model of the detailed design; the toolkit is available at https://github.com/LasterLi/Sim4RAD.

papers.title: Electric Edelstein Effect in Two Dimensions
papers.abstract: We propose the electric Edelstein effect (EEE) in two-dimensional (2D) systems, where crossed out-of-plane and in-plane electric fields generate a spin polarization. The gate field converts the Edelstein response from a material-fixed spin polarization into a gate-tunable one. A symmetry analysis over all magnetic layer point groups shows that the EEE is allowed in a wide range of magnetic and nonmagnetic systems, including ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, and altermagnets. The EEE plays two distinct roles: it generates spin polarization where the linear Edelstein effect (EE) is symmetry-forbidden, as in centrosymmetric materials; and it adds a new gate-tunable component, generally non-collinear with the conventional one, where the EE is already present. The two fields then act as independent knobs and raise the control dimension of the spin polarization from one to two. Our microscopic theory traces the EEE to band-geometric quantities, which are strongly enhanced near small band gaps. First-principles calculations predict pronounced effects in the centrosymmetric ferromagnet MnSe2, where the linear EE is symmetry-forbidden. In the nonmagnet SnSe where the EE and EEE coexist, the two knobs cover an extended region of the spin sphere. Our findings establish the EEE as a symmetry-guided, gate-tunable route to electrical spin manipulation and open avenues for multistate spintronics in 2D quantum materials.

papers.title: Hyperelliptic curves on $K3$ surfaces
papers.abstract: We study hyperelliptic curves on $K3$ surfaces. We show that any number of general points on a $K3$ surface of Picard rank one can be connected by a hyperelliptic curve. As a by-product we recover the Beauville--Voisin decomposition of the small diagonal, together with some new bounds on its torsion order in the integral Chow group. On the arithmetic side, given a $K3$ surface $X$ of geometric Picard rank one defined over a number field $k$, we show that there exists a finite extension $k\subset k'$ such that quadratic points are dense in $X_{k'}$, extending a theorem of Corvaja--Zucconi to $K3$ surfaces of arbitrary degree.

papers.title: On a finite group in which every non-supersolvable maximal subgroup is a TI-subgroup
papers.abstract: We provide a complete characterization of a finite group in which every non-supersolvable maximal subgroup is a TI-subgroup, which generalizes some known related results.

papers.title: Everyone Was Right: Lexical Representations in Language Models Are Both Abstract and Holistic
papers.abstract: Lexical representations can encode both abstract information and information specific to particular contexts. We investigate how these forms of information are organized in language models by decomposing contextual word representations into item, class, and word-class interaction components. Across six pretrained transformers and two linguistic categories, we find that the interaction is consistently present, grows across layers, and contains information associated with both item and class. Unlike the nearly orthogonal item and class effects, the interaction overlaps with both and encodes class information beyond the shared class effect. An interaction also emerges in artificial-language learners even when the input contains only additive structure. Together, these findings show that lexical representations combine abstract information with structure specific to particular word-class combinations.

papers.title: Sharp Damping Location for Stability of a Locally Damped Wave Equation and its Galerkin Approximation
papers.abstract: We study the stability of the variable coefficient wave equation $u_{tt}-u_{xx}-(1+x^{2})u_{yy}+χ_{\mathbb G}u_{t}=0$ on the rectangle $(-1,1)\times(0,π)$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions, where the viscous damping acts on a vertical strip $\mathbb G=(η-δ,η+δ)\times(0,π)$. We establish a precise relationship between the location of the damping region and the rate of energy decay. We prove that the associated semigroup is exponentially stable whenever the closure of the damping strip meets the line $x=0$, i.e., $|η|\leqδ$, despite the existence of rays that never enter the damped region. When the damping region is strictly bounded away from $x=0$, the semigroup decays at the sharp rate $(\log(2+t))^{-1}$. The proofs combine separation of variables, one-dimensional resolvent estimates, a reflection identity for the harmonic oscillator, and Gaussian quasimodes. We then consider the spectral Galerkin approximation based on the Dirichlet eigenfunctions of the constant coefficient Laplacian and show that, although the sequence of semigroups resulting from the approximation converges to the continuous one, it fails to be uniformly exponentially stable.

papers.title: TacitVLA: Reasoning Vision-Language-Action Models Without Reasoning Latency
papers.abstract: Textual reasoning before acting has improved vision-language-action (VLA) models, but at the cost of latency: every action conditioned on the reasoning text must wait for autoregressive decoding. We show that actions do not need to wait for or condition on the generated reasoning to benefit from it, because the reasoning supervision already improves the backbone representation. We introduce TacitVLA, a reasoning VLA whose action expert never attends to the reasoning it generates for the current call. On long-horizon tasks where the reasoning text also serves as episodic memory, it can generate each entry during action execution rather than before acting. We evaluate it in a controlled study on four benchmarks spanning manipulation and autonomous driving, memory and non-memory tasks: RoboMME, RMBench, LIBERO, and PhysicalAI-AV. On all four, TacitVLA matches the performance of its explicit-reasoning counterpart at up to 3.4x lower latency, and matches the latency of the same architecture trained without reasoning at up to +17.1% success. In absolute terms, it surpasses the best previously published results on the RoboMME Counting suite (82.7% vs. 66.8%) and RMBench (77.5% vs. 56.5%), and reaches 72.9% on LIBERO-Plus and a 52.5% scene score on the public split of the PhysicalAI-AV closed-loop driving challenge. Project page: https://tacitvla.github.io.

papers.title: Convex-Analytic View of Query Selection for Safety Verification of Markov Decision Processes
papers.abstract: Safety verification of a Markov decision process (MDP) asks whether the probabilities of reaching several failure states jointly lie in a convex safe region under every scheduler. Watanabe and Unno (2026) prove safety by refining an outer approximation of the failure probabilities, where each query bounds a nonnegative weighted sum of the probabilities. Their rule selects weights by the largest Euclidean violation. We present a unified framework to measure violation in an explicitly chosen error unit: directions are scored by the support-function gap between the outer approximation and the safe region, normalized by the support function of the unit. We show that the maximal score, when positive, equals the smallest enlargement of the safe region in multiples of that unit that contains the outer approximation. The Euclidean unit recovers the earlier rule; two new rules are generated by the unit cube and the safe region itself. We experimentally evaluate how the choice of measurement rule affects the performance of safety verification for MDPs.

papers.title: Discovery or Memorization? A Faithful Benchmark for Real-World Business-Logic Vulnerability Discovery
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of cybersecurity agents in vulnerability discovery has increased the need for benchmarks that evaluate their capabilities accurately. However, synthetic benchmarks lack realism, real-life benchmarks are prone to contamination, and many existing benchmarks have already been saturated by current models. We therefore set out to develop a benchmark that is realistic, reproducible, resistant to contamination, and challenging. Our key insight is that real-life business-logic vulnerabilities are subtle and exercise complex application interactions, making them naturally demanding. The difficulty lies in specifying evaluation criteria precise enough to faithfully measure model capabilities while keeping the tasks free of data-leakage. We introduce AnonVul, a cross-language benchmark of 132 application-level business-logic vulnerabilities, built by a semi-automated pipeline that anonymizes each task, injects oracles from expert-written specifications, and differentially verifies proof-of-concept exploits. The benchmark spans nine languages, with two evaluation tracks on black-box and grey-box settings, where each task runs in a sandbox with specialized oracles embedded in key exploitation steps. We evaluate six state-of-the-art vulnerability-discovery agents on the AnonVul benchmark, measuring discovery success, cost-effectiveness, anonymization sensitivity, oracle validity, and failure modes. Our results show that AnonVul remains challenging, with the best agent succeeding in only 23.11% of attempts. On a matched cohort of 20 vulnerabilities, restoring software identity increases discovery from 21.25% to 40.83%, highlighting the importance of controlling recognizable software knowledge when evaluating vulnerability discovery.

papers.title: Aperiodic automorphisms of the Razak--Jacelon algebra
papers.abstract: We completely classify aperiodic automorphisms of the Razak--Jacelon algebra $\mathcal{W}$ up to outer conjugacy. As a technical ingredient, based on the works of Connes, Herman--Ocneanu, Kishimoto, and Sato, we introduce a notion of weak stability for automorphisms of simple separable monotracial C$^*$-algebras. We also consider automorphisms of UHF algebras of infinite type and the Jiang--Su algebra. In particular, we classify aperiodic ``UHF-absorbing'' automorphisms of UHF algebras of infinite type up to outer conjugacy.

papers.title: Many Steps into One: Reasoning Contraction and the Limits of Safe Memory Reuse for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Thought templates, skill libraries, agent memories and caches turn many reasoning steps into one. We call this reasoning contraction. A contracted memory saves reasoning steps and errors until its facts change, then quietly answers wrong. Most systems trust memories by counting successes and failures. We prove that such counters are badly tuned change detectors: a symmetric counter notices a partial change only after a power of its false-alarm horizon, and an unclipped one may never notice it. On five LLMs answering multi-hop questions over edited facts, ExpeL- and ACE-style counters serve 7.0-13.5x more stale answers than certified memories given the same information, and on code tasks with an exact verifier 35-73x more. Safety also has a price. When facts change and each memory is judged only by its own verified outcomes, one number, the certification load, sets how much reasoning any safe memory can skip, and under Zipf demand it yields a scaling law. Our recipe weighs each memory's failures by its own likelihood ratio, certifies its utility against live reasoning, and restarts the certificate when facts change, with the likelihood-ratio detector as the safety net for unannounced changes; for large edits it also invalidates the memory.

papers.title: Certifying Capacity and Gaps of the Rank-Dependent Gain-Sharing Framework for Ranking
papers.abstract: The randomized primal-dual framework of Devanur, Jain, and Kleinberg (SODA 2013) splits each unit matching gain between endpoint dual variables according to the matched offline rank. The gain-sharing function affects the certificate but not Ranking's decisions. Keeping the splitting rule and expected edgewise feasibility criterion fixed, we define certifying capacity as the strongest uniform guarantee obtainable by functional optimization over a prescribed function class. Its shortfall from Ranking's actual competitiveness is the certifying gap. We study unweighted online bipartite matching under adversarial arrivals on graphs with online degree at most $d$ and on $d$-regular graphs. The optimized protocol is tight on both degree-one classes and in the unrestricted setting, but has a strictly positive gap on both degree-two classes, even over all measurable nonnegative complementary splits. In both degree-two settings, we determine Ranking's exact competitiveness and the exact certifying capacity over nondecreasing gain-sharing functions. For general $d$, we optimize over nondecreasing, right-continuous functions $f:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ with $f(1)=1$, using their probability-measure representation. Both the certifying capacity and actual competitiveness converge to $1-1/e$ in both instance families as $d\to\infty$. The resulting gap is at most $1/(2ed)+O(d^{-2})$ for online degree at most $d$; on $d$-regular graphs, it vanishes but is at least $(1/(2e)-o(1))/d$. These results distinguish function-class restrictions from limitations of the fixed protocol and motivate tighter randomized primal-dual frameworks.

papers.title: FLAI Protocol: Decentralized Federated Learning with On-Chain Rewards and sPEG-Based Contribution Scoring
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without data centralization but struggles with incentive alignment, accountability, and robustness under heterogeneous non-IID data. Existing decentralized FL (DeFL) systems leverage blockchains for coordination yet face high on-chain overhead, unverifiable self-reports, and weak fairness guarantees. We present the FLAI Protocol, a trusted execution environment (TEE)-backed DeFL framework that integrates enclave-validated aggregation, sparse Peer Evaluation Graph (sPEG) scoring, and on-chain settlement. sPEG incorporates peer-based quality, class coverage, promptness, effort, and reputation into composite contribution scores. The protocol formalizes contribution evaluation and tokenized incentive distribution, ensuring verifiable fairness and resilience against free-riding and collusion. We evaluate FLAI on image, text, and healthcare datasets and demonstrate parity with FedAvg in utility while improving fairness and accountability. A case study in consumer eHealth (aggregating wearable and electronic health record data for real-world evidence generation) illustrates the protocol's applicability to privacy-critical domains where equitable rewards, auditability, and data sovereignty are essential.

papers.title: Fragments of SRP, the nonstationary ideal, and diagonal reflection
papers.abstract: We investigate the relationships between fragments of SRP and diagonal reflection principles. It turns out that the subcomplete fragment of SRP, augmented with CH, implies that the nonstationary ideal on $ω_1$ is not saturated, but that Larson's diagonal reflection principle $OSR_{ω_2}$ holds. In contrast, it was known that the full principle SRP implies the saturation of the nonstationary ideal on $ω_1$, but it does not imply $OSR_{ω_2}$. We find several instances of this phenomenon: pairing (variations of) the subcomplete fragment of SRP with stronger failures of the nonstationary ideal on $ω_1$ to be saturated allows us to conclude more instances of diagonal reflection principles, while boosting (the corresponding variations of) the full principle SRP with strong forms of the saturation of the nonstationary ideal allows us to produce models where these principles still hold, yet weaker versions of diagonal reflection fail.

papers.title: On the generalized cospectral mates of chain graphs of rank 4
papers.abstract: A graph is called a chain graph if it is bipartite and the neighborhoods of the vertices in each color class are linearly ordered by inclusion. We study the generalized spectral determination of chain graphs of adjacency rank $4$. We first show that generalized cospectral chain graphs have the same number of isolated vertices, reducing the problem to the connected case. For connected rank-$4$ chain graphs, we derive four explicit equations in the cell parameters that are necessary and sufficient for generalized cospectrality. These equations reduce to a quadratic equation in a single parameter. As a consequence, every connected rank-$4$ chain graph has at most one generalized cospectral mate, and the possible mate can be reconstructed explicitly. We further obtain a simple sufficient condition for a rank-$4$ chain graph to be determined by its generalized spectrum (DGS) and, in particular, prove that every double star graph is DGS. Finally, we construct an explicit infinite family of non-double-star rank-$4$ chain graphs that are DGS but not determined by their adjacency spectra, with both the graphs and their complements being connected.

papers.title: On Open Borel Orbits in Conormal Bundles to Schubert Cells
papers.abstract: Let $C(v)$ denote a Schubert cell in the flag variety $\operatorname{GL}_n/B$, and let $X(w)$ be a Schubert variety containing $C(v)$. Mellit has conjectured that, if $X(w)$ is smooth, the existence of an open $B$-orbit in the conormal bundle to $C(v)$ in $X(w)$ is equivalent to $C(w_0w)$ being contained in the smooth locus of $X(w_0v)$. We prove a stronger version of this conjecture, requiring only that $X(w)$ is factorial. We prove our result by constructing a sequence of graphs associated to the pair $v,w$ such that the existence of a cycle in one of these graphs is equivalent to the non-existence of such an open orbit.

papers.title: Reference Wording Shapes Retrieval of Robot Task Instructions
papers.abstract: Identifying a robot task from a short instruction is sensitive to which descriptions are available for retrieval. We investigate this effect in the natural-language instructions included with the RLBench manipulation benchmark. We extract 296 fixed descriptions from 62 publicly available task files and compare five training-free lexical rankers over 80 random choices of one indexed description per task. Exact strings assigned to conflicting task labels are excluded from the primary score. Character n-gram TF-IDF achieves 61.3% mean top-1 accuracy on the resulting held-out instructions, compared with 55.6% for BM25 and 54.9% for word TF-IDF. Across gallery choices, character TF-IDF ranges from 55.2% to 66.8%; its 5th-95th percentile range is 56.9%-64.8%. Adding a second indexed description improves character TF-IDF by 7.0 percentage points on matched queries. These results quantify the influence of reference wording and representation choice on instruction-to-task retrieval under a consistent evaluation protocol.

papers.title: Hurricane recovery gaps lie in reconnection, not local restart
papers.abstract: Climate-intensified hurricanes disrupt urban mobility, yet whether recovery is equitable across the rural-urban gradient is unclear. Analyzing device-based mobility for Hurricanes Helene and Milton, we find local activity restarted within approximately 4.5 days in both storms, whereas reconnection to the outside world took 5 days in coastal-urban Florida but 11 in inland-rural Appalachia. The gap lies in external reconnection, not local restart, implying planners should target rural isolation.

papers.title: Capacity over TFLOPS: Memory-Centric Deployment of Large Clinical Language Models on Consumer CPUs
papers.abstract: The dominant barrier to running large clinical language models at the point of care is not arithmetic throughput but graphics memory: consumer GPUs cap at 4-16 GB, while the working set of a 27-billion-parameter model in 4-bit precision is 17-25 GB. We argue that the edge node should be treated as capacity-enabled (system RAM) rather than compute-limited (GPU VRAM), and we test this on commodity hardware. Using an INT4 build of a 27B open model as an architecture-faithful stand-in for a 27B medical model, we measure the memory footprint, inference latency, energy, and federated communication cost of a fully CPU-based pipeline driven by synthetic Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) prompts. On two independent consumer machines (a desktop-class machine with 67 GB of RAM and a 6 GB GPU, and a mobile workstation with 34 GB of RAM and a 4 GB GPU) the model loads entirely into system RAM (37% and 60% utilization, respectively) while both GPUs are out-of-memory before the first step. Inference runs at overnight-batch speed (0.6-2.4 tokens/s for the 27B model), and federated fine-tuning would transmit only a 22.6 MB low-rank adapter, a 99.96% reduction over full weights. The capacity result is independent of CPU microarchitecture, RAM size, operating system, and GPU. We further identify an open, CPU- and NPU-optimized inference runtime as the natural production path for this approach, indicating a privacy-preserving and broadly deployable route for on-premises clinical AI. All data is synthetic; this is a research artifact and not a medical device.

papers.title: FlashVSR+: Efficient Video Super-Resolution via Hybrid Attention and Reward-Yield Distribution Matching
papers.abstract: Recent video super-resolution (VSR) models achieve efficient one-step generation through diffusion distillation. However, high-resolution inference remains costly, and distilled models are difficult to align with human preferences. These challenges call for improvements in both model architecture and training strategy. We present \textbf{FlashVSR+} to address both limitations. On the architecture side, we introduce hybrid attention based on the strong locality observed in pretrained VSR models, while retaining sparse global interaction for long-range consistency. It achieves up to $2\times$ DiT speedup and 45\% lower peak memory, enabling spatially untiled 4K VSR on a single 24GB RTX 4090. On the training side, we propose Reward-Yield Distribution Matching Distillation (Ry-DMD) for preference-aligned one-step generation. Ry-DMD uses reward-weighted teacher rollouts to incorporate black-box rewards into distribution matching, without backpropagating through the reward model. We further show that Ry-DMD generalizes beyond VSR to T2I generation. Together, FlashVSR+ delivers stronger restoration quality and substantially improves high-resolution efficiency, with consistent gains in user preference. We release our code, models, and training data at \href{https://www.flashvsr.tech}{\textcolor{FlashBlue}{\textbf{www.flashvsr.tech}}}.

papers.title: Efficient Shallow Ritz Method: 1D Semi-Linear Diffusion-Reaction and Allen-Cahn Equations
papers.abstract: An efficient shallow Ritz method was developed in [8, 9] for one-dimensional linear diffusion and diffusion-reaction problems. In this paper, the method is extended to a nonlinear diffusion-reaction equation with a cubic reaction term: (1) a basic error estimate of the shallow Ritz discretization is established and (2) a reduced block Newton (rBN) method for solving the resulting non-convex optimization problem is developed. Again, the computational cost of the rBN method is $\mathcal{O}(n)$ for one-dimensional problems, where $n$ is the number of neurons. Combining a convex splitting scheme for time discretization with the efficient shallow Ritz method, we develop a time-stepping neural network method for solving the Allen-Cahn equation. The unconditional energy stability of the time discretization and an error estimate in the $L^2$ norm are established. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the neural network approach yields accurate solutions for singularly perturbed nonlinear diffusion-reaction equations and the Allen-Cahn equation. The method effectively resolves interior and boundary layers without oscillations and significantly outperforms the finite element method on fixed uniform meshes.

papers.title: Timing Misalignment and Its Impact on OTFS and Other Delay-Based Waveforms
papers.abstract: The shift towards 6G wireless networks calls for advanced waveforms to support emerging applications such as ultra-reliable and massive machine-type communications. Among the proposed candidates, OTFS, ODDM, OTSM, and OCDM share the common feature of exploiting the delay domain for data transmission. While these waveforms offer significant advantages in high-mobility and sensing scenarios, their integration into multi-user uplink systems reveals a critical challenge: timing misalignment (TM). Unlike OFDM, where residual timing offsets translate into phase rotations, delay-based waveforms experience actual shifts of resources, whose impact we investigate in this work. We show that the aforementioned waveforms can be unified under a time-invariant setup through a common input--output relation, which enables a unified analysis of TM in uplink resource allocation. The results reveal a fundamental trade-off between interference mitigation and guard overhead in the presence of TM. We further benchmark the observed behavior against OFDM under Doppler spread as a reference impairment and highlight the analogy between TM in delay-based allocation and Doppler spread in frequency-based allocation. The results show that delay-based waveforms can maintain a net performance advantage over OFDM in the considered setup. Beyond this unified Doppler-free analysis, we evaluate the joint impact of Doppler spread and TM on each waveform individually. We also investigate BER performance and show how coding can mitigate the resulting interference. This study therefore establishes a problem framework that motivates the development of future compensation and scheduling strategies for practical multi-user operation of delay-based waveforms.

papers.title: ATOM: Abstract Transition and Option Modeling - Experience-Informed Hierarchical Navigation
papers.abstract: We propose ATOM (Abstract Transition and Option Modeling), a hierarchical navigation framework that combines higher-level graph planning with reusable lower-level option policies for efficient repeated navigation in large-scale 3D environments represented by hierarchical structures such as 3D scene graphs (3DSGs). ATOM operates on a hierarchical graph representation, implemented using, for instance, the Rooms and Places layers of a 3DSG, where each directed abstract transition is associated with a navigation option. For each transition, ATOM computes and stores a reusable option policy along with its state-dependent cost-to-go. Across repeated navigation tasks, ATOM maintains a smoothed empirical distribution over option initiation states and uses it to progressively refine the corresponding abstract transition cost. Ablation studies show that ATOM reduces cumulative repeated-planning time by 97.5% relative to a monolithic MDP baseline while maintaining trajectories within approximately 7% of a Global Places A* shortest-path reference. Experience-informed refinement further reduces abstract transition-cost estimation error by 10.3%. Physical experiments validate ATOM on an F1Tenth vehicle, successfully completing all five navigation queries with 43% of inter-region option executions reusing previously generated solutions.

papers.title: Sulphur-bearing molecule survey towards prestellar and starless cores in the Perseus molecular cloud
papers.abstract: Sulphur is drastically depleted from the gas phase in dense starless and prestellar cores, creating the long-standing "missing sulphur problem". Observations of sulphur-bearing molecules are crucial to understanding sulphur chemistry, core-environment relationships, and the physical evolution of star-forming regions. We present a survey of four sulphur-bearing molecules, HCS+, OCS, H2CS, and SO, towards 15 starless and prestellar cores in the Perseus molecular cloud using the Yebes 40m telescope. The HCS+ 1-0, OCS 3-2 and 4-3, H2CS 1_{0,1}-0_{0,0}, and SO 3_2-2_2 transitions were observed, fitted with Gaussian profiles, and column densities were calculated assuming local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE). We also compare these with observations of CS, CCS, and CCCS from a previous study. HCS+, OCS, H2CS, and SO are detected in 100%, 93%, 100%, and 73% of the sample, respectively. Derived column densities are (2.2-17.0)x10^11 cm^-2 for HCS+, (1.9-25.0)x10^12 cm^-2 for OCS, (1.0-15.0)x10^12 cm^-2 for H2CS, and (0.3-17.0)x10^13 cm^-2 for SO, spanning over an order of magnitude. HCS+ and SO abundances strongly correlate (inversely and directly, respectively) with core volume density, reinforcing their early- and late-type status. Correlations indicate a differentiation between carbon and oxygen chemistry for sulphur-bearing molecules, with CS showing the strongest correlations as expected. Cores in protostellar outflow paths do not show consistently higher abundances. The chemical age (SO/CS) correlates with physical age (volume density), except for Per752, an outlier likely linked to an enhanced cosmic ray ionization rate. These results provide a robust observational baseline constraining chemical models of sulphur chemistry in early star formation.

papers.title: A modern particle-in-cell code for beam-beam simulations of future colliders
papers.abstract: A key challenge in the design of next-generation colliders is predicting the effects of beam-beam interactions and using these predictions to optimize machine performance. Beam-beam interactions are characterized by strong focusing forces, radiative effects, and the generation of background particles. While analytical formulas provide insight into the dynamics of beam-beam interactions, these nonlinear, coupled effects are most accurately described with numerical methods. In this paper, we introduce the open-source particle-in-cell code WarpX as a modern tool for modeling the interaction point in future lepton colliders. WarpX provides high-performance execution on distributed GPU architectures within an open-source and actively maintained code base. We present convergence scans and benchmarks against the established beam-beam codes GUINEA-PIG (v1.2.2) and CAIN (v2.42) for luminosity spectra, photon emission, and secondary-particle production under a wide range of beam parameters corresponding to different collider concepts. Our results show that WarpX (v26.09) reproduces the benchmark beam-beam observables while enabling GPU-portable, extensible simulations. These results establish WarpX as a scalable platform for high-fidelity beam-beam modeling in future collider studies.

papers.title: The $\ell$-degree Turán densities of hypergraphs: infinite families and their finite subfamilies
papers.abstract: Let $k>\ell\ge 1$ be integers. For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-uniform hypergraphs ($k$-graphs), its $\ell$-degree Turán density $γ^{(k)}_\ell(\mathcal{F})$ is the asymptotic maximum of the normalized minimum $\ell$-degree over all $\mathcal{F}$-free $k$-graphs. In this paper, we prove that for all integers $k>\ell>2$ and every $α\in[0,1)$, there exists an infinite family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-graphs such that $γ^{(k)}_\ell(\mathcal{F})=α$, while every finite subfamily $\mathcal{F}'\subset \mathcal{F}$ satisfies $γ^{(k)}_\ell(\mathcal{F}')>α$. This confirms the conjecture of Mubayi and Zhao on codegree Turán densities for every $k > 3$. As an immediate consequence, the set $Γ^{k,\ell}_{\infty}$ of $\ell$-degree Turán densities of nonempty $k$-graph families is $[0,1)$ whenever $k>\ell>2$, which answers a question of Lo and Markström from 2014.

papers.title: A radio counterpart of the local little-red-dot J092359+415736
papers.abstract: Little red dots (LRDs) are compact red sources at z>~4. Broad lines suggest accreting black holes, yet radio and X-ray measurements are usually weak. Local LRDs allow multi-frequency, multi-epoch radio studies that are inaccessible at high redshift. We search archival radio images for a counterpart to the local LRD J092359+415736 at z~0.323, quantify its long-term radio variability, and identify the plausible origin of the radio emission. Flux densities at the optical position are measured in FIRST, LoTSS, RACS, VAST, and VLASS products spanning 0.144-3.0 GHz and 1994-2024. A compact 144 MHz counterpart is detected at 42sigma in LoTSS, coincident with the Gaia position, and is recovered in FIRST, RACS, VAST, and VLASS. LoTSS and ASKAP give a spectral index alpha ~ -0.30 +/- 0.11. The source varies on multiple timescales: FIRST at 1.4 GHz (1994) is a factor of ~2.6 below ASKAP (2021-2024) and below the extrapolated LoTSS-ASKAP spectrum, indicating long-term brightening over 26 yr; the 3 GHz flux density rises by 2.3sigma between VLASS epochs 2.2 and 3.2. A star-formation-only origin would require ~200 Msun/yr, against an unobscured H-alpha upper limit of 3.3 Msun/yr, implying an extreme obscured starburst. Ordinary radio supernovae and tidal disruption events are strongly disfavoured by the luminosity and 30-yr recovery, while refractive scintillation would itself require an ultracompact nuclear emitter. The persistent radio counterpart is best explained by accretion onto the central black hole. Among the three radio-detected local LRDs, this source is intermediate in luminosity and the only one with reported multi-year variability, adding a temporal dimension to the radio diversity of the class.

papers.title: EdgeWise: Bringing Long-Horizon Agents to the Edge via Selective Cloud Delegation
papers.abstract: Complex and long-horizon agent tasks often rely on frontier models deployed in the cloud to achieve strong performance. However, using these models for every step of a long-horizon trajectory incurs substantial inference cost, even though not all steps may require the same level of model capability. In this paper, we find that allocating the LLM to only a small subset of key steps can achieve performance comparable to full LLM execution while significantly reducing inference cost. Motivated by this observation, we propose EdgeWise, an edge-cloud collaboration framework that deploys an SLM on the local device as the primary solver and selectively delegates critical steps to a cloud LLM when stronger model capacity is needed. To enable autonomous delegation without additional models at inference time, we introduce a step-level RL method that jointly optimizes task solving and delegation, with fine-grained credit assignment for individual delegation decisions. We also introduce an external judge-based delegation strategy and use it to systematically investigate key design choices in edge-cloud collaboration, including when to delegate, how delegation decisions should be made, what context should be shared, and how frequently the cloud LLM should be invoked. Experiments show that EdgeWise matches or outperforms pure-LLM execution while reducing inference cost up to 62% on SWE-Rebench and 34% on Terminal-Bench 2.1. We further deploy EdgeWise on a local workstation, demonstrating comparable cost savings in a practical edge-cloud setting.
