papers.title: The hypervariational method: a general, automated technique based on innovations to tune the parameters of the Hybrid covariance matrix
papers.abstract: The Hybrid forecast covariance model is an operationally successful way to build a background error covariance matrix. It is constructed as a weighted sum, with scalar weights, of the climatological covariance matrix and a localized ensemble covariance matrix, with a localization matrix typically depending on a localization length. For best performance, the Hybrid needs to be optimized by tuning those weights and, possibly, other parameters, such as the localization length. Here, a systematic and automated method for this tuning operation is introduced. This technique is referred to as hypervariational method, and it is formulated in terms of a cost function, built using a time series of innovations as an essential ingredient. This cost function, which depends on the parameters, is minimized when they have optimal values. Equations for its minimization, based on Newton's method, are derived. Besides the aforementioned, commonly used Hybrid, the hypervariational method is applicable to any known Hybrid (and to any set of parameters on which it depends analytically), including recently developed Hybrids, not necessarily constructed as weighted sums. Here, the hypervariational method is applied to tune the ensemble covariance matrix weight in the seminal-formulation Hybrid (which does not feature localization). This is done in a synthetic experimental setting where a theoretically-derived expression for the optimal value for that weight is known. Moreover, in that experimental setting, a further method, based on a linear fit procedure, to determine that optimal value is possible. Both the hypervariational method and that linear fit procedure are shown to produce an optimal weight value matching (up to a tolerance of $0.1$) the optimal value known from the theory. Furthermore, Newton's minimization in the hypervariational method is shown to converge immediately (at the first recursive step).

papers.title: Mobility-Budget-Constrained Submodular Maximization for Distributed Semantic Multi-Robot Exploration
papers.abstract: Multi-robot exploration under communication and mobility constraints requires balancing information gain with reachability. We present a distributed semantic exploration framework that combines Dirichlet mapping, budget-constrained trajectory selection, and Resource-Aware distributed Greedy (RAG) coordination. Each robot clusters frontiers, computes terrain- and heading-aware least-cost paths with a single budget-limited Dijkstra search, and selects feasible paths by marginal information gain, represented by the expected reduction in Dirichlet entropy. Each robot's per-round selection is exact, the team's joint per-round information gain is at least half the centralized optimum, and the bound degrades gracefully under limited communication. Ten-run gridworld ablations show improved coverage, semantic mIoU, and map certainty with lower entropy and traversal cost per unit distance than shortest-distance frontier selection. Budget-sensitivity experiments show that an intermediate budget best balances path reach and receding-horizon execution. In photorealistic full-system simulation against five coordination rules run in their native published forms, the proposed method attains the highest mean coverage and semantic accuracy while being the only one that respects the per-trajectory mobility budget.

papers.title: Boundary Control of a Modified Timoshenko-Ehrenfest Beam via Reduced-Order Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the active vibration control of an elastic beam using reinforcement learning (RL). The physical system is modeled by a modified Timoshenko-Ehrenfest type linear partial differential equation with simply supported boundary conditions. The dynamics are approximated by a reduced-order model (ROM) obtained through eigenvalue expansion and truncated Galerkin projection. Control is applied through boundary actuation. The resulting finite-dimensional system is formulated as a continuous-time Markov decision process and solved numerically using the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm. All modeling steps, from physical formulation to temporal discretization and control design, are explicitly described. A systematic comparison is performed between the controller learned via PPO and the classical linear quadratic (LQR) regulator. The analysis highlights the strengths and limitations of each approach, both from a theoretical and practical point of view, with particular emphasis on energy dissipation mechanisms and actuator constraints.

papers.title: Elastic Properties of Titan Tholins Revealed by Brillouin Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Titan tholins, complex organic solids synthesized by simulating photochemical processes in Titan's atmosphere, are widely regarded as analogs to organic surface materials on the Saturnian moon. Their mechanical properties are critical for understanding the evolution of Titan's geomorphology and crustal layering. Here, we report the first direct experimental determination of the complete set of aggregate elastic moduli of tholins using Brillouin spectroscopy. Measurements conducted on tholin powder samples yielded a bulk modulus of 11 (2) GPa and a shear modulus of 3.9 (5) GPa, from which we derive a Young's modulus of 11 (1) GPa and a Poisson's ratio of 0.34 (3). Thin-film samples synthesized under slightly different conditions yield similar results. Compared with other Titan-relevant organic compounds, tholins exhibit the highest elastic stiffness measured to date, exceeding even H2O ice in both bulk and shear moduli. These results support the interpretation that complex organics contribute significantly to the mechanical stability and transport behavior of Titan's equatorial dune sediments. Measurements following prolonged atmospheric exposure reveal persistent stiffening of tholins that remains after vacuum treatment, likely associated with minor chemical modification and physical reorganization, highlighting the importance of controlled sample handling for future laboratory investigations. This study also demonstrates the effectiveness of Brillouin spectroscopy as a non-destructive technique for characterizing planetary organic materials and provides new constraints relevant to future seismic and geophysical investigations by the Dragonfly mission.

papers.title: On the Real Waring Rank of a Biharmonic Form
papers.abstract: We develop an effective method for determining the real Waring rank and the real border rank of biharmonic binary forms. By means of real apolarity, we convert both of these problems into membership questions for regions bounded by a hypocycloid and an epicycloid. We further provide a computable algebraic criterion for the relevant memberships, which involves only the signs of certain real-valued resultants.

papers.title: Learning or Modeling? Virtual XL-RIS Observation Reconstruction for Near-Field Sensing
papers.abstract: A passive extremely large-scale reconfigurable intelligent surface (XL-RIS) offers a position-sensitive aperture for near-field sensing, but its element-wise signals are not directly observed. Recovering this virtual RIS observation (VOR) from fewer base-station measurements requires prior information. This paper investigates when calibrated propagation geometry or paired training data provides the more effective reconstruction prior. For a common sensing operator and target signal, we develop off-grid near-field sparse parametric reconstruction (OG-NF-SPR) and compare it with compact and DenseNet-based deep reconstructors. OG-NF-SPR uses reflected-path projection for position initialization, followed by Bayesian estimation of all path gains and continuous position refinement. A causal extension incorporates temporal correlation without trajectory labels. Controlled simulations use near-field UAV tracking as an illustration and separately examine noise, position-distribution shift, calibration error, and propagation mismatch. Under matched propagation at 20 dB, OG-NF-SPR achieves approximately 67% lower reconstruction NMSE than the two nominal deep networks. At low SNR, statistical averaging is more effective than selecting a single geometric explanation. Under sufficiently strong repeatable mismatch, a same-size network trained on the mismatch family outperforms the nominal physical estimator, whereas nominal training does not provide this benefit. Temporal regularization also reduces position RMSE from 0.653 m to 0.225 m on a shared trajectory. The results relate reconstruction performance to measurement quality, calibration accuracy, and training coverage, providing guidance on when geometry can replace supervised labels and when additional data are useful.

papers.title: Targeted Entropy-Stable Nonlinear Artificial Dissipation for High-Order Spectral-Element Summation-By-Parts Discretizations
papers.abstract: Artificial dissipation improves the robustness of high-order methods for under-resolved flows, but can compromise accuracy and suppress physically relevant structures if its strength and spatial distribution are not appropriately controlled. We present a sensor-activated nonlinear artificial-dissipation framework, inspired by the residual correction method, for continuous and discontinuous summation-by-parts discretizations. In contrast to many existing spectral-element dissipation operators that either reduce the formal order of accuracy or target only the highest polynomial modes, the proposed framework permits design- and higher-order dissipation with explicit control over its magnitude, spatial distribution, activation, and convergence rate under mesh refinement. This modular construction also recovers several existing methods through appropriate choices of its components. The dissipation preserves discrete conservation and semidiscrete entropy stability whenever the base method satisfies these properties. It is dimensionally consistent, element local, and discretization agnostic, as the added term is constructed independently of the base spatial residual. For smooth solutions under suitable mesh assumptions, we establish parameter choices that retain the formal accuracy of the base discretization. Numerical experiments with summation-by-parts discretizations of the Burgers and Euler equations demonstrate substantially improved robustness for under-resolved flows and flows with shock waves while retaining high-order accuracy for smooth solutions, using the same parameter choices across several test problems. Overall, these results show that targeted dissipation can improve the robustness of high-order methods without excessive damping of resolved flow structures.

papers.title: A Structure-Preserving Effective Linear Approximation of the Quantum Boltzmann Collision Operator
papers.abstract: We construct a structure-preserving effective linear approximation of the quantum Boltzmann collision operator for Bose and Fermi gases in the normal phase. For variable hard-sphere kernels, the resulting Fourier spectral evaluation costs $O(N_v^4\log N_v)$, with $N_v$ velocity nodes per direction and no angular quadrature factor. The continuous operator conserves mass, momentum and energy and satisfies a linearized $H$-theorem. We also use the operator at local quantum equilibrium as an approximate collision Jacobian in a modified Newton solver that retains the full nonlinear residual. Numerical tests show smaller errors than the quantum BGK model in homogeneous relaxation and fewer full collision evaluations for steady Couette and Fourier flows than the same Newton solver using a quantum BGK Jacobian.

papers.title: An $\eps$-regularity criterion at one scale for 3-D Navier-Stokes equations and improved upper bound on the box dimension of the interior singular set
papers.abstract: In this paper, we obtain an $\varepsilon$-regularity criterion at one scale for 3D Navier-Stokes equations using a coarse-to-refined estimate argument based on mean-fluctuation decomposition. Making use of this $\varepsilon$-regularity criterion, we improve the upper bound on the box dimension of the interior singular set to $15/13$.

papers.title: Puncturing-inclusion constructions of optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes using semifield codes
papers.abstract: Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes are essential components of the multilevel construction of constant dimension codes for random network coding. This paper aims to construct optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes, focusing on the diagram \([3,3,3,5]\) with rank distance \(3\). We construct an optimal \([[3,3,3,5],6,3]_q\) Ferrers diagram rank-metric code for every prime power \(q\), thereby answering an open problem posed by Etzion et al. in 2016~\cite{Etzion2016}. The construction first builds a \([3\times4,4,3]_q\) MRD code and then proves that the Delsarte dual of its puncturing on the last column contains a \([3\times3,3,3]_q\) MRD code, which comes from semifield codes. We further construct optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes for two infinite families of Ferrers diagrams: the first relies on the \([[3,3,3,5],6,3]_q\) construction and holds for every prime power \(q\), while the second is binary and obtained directly by the puncturing-inclusion construction.

papers.title: On the existence problem for a double mean field equation and its application to prescribed curvature problems
papers.abstract: Let $(M,g)$ be a compact Riemann surface with smooth boundary $\partial M$. Let $K(x)>0$, $h(x)> 0$ or $h(x)\equiv 0$ be two smooth functions on $M$ and $\partial M$ respectively. In this paper, we consider the following double mean field type equation with a nonlinear Neumann boundary condition related to a prescribed curvature problem \begin{equation}\label{equation:01} \begin{cases} \displaystyle -Δ_g u+\frac{4π}{|M|} =2ρ\frac{Ke^u}{\int_MKe^u\,dv_g}, & \text{in }M,\\[1.2em] \displaystyle \partial_νu =2ρ'\frac{he^{u/2}}{\int_{\partial M}he^{u/2}\,ds_g}, & \text{on }\partial M, \end{cases} \end{equation} where $ρ> 0,\ ρ'\geq 0$ and $ρ+ρ'=2π$, $ν$ is the outward unit normal vector to $\partial M$. When $h\equiv 0$, the second equation changes to $\partial_νu=0$ on $\partial M$. By introducing a boundary integration constant, we obtain a sufficient condition under which \eqref{equation:01} admits a solution. As a geometric application, we solve the prescribed curvature equation for both the Gauss curvature and the geodesic curvature in the case that $M$ is topologically a disk. When $(M,g)$ is the standard hemisphere $\mathbb S^2_+$, let $p\in \partial \mathbb S^2_+$ be a maximum point of $$ Φ(q)=h(q)+\sqrt{h(q)^2+K(q)}, \qquad q\in\partial \mathbb S^2_+. $$ Suppose \begin{equation*} K_ν(p)+2Φ(p)(-Δ_{\partial \mathbb S^2_+})^{1/2}h(p)<0. \end{equation*} Then the prescribed curvature problem \begin{align*} -Δ_g u+\frac{4π}{|M|}=2Ke^u, \text{in }\mathbb S^2_+,\ \ \partial_νu=2he^{u/2}, \text{on }\partial \mathbb S^2_+. \end{align*} admits a smooth solution.

papers.title: EgoCPT: Learning Dexterous Manipulation from a Single Ego-Centric Video with Contact-Aware Optimization
papers.abstract: While expert demonstrations on real robots are difficult to collect, human ego-centric videos are easy to collect and abundant on the internet. However, learning dexterous manipulation policies from human videos remains challenging---one of the most important challenges being the difficulty of reconstructing physically grounded robot trajectories due to the large embodiment gap. In this paper, we propose EgoCPT, a novel paradigm for learning high-quality retargeted dexterous hand trajectories directly from an ego-centric video, which can then be deployed directly on real robots. The only inputs to our method are an ego-centric RGB video and a reference hand pose trajectory, which can be easily obtained through off-the-shelf software or specialized cameras during recording. Our method is particularly robust to noisy hand poses attributed to our novel contact-aware optimization framework, which iteratively optimizes the contact points between the robot hands and objects. Across five manipulation tasks, our method achieves overall success rates of 67.3% on noisy EgoDex hand-pose reconstructions and 92.0% on high-quality TACO reconstructions collected using motion-capture hardware, outperforming multiple baselines on both benchmarks.

papers.title: Benchmarking Self-Supervised 3D Medical Vision Foundation Models and Transferability Estimation
papers.abstract: Self-supervised pretraining has expanded the pool of 3D medical foundation models, but published evaluations use different datasets, endpoints and fine-tuning protocols. Models also differ in architecture, pretraining objective and data, while downstream targets range from voxel-level masks to patient-level diagnoses and outcomes. As a result, published findings provide little directly comparable evidence for choosing a model for a new task. Direct comparison of adaptation performance requires fine-tuning candidates on labelled target data, at substantial computational cost. We benchmark 23 candidates across the same 14 segmentation, classification and regression tasks spanning multiple anatomies and modalities. No candidate ranked among the top three across all segmentation tasks or across all classification and regression tasks; a convolutional encoder could outperform a transformer trained with the same objective on one task but underperform it on another. We benchmark transferability estimators against the fine-tuned rankings and find that their agreement varies across dense segmentation, classification and regression. InsightRank uses task-appropriate frozen-feature statistics and architecture-aware pairwise comparisons to rank candidates before fine-tuning. Across the 23-model pool, mean Kendall tau-b was 0.431 for segmentation and 0.352 for classification and regression. The segmentation Top 3 contained a task winner on four of nine tasks; the image-level Top 3 contained none on the five tasks, despite better full-ranking agreement than the matched conventional estimators. A three-model shortlist reduced recorded extraction-plus-training job time by 85.8% across seven segmentation tasks. Together, the benchmark provides a common reference for model selection and InsightRank offers a lower-cost way to prioritize fine-tuning, with shortlist performance that differs by target type.

papers.title: TacSpin: Tactile Tracking of In-Gripper Object Rotation on SO(3) via Axis-Magnitude Estimation
papers.abstract: Tracking object motion within a gripper provides essential feedback for robotic manipulation. However, limited contact coverage and uneven deformation make tactile estimation challenging. In this study, we present TacSpin, a method that tracks in-gripper object rotation on SO(3) using only two vision-based tactile sensors. The key idea is to estimate the axis and magnitude of the rotation response separately, rather than fitting a rigid-body model by least squares. Each finger's response is further refined with contact-boundary cues. The two fingers are then fused according to their agreement. On standard objects, TacSpin achieves lower mean checkpoint errors. Qualitative demonstrations on real-world objects, using calibration transferred from a standard sphere, illustrate tracking under different contact geometries.

papers.title: Mergers may not be the main channel for galaxy stellar mass growth at redshift $z\gtrsim5$: Predictions from cosmological hierarchical models and simulations
papers.abstract: Mergers are a crucial channel of galaxy growth, but their role relative to star formation remains uncertain at high redshift. Here we investigate merger rates and merger-driven stellar mass assembly for galaxies with stellar mass $M_\star \gtrsim 10^8 \, {\rm M_{\odot}}$ at $z\simeq 5-11$, by combining complementary theoretical approaches within $Λ$CDM. These include the DECODE semi-empirical model, the TNG100 and EAGLE hydrodynamical simulations, and the \textsc{L-Galaxies} semi-analytical model, together with the Millennium and TNG100-Dark simulations used to examine dark matter subhalo statistics and merger timescales. This compares models with different treatments of baryonic physics and galaxy-halo connections. We find that dark matter-only simulations predict merger timescales $\sim 30\%$ longer than those inferred from cosmological simulations including baryons. Galaxy major merger ($M_{\rm \star,sat} / M_{\rm \star,cen} > 0.25$) rates are high at cosmic dawn and increase towards earlier epochs, reaching $\sim 1/{\rm Gyr}$ at $z\sim 5$ and peaking at $\sim 3/{\rm Gyr}$ at $z\sim 8$. Despite these high rates, mergers contribute only $\lesssim 10\%$ of the total cosmic stellar mass density evolution. The ex-situ stellar mass fraction ranges from a few percent to $\sim 20\%$ for all galaxies at $z\gtrsim 5$, across different models and simulations. Their broad agreement implies that stellar mass assembly at cosmic dawn is dominated by in-situ star formation rather than mergers. These findings suggest that the high pair fractions identified by JWST may not directly trace efficient ex-situ stellar mass growth, highlighting the need for physically motivated merger timescales to interpret galaxy assembly in the early Universe.

papers.title: Dissociating Answerability from Extraction in LLM Question Answering over Radiology Reports
papers.abstract: Answering questions from radiology reports involves two decisions: whether the report contains an answer and which span gives it. A false answer presents an unsupported claim as fact; an over-abstention hides what the report says. Yet RadQA results are reported as a single F1 that merges both. We propose an evaluation method that separates them, reporting false-answer and over-abstention rates beside F1 and splitting F1 changes into extraction and answerability terms. We apply it to 13 LLMs on the RadQA test set, zero-shot and with three cumulative demonstration sets, the last adding an unanswerable example. Models with similar F1 differed more than twofold in false-answer rate. The unanswerable example changed when models answered, not how well they extracted: 12 of 13 models abstained more often, and three-quarters of the answers they withdrew had F1 $\geq$ 0.5. Within models, false answers showed no clear association with extraction quality, but acting on the decision itself helped: keeping an answer only when enough other models also answered lowered the zero-shot false-answer rate by 4 points without a detectable F1 change. Because the two decisions can change independently, we suggest radiology QA evaluations report them separately, not through F1 alone.

papers.title: Non-equilibrium chemistry and radiation hydrodynamics in metal-poor and metal-rich interstellar gas
papers.abstract: We present a flexible implementation of non-equilibrium chemical networks with the $\texttt{KROME}$ framework, coupled to a nonlocal variable Eddington tensor-closed radiation transport scheme ($\texttt{VETTAM}$). Our fiducial network is designed to explicitly capture the formation pathways of important molecular species such as CO, OH, and $\rm H_2O$, intermediaries like $\rm H_3^+$, and the destruction of these species through photon and cosmic-ray dissociation. We validate our scheme through benchmark tests, and demonstrate its success in 1D and 3D problems covering a broad range of metallicities ($0 \leq Z \lesssim \rm Z_{\odot}$) and densities ($n \lesssim 10^{17} \, \rm cm^{-3}$). We confirm earlier works that suggest that OH and $\rm H_2O$ are the key molecular species in dense gas ($n \gtrsim 10^{5} \, \rm cm^{-3}$) for $Z\lesssim 0.01 \rm Z_{\odot}$, dominate the cooling at these densities, and demonstrate that our scheme can reproduce their abundances with similar accuracy as dedicated static photo-dissociation region (PDR) codes. We also find that the dominant fine-structure coolant in dense ($n \gtrsim 10^3 \, \, \rm cm^{-3}$) PDRs transitions from CI to CII to OI at increasingly lower $Z$. Finally, we find that in turbulent media, rapid mixing at PDR interfaces renders the chemical species out of equilibrium, and show that this could potentially alleviate the long-standing problem of (static) PDR models producing excess CI in the diffuse ISM over UV absorption-line measurements. We conclude by presenting and comparing with alternative implementations of reduced but faster chemical networks in our scheme, discussing the problem-dependent performance-accuracy tradeoffs and future prospects.

papers.title: Cross-Project Bug Localization: What Works, What Doesn't, and Why
papers.abstract: Bug localization models require substantial within-project training data that newly active or small open-source projects rarely have. Cross-project learning (CPL) promises to close this gap by reusing labeled bugs from mature projects, but prior CPL studies evaluate a single model against ample-data within-project baselines that data-scarce projects cannot reach. We ask whether CPL's effectiveness is a property of the transfer setting or depends on model architecture. We evaluate three architecturally distinct models, embedding-based BLAZE, convolutional TRANP-CNN, and GNN-based adversarial COOBA, on 63 source to target pairs from 13 open-source Python projects under identical bug corpora, data splits, retrieval candidates, and baselines. The primary baseline is within-project limited training (WP-small, 20% of target labels, the same target-side share as CP-transfer). CPL outperforms WP-small most clearly for TRANP-CNN (Cohen's d = 0.95, win rate 81.0%, p < 0.001, robust to clustering pairs by target project), and less so for BLAZE (d = 0.49, win rate 60.3%, p = 0.002; not significant once pairs are clustered by target). COOBA, under our re-implementation, shows a small gain that does not survive multiple-comparison correction (d = 0.27, p = 0.027). Negative transfer affects 9.5% of TRANP-CNN pairs and 30.2% of BLAZE's and COOBA's. Cross-model direction agreement is only 44-54%: the same pair can help one architecture and harm another, although the models' gains are positively correlated (rho = 0.24-0.42). CPL outcomes are therefore architecture-dependent: practitioners should validate CPL for their chosen model, and CPL studies should report results per architecture.

papers.title: Risk-Averse Inference-Time Diffusion Model Alignment with Finite-Sample Guarantees
papers.abstract: Inference-time alignment steers diffusion models toward downstream objectives without costly fine-tuning, but existing methods typically optimize expected cost (or reward) without explicitly controlling tail risk. In this work, we propose a risk-averse framework for inference-time alignment of diffusion models that balances expected cost and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) under trajectory-level Kullback-Leibler regularization. We characterize the optimal path distribution and reverse transitions as functions of the CVaR threshold, reducing the alignment problem to a one-dimensional optimization problem over the threshold. We show that this one-dimensional optimization problem can be nonconvex in general, establish sufficient conditions for convexity, and introduce quadratic regularization to enable efficient derivative-free ternary search. Under suitable assumptions, we provide finite-sample guarantees for threshold optimization and value estimation, and combine them into a terminal total-variation bound relative to the regularized target under exact resampling. Experiments on synthetic data and image generation using Stable Diffusion demonstrate improved tail performance over risk-neutral baselines while maintaining competitive average cost.

papers.title: Nonhomogeneous Subordinators and Lévy Copulas for Reliability Analysis of Time-Dependent Degradation Processes
papers.abstract: Many systems in engineering applications may experience complex multi-dimensional degradation processes involving random jumps. Analyzing the reliability of such degradation processes presents significant challenges. Previously developed models have utilized multi-dimensional Lévy subordinators and Lévy copulas to describe these processes, with reliability functions expressed through characteristic functions and Laplace transforms (Shu et al., 2015, 2016, Shi et al., 2020, Shi and Feng, 2024). However, these models are restricted to stationary linear paths and homogeneous Lévy subordinators. In real-world scenarios, increments in a degradation process are often time-dependent and nonhomogeneous. To address this limitation of previous studies, this work extends existing degradation models by introducing nonhomogeneous Lévy subordinators, which are designed to capture time-varying complexities inherent in degradation processes. Unlike conventional degradation models that often assume a constant rate of jumps, nonhomogeneous Lévy subordinators aim to provide a more flexible representation of degradation behaviors that evolve under varying external conditions and internal system dynamics. Additionally, the joint behaviors of multiple degradation processes are characterized using Lévy copulas, enabling a more comprehensive analysis of system reliability. Numerical examples are provided to illustrate the applicability of these models in lifetime analysis.

papers.title: Query Complexity of Densest Sub(hyper)graph Problems
papers.abstract: Rubinstein et al. introduce the study of connectivity and minimum cut problems in the cut query model, where an algorithm can only access the edges of a graph through CUT queries. In this work, we examine the query complexity of densest subgraph problems. Our first contribution is to generalize the uniform sparsification approach for Densest Subgraph and other heavy subgraph problems to weighted graphs, achieving the following results. >A $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximation for weighted Densest Subgraph in $O(n\log^2 n/\varepsilon^2)$ queries, roughly matching the $Ω(n/\log n)$ lower bound we prove for randomized algorithms. >A $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximation for weighted Max Cut in $O(n\log^2 n/\varepsilon^2)$ queries. This improves upon the bound of $O(n\log^3 n(\log n+1/\varepsilon^2))$ queries achieved by Plevrakis et al., making significant progress towards their lower bound of $Ω(n/\log n)$ queries. In contrast, we rule out approximation schemes with truly subquadratic query complexity for Densest $k$-Subgraph and settle its exact query complexity in both the unweighted and deterministic settings. For hypergraphs, we show CUT queries alone cannot achieve $o(\sqrt{n})$-approximation for Densest Subhypergraph or $o(n)$-approximation for Densest $k$-Subhypergraph, regardless of the number of queries. Augmenting CUT queries with the EDGE oracle of Chen et al., we overcome this barrier for Densest Subhypergraph and obtain a $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximation on rank-$r$ hypergraphs using $O(nr\log n/\varepsilon^2)$ queries. We also extend our Densest $k$-Subgraph hardness results to hypergraphs and prove exponential query lower bounds for exact Densest $k$-Subhypergraph. Lastly, confirming a conjecture of Chakrabarty and Liao, we show that simulating an ADD query using CUT and IS-EDGE$^?$ queries requires exponentially-many queries.

papers.title: Chasing Label Shifters: A Change-Aware Framework for Dynamic Graph Node Classification
papers.abstract: Entities in real-world systems often evolve over time: users shift between information consumption patterns, researchers migrate between fields, and firms transition between financial risk states. When such systems are modeled as dynamic graphs, these transitions correspond to nodes whose class labels change between consecutive snapshots, which we call shifters. Correctly classifying shifters is often more consequential than classifying stable nodes with persistent labels, as detecting such transitions enables timely intervention in high-stakes settings. Yet, we identify a systematic failure mode across all major dynamic graph neural network architectures: shifter performance consistently lags behind stable nodes, with errors concentrated on the old label. Our structural analysis traces this failure to embedding inertia: neighborhood aggregation keeps shifter representations anchored to the old-class centroid, and this effect is strongest precisely where it is hardest to correct, namely for shifters whose neighborhoods remain aligned with the old class. Guided by this finding, we propose CHASE, a model-agnostic CHange-Aware framework for Shifting nodEs that wraps any dynamic GNN with targeted components for detecting label shifts and overriding stale neighborhood signals. CHASE consistently improves shifter performance across all tested models and datasets (up to 114.9% and 202.5% improvement on accuracy and F1 score, respectively) while preserving stable-node performance. We additionally contribute three dynamic graph benchmarks with naturally shifting labels, filling a gap in existing resources. The source code is available at https://github.com/jhkim611/CHASE

papers.title: Coherent optical control of a thousand qubits in a three-dimensional trapped-ion crystal
papers.abstract: Leading quantum platforms are largely limited to one or two dimensions, whereas three-dimensional Coulomb crystals of trapped ions self-assemble into dense qubit arrays with no rearrangement overhead. Coherent optical control of such crystals has nonetheless been out of reach, because the optical transition couples to nearly all $3N$ collective modes, i.e., a thermally occupied quasi-continuum bath. Here we cool about 3,600 modes of a crystal of over 1,200 ions below single-phonon occupation, using a continuous cooling band that spans more than five octaves in vibrational spectrum, from about 50 kHz to 2.1 MHz. The crystal then serves as a register of optical qubits, allowing global initialization, coherent manipulation and collective detection. We demonstrate ensemble optical coherence of 21.6 milliseconds and reduce the optical-transition frequency uncertainty from 389 Hz for a single ion to 12 Hz for over a thousand ions, approaching the expected projection-noise scaling. Our approach could be extended to even larger crystals with phonon-mediated many-body couplings, opening a route towards entanglement-enhanced precision metrology and three-dimensional quantum simulation, particularly with spatial-shaped illumination for region-resolved collective control.

papers.title: RAN-JEPA: An Action-Conditioned World Model for Energy-efficient Mobile Network Control
papers.abstract: Operational mobile networks are rich in observations but poor in interventions: they continuously generate large volumes of passive telemetry, while controlled action--response trajectories remain comparatively scarce and costly to collect. This observation--intervention asymmetry is a central obstacle to building practical world models for RAN control. We address this problem with RAN-JEPA, an action-conditioned world model that separates representation learning from intervention learning. The model first learns a predictive latent representation from observation-only network data, adapts that representation to the target deployment domain, and then learns action-conditioned latent dynamics from controlled sleep/wake trajectories while keeping the encoder fixed. We evaluate RAN-JEPA using public operator performance data for pretraining and a real-equipment four-cell 5G testbed for domain adaptation, post-training, and control. Across four future 15-minute intervals, RAN-JEPA achieves lower action-conditioned prediction error than a GPT-2 world-model baseline and a mechanistic rule, while remaining close to a strong persistence reference. What-if evaluation further shows that the model produces distinct and coherent future trajectories under matched SLEEP and KEEP plans. In closed-loop control, RAN-JEPA consistently supports higher sleep ratios than the two baselines at comparable congestion cost. These results show that observation-first, action-conditioned learning can turn abundant passive telemetry and limited intervention data into a practical predictive model for energy-aware RAN control.

papers.title: Global existence of large strong solutions to the 3D compressible micropolar equations with density-dependent viscosities
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the Cauchy problem for the three-dimensional (3D) compressible micropolar equations with density-dependent viscosities. By classical $L^p$ estimates to elliptic system, defining suitable energy functions, after the elaborate index analysis, we establish the global existence of strong solutions to the system with all viscosities depending density as long as the initial density is large enough. By product, We also prove the existence of global large strong solutions with only large initial shear viscosity $μ_1(ρ)$ and angular viscosity $μ_2(ρ)$, which consists with the research work \cite{ZZ2014} of 3D compressible Navier-Stokes equations with constant viscosities and improve the recent result of \cite{HLZ} in some extent where they requiring both initial shear viscosity and bulk viscosity to be large.

papers.title: High-Throughput LLM-Based Compression and What It Takes: A Systems Study of Inference Engines and Entropy Coding Optimizations
papers.abstract: Large language models are attractive text compressors because next-token probabilities can be converted into code lengths. In practice, however, the main bottleneck is often not modeling quality but systems cost: a compressor must obtain logits quickly enough to compete with strong classical baselines. This paper examines systems optimizations for LLM-based compression, including multistream pipelined arithmetic coding and target-interval capture, and evaluates their trade-offs across inference engines, configurations and datasets. We evaluate LLM-based text compression on three different inference engines: Transformers, vLLM, and TensorRT-LLM. Notably, we obtain a speedup of 18.84x compared to prior work's Transformers implementation and a maximum recorded inference speed of 181 kilobytes per second at a compression ratio of 7.17, when running on an NVIDIA A100.

papers.title: Inverse design of poles and zeros: tailoring phase control in metasurfaces
papers.abstract: We develop a physically interpretable inverse-design framework for generalized Huygens metasurfaces, using prescribed scattering poles and zeros to engineer resonance interference and transmission-phase control. Compared with direct optimization of transmission or reflection coefficients, this approach offers a physically transparent route to rationally controlling resonance properties, including linewidth and group delay, while reducing computational work. The resulting designs demonstrate how near-unity transmission and $2π$ phase excursion can arise from resonance interference. These signatures of the Kerker effect extend beyond the conventional alignment of electric and magnetic dipole resonances to other mechanisms, including guided-mode resonances and quasi-bound states in the continuum. We further optimize the Kerker condition across a continuum of refractive-index states in a reconfigurable phase change material metasurface, enabling high-transmission $2π$ phase tuning. Our results establish a versatile and practical approach to metasurface phase control through the targeted design of scattering poles and zeros.

papers.title: Taming Softmax at the Limits of Muon: A Unified Approach through Hilbert Geometry
papers.abstract: Muon controls weight updates through the RMS movement of a linear layer's output. This implicitly treats the linear output as a proxy for the full module, including the nonlinearity that follows. This proxy can be misleading for softmax, where the RMS shift in activations does not faithfully measure the change in the output distribution. We propose Hilbert distance as a natural metric for bounding changes in these output distributions. Hilbert distance bounds changes in cross-entropy loss and limits probability redistribution. For softmax, it takes the form of the variation seminorm of the preactivation perturbation, allowing probability constraints to be expressed as parameter constraints. Formulating the steepest descent problem with a Hilbert distance constraint brings two recently proposed methods under a unified mathematical framework. For the LM head, solving a row-wise approximation to the resulting diameter-constrained problem leads us to RowNorm \citep{pethick2025trainingdeeplearningmodels}. For scaled dot-product attention, the same principle yields the first-order query--key steepest descent problem underlying Compositional Muon \citep{keigwin2026compositional}. These connections motivate using Hilbert distance as a guiding principle for optimizer design in softmax modules.

papers.title: Roth's theorem on weighted projective lines
papers.abstract: Let ${\mathbb P}^1_{\mathfrak q}$ be the weighted projective line with coprime weights ${\mathfrak q}=(q_0,q_1)$ and $L=q_0q_1$. The weighted Veronese map $Φ\colon {\mathbb P}^1_{\mathfrak q}\to {\mathbb P}^1$ satisfies $h\circΦ=L\,{\mathfrak s}$. Pulling back Roth's theorem gives the optimal exponent $2L$ for the full rational orbit set. For points represented by coprime integral coordinates, counting suggests the smaller exponent $q_0+q_1$. We formulate this as a conjecture and prove an $S$-adic radical form under the $abc$ conjecture. For ${\mathfrak q}=(2,3)$ the resulting inequality at the target $[1:1]$ is the coprime Hall-type inequality, and Danilov--Elkies examples show that the exponent $5$ is sharp. We also prove the expected exponent unconditionally over characteristic-zero function fields for constant targets and polynomial approximants, and for almost every real target. A weighted $abc$ formulation is introduced; in signature $(3,2)$ finitely many coefficient pairs are equivalent to $abc$, and weighted Belyi maps transfer this input to arbitrary algebraic targets. Applications include a pullback form of Schmidt's subspace theorem, weighted Thue inequalities, and a counterexample to a naive weighted rescaling of Roth's index construction.

papers.title: Revisiting the 16x Pretraining Compute Gap between Diffusion and Autoregressive Language Models
papers.abstract: Diffusion language models (DLMs) have attracted wide attention for their fast, parallel decoding, but they are believed to be far less efficient to train than autoregressive language models (ARMs): a widely cited study reports that a DLM needs roughly 16x the training compute of an ARM to match its likelihood, a figure that has made pretraining DLMs from scratch look prohibitive at scale. We find that the methodology behind this figure has fallen out of step with current DLM practice: it scores the model with its evidence lower bound (ELBO) and trains a full-sequence, decoder-only model. We therefore revisit the scaling laws of DLMs, adopting the exact likelihood under the model's own decoding order, block diffusion training, an encoder-decoder architecture, and a sweep over the block sizes used in practice. Under this new protocol, we study across ten model variants, about 1,700 models in total, and find that pretraining DLMs is far cheaper than previously thought. Concretely, scoring with the exact likelihood reduces the compute multiple to 12.8x; block diffusion training and an encoder-decoder architecture further reduce it to 7.8x at block size 32, and smaller block sizes narrow it to 4.6x at block size 8 and 3.0x at block size 4. We complement these scaling analyses with an empirical rule for the optimal decoder depth of encoder-decoder block diffusion, a held-out compute budget beyond the fitting range at which the gap between variants persists, and downstream benchmark results where likelihood improvements carry over to accuracy. Overall, the 16x figure substantially overstates the pretraining cost gap between DLMs and ARMs, and pretraining DLMs from scratch is far more viable than previously assumed.

papers.title: Physical-Field-Bridged Material Parameter Inference from Multi-View Deformation Videos
papers.abstract: Estimating simulation-ready material parameters from visual observations is crucial for deformable-object manipulation but challenging because material properties are only indirectly revealed through physical responses. We introduce physical-field-bridged material inference, a single-pass framework that uses dense physical responses to connect multi-view RGB deformation videos with constitutive-type classification and continuous parameter regression. Unlike inverse-physics methods requiring per-scene reconstruction, online tuning, or simulation-in-the-loop optimization, our model predicts force/contact masks, projected motion-flow fields, and projected stress-response maps, then conditions material inference on these fields to reduce reliance on appearance or category shortcuts. We construct DeformFieldBench, a 3DGS MPM learning environment comprising 5,000 simulations across 100 object shapes and five mechanically informative loading modes, with dense pixel-aligned physical supervision. Our method achieves the best median errors on all four continuous parameters, improves stress-hotspot recall from 0.0762 to 0.5121, and attains 0.8676 SSIM/36.82 dB PSNR in same-simulator replay on unseen objects. Under a protocol-matched GSO evaluation, inference and future-state prediction take approximately 30 seconds, compared with 15-120 minutes for per-scene optimization. The method also yields measurable replay agreement on five real-world sequences. These results support dense physical fields as an effective bridge for fast material inference, while cross-simulator and real-world tests reveal remaining domain and identifiability gaps.

papers.title: Universal entanglement detection with geometrically optimal witnesses
papers.abstract: Constructing optimal entanglement witnesses for arbitrary quantum systems remains a formidable challenge, hindered by the structural complexity of high-dimensional quantum state spaces. In this work, we overcome this barrier by introducing a unified framework for constructing geometrically optimal witnesses capable of identifying arbitrary entanglement structures. By leveraging the geometric properties of a target quantum state relative to a specific entanglement structure in Hilbert-Schmidt space, these witnesses are constructed in an efficient and effective manner. Among all nontrivial witnesses, they provide maximal distinguishability between the target state and the set of states without the desired entanglement structure. As a result, our approach enables the universal detection of bipartite, multipartite, and high-dimensional entanglement. To demonstrate its experimental feasibility, we apply the framework to a four-qubit nuclear spin quantum system. Compared to existing methods, our approach offers enhanced noise robustness, broader detection universality, and improved construction efficiency, providing a powerful and versatile tool for advancing the characterization and understanding of entanglement in quantum systems.

papers.title: Training Generalist Navigation Policies via Action Self-Distillation
papers.abstract: Language provides a natural interface for humans to specify and reason about goals, but training language-conditioned robotic policies and reasoning typically requires expensive manual annotations. We propose Action Self-Distillation (ASD), a method for learning language-conditioned reasoning for robotic navigation without human-annotated language or reasoning labels. ASD uses an open-source VLM, which contains broad world knowledge and reasoning capabilities, as both a teacher network and a student policy. During training, the self-teacher receives privileged trajectory feedback and infers the underlying navigation goal together with goal-oriented reasoning. The student is then trained to condition on the inferred navigation goal, predict future ego-frame trajectory, and provide a description of the scene semantics, plan, and reasoning, from onboard observations alone. Across 13 challenging indoor and outdoor real-world navigation tasks, our method improves success rate over the strongest baseline by $30\%$ in indoor settings, $30\%$ on multi-stage tasks, and achieves $95\%$ success rate on outdoor tasks, validating that privileged trajectory feedback can enable self-distillation for scalable generalist navigation policies without human annotations.

papers.title: Effects of Coulomb Collisions on the Structures of Fast Magnetosonic Shocks
papers.abstract: We present fully kinetic particle-in-cell simulations to demonstrate qualitative effects of binary Coulomb collisions on fast magnetosonic shocks. We find that with sufficiently high collisional frequencies, shock rippling and reformation can be inhibited, leading to stationary, laminar shock fronts. We observe that ion-ion collisions disrupt the motion of particles reflected back upstream that is the key for cyclical reformation. Meanwhile, the electron-ion collisions provide a Spitzer resistivity that can dissipate energy from the instability that causes shock rippling. This result helps us understand the role of collisions in laboratory shocks and possibly the outer heliosphere.

papers.title: Gas radiation and the gravity limit of flicker in a co-flowing hydrogen jet diffusion flame
papers.abstract: Although weak at normal gravity, gas radiation sets the gravity at which a co-flowing hydrogen jet diffusion flame stops flickering. Flamelet-based simulations with unity Lewis numbers, which reproduce the flicker frequency measured by femtosecond coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering within 4%, are combined with local stability analysis. At one tenth of normal gravity, the adiabatic flame flickers, the radiating flame does not, and switching the emission off restores flicker. Radiation acts through two mechanisms that do not weaken at reduced gravity. The hot outer layer loses buoyancy in proportion to the gas residence time, and a disturbance that displaces the flame also displaces its emission, which damps the disturbance on the lean flank (displaced-emission damping). Freezing the radiative source, which removes only its response to disturbances, slows the downstream recession of the oscillation more than tenfold. Both mechanisms slow the upstream spreading of disturbances. This spreading, competing with the co-flow, sets the onset location and the critical co-flow. Without radiation, the spreading speed scales with the square root of gravity; its radiative reduction does not. At reduced gravity, the flicker limit therefore becomes a straight line relating the square root of the co-flow Froude number to a radiation number, the ratio of buoyant to radiative time scales. The calibrated line places the critical gravity for the experimental co-flow at 0.13 times normal gravity, 2.6 times the adiabatic value. It correctly predicted whether two further flames keep flickering. Beyond the limit, transient wave packets can mimic flicker throughout a short drop-tower test.

papers.title: Tanawpamana: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models on Philippine Cultural Heritage Sites
papers.abstract: Vision-language models are increasingly used to identify and describe places, yet their recognition and knowledge of specific cultures remain poorly understood, particularly in underrepresented regions such as the Philippines. This study introduces the Tanawpamana Dataset, a repository of Philippine heritage site images with metadata based on the Talapamana registry of the National Commission for Culture and the Arts of the Philippines. We also introduce the Tanawpamana Benchmark, comprising 4,046 tasks designed to evaluate models' recognition and knowledge of heritage sites. Evaluating seven vision-language models, we find that they struggle more with fine-grained visual discrimination among similar heritage sites than with coarse recognition, and that their geographic knowledge is weaker when inferred from image inputs than from text.

papers.title: TDR: Tagalog Diacritic Restoration Dataset
papers.abstract: Homographs are words that share identical spelling but differ in meaning and pronunciation. In Tagalog, these distinctions are disambiguated in writing through tuldik (diacritical marks), which are rarely preserved in contemporary Tagalog text. This scarcity of diacritics limits diacritic restoration, which is useful for downstream tasks such as prosody selection for text-to-speech synthesis. To address this gap, this study introduces TDR, an annotated corpus of 40 frequent Tagalog homographs constructed from news text. It also introduces a collocation-driven retrieval method to expand the dataset and mitigate severe class imbalance among minor variants. Finally, we show that TDR supplies a capability absent from pretrained models, and that this capability can be learned by small, inexpensive models as well as by fine-tuned LLMs.

papers.title: On extending induced subgraphs
papers.abstract: When characterizing graphs defined by forbidden induced subgraphs, it is often desirable to understand how a graph $G$ can be generated incrementally from a given induced subgraph $H$. In this paper, we study a number of problems within this framework. First, for several notions of connectivity, we determine all minimal induced subgraphs of $G$ that contain $H$ and attain the connectivity of $G$. Second, we establish how to grow $H$ inside $G$ while preserving twin-freeness and certain forms of connectivity. Third, we establish {\it finite test theorems} for various graph classes, proving that agreement with the recursively generated graphs for a few initial iterations forces agreement at all subsequent iterations. Consequently, such an infinite graph family can be completely determined by finitely many of its initial generations. As an application, we characterize $\{\mathbb L_1,\mathbb L_3\}$-free graphs, where $\mathbb L_1$ is the claw and $\mathbb L_3$ is another forbidden graph for line graphs. Our structural results reduce this problem to a finite verification, which is completed through computer-assisted computation.

papers.title: Fast charging of quantum batteries assisted by nonlinear couplings
papers.abstract: Charger-mediated quantum batteries offer promising opportunities for efficient energy transfer and storage at the quantum level, with potential advantages beyond their classical counterparts. Here, we theoretically demonstrate that nonlinear charger-battery interactions can substantially accelerate the charging of quantum batteries. In the weak-driving regime, sufficiently strong nonlinear coupling can dominate over the effect of dephasing and significantly reduce the charging time. In the strong- and optimal-driving regimes, where the optimal driving strength maximizes the steady-state ergotropy in the linear-coupling regime, nonlinear coupling gives rise to a new optimum in the charging time beyond that of the linear-coupling regime, accompanied by nearly critically damped dynamics. Remarkably, even in the absence of external driving, nonlinear coupling alone can substantially reduce the charging time, providing an alternative route toward fast battery charging. Our results establish nonlinear charger-battery coupling as an effective resource for accelerating quantum-battery charging and broaden the scope of interaction-enabled quantum advantages in energy transfer and storage.

papers.title: Strong convergence rate of the implicit midpoint method for stochastic KdV equations
papers.abstract: We establish a strong convergence rate for the implicit midpoint method applied to the periodic stochastic Korteweg-de Vries equation with additive noise, addressing a question that has remained open since the work of Debussche and Printems. To control nonlinear error growth, we obtain exponential integrability estimates for the exact and comparison solutions using the coercivity of a classical KdV invariant. We then derive local error bounds from estimates for the comparison solutions and control error accumulation through an $L^2$ error propagation identity that isolates a martingale increment. Under $H_0^{9/2}$ regularity assumptions on the noise and the deterministic initial data, we prove that, on every fixed finite time interval, the maximum $L^2(\mathbb{T})$ error at the time points is $O(h)$ in $L^p(Ω)$ for every $1\le p<\infty$. Notably, the exponential integrability and the convergence rate hold for every damping coefficient $λ\ge0$, including the undamped case $λ=0$. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted first-order convergence.

papers.title: Existence of positive solutions to anisotropic elliptic equations in the entire Euclidean space
papers.abstract: In this paper, we research an anisotropic elliptic equation in the entire Euclidean space R^{N} . Under the assumption that the nonlinearity of the equation has exponential or critical growth, we prove, by means of the mountain-pass theorem, that the equation admits a nontrivial positive weak solution. Moreover, applying the mountain-pass theorem and Ekeland's variational principle, we show that a perturbation of the equation possesses two distinct positive weak solutions.

papers.title: Clean handshake sequences
papers.abstract: After a basketball game, each of the $n$ players on Team A must shake hands with each of the $n$ players on Team B. What is the minimum number of (reversible, ambidextrous) gloves required so that zero germ transmission occurs? We show that the answer is $3n/2+o(n)$ and develop a general theory for prescribed handshake sets.

papers.title: Morphology-aware deep learning predicts colorectal cancer survival from whole-slide images
papers.abstract: Background: Five-year survival prediction from hematoxylin-and-eosin whole-slide images could support risk stratification, but the task is weakly supervised, and the tissue morphologies carrying prognostic information remain incompletely characterized. Methods: We conducted a retrospective secondary analysis using TCGA-COAD/READ (n=562) for morphology-specific analysis, Alliance/ CALGB 89803 (n=424) for model development, and SurGen (n=218) for external evaluation. We propose MorphContrast, a morphology-aware contrastive multiple-instance learning framework that uses tissue labels as structural supervision for five-year survival prediction. MorphContrast combines gated-attention pooling with three auxiliary objectives: patch-level morphology labels define within-patient contrasts, outcome concordance or discordance defines cross-patient contrasts within matched morphologies, and diversity regularization discourages representational collapse. Morphology-matched patches from patients with discordant outcomes serve as hard negatives, encouraging prognostic discrimination within comparable histologic contexts. Results: Morphology-specific models show weak but distributed prognostic discrimination: adipose tissue achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.622, stroma achieves 0.604, and both perform comparably to tumor epithelium (0.601-0.605). On Alliance/CALGB 89803, the single model achieves an AUC of 0.642, while the post hoc ensemble reaches a pooled out-of-fold AUC of 0.70 and a risk-group hazard ratio of 3.79 (95% confidence interval: 2.55-5.63). On the external SurGen colon cancer cohort (n=218), the single model and ensemble achieve AUCs of 0.669 and 0.678, respectively. Conclusions: These findings support tissue morphology as structural supervision for outcome-aware representation learning in colorectal cancer prognosis.

papers.title: Stability Transfer for Autonomous Systems via Higher-Order Taylor-Truncated Lyapunov Certificates
papers.abstract: We develop analytical sufficient conditions for certifying the local asymptotic stability of nonlinear autonomous systems based on Lyapunov functions derived from their finite-order Taylor polynomial approximations. This approach translates the stability analysis problem from the original nonlinear dynamics to a more computationally tractable polynomial domain. The derived conditions allow for the explicit calculation of a guaranteed inner approximation of the region of attraction ($\mathrm{ROA}$). We show how sum-of-squares (SOS) programming and grid search can be used to systematically search for polynomial Lyapunov functions that yield a large certified threshold radius and extract a certified invariant set inner approximation of the $\mathrm{ROA}$ of the nonpolynomial original system. The framework is then applied to a control tuning problem: finding reduced-effort Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) controllers that ensure that a given initial state of interest belongs to the certified $\mathrm{ROA}$ of the nonpolynomial closed loop system. The effectiveness of the overall methodology is demonstrated using a pendulum with nonlinear damping and a nonlinear control system.

papers.title: PLEDGE: Progressive Lossy Error-Bounded Compression of 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: Existing 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) codecs report reconstruction quality after compression, and give users little control over the distortion of individual primitives. We present PLEDGE, a training-free, progressive, error-bounded codec that translates four user-declared tolerances into per-primitive quantization bounds: screen-space position, footprint deformation due to rotation and scale, view-dependent color, and opacity. The bounds apply throughout a declared camera domain, including previously unseen viewpoints. Position and opacity are bounded directly; footprint deformation is bounded under the rasterizer's affine projection model, and color is bounded over all viewing directions. PLEDGE organizes quantized residuals into a progressive bitstream with explicit error bounds for every valid prefix. Experiments across thirteen scenes verify all declared per-mechanism bounds and demonstrate competitive rate-distortion performance. The four tolerances incur substantially different rate costs, so users can spend rate where their application needs it.

papers.title: Memorix: Managing Memory Selections for AI Agents
papers.abstract: AI agents now handle a growing share of tasks across sessions within a persistent project. Their behavior depends not only on the model, but heavily on the persistent state they read from the environment. Existing systems assemble this memory at use time, splicing selected files into the prompt as a one-off payload. As a result, per-task assembly is costly and can still miss critical material, failures cannot be traced or replayed, and agents can read documentation written for the wrong version. Our key insight is that what an agent should read is mostly determined by its project, so the selection can be computed once, ahead of time, and reused across tasks. We propose Memorix, an agent memory system that realizes this insight. Memorix achieves this via three key mechanisms: (1) an immutable and versioned Store pins every source by identity and reproduces historical layouts cheaply, (2) a View that splits selection (Derivations) from composition (Environment), making the result reproducible and shareable, and (3) Quests and Profiles keep a delivered view refreshable and available inside the project as sources evolve. We implement Memorix and evaluate it on SWE-ContextBench and LibEvolutionEval against mainstream agent memory systems. Precomputed Environments raise resolved rate by up to 1.5X and deliver the correct library version on every version-conditioned task, while cutting amortized cost by up to 100X and build time by up to 38X.

papers.title: Constrained Grid-Forming Control for Photovoltaic Systems: A Control Barrier Function Approach
papers.abstract: This paper leverages control barrier functions (CBFs) to systematically account for constraints of voltage source converters (VSCs) and photovoltaic (PV) resources in grid-forming (GFM) control. The proposed control combines (unconstrained) dual-port GFM control with control barrier functions (CBFs) to ensure reliable and safe operation of a GFM PV system under grid faults, sudden changes in irradiance, and load perturbations. First, CBFs are used to encode physical and operational limits of the PV system, namely current and voltage limits at its ac and dc terminals. Then, CBFs are used to restrict the dynamics of dual-port GFM control to within the VSC and PV limits during both transient and steady states. To this end, a cost function is defined that encodes trade-offs between forming the ac voltage phase angle/frequency and voltage magnitude under constraints. Then, real-time optimization is used to make the least modification, as measured by the cost function, to the (unconstrained) dual-port GFM control state to remain within the safe set encoded by the CBFs. Finally, the performance of the developed constrained GFM control is evaluated through EMT simulations in MATLAB/Simulink.

papers.title: Facts Don't Speak Louder than Words: The Behavioral Essence of Long-CoT Distillation
papers.abstract: While long chain-of-thought (CoT) distillation significantly improves the reasoning abilities of language models, its underlying mechanism remains poorly understood. Current pipelines generally rely on rejection sampling to gather reasoning traces across diverse prompts, assuming that factual correctness and broad problem coverage are indispensable. Surprisingly, we find that training exclusively on flawed reasoning trajectories or a restricted prompt set yields nearly comparable performance. Driven by this counterintuitive finding, we propose the Behavioral Hypothesis: the essence of Long-CoT distillation is behavioral alignment with structured reasoning patterns, rather than factual knowledge memorization. We then validate this by demonstrating substantial reasoning gains even when models are fine-tuned exclusively on previously mastered problems-effectively isolating behavioral alignment from novel knowledge injection. Having established that reasoning patterns are the true bottleneck, we investigate how to learn them across varying levels of complexity optimally. We reveal a critical interplay: while the recent probability-based loss excels at learning simple patterns, the standard cross-entropy loss is essential for scaling to complex CoTs. We believe these insights demystify CoT distillation and provide a principled foundation for the future development of reasoning models. Code is available on https://github.com/yuyongcan/Long-CoT-Distillation.

papers.title: $3$-manifold groups are linear
papers.abstract: We prove that the fundamental group of every compact graph $3$-manifold is linear over the complex numbers. As a corollary, all fundamental groups of compact $3$-manifolds are linear over the complex numbers.

papers.title: Verifier-Harness Co-Evolution for Training-Free Self-Improvement on Open-Ended Tasks
papers.abstract: Training-free self-improvement lets an agent use feedback to revise the response it is about to return and to update the harness state that shapes how it handles later tasks. On open-ended tasks that feedback rarely comes from reference answers or executable tests, so the agent has to rely on a model-based verifier. When the verifier is wrong, the current response can get worse, and misleading experience can persist across the task stream. A verifier that never changes also grows stale as the agent's responses improve and task demands shift. We introduce Unified Co-Evolution (UCoE), a training-free method that evolves an executable verifier program together with the agent's harness state while all model parameters stay fixed. UCoE synthesizes candidate verifier programs and tests them on response contrasts, pairs of responses that differ in one declared property and have a known preferred side. It selects the candidate whose discrimination on its weakest contrast family is highest, a quantity we call driving capacity. The selected verifier diagnoses one weakness in each draft, guides a single repair, decides which response is served, and determines whether the accepted repair may enter the harness state. As tasks complete, their diagnostics seed new candidate verifiers, which must beat the current verifier on the same contrasts before adoption. Across six open-ended benchmarks, UCoE averages 59.00% preference against matched direct generation with Qwen3-8B and 57.19% with Qwen3.8-27B, margins of 9.00 and 7.19 percentage points. On three verifiable benchmarks, the same method raises the mean from 36.06% for direct generation to 38.48%. Code is available at https://github.com/tianyi0216/Unified-Co-Evolution.

papers.title: OpenDepth: Repurposing Image Editing Priors for Robust Open-World Monocular Depth Estimation
papers.abstract: Recently, the integration of generative priors has revolutionized Monocular Depth Estimation (MDE), achieving state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance with remarkably high data efficiency. However, although methods based on Text-to-Image (T2I) models excel in general scenes, their efficacy degrades sharply when confronted with open-world environmental perturbations, such as illumination variations and adverse weather. Since T2I priors are optimized for semantic synthesis rather than preserving pixel-level structure, they struggle to decouple geometry from appearance under severe visual shifts, easily triggering structural hallucinations. Therefore, our core insight is to model open-world depth estimation as consistent geometric inference across multi-style images, fully leveraging the powerful structure-preserving editing priors of Image-to-Image (I2I) models. Based on this, we propose OpenDepth, a robust open-world MDE framework that introduces "Intra-Domain Awareness" -- the capability to map diverse stylistic inputs sharing identical geometry into a unified latent space. To achieve this, we first align shallow features within the Diffusion Transformer (DiT) to anchor degraded observations to unified geometric representations. Additionally, we introduce a joint RGB latent reconstruction task, requiring the model to recover clean RGB information from degraded inputs. This multi-stage strategy effectively decouples environmental style interference, compelling the model to focus strictly on underlying geometric recovery. Extensive evaluations show that OpenDepth sets new SOTA records for robust zero-shot depth estimation across standard and extreme weather benchmarks, demonstrating exceptional structural integrity and adaptability.

papers.title: A grand potential for molten-salt electrochemical phase diagrams from first principles
papers.abstract: The clean-energy transition is driving unprecedented demand for metals, whose extraction is among the largest industrial sources of carbon emissions. Molten-salt electrolysis offers a path toward carbon-free production of aluminum, iron, titanium, and critical metals. However, corrosive operating conditions and complex, multicomponent feedstocks make experimental development costly and challenging. Here, we introduce a first-principles framework for constructing electrochemical phase diagrams of multicomponent systems to accelerate electrode and electrolyte design and guide the selection of compatible materials and operating conditions for electrochemical cells. We derive a grand potential that generates these diagrams at scale, and supply free energies using first-principles data obtained through a fine-tuned foundation machine-learned interatomic potential. For silicon in molten CaCl$_2$, the construction not only recovers the experimental diagram when using the first-principles framework on a limited set of structures, but also predicts further domains when extended to a larger set of crystal structures. Finally, we demonstrate the predictive power of the approach by screening ten alkali and alkaline-earth halide electrolytes for aluminum electrowinning. Three thermodynamic criteria identify NaF, where cryolite emerges as the stable aluminum-bearing phase, recovering the chemistry that Hall and Héroult established empirically in 1886. The framework provides a first-principles basis for selecting compatible electrodes, electrolytes, and operating conditions toward low-carbon metal production from complex source materials.

papers.title: From Syndromes to Computation: A General Framework for Logical Operations in Quantum Error-Correcting Codes
papers.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires error-correcting codes that not only protect quantum information but also support useful logical operations with practical physical realizations. Here we develop a general framework in which the stabilizer syndromes of commuting Pauli rotations directly organize logical-gate design. We derive an exact codespace-preservation condition valid at arbitrary rotation angles, providing a common stabilizer-level description for CSS and non-CSS codes and for both Clifford and non-Clifford operations. A particularly useful equal-syndrome specialization reduces Clifford gate design to stabilizer factorization, yields a general generator weight bound of $\lceil d/2\rceil$ for distance-$d$ codes, and systematically extends to logical rotations higher in the Clifford hierarchy. Applied to bivariate-bicycle (BB) and non-CSS Mirror qLDPC codes, the framework gives explicit low-weight Clifford and controlled-phase gates. Our implementations yield new low-weight gates, including an addressed $T$ gate on the $[[16,4,4]]$ BB code, $T$-type rotations on the $[[64,8,8]]$ BB code, and CCZ-, CS-, and $T$-type operations on the $[[36,6,6]]$ Mirror code. We also develop analytic constructions using Clifford algebra bases, which turn the syndrome constraints into explicit algebraic relations and provide a systematic route to logical addressability. We use this approach to analytically construct addressed CNOT, SWAP, controlled, and CCZ-type gates on recursive hypercube codes. An independent construction on middle quantum Reed--Muller codes yields C${}^r$Z gates that saturate the equal-syndrome weight bound. These results establish stabilizer syndromes as a constructive link between the stabilizer structure of a quantum code, the logical computations it can directly support, and the fault-tolerance properties of their physical realizations.

papers.title: MAS-Gate: Unlocking Multi-Agent System Lifecycle via Node-Centric Quantification
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) can solve complex problems beyond the reach of a single agent by decomposing tasks and coordinating complementary capabilities. Despite extensive research on MAS, existing work largely focuses on specific aspects or individual phases of their development and operation, resulting in fragmented perspectives with objectives and signals that are difficult to reconcile across these different settings. To bridge these disconnected perspectives, we conceptualize MAS development and operation as a three-phase lifecycle spanning design-time orchestration before execution, runtime intervention during execution, and post-hoc attribution after execution, and introduce MAS-Gate, a unified node-centric quantification applicable across these phases. Modeling each execution as a directed acyclic graph, MAS-Gate combines within-node utility, which estimates a node's contribution through changes in reference-answer likelihood, with inter-node strength, which approximates semantic uptake and potential downstream reach. We adapt this shared quantification to three objectives: providing a structure-aware dense reward for Orchestrator training, training an Editor to act on execution prefixes using paired rewards from completed edited and unedited trajectories, and supplying risk-ranked nodes as auxiliary evidence for LLM-based post-hoc attribution. Experiments spanning interaction environments, knowledge-intensive multi-hop question answering, general reasoning, and post-hoc attribution demonstrate that MAS-Gate improves workflow construction, targeted runtime editing, and LLM-assisted error localization over corresponding phase-specific baselines. Together, these results establish MAS-Gate as a unified structural interface for improving MAS generation, dynamic editing, and error attribution throughout the lifecycle.

papers.title: Extending Layered Attestation into ARM Application Run-Times
papers.abstract: Modern mobile and edge platforms provide hardware-backed attestation of application and platform integrity at load-time. However, they offer little support once application execution begins. We present ARA, an Application-Runtime Anchor for ARM that extends this load-time chain of trust into execution. ARA bootstraps from the underlying ARM platform Root of Trust (RoT) through a measured loading chain and establishes an attested protected run-time within the application address space using recently introduced ARM Permission Overlay Extensions (POE). The resulting run-time domain can host programmable RoTs for Measurement and Storage (RTM/RTS), enabling application run-time integrity verification, attestation evidence generation, and protected use of secrets while retaining efficient access to application run-time state. As exemplary uses, we instantiate ARA for protected media decryption and application control flow measurement. Our prototype and evaluation show that ARA supports frequent run-time RoT-backed operations at near in-process cost, with roughly 10x and 50x lower overhead than out-of-process equivalents. This offers a practical bridge from layered attestation to application run-time trusted computing on ARM.

papers.title: Background2Background: a self-supervised background removal framework for high dimensional microscopy
papers.abstract: High-dimensional microscopy captures features across space, time, and spectrum, but complex backgrounds obscure signals. We present Background2Background (B2B), a self-supervised background removal framework leveraging the backgrounds larger correlation relative to the signal. Local pixel shuffling disrupts signal correlations while preserving background structure, transforming signals into effective noise for Noise2Noise-based background removal. Across fluorescence, stimulated Raman scattering and mid-infrared photothermal imaging, B2B achieves over 40-fold background suppression and reveals hidden signatures.

papers.title: StateHarness: Maintaining Evolving Project State for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Long-horizon coding requires agents to maintain an evolving view of the project they are changing: what problem is currently being solved, what has already been learned or modified, which other artifacts may be affected, and what work remains unresolved. When this information is scattered across a growing interaction history, local edits can become disconnected from their later consequences and progress can be difficult to carry forward. We introduce StateHarness, a runtime framework that maintains evolving project state without updating model parameters. The working agent records its current problem and hypothesis, important findings and decisions, discovered repository relationships, and unfinished work. Runtime support prompts record updates, searches for callers, tests, and documentation that may be affected by a change, and maintains a compact working brief for subsequent decisions.
