When behavioral signals accumulate, a separate diagnostic session revisits the recorded history and surfaces overlooked evidence. Across three repository-level evaluations, StateHarness improves task completion and several measures of change consistency. On RefactorBench, full-chain completion increases from 29.4% to 35.3% and cleanup-check accuracy from 87.0% to 95.4%. On five LHTB software-engineering tasks, mean reward improves from 0.427 to 0.576, exceeding LongHorizon-Harness at substantially lower recorded execution cost. On ChainSWE, bug-fix rate increases from 35.1% to 39.5% and residual debt decreases from 60 to 43 items, although pass-to-pass regressions increase. These results show that maintaining project state can improve long-horizon coding while introducing measurable execution and regression trade-offs.

papers.title: What Do Deepfake Audio Detectors Hear? From Self-Supervised Models to Audio LLMs
papers.abstract: Real-world audio recordings for deepfake detection rarely consist solely of speech; they often are mixtures of speech and background events that themselves may also be synthetic. When processing these mixtures, it remains unclear whether detectors attend to the speech or the background event, and where their spectral evidence lies. We study this on the CompSpoof V2 database, whose mixtures pair independently real-or-fake speech and event components. Our results show that all systems detect fake events more accurately than fake speech. However, this performance gap is largely driven by poor generalization to an unseen fake speech domain, rather than a true difference in difficulty. Furthermore, sub-band probing reveals that the front-end encoder dictates where a countermeasure focuses its frequency evidence. To enable reliable deployment in real-world scenarios, future countermeasures should address out-of-domain generalization failures and carefully select front-end encoders aligned with their target acoustic evidence. Our source code and checkpoints are released at https://github.com/nii-yamagishilab/AntiDeepfake-AudioLLM.

papers.title: Observational evidence of black hole event horizon from ultra-compact X-ray binaries
papers.abstract: The event horizon is the most crucial feature that distinguishes black hole (BH) from all other objects in the universe. However, since no radiation can escape from the event horizon, its direct observational evidence remains lacking. Although both are compact objects, the event horizon leads to differences in the radiative behavior between black hole and neutron star (NS) X-ray binaries. Historically efforts to probe the existence of event horizons revealed that the BH X-ray binaries are fainter than NSs with similar orbital periods in their quiescent states. Here, we use a special class of X-ray binaries namely the ultra-compact X-ray binaries (UCXBs), to reveal the existence of the event horizon near stellar-mass black holes. In short-period UCXBs, gravitational radiation dominates the orbital angular momentum loss, allowing us to accurately determine their accretion rates. Based on five UCXBs with orbital periods shorter than 40 min, located in globular clusters, and identified accretors (NS or BH), we obtained their accretion rates. Combining their accretion rates and X-ray luminosities, we calculated the X-ray radiative efficiencies of NS and BH. The radiative efficiency of BH is about two to three orders of magnitude lower than that of NS systems, indicating the accretion energy is swallowed by the BH, thereby indirectly probe the presence of the event horizon.

papers.title: When Does an ASR Error Matter? Task-Role Diagnostics for Tool-Using Voice Agents
papers.abstract: In cascaded voice agents, ASR errors can have markedly different downstream consequences: a small transcription error may leave a tool call unchanged or alter its intent or arguments. Conventional word error rate (WER), however, does not capture these differences. We introduce SpeechEvalX, a paired diagnostic protocol that evaluates how task roles affected by ASR errors influence structured tool calls. Controlled edits are matched by source utterance, edit count, and operation, while task-role labels are compared with lexical severity, BERT cosine distance, Semantic-WER, and binary criticality. Across 594 source utterances, joint call accuracy falls from 82.3% with reference transcripts to 71.9-74.9% across three ASR front ends. Number and negation edits cause 21.9-25.7 percentage-point losses, versus 1.4-2.9 points for control edits. Detailed task-role labels improve source-grouped ROC-AUC from 0.73 to 0.78 over binary criticality, showing that downstream impact depends strongly on the task role affected.

papers.title: Smartphone-Based, Field-Deployed AI Inspection System for Power Distribution Infrastructure
papers.abstract: Routine inspection of power distribution infrastructure remains challenging for utilities operating geographically dispersed networks, where conventional manual inspection can be difficult to perform consistently and at scale. This work presents a smartphone-based AI inspection system for assessing targeted distribution-infrastructure conditions from images captured by field personnel. The proposed workflow integrates image-quality and viewing-perspective validation with AI-assisted assessment of pole lean, crossarm and top-cleat tilt, voltage level, vegetation-clearance risk, and distribution-transformer (DTR)-ground clearance. The system integrates deep-learning models with monocular depth estimation, geometric analysis, and rule-based processing within a common multi-stage inspection workflow designed for practical field operation. The system was pilot deployed across five selected distribution feeders within the Eastern Power Distribution Company of Andhra Pradesh Ltd. (APEPDCL), where 1,222 defect instances were identified across the assessed categories and subsequently tracked through a rectification and verification workflow, with 84 defect instances recorded as rectified during the study period. Feeder-level interruption records were also examined over the study period; however, the available observations do not provide sufficient evidence to establish a reliability improvement attributable to the proposed system. A curated multi-module field-captured dataset, PD-Defect, is also publicly released to support reproducible research in distribution-infrastructure inspection. The field deployment demonstrates the practical integration of smartphone-based AI-assisted inspection into field inspection and maintenance activities, providing a mechanism for systematic identification, documentation, rectification tracking, and verification of targeted distribution-infrastructure defects.

papers.title: FedLoRD: Personalized Federated Learning based on Low-Rank Structures of Model Parameter Differences
papers.abstract: We propose FedLoRD, a personalized federated learning (PFL) method based on the low-rank structure of the differences between the global and personalized model parameters. PFL is a branch of federated learning that aims to learn models tailored to the local data of each client under biased local data distributions. In its local training, each client learns a personalized model by regularizing the difference between its model parameters and the global ones sent from the server. The regularization function needs to be designed with priors on the model parameter difference; however, the existing PFL methods rely on empirical choices (e.g., $\ell_1$- and $\ell_2$-norms), which do not take into account the actual characteristics of the difference. The resulting mismatch of priors can lead to suboptimal personalized models. To address this issue, we propose a PFL method whose regularizer is built on an observed characteristic of the model parameter differences: they are approximately low-rank at every layer. In our method, we first formulate a local training problem with nuclear norm regularization on the layer-wise differences. We further rewrite this problem via the factorized representation of the nuclear norm so that it can be efficiently solved by a plain stochastic gradient descent method. Image classification experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that FedLoRD outperforms several existing PFL methods.

papers.title: Kernel moments and thermodynamic stability in nonlocal Nambu--Jona-Lasinio models
papers.abstract: We study thermodynamic consistency and stability in a covariant two-flavor nonlocal Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model at zero chemical potential in the homogeneous quark mean-field approximation. A controlled large-source expansion gives a sufficient entropy-sign criterion directly from Euclidean kernel moments, without locating propagator poles. At fixed couplings and kernel, every admissible positive Gaussian mixture develops negative total entropy at sufficiently large source mass for each fixed positive temperature. In a separate light-source fit to pion observables and a subtracted condensate, one quartic-exponent kernel has positive entropy and heat capacity for all $T>0$, while $dP/dε=s/C_V$ exceeds unity on a finite interval. This constructive example separates thermal positivity from the static EOS slope test. Numerical refits show that the enhancement weakens with the condensate input, and a certified counterexample excludes uniform thermal positivity over the adopted matching domain. The results provide diagnostics of the mean-field functional, rather than a preferred phenomenological kernel. Omitted thermal mesons can change the low-temperature slope test, and the static derivative does not determine a real-time front velocity.

papers.title: RELAY: Selective Self-Distillation with Adaptive Hand-off for Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Rubric-based reinforcement learning grades a response against many written criteria but collapses them into one reward, which discards the detail the rubric carries and gives no GRPO reward gradient when a group's responses tie. A frozen teacher that reads the rubric as privileged context provides token-level supervision, but we observe an early plateau in the gains over GRPO. RELAY uses advantages and rewards to select positive-advantage and low-scoring zero-advantage rollouts, and monitors the distillation loss to decide when to retire the teacher. Stage 1 combines selective distillation from a frozen teacher with GRPO; a plateau detector then removes the teacher, and Stage 2 continues with GRPO alone. Calibrated on one model-domain pair and reused unchanged in three others, the plateau detector fires between steps 122 and 171. RELAY scores highest in-domain among the compared methods in all four settings, ahead of GRPO on RaR-Medicine by 4.62 points with Qwen3-1.7B and 6.02 with Qwen3-4B. On Qwen3-1.7B/Medicine, removing the teacher from a shared checkpoint outperforms keeping, weakening or refreshing it. Distilling selected rollouts covering about half the response tokens also outperforms distilling all rollouts at a matched average coefficient.

papers.title: Octupole parton structure of spin-3/2 targets
papers.abstract: In spin-$3/2$ targets, octupole polarization can reveal quark and gluon correlations beyond those probed by vector polarization and quadrupole alignment. Here, we construct the complete leading-twist gluon transverse-momentum-dependent distribution basis, with 32 independent coefficients for each specified Wilson-line and color structure. Fourteen of these describe octupole dependence in gluon number, helicity, and linear polarization. In heavy-quark-pair leptoproduction at small, nonzero pair imbalance, comparing target states with opposite octupoles and identical lower moments isolates the octupole contribution. Beam-helicity reversal and joint angular projections in target orientation and pair-imbalance azimuth can then separate all fourteen gluon octupole responses at leading-power Born order. We also derive the incoming-target quark responses in semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering and Drell-Yan production. Time-reversal relations between distributions remain valid under symmetry-preserving renormalization and evolution, while predictions across processes require factorization formulas connecting those distributions to scattering observables. Finally, we connect this framework to polarized $^{7}$Li through its collinear limits and nuclear spin-orbital correlations.

papers.title: 4LC: 4D Latent Cache for Efficient Conditioning in Dynamic World Modeling
papers.abstract: For video generation in dynamic world modeling, observed static and dynamic content should be efficiently reused to provide conditions for repeated generation at different times and viewpoints. We introduce 4LC, a 4D latent cache with composite visual representations and a flexible spatiotemporal access interface. As a latent cache, 4LC directly reuses visual representations of static and dynamic content to provide generation conditions, avoiding per-request RGB rendering and re-encoding. As a composite cache, 4LC binds visual representations from multiple visual encoders (e.g., VAE, DINO, V-JEPA, VGGT) to shared geometry and motion, allowing the composite representations to describe the dynamic world with rich information. Besides, we design a flexible spatiotemporal interface, which directly reads the cache at independently specified times and viewpoints and combines readouts across observations, providing a common conditioning format for diverse downstream tasks. Building on 4LC, we develop 4LC-Video to address multiple video generation tasks through different configurations of source observations, spatiotemporal requests, and historical reuse, including camera control, temporal control, novel-view synthesis, scene revisits, and long-term generation. Our experiments show more efficient condition acquisition, effective spatiotemporal controllability, and scene consistency across tasks using a single 4LC-Video model without task-specific fine-tuning.

papers.title: Optimal transportation under McKean-Vlasov dynamics
papers.abstract: We study a broad class of stochastic transport problems under controlled McKean-Vlasov dynamics, allowing control of both drift and volatility, with weak terminal constraints. In contrast to the classical Schrödinger problem, the reference dynamics depend on the evolving law of the process, leading to nonlinear optimization problems on path space, while the terminal constraint is formulated through weak optimal transport, permitting a flexible treatment of distributional targets. This framework encompasses several problems of current interest, including the mean field Schrödinger problem, martingale optimal transport, and Schrödinger-Bass bridges. We establish three main results. First, we prove the existence of optimal controls under general coercivity, continuity, and convexity assumptions. Second, we derive a convex dual representation that extends weak Kantorovich duality and stochastic optimal transport duality to controlled McKean-Vlasov dynamics. Finally, for the mean field Schrödinger problem, we prove convergence, at the level of value functions, of the associated finite-particle Schrödinger bridge problems to the mean field limit, thereby identifying the nonlinear problem as the exact infinite-particle limit of finite-particle Schrödinger bridges. As a byproduct, we establish the existence of an optimal mean field Schrödinger potential, providing a variational foundation for duality in nonlinear stochastic transport.

papers.title: AiSAQ-in-Filtering for DRAM-free Filtered Information Retrieval
papers.abstract: Filtering search is one of the crucial applications of approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS). In filtering search, label information is used in conjunction with unstructured vector data. ANNS provides efficient similarity search in large-scale datasets, however, the memory footprint of storing both vector data and their associated label becomes a significant cost factor as dataset sizes grow. To address this problem of increasing DRAM usage, we propose AiSAQ-in-Filtering, with a novel quantization method called LiPQ (Label-inclusive Product Quantization). LiPQ combines unstructured data and structured labels into a single representation, leading no growth of encoded data. Our proposal increased recall@1 of single-label searches by up to 55% and fewer disk I/Os compared with existing methods. This also retains the main advantages of AiSAQ, which can reduce DRAM footprint by up to 1/78 and index switching time comparing with existing methods. This proposal can also be applied to sparse-dense hybrid search beyond label filtering such as semantic and keyword search of documents.

papers.title: Black holes with dark matter halos and a positive cosmological constant: Energy conditions and signatures
papers.abstract: We study static, spherically symmetric black holes surrounded by dark matter halos in the presence of a positive cosmological constant. Assuming vanishing radial pressure, we derive the constraints imposed by the null, weak, strong, and dominant energy conditions on the halo matter. The halo is confined to a finite radial interval separated from both horizons, and the total mass is bounded above by the Nariai value. We construct a Hernquist-type profile and study black hole images, showing that a positive cosmological constant can substantially change the images. We also compute scalar quasinormal modes of the Hernquist-type spacetime. When the dark matter mass is sufficiently small, the relative difference of a selected mode is approximately linear in the compactness of the matter halo, i.e., the ratio of mass parameter $M_{\text{DM}}$ and scale parameter $a$, with a coefficient that depends on the cosmological constant.

papers.title: Exact radial stability threshold for a Minkowski-Schwarzschild thin shell
papers.abstract: We study the stability of a thin shell of ordinary matter that separates a flat interior from a Schwarzschild exterior, which is the simplest model of a subluminal warp drive. The matter content of the shell is fixed by the junction conditions and satisfies all the standard energy conditions except very close to the horizon. For a shell made of causal matter we find an exact radius below which it cannot be stable under radial perturbations. We then place a black hole inside the shell and show that this radius grows with the black hole mass, so that the flat interior is the most favourable case. Since such shells are known to be unstable to non-radial perturbations, our result marks the boundary of the region in which any stabilising mechanism would have to operate.

papers.title: From Pixels to Executable Physics: Behavior-Grounded World Models for Embodied Action Consequence Prediction
papers.abstract: In outdoor environments, varying terrain and contact conditions can cause identical action commands to produce different motion outcomes for quadruped robots. Predicting these outcomes is essential for reliable navigation and informed path selection. Existing video world models can generate visually plausible futures, yet often struggle to capture robot dynamics and terrain interactions, leading to overly optimistic predictions of action outcomes. We present DR-WM, a physically consistent world model that incorporates robot-terrain contact dynamics to predict the consequences of quadruped actions. Starting from an initial RGB image, our method reconstructs scene geometry and integrates dense, dimensionless priors over terrain contact properties, calibrated using real-world action-response data. The resulting terrain model supports the simulation of physics with spatially varying contact properties such as friction. Given the initial state of the robot and candidate action sequences, we simulate its future motion and use the resulting camera trajectories and rendered geometry to guide the training of a video world model. The generated future observations are then used to update the terrain reconstruction, enabling iterative model rollouts without additional real-world images. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DR-WM substantially outperforms geometry-only baselines and baselines with uniform physical parameters on key physical metrics characterizing action outcomes, while achieving the best performance among the evaluated baselines. These physically grounded predictions support more informed action selection: across 90 challenging scenarios, an 8B vision-language model augmented with DR-WM outperforms an unassisted 32B vision-language model on five of six evaluation metrics.

papers.title: Complete mappings stabilizing Sylow $2$-subgroups in central quotients of special linear groups
papers.abstract: A complete mapping of a finite group $G$ is a permutation $θ$ of $G$ such that $x\mapsto xθ(x)$ is also a permutation of $G$. Complete mappings have applications in cryptography, particularly in the design of round functions for cryptographic systems. The study of their parity has led to the question of which finite groups admit complete mappings of both parities. A useful approach to this question is to construct complete mappings stabilizing suitable subgroups, in particular Sylow $2$-subgroups. We show that, for every $n\geq2$, every prime power $q$, and every $Z\leq Z(\mathrm{SL}_n(q))$, the group $\mathrm{SL}_n(q)/Z$ admits a complete mapping stabilizing a Sylow $2$-subgroup if and only if $(n,q)\neq(2,2)$.

papers.title: Toward Interpretable Quantum Generators for Financial Returns through Problem-Informed Circuit Design
papers.abstract: When used as function approximators, quantum circuits often lack interpretability and face a fundamental trade-off between expressivity and trainability. We propose a problem-informed framework for financial return generation that uses relational structure and symmetry-inspired parameter sharing to guide the construction of quantum circuits with few trainable parameters and empirically testable operator roles. We evaluate three quantum generator architectures, referred to as ZZ, directed ZZ-CRX, and structured time evolution, within a hybrid Wasserstein quantum generative adversarial network trained to generate 16-step Bitcoin return windows. Across circuits with one to four layers and one to eight trainable coefficients, these generators recover meaningful marginal and temporal distributional features, while single-layer configurations remain competitive with deeper variants. Across matched depths, independently trained ZZ-CRX configurations exhibit a predominantly downward shift in median leverage relative to ZZ, consistent with the intended directional role of the controlled-rotation construction. The small number of coefficients also enables direct landscape analysis, revealing competing parameter preferences between marginal and temporal objectives and helping to explain the difficulty of finding parameter settings that perform well on both. These results provide an initial demonstration that structural assumptions can guide the design of compact quantum generators and link circuit architecture to observable statistical behaviour, motivating more systematic and parameter-efficient approaches to quantum circuit construction.

papers.title: Executable Prefix Values for Locating Agent Failures
papers.abstract: Work on debugging LLM agents treats the "first mistake" marked by a human or LLM judge as ground truth for where a trajectory failed. We ask whether such labels point at causes or symptoms, and make the distinction executable: we restart the agent from reconstructed intermediate states of a failed trajectory and estimate its prefix value V(h_t), the probability of success from each step, with a certified point of no return (PNR) for a failure. On 150 SWE-bench Verified tasks with two frozen open-weight agents, we build such curves for 47 and 60 failed trajectories and probe every step labeled by four frontier judges under the Traverse rubric. We find that the labels do not mark what a controller needs. Judges of different lineages agree on the exact step in only 21/57 cases, and the newest judges flag mistakes in 8/10 and 10/10 successful runs. For 66% of the labels, the agent's success probability does not drop at the labeled step; only 7/188 answers name the decisive step. Restarting at the measured restart point raises expected success from 0.44 to 0.57 offline, and real restarts confirm the advantage, whereas restarting at a judge's label does not (-0.08 to -0.03). We release our code, curves, and labels.

papers.title: Berezin Ranges of Composition Operators on $H^2$
papers.abstract: We explore properties of the Berezin range $B(C_φ)$ of a composition operator $C_φ$ on the Hardy space $H^2$, including constraints on its location in the complex plane $\mathbb{C}$, topological properties, shape, symmetry, and convexity. For example, we show that $B(C_φ) \subseteq \{z\in \mathbb{C}: \Re(z) > 0 \ \text{and}\ |z| \le 1 + |φ(0)|\}$, that $B(C_φ)$ is closed if and only if $C_φ$ is the identity operator, and that $B(C_φ)$ containa all its boundary points except for $0$ if $C_φ$ is compact. Addressing questions raised by Cowen and Felder, we show that $C_φ$ can be a (nondegenerate) disk and characterize when $B(C_φ)$ is convex if $φ$ is linear.

papers.title: Calibrated Disambiguation for Partial Multi-label Learning
papers.abstract: Partial multi-label learning (PML) aims to train a classifier on datasets whose instances are over-annotated with not only relevant labels but also irrelevant labels, which is common when datasets are collected from crowd-sourcing platform. Existing works primarily approach it from a curriculum learning perspective, leveraging the memorization effect to disambiguate noisy labels and produce robust predictions. However, these methods are based on non-adaptive weighting functions and lack theoretical guidance for optimal weighting. To overcome these issues, a calibrated disambiguation model named PML-CD is proposed. We first formulate the optimal weighting function for curriculum-based disambiguation, which is equivalent to the calibration of the model's predicted confidences, thus providing guidance for curriculum designing. To obtain the optimal weighting function from PML dataset during the training, a transferable calibrator is designed, which takes the histogram of positive samples' confidences as input, and outputs the optimal curriculum weighting for training. Prototype alignment regularization is also proposed to promote the model's performance. Experiments conducted on Pascal VOC, MS-COCO, NUS-WIDE and CUB have verified that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art PML methods.

papers.title: The Tokens Strike Back: Safety-Aware Denoising with Directional Embedding-based Revision
papers.abstract: The Safety-Aware Denoiser (SAD) is a recent, training-free, safety-guidance framework for text diffusion models. During inference, SAD steers text samples toward safe regions of the token probability space. In this paper, we propose $\mathit{SADDER}$ (Safety-Aware Denoising with Directional Embedding-based Revision), which improves the safety and quality trade-offs of SAD by exploiting a safety-guidance signal in the embedding (or activation) space for each token position, then updating the token positions using the SAD update rule multiplied by the guidance signal. This multiplication acts as a gating mechanism: tokens with a high unsafe signal are more likely to be modified during inference following the SAD update rule. However, such an update does not automatically preserve the conditional mean, i.e., the denoiser of a fixed target distribution. We therefore theoretically derive new position-wise target distributions for which the modified denoiser is exact. Furthermore, we derive conditions under which the position-wise target distributions match a global target distribution. We test our $\mathit{SADDER}$ method on popular Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs) and Uniform-State Diffusion Models (USDMs) across unsafe continuation and jailbreak settings, and show that $\mathit{SADDER}$ achieves a better balance between safety, generation quality, and inference cost than existing methods.

papers.title: Mixed Precision Scaling Laws for Quantized Pretraining
papers.abstract: Since scaling laws were introduced for modern LLMs (Kaplan et al., 2020), several works have extended them to account for quantization, tracking the emerging low-precision data types supported on AI accelerators. We develop a more accurate scaling law for quantized pretraining with mixed precision across the forward and backward passes, grounded in optimization theory and validated empirically. Our formulation separates the effects of quantization on model capacity and on optimization efficiency, and explicitly models the persistent optimization error from forward and backward quantization identified through convergence analysis. To select the regimes for fitting and evaluating our law, we first decompose existing 4-bit training recipes into their forward and backward components, isolating those that most affect loss. Our Qwen3 experiments under selected 4-bit regimes, together with published Llama-style experiments, show that our law predicts loss with up to $11\times$ lower MSE than existing laws as model size and token count scale. Finally, we extend our law to layer-wise mixed precision and identify the optimal quantized-pretraining recipe, i.e., model size, training tokens, and per-layer forward/backward precision, under a hardware-aware compute budget. Unlike prior precision scaling laws, our law predicts that the optimal precision increases with the compute budget.

papers.title: Acting Through Registers
papers.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) use generative visual representations to condition robot actions, yet how these representations organize action-relevant information remains poorly understood. We identify persistent high-norm spatial outliers in WAM representations and find that their action relevance persists even after normalization and K/V projection attenuate their extreme magnitude. Motivated by this observation, we introduce RegisterWAM, which adds learnable non-spatial registers to the world model and uses them directly for action conditioning. Registers alone do not fully eliminate spatial outliers; pairing them with observation flow-matching (FM) loss supervision suppresses spatial outliers while concentrating high-norm responses in registers. Beyond this reorganization, observation FM loss supervision also improves action learning without registers, motivating an additional noised-observation FM objective that learns current-scene recovery from corrupted inputs. The resulting model achieves 81.64\% success on LIBERO-Plus without additional embodied pretraining data or foundation models, reaches 93.0\% average success on RoboTwin 2.0, and improves real-world manipulation performance.

papers.title: FrameLite: Decision-Oriented Aesthetic Cropping with a Compact Vision-Language Model
papers.abstract: Aesthetic image cropping improves composition by balancing subjects, context, and image boundaries. Large vision-language models bring semantic knowledge to this task, but their scale limits lightweight photography assistance. We propose FrameLite, a compact cropping model built on Qwen3.5-0.8B. Our approach is motivated by the observation that a small model can generate better crops than its first answer suggests. We develop three-stage training to turn this potential into stronger direct predictions. Spatial and composition training establishes localization and framing preferences. Quality-Guided Online Supervision (QOS) then learns the highest-quality complete answers among the current policy's generated candidates. Greedy-Referenced Optimization (GRO) further refines the policy using positive and negative quality differences relative to its current greedy answer. Both online stages use annotation-derived feedback, while inference returns one coordinate answer without search or an external scorer. Experiments show that FrameLite outperforms the compared large-VLM croppers across public benchmarks with a substantially smaller backbone. Controlled studies confirm that selecting high-quality training answers improves the final model beyond online sampling alone. We will release our code and model weights at https://github.com/JianzeLi-114/FrameLite .

papers.title: MemAct: Streaming Spatial Understanding with Memory and Active Exploration
papers.abstract: Spatial understanding is essential for embodied agents navigating and interacting with the physical world. As observations arrive incrementally, agents must reason in a streaming manner. Yet streaming understanding must also be closed-loop: task-relevant evidence may require both recalling past observations and actively acquiring new views. Existing streaming approaches largely emphasize processing incoming observations, leaving task-driven active exploration underexplored. We introduce MemAct, a framework for streaming spatial understanding with memory and action. A shared vision--language model incrementally writes structured historical memory, retrieves records and past frames on demand, and acquires additional evidence through movement and turning. Retrieved evidence and action observations inform subsequent decisions, enabling the agent to continue exploring or answer within a unified reasoning loop. We develop the MemAct suite, a data generation pipeline and collection across real and simulated environments, with approximately 1M training examples for spatial reasoning, memory writing, retrieval, and exploration. Its MemAct-bench comprises 20,000 main QA pairs evaluating current-observation understanding, historical evidence use, and active exploration, plus 2,000 separate Timing questions. MemAct combines supervised fine-tuning for memory and interaction with counterfactual action optimization using cumulative evidence gains, action costs, and terminal answer quality to improve exploration and stopping decisions. Experiments show that MemAct outperforms existing spatial understanding and streaming baselines and approaches frontier multimodal models on MemAct-bench while retaining streaming inference efficiency.

papers.title: Beyond Bias Scores: Answerability Confounds in Activation Steering with Gradient-Constrained Direction Design (GCD)
papers.abstract: Bias scores in language-model evaluations often conflate what a model prefers with whether it answers at all. We identify this confound in \textsc{BBQ}, whose ambiguous score factorizes into answerability and signed preference. Across 11 categories, 28,}824 items, and five models, contrastive steering lowers the signed ambiguous score in 11/11 categories but lowers the signed disambiguated preference score in only 8/11. Across 99 configurations, the answerability channel exceeds half of the observed score change in 17\% and accounts for the entire change in 11%. In a six-category disambiguated evaluation, 20.8\% of 1,500 items flip to the unknown option, where abstention is incorrect; \textsc{StereoSet} shows no analogous answer-rate shift. The effect reflects selection and near-orthogonality between the contrastive and preference-gradient directions. We introduce Gradient-Constrained Direction Design (\textsc{GCD}), an option-gradient construction with a first-order unknown-logit constraint. Under a matched Qwen-7B protocol, GCD reduces answer-rate distortion 14-fold and yields a 4-fold larger preference change, while ablations show similar gains for alternative and unconstrained option-gradient directions; nulling the unknown gradient alone is not responsible for the gain. We recommend reporting answerability alongside published scores.

papers.title: Low-Altitude Agentic Networks: From UAV Connectivity to Workflow-Driven Capability Orchestration
papers.abstract: Low-altitude platforms are evolving from connected sensing nodes into autonomous agents capable of bounded task interpretation, skill invocation, and local decision making. Increasing the intelligence of individual unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), however, does not resolve the organization problem that arises when mission workflows depend on capabilities distributed across multiple platforms and provider feasibility changes with network, resource, and mobility conditions. We propose low-altitude agentic networking as a task-level networking paradigm and develop a reference architecture that separates workflow logic from executor identity. Within a validated domain-specific workflow space, each ready operation is translated into a capability requirement and dynamically bound to an agent that remains feasible under current conditions. Task contracts and structured evidence govern workflow execution, while routine provider and link changes are handled through workflow-preserving local adaptation before high-level repair is invoked. A trace-calibrated discrete-event case study identifies a bounded operating region: conventional organization remains effective for simple workflows under stable conditions, whereas agentic networking becomes beneficial when workflow dependencies are tightly coupled, capability feasibility changes during execution, and viable local recovery paths remain available.

papers.title: When Should Enterprise Policy Decisions Be Learned, and When Should They Be Reasoned?
papers.abstract: An enterprise agent that answers under a written policy must choose an action before it says anything: answer, ask for a missing fact, ask for confirmation, call one or several tools, escalate, or refuse. Holding one 27B Korean enterprise model fixed, we vary whether the decision is a generated JSON object or a single constrained token, and whether the model may reason first. On 2800 in-distribution items we did not detect an accuracy difference between the two deployed paths (93.46% vs 94.14%), while they differ about tenfold in restart stability (3.00% of actions flip vs 0.29%); they also differ in reasoning, so this is an operational comparison. On a sealed benchmark of 300 items whose labels come from a hidden executable policy, reasoning is worth +17.3 points [+12.3, +23.0] on exact action. With reasoning off, the format difference was 0.0 points [-4.3, +4.0], a failure to detect an advantage for either interface, not equivalence; with reasoning on it is unresolved. Against a token-matched random control, boundary-targeted supervision moves the two covered boundaries by +17.5 and +20.0 points and leaves a held-out boundary unchanged. In a 3-seed training x reasoning factorial, the sealed-rendering interaction is -4.9 [-8.1, -1.7], consistent with partial substitution. All supervision was Korean. On independently rendered English versions, the model is 0.82 points lower [-2.68, +0.93] with reasoning on, the same order as re-rendering in Korean; the reasoning-off gain from targeted supervision is not stable in either language, so we do not claim transfer. The original text stays private as the confirmatory set. An open-model re-rendering made after these results reproduced the reasoning effect and the English verdict; the interaction kept its sign but did not replicate under item-clustered intervals. We release the model and that re-rendering with gold labels.

papers.title: DisaggKD: Efficient Knowledge Distillation through Teacher-Student Disaggregation and a Fused Loss
papers.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) frameworks place teacher and student on the same GPUs, so per-GPU memory limits the teachers that fit. DisaggKD separates them across nodes: teacher replicas stream hidden states to the student, a KD loss over row windows and vocabulary shards equals the full-vocabulary loss in exact arithmetic without forming the full-vocabulary logits, and a prefetch ring paces producer and trainer. Closed-form memory and traffic models locate the memory limits of each layout. On the Qwen3.5-35B-A3B to 9B pair, the disaggregated layout matches the LM loss of the colocated run with the same loss and is faster than that run; our fused loss also lets a colocated run train on as few nodes at faster speed, while the split is memory efficient when the student spans several nodes. On the larger pairs, colocated runs with a fused loss still run OOM where the split trains, because teacher weights and student states fill the budget.

papers.title: Service-Aware Hosting Capacity Assessment of Edge Data Centers with Workload Flexibility
papers.abstract: The growing demand for edge computing, content delivery, and AI services is driving the interconnection of edge data centers (DCs) with distribution networks. Before interconnection, utilities evaluate how much DC capacity can be accommodated without violating feeder current and voltage limits. Fixed peak load representations can overlook service dependent demand patterns, cooling related facility demand, and delay tolerant computing tasks. This paper develops a hosting capacity (HC) assessment model for edge DCs with shiftable workload scheduling. Three representative types are considered: mobile edge computing (MEC), content delivery network (CDN), and AI DCs. Facility demand is modeled by combining fixed base demand, service driven demand, prescribed cooling-overhead coefficient, and a shiftable workload component. Workload execution is optimized under arrival causality, maximum delay, daily energy balance constraints, and the resulting active and reactive loads are embedded in a distribution power flow model. Compared with the baseline without load shifting, the maximum bus level HC gain on the IEEE 33-bus system reaches 4.46% for MEC DCs and 9.89% for AI DCs, while CDN case shows negligible gain under the assumed cache management windows.

papers.title: A subcategory with remarkable homological properties via actions of tensor categories
papers.abstract: By equipping the category $\mathcal{M}$ of modules over a finite dimensional algebra with the action of a finite tensor category $\mathcal{C}$, we introduce a subcategory $\mathcal{PM}$ satisfying numerous remarkable properties: it is generating and cogenerating, functorially finite, closed under Auslander--Reiten translations (i.e. precluster tilting), and it computes the finitistic dimension. Through a functor category perspective, $\mathcal{PM}$ is identified with the $\mathcal{C}$-module functors that are projective, and we also prove a $\mathcal{C}$-equivariant version of the Auslander(--Solberg) correspondence. As examples, we show that $\mathcal{PM}$ contains only finitely many indecomposable modules for some tensor product algebras. For some family of 1-Iwanaga--Gorenstein algebras introduced by Geiss--Leclerc--Schröer, we show that $\mathcal{PM}$ is exactly the subcategory of $τ$-locally free modules.

papers.title: The Promise of Gravitational-Wave Astronomy
papers.abstract: We review the promise of upcoming gravitational-wave (GW) observations in addressing some of the important open questions in astrophysics and cosmology. A decade after the first direct detection of GWs, the field is entering a transformative phase driven by progressive detector upgrades and the anticipated advent of space-based and next-generation ground-based observatories. These instruments will not only push the distance horizon of GW observations to cosmological redshifts, but will dramatically extend the accessible frequency band, opening entirely new source classes that lie beyond the reach of current detectors. The source landscape is rich enough that surprises are likely. This review surveys our current understanding across this landscape and offers some perspective on the discoveries that upcoming GW observations are poised to deliver.

papers.title: Nearly Optimal Quantum Sample Complexity of Learning Fourier-Sparse Boolean Functions
papers.abstract: We study the number of uniform quantum examples needed to exactly learn a Boolean function with at most $k$ nonzero Fourier coefficients. We give a learner with near-optimal $\widetilde{O}(k)$ sample complexity independent of the input length $n$. The learner uses only separate measurements of individual examples. This improves the previous $O(k^{3/2}\log^2 k)$ upper bound (Arunachalam, Chakraborty, Lee, Paraashar, and de Wolf, 2021). The main ingredient is a candidate set formed by symmetric differences of subsets from independent groups of Fourier samples. A multilinear majority polynomial combines unbiased random approximations into an accurate witness whose Fourier support lies in this set. Granularity then forces the set to contain the entire Fourier support, including subsets never directly sampled. For comparison, we derive the tight classical sample complexity $Θ(nk)$ by combining known sparse-recovery and lower-bound results.

papers.title: Supervised Fine-Tuning for Reasoning Large Language Models: A Survey
papers.abstract: Large reasoning models have recently demonstrated remarkable capabilities in solving complex tasks, where supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on long chain-of-thought data serves as a crucial foundation for eliciting and enhancing their reasoning abilities. Despite rapid progress in both improving and analyzing reasoning-oriented SFT, the field still lacks a systematic survey that consolidates its fast-growing literature. To fill this gap, we present a comprehensive review of recent advancements in reasoning SFT, examining the literature through the dual lenses of methodological design and analytical investigation. First, we review methodological improvements across the SFT pipeline and categorize them into data-centric approaches and algorithm-centric innovations. Second, we reorganize analytical studies along three dimensions: data characteristics, optimization dynamics, and mechanistic insights. Finally, by synthesizing current research focuses and remaining bottlenecks, we outline promising future directions for reasoning SFT. We hope this survey deepens the understanding of reasoning SFT and paves the way for advanced reasoning models.

papers.title: Ray class groups in the cyclotomic tower
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $Σ$ be a nonempty finite set of rational primes different from $p$. In the cyclotomic tower $\mathbb{Q}(μ_{p^{n+1}})$, we determine the kernels of the natural maps from the minus $p$-primary ray class groups, with modulus the product of the primes above $Σ$, to the corresponding ordinary minus $p$-primary class groups. We give their character components and elementary divisors at every finite layer, including the layers before splitting stabilizes. In the norm inverse limit, we obtain an explicit integral cyclic decomposition of the local module modulo the single diagonal global Tate module. Its coinvariants recover the finite local kernels. Together with ordinary class-group control, this gives exact control for the minus ray class groups. We identify the local Frobenius factors with Bernoulli regularization factors. For nonexceptional characters, the classical main conjecture then yields regularized measure generators of the ray class characteristic ideals. The exceptional Teichmüller component is treated without the main conjecture: the single Tate correction corresponds to the single pole of the $p$-adic zeta function. At the bottom layer, the local calculation and Herbrand--Ribet yield characterwise nonvanishing criteria involving regularized Bernoulli values. For a single auxiliary prime, the exceptional component detects the Wieferich condition. We also deduce Eisenstein congruence consequences from existing modular-form theorems.

papers.title: Simultaneously preperiodic points and colliding orbits for families of polynomials in characteristic $p$
papers.abstract: Let $k=\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ and let $f\in k[X]$ be a polynomial of degree at least $2$ such that $f-f(0)$ is non-additive. For $α,β$ in an algebraically closed extension $L$ of $k$, we prove that there are infinitely many $λ\in L$ for which both points are preperiodic under $f(X)+λ$ if and only if $α,β\in k$ or $f(β)-f(α)\in E_f$. Here $E_f=\{c\in G_f:(f-f(0))^n(c)\in G_f\text{ for every }n\ge0\}$, where $G_f=\{c\in k : f(X+c)-f(X)\in k\}$. We also provide a necessary and sufficient criterion for the corresponding colliding orbits set to be infinite.

papers.title: Code2Worlds-2: Physically Plausible Agent Harness for Embodied World Simulation
papers.abstract: Recent coding large language models (LLMs) can synthesize dynamic 4D worlds from natural language, but the resulting content remains a visual artifact. It lacks physical semantics such as the collision geometry, mass, friction, inertia, and joint structure, required to enable it to simulate the physical world, and its dynamics are scripted to look plausible rather than designed to execute. What is needed is an executable world: one that a physics engine can load and step, resolving contact physically. We present Code2Worlds-2, an extension of Code2Worlds that turns 4D world generation into an embodied world simulation. We keep the original dual-stream generation pipeline intact and append two modules. First, a SimReady Scene Compiler that turns a generated visual scene into a simulator-compatible representation: it assigns collision meshes via convex decomposition, estimates physical attributes with a vision-language model, infers a lightweight support graph, instantiates the engine's contact, friction, and dynamics constraints, and applies a gravity settling pass, before exporting the scene as MuJoCo MJCF. Second, a Simulator-in-the-Loop 4D Refiner that implements an automated agent harness-a compile, simulate, critique and refine loop-that converts visual dynamics into executable rigid and articulated dynamics and evolves the physical settings rather than only the code, replacing the purely visual motion critic with a simulator critic that inspects penetration depth, collision pairs, stability, contact forces, joint limits, and robot reachability. We further propose SimCode4D, a state-based benchmark with five task templates for evaluating embodied simulation. Experiments on SimCode4D and across natural, indoor, industrial, urban, and service scenes show that Code2Worlds-2 produces physically plausible, simulator-compatible, and robot-interactable scenes.

papers.title: Experimental evidence for a physical alteration of fine regolith on near-Sun asteroids
papers.abstract: The surfaces of airless bodies evolve through processes such as (micro-)meteoroid impacts and thermal fatigue, which can modify physical properties such as grain size, porosity, and mineral texture. These properties provide clues as to the evolution of airless surfaces, and understanding them is also necessary for interpreting telescopic observations. Near-Sun asteroids (NSAs), which approach the Sun at heliocentric distances of $\lesssim$0.2 au, are notable targets, as their surfaces are likely modified by intense solar radiation. However, experimental studies of how radiative heating modifies the physical properties of carbonaceous asteroid surfaces remain scarce compared with studies of thermally induced changes in mineral composition and spectra. We simulated near-Sun conditions ($0.09<r<0.19$ au) in the laboratory using the Space and High-Irradiance Near-Sun Simulator and irradiated CM-type carbonaceous chondrite simulants under vacuum. Brightness changes were monitored in situ with a video camera during heating, and morphology was examined with a stage microscope and a scanning electron microscope (SEM). The irradiated samples show initial darkening followed by brightening, consolidation, and morphological modifications from sub-micrometer to millimeter scales. The brightness modifications are more consistent with changes in the absorption properties than with variations in surface roughness. SEM imaging of the heated samples shows structures similar to those formed by sintering, which are completely absent in unheated samples. These results suggest that sintering is a likely candidate for the mechanism responsible for the observed consolidation and morphological changes. This work provides experimental evidence to help constrain the surface evolution of NSAs in general, and supports the sintering hypothesis as a possible mechanism proposed for (3200) Phaethon in particular.

papers.title: New results from electron-positron heavy-flavor factories
papers.abstract: The electron-positron heavy-flavor factories --- BaBar, Belle, Belle~II, and BESIII --- continue to deliver a broad and sensitive physics program. I report selected highlights presented at ICHEP 2026, covering neutral- and charged-current $B$ processes, tests of lepton-flavor universality in $b\to c\ellν$ transitions, precision measurement of Cabibbo--Kobayashi--Maskawa matrix elements, and hadron spectroscopy.

papers.title: Decouple to Forget: Semantic Mediation for Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Machine unlearning for large language models seeks to remove specified knowledge while preserving general capability, yet current methods often treat an entire response as the unit of forgetting. This coarse granularity causes unnecessary utility loss when the forget target is only a small set of sensitive facts embedded within otherwise benign explanations. In this paper, we introduce Decouple to Forget (D2F), a targeted unlearning method inspired by semantic mediation that separates sensitive factual content from non-sensitive meaning and surface expression. For each example to be forgotten, D2F extracts a fact-level "mediator" representation from the answer, identifies which parts are sensitive, and removes only those parts while leaving the rest of the structure intact. We then generate counterfactual answers grounded in this mediator that preserve non-sensitive content but exclude sensitive facts, employing preference-based contrastive optimization to reduce the likelihood of information leakage while maintaining helpfulness and fluency. Experiments across various benchmark datasets show that D2F achieves a better balance between forgetting and retention than strong baseline methods. Our code is available at https://github.com/JingyueCong/D2F.

papers.title: textGrain watermarking is harder to detect: can sum-tests still do it optimally?
papers.abstract: Watermarking embeds an imperceptible signal in text from large language models that is statistically detectable with a secret key. The recent textGrain watermark (Li et. al. (2026b)) calibrates this signal against the model's sampling entropy through an explicit entropy budget, combining the stochasticity of Red-Green and the unbiasedness of Gumbel-max watermarks, and its accompanying report proposes a detector that sums pivotal statistics. We study when, and how efficiently, textGrain can be detected after human edits, modeled as a sparse mixture in which a fraction $\varepsilon_n\asymp n^{-p}$ of positions retain the watermark and token uncertainty decays as $n^{-q}$. First, entropy calibration comes at a cost: the minimax detection boundary of textGrain is $p+q=1/2$, so its detectable region is strictly smaller than that of Gumbel-max and maximal-coupling watermarks, whose boundary is $2p+q=1$. This cost stems from textGrain's construction rather than from entropy calibration itself: an unbiased scheme with the same entropy loss remains detectable where textGrain is not. Second, perhaps surprisingly, this loss makes the sum detector optimal at the boundary when the number of transport columns is fixed, unlike for Gumbel-max. When the number of columns grows and the entropy budget does not vanish, the detectable region expands while that of the sum detector does not. Third, for a fixed edit fraction, we characterize the optimal exponential rate of type II error decay and show that the sum detector falls strictly short of it at every fixed alternative. Finally, we propose a weighted multiscale binomial scan, valid in finite samples and needing no knowledge of the next-token distributions, entropy budget, or edit fraction; it attains every detection boundary above and the optimal exponent.

papers.title: Open-o3-Video-v2: Seek, Ground, and Reason with Verifiable Spatio-Temporal Evidence
papers.abstract: Reliable video reasoning requires models to produce correct answers and expose supporting visual evidence. Open-o3-Video enables verifiable reasoning by embedding timestamps and object-level bounding boxes into reasoning traces, but is restricted to frames from an initial sparse sampler. We introduce Open-o3-Video-v2, which formulates video reasoning as a unified agentic evidencegrounded process. The model identifies missing information, acquires additional observations, grounds the moments and objects supporting its reasoning, and writes this evidence into the trajectory before continuing or answering. To support this behavior, we construct STGR-v2-CoT135K, including 52K multi-turn agentic grounded reasoning trajectories, and STGR-v2-RL-13K for reinforcement learning. We further propose Clue-Seek GRPO (CS-GRPO), which tracks how tool calls change accumulated evidence, rewards clue coverage and step-wise gains, and penalizes excessive, repetitive, or uninformative retrieval. On V-STaR, Open-o3-Video-v2-4B achieves 40.4% mAM and 56.3% mLGM, outperforming its Qwen3-VL-4B backbone by 8.5% and 12.6%, respectively. It also delivers consistent gains across general video understanding, long-video reasoning, and temporal grounding benchmarks. These results show that active evidence acquisition and verifiable object-level grounding are complementary for reliable video reasoning. The code and models are released at https://msalab-pku.github.io/projects/Open-o3-Video-v2.

papers.title: Towards a Systematic Study of Embodied System 2 over Full Task Execution Cycles
papers.abstract: An embodied brain, or System 2, must turn an abstract goal into actions while discovering relevant scene conditions and checking whether executed skills achieved their intended effects. Open-loop evaluations cannot test observations shaped by an agent's decisions, while some closed-loop evaluations provide limited evidence during execution or assume idealized skill outcomes. We introduce SCOPER, a suite for studying observation-grounded planning, execution, and recovery. SCOPER-bench combines high-level goals, ongoing visual observations, a shared rule-based System 1 for low-level actions, and controlled execution failures. Its construction and validation pipeline yields 870 tasks across BEHAVIOR and ProcTHOR, complemented by about 3,500 situated questions tied to the evaluated agent's execution. Benchmark results reveal difficulties in retaining scene evidence, monitoring progress, and recovering from unexpected outcomes. To address these difficulties, SCOPER-harness combines Evidence Memory and Progress Verification with a dynamic task agenda and bounded exploration, without additional model training. Across two evaluated open-source backbones and two simulators, the harness improves task success by 11.1-28.6%; a harnessed 9B model outperforms a directly executed 27B model on both simulators. In an offline next-action evaluation using observations from 200 real-robot demonstrations, the harness also improves full-call accuracy by 14.7% and 15.3%. SCOPER provides a setting for diagnosing and improving embodied reasoning throughout a complete task execution cycle.

papers.title: Worth Their Weights? Evaluating Generative Models for Discourse Parsing
papers.abstract: Rhetorical Structure Theory (RST) parsing has historically been dominated by discriminative models based on pretrained encoder-only language models. The recent availability of high-quality generative language models has made it unclear whether RST parsing is better approached as a generative task. In this work, we investigate whether generative language models are better at parsing RST than traditional discriminative ones. We find that at matched parameter counts, discriminative parsers perform much better than generative ones, though much larger generative models sometimes outperform them. Generative models hold a particular advantage in elementary discourse unit (EDU) segmentation, and we report new state-of-the-art results on the RST-DT benchmark in end-to-end parsing as well as segmentation.

papers.title: Can Agents Truly Forget? Explore Machine Unlearning for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents have shown strong capabilities in interactive problem solving, tool use, and long-horizon task execution. However, they may also acquire sensitive or private knowledge during training and expose it during deployment. Retraining a model from scratch to remove such knowledge is prohibitively costly, making machine unlearning a more practical approach. Machine unlearning aims to remove targeted undesirable knowledge from trained models without retraining from scratch while preserving general utility. When language models are deployed as agents, parameter-level unlearning becomes insufficient: forgotten information may still persist in memory artifacts or be reacquired via tool calls. In this paper, we formulate the problem of agent unlearning as removing private information from an LLM-based agent across three information channels: parametric knowledge, persistent memory, and tool-call acquisition. To study this problem, we introduce we introduce Agent Unlearning Benchmark (AUBench), a controlled benchmark that extends the fictitious-author setting of TOFU into an agent environment with persistent memory, an offline web snapshot, tool-accessible documents, and provenance-tracked interaction trajectories. By evaluating existing parameter-level and memory-level unlearning methods in this setting, AUBench reveals the gap between model-level forgetting and system-level agent unlearning, and provides a foundation for developing unlearning methods that operate across the full lifecycle of LLM agents.

papers.title: InSight: A Mobile Assistant Helping Visually Impaired People Navigate Unfamiliar Environment
papers.abstract: Navigating unfamiliar outdoor environments is one of the most demanding everyday tasks for people with visual impairments (PVI). However, existing navigation systems cannot simultaneously satisfy the needs of informative perception and precise localization during navigation. This paper explores the core navigation demands of PVI through a preliminary study. Based on the results of the pre-study, we present the design of InSight, a mobile assistant that combines scene descriptions with precise localization to support PVI navigating unfamiliar outdoor environments. The offline mode of InSight runs entirely on device for real-time navigation, while the online mode streams camera frames to a self-hosted server for arbitrary object detection and accurate localization. Finally, a user study with 21 visually impaired participants validates that InSight could assist users in navigating unfamiliar outdoor environments with increased success rate and confidence compared to mainstream navigation applications like Apple Maps.

papers.title: ScenePercept: Scenario-Conditioned Perceptual Assessment of Real-World User-Generated Content Images
papers.abstract: The rapid development of mobile imaging and social platforms has led to explosive growth in user-generated content images, making their systematic and comprehensive perceptual assessment increasingly important. Existing image perception benchmarks are typically task-oriented, curating specific scenarios for quality or aesthetic assessment and applying a uniform perceptual criterion across diverse scenarios. This limits their ability to capture the scene diversity and perceptual complexity of real-world UGC images. To address these limitations, we introduce ScenePercept-Bench, a benchmark designed to reflect the distribution of real-world UGC images, comprising 23,100 images across 21 categories and 105 fine-grained scenes. To account for the influence of scene context on human perception, we design a hierarchical, scene-aware annotation protocol, covering visual quality, aesthetic perception, and scene semantics, with 15 attributes in total. Each image is annotated with an overall score, 15 attribute-level scores, and structured explanatory reasoning. Building on this benchmark, we further introduce Scenario-Conditioned Perceptual Alignment, a training framework that tackles the heterogeneity of perceptual criteria across scenarios. SCPA jointly optimizes absolute score prediction, preference ranking, and cross-scenario calibration, preserving the model general perceptual assessment ability while encouraging it to explore and adapt perceptual criteria across different scenarios. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SCPA achieves state-of-the-art performance in UGC image perception and generalizes effectively to established IQA and IAA benchmarks.

papers.title: Zero divisors in group algebras of torsion-free groups in odd characteristic
papers.abstract: A recent preprint constructs a finitely presented torsion-free group $G$ with a finite two-dimensional classifying space such that $\mathbb F_2[G]$ contains nonzero zero divisors. We extend this to every odd prime $p$: there is a finitely presented torsion-free group $G_p$, again with a finite two-dimensional classifying space, such that $\mathbb F_p[G_p]$ contains nonzero elements $α,β$ with $αβ=0$. Together with the case $p=2$, Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture therefore fails over every field of positive characteristic. The new ingredients are a signed version of the parity cancellation, made possible by a bipartite random model on one side; a type design built from the projective plane over $\mathbb F_{p^3}$ with $p$ additional letters, which makes every cross-intersection congruent to $1$ modulo $p$; and a squared-word decay estimate for this design, proved with an explicit test vector. The geometric part of the argument is taken from the characteristic-two construction. The characteristic-zero case remains open.

papers.title: The Image Still Has a Say: Final-Answer Repair for Multimodal Chain-of-Thought
papers.abstract: Although chain-of-thought prompting has improved multimodal reasoning, it is still difficult to produce correct final answers, as the reasoning can drift away from the image. Besides, the trace is already fixed when the answer is generated, leaving no room for self-correction. Considering the image is still available at the final-answer step, we think it is reasonable to fix the answer there without rewriting the reasoning. As such, the problem becomes to correct the final answer using the image under fixed reasoning. Unlike methods that improve trace generation through training, resampling, or decoding-time grounding, we repair the final-answer readout while keeping the reasoning trace fixed. The motivation is based on our finding that a wrong option can become prematurely committed in the reasoning while the correct option still has stronger image support in middle-to-deep layers. Thus, we propose Text-to-Visual Evidence Reallocation (TVER), a training-free method for final-answer repair. Specifically, TVER selects answer-related text and question-matched image patches, and moves bounded attention from text to patches. Furthermore, the patches are chosen in a middle-to-deep layer window based on question relevance. Our method improves answers across benchmarks and backbones, with gains in both multiple-choice and open-answer evaluations.

papers.title: Hitting Minors: Stronger Lower Bounds
papers.abstract: For a fixed finite collection of graphs $\mathcal{F}$, the $\mathcal{F}$-Minor-Free Deletion problem asks, given a graph $G$ and an integer $k$, whether there is a set $S\subseteq V(G)$ with $|S|\leq k$ such that $G-S$ contains no graph of $\mathcal{F}$ as a minor. This generalizes Vertex Cover, Feedback Vertex Set, and Vertex Planarization, among many others. Baste, Sau, and Thilikos [JCSS 2020, SICOMP 2023] showed that, assuming the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH), there are collections $\mathcal{F}$ for which the problem cannot be solved in time $2^{o(\mathrm{tw}\log\mathrm{tw})}n^{O(1)}$ on $n$-vertex graphs of treewidth $\mathrm{tw}$, and gave a matching algorithm. We ask whether this super-exponential dependence persists under more restrictive structural parameters. First, we strengthen their lower bound. Assuming ETH, for every fixed $h\geq 6$, $\{P_h\}$-Minor-Free Deletion, where $P_h$ is the path on $h$ vertices, cannot be solved in time $2^{o(t\log t)}n^{O(1)}$, where $t=\mathrm{fvs}+\mathrm{td}$ is the sum of the feedback vertex set number and treedepth of the input graph. These two parameters are incomparable, but both individually upper bound the treewidth. Together with the $2^{O(\mathrm{tw}\log\mathrm{tw})}n^{O(1)}$-time algorithm of Baste, Sau, and Thilikos [SICOMP 2023], our lower bound is tight. In contrast, we show that asymptotically faster algorithms are possible when parameterized by the vertex cover number $\mathrm{vc}$. Specifically, for any finite family $\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{F}$-Minor-Free Deletion can be solved in time $2^{O(\mathrm{vc})}n^{O(1)}$. Taken together, our results show that the boundary between single-exponential and super-exponential complexity for this problem lies between the vertex cover number and the feedback vertex set number (plus treedepth).

papers.title: RoTA-Bench: Evaluating 3D Spatial Reasoning through Interactive Projection Alignment
papers.abstract: Can vision-language models turn 2D observations into 3D understanding that supports precise action? This requires inferring object geometry, anticipating the effects of rotation, and refining actions through visual feedback. We introduce RoTA-Bench to evaluate these abilities through interactive 3D-to-2D projection alignment. Given a target silhouette, a model observes a rotated object and chooses successive rotations to recover the target projection within a limited action budget. Our automated pipeline constructs silhouette-preserving 3D objects from 2D icons and uses reversible initialization to guarantee solvability, yielding 674 tasks and a stratified 100-task test set. Empirically, we find that (i) a substantial human-model gap persists: GPT-5.6-Sol succeeds on only 17% of tasks, whereas 20 undergraduate participants collectively complete the test set four times with a 100% success rate; (ii) image-space and pose-space progress can diverge: at matched states, the model more often improves silhouette overlap while worsening pose alignment than humans (19.4% vs. 10.9%); and (iii) fine-grained control is sensitive to interaction history: removing it leaves 96.8% of the model's actions at a coarse 30-degree step size and sharply reduces observed task success. These findings highlight the challenge of converting visual evidence into precise 3D control, beyond recognizing or matching individual images.

papers.title: DeltaTTG: Training Multi-Turn Agents with a Token-to-Go Progress Meter
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) for multi-turn agents relies on sparse terminal rewards that say little about individual steps. Within-group step comparisons depend on reliable state matching and sufficiently diverse sampled outcomes, while direct step scoring may require costly external evaluators, human annotations, or task-specific heuristics. We introduce DeltaTTG to learn a reusable progress signal through a shared progress meter, using low-cost supervision from diverse policies' recorded trajectories without task-specific progress rules. Its supervision target, Token-to-Go (TTG), the number of tokens remaining to be generated until task completion, serves as an observable proxy for remaining completion effort. During actor training, changes in the frozen meter's estimates redistribute outcome-derived advantages across steps without altering the reward, preserving each trajectory's advantage sign and token-average scale. On ALFWorld, PaperSearchQA, and BFCLv3, DeltaTTG improves the average score over GRPO by 5.7 and 7.2 points with Qwen3-4B and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, respectively, outperforms all compared RL baselines on average, and keeps actor-training GPU-hours close to GRPO. Further experiments show improved sample efficiency and out-of-domain performance, and support the meter's ability to distinguish step quality and guide test-time action selection across actor sizes. The code is available at https://github.com/Xuyan923r/DeltaTTG.

papers.title: PrT-Flow: Probability-Tractable Flow Matching for Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Diffusion models and Flow Matching can represent flexible distributions over robot actions, but many reinforcement learning algorithms also require the probability of each action. We introduce PrT-Flow (Probability-Tractable Flow Matching), which computes probability density while retaining multimodal, multi-step action generation. Its Jacobian-Tractable Transformer (JTT) makes each sampling step invertible and enables efficient computation of its Jacobian determinant. We train these finite steps with Conditional Euler-step Training (CET), which supervises their displacement over one step during sampling rather than their instantaneous velocity. We prove that, under certain assumptions, CET has the same minimizers as fitting the Euler-solver updates of Flow Matching. PrT-Flow achieves 96% success on Robomimic Lift after 300 epochs of imitation learning, matching the diffusion policy reference, and 96% success on OGBench Cube-Triple after 600k online steps. These results demonstrate that invertible networks with tractable probability densities can learn effective robot policies and support SAC-style actor-critic training. Our code is available at https://github.com/Sunlight-zero/PrT-Flow .

papers.title: Global existence of the $s$-Schrödinger maps in $n \geq 5$
papers.abstract: We study the $s$-Schrödinger map equation \[ \begin{cases} \partial_t u = -u \wedge (-Δ)^s u \quad \text{on } \mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R}\\ u: \mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{S}^2\\ u(x,0) = u_0. \end{cases} \] For $s \in (1/2,1)$ and $n \geq 5$ we prove that for small initial data $u_0$ in the critical Besov space one can obtain a global solution.

papers.title: Large deviation principle for determinantal point processes on Stein manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study natural determinantal point processes on Stein manifolds defined by canonical sections and plurisubharmonic weight functions. We present a natural condition on the weights under which these processes satisfy a large deviation principle with a good rate function given by the Fenchel--Legendre transform of the pluripotential equilibrium energy. Along the way, we prove some pluripotential theoretic results on Stein manifolds, such as the $C^{1,1}$ regularity of appropriate envelopes. These results are noncompact analogues of results of Berman and Berman--Boucksom on compact Kähler manifolds.

papers.title: Cowork-Gym: Synthesizing Interactive Work Environments at Scale
papers.abstract: Cowork agents navigate dependencies across tools and files while adapting to changing user requirements and edits to shared workspaces. Scaling such environments requires maintaining consistency among task objectives, executable resources, user behavior, and success criteria. We introduce Cowork-Gym, a framework that synthesizes Cowork environments through a build-execute-revise loop that uses execution evidence and review feedback to validate and repair generated environments. To capture realistic Cowork dynamics, a stateful user simulator responds to the agent's actions through dialogue and direct edits to the shared workspace. We synthesize 64.9K environments across 14 application scenarios and use them to post-train 9B, 27B, and 35B-A3B Qwen models with supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and on-policy distillation. Averaged across six agentic benchmarks, these models outperform their corresponding base checkpoints by 8.7, 6.4, and 4.1 points, respectively. Ours-27B ranks second overall among the evaluated models and achieves the highest average scores on PawBench and ClawEval, outperforming models with over 100B total parameters on both benchmarks.

papers.title: Integrating 3D Posture Neutralization with Statistical Shape Modeling for Head-Neck-Shoulder Ergonomic Design
papers.abstract: The design of ergonomic products and workspaces requires a deep understanding of human anatomy and posture. In particular, the head-neck-shoulder region is critical for many applications such as cervical orthoses, helmets, and other head-worn or neck-worn devices. This paper presents a framework that integrates posture neutralization with statistical shape modeling (SSM) for the head-neck-shoulder (HNS) region. We acquire a single three-dimensional (3D) scan of the head-neck-shoulder region from each of 200 Chinese adults in a natural posture for each subject. Every scan is then posture-neutralized before SSM. We fit a parametric head-neck model to each scan to separate cervical pose from anatomy, and reset the cervical pose to a common neutral configuration, so that the resulting model captures anatomical shape variation rather than posture-induced deformation. The resulting shape space yields a standardized template and population-wide modes of variation, providing baselines for parametric ergonomic design. We further discuss how the model supports population coverage analysis and the design of products that accommodate anatomical diversity while maintaining neutral cervical posture.

papers.title: Encounter-Driven City-Scale Human Mobility Generation with Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong potential for human mobility generation by modeling individual routines, activities, and mobility preferences. However, existing approaches remain largely resident-centric: generating realistic individual trajectories does not necessarily recover the encounters that emerge when multiple residents co-occur at the same place and time. To this end, we study encounter-aware human mobility generation, which jointly preserves individual mobility and population-level interaction structure. We propose EncounterMob, an encounter-driven LLM framework consisting of a coarse-to-fine Encounter Generator and an Iterative Coupling Framework. The Encounter Generator first captures city-level encounter rhythms and then instantiates participant-time-venue encounters, while the Iterative Coupling Framework coordinates these encounters with personal mobility behavior through successive refinement. We further introduce an encounter recovery protocol covering encounter marginal and joint distributions over residents, times, and venues. Experiments on the Japan and NYC datasets show that EncounterMob outperforms all external baselines on all seven encounter metrics and all six personal mobility metrics. Compared with ELLMob, it reduces the participant-time-venue joint error by 40.4%/41.7% and the mean personal mobility error by 58.8%/32.7% on Japan/NYC, respectively.

papers.title: RALI@iKAT 2026: Retrieval-aware User Profile Denoising via Personalized Conversational Dense Retrieval
papers.abstract: Modern conversational information access systems continuously extract user information from conversations to build user profiles for personalized retrieval. As user profiles accumulate over time, they inevitably become noisy, making effective user profile denoising a fundamental challenge.
