For a detailed investigation of the latter, one requires a kinetic plasma model to describe the interacting magnetospheres of the stars. We present a three-dimensional particle-in-cell kinetic simulation of the combined magnetosphere of a binary neutron star in which the two stars physically orbit one another so that the orbital motion itself twists the magnetic loops. We find that the stellar magnetic-field intensity ratio controls the emergence of flares, while the stellar spins set the direction and modulation of the flare. We identify four spatially and dynamically distinct regions of strong electromagnetic energy release: (i) an expanding fast magnetosonic wave that steepens into a monster shock, (ii) a plasma flare being pushed by (iii) an expanding fireball and containing (iv) a reconnecting current sheet. The fast magnetosonic wave is a promising source of coherent radio emission. It is released when orbital motion cuts a closed plasma loop. The electric and magnetic wave amplitudes are similar and reach that of the background magnetic field. Our kinetic treatment yields particle spectra and plasma structures that can be used to assess coherent emission in kinetic-scale simulations. In conclusion, the stellar orbital motion constitutes a driving channel distinct from models with spin-driven magnetospheric twisting.

papers.title: Closing the Estimation Gap: Training-Free Transductive Inference for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Action Recognition
papers.abstract: Cross-domain few-shot action recognition (CD-FSAR) aims to recognise unseen action classes in a target domain from a handful of labelled videos. Despite advances in representation learning, CD-FSAR inference still relies on prototypes estimated from extremely limited support examples. To assess this bottleneck, we perform an oracle analysis with the representation fixed. Constructing oracle prototypes and decision boundaries from ground-truth query labels improves 5-way 1-shot accuracy by 7--20 percentage points across five target datasets. This reveals a substantial estimation gap: the representation contains useful discriminative information, but prototypes and boundaries estimated from scarce supports fail to capture each episode's true class structure. Motivated by this, we propose TRACE, a training-free transductive inference framework that improves episode-level estimation without modifying the backbone. TRACE comprises two complementary stages. Confidence-Thresholded Transductive Prototype Refinement (CTPR) refines support-based prototypes using confidently predicted queries. The refined prototypes initialise a lightweight per-episode classifier, which Transductive Classifier Refinement (TCR) further adapts by encouraging confident, class-balanced predictions over all queries. Together, the two stages improve prototype and boundary estimation, enabling better use of information in the unlabelled queries. Across five target datasets (HMDB51, UCF101, SSv2, Diving48, and RareAct) in both 1-shot and 5-shot settings, TRACE consistently improves a strong CD-FSAR baseline, including gains of more than six percentage points on HMDB51 1-shot, while recovering much of the oracle-estimated gap. These results suggest that improving test-time estimation is a powerful, broadly applicable complement to representation learning for CD-FSAR under extreme support scarcity.

papers.title: Operator Surrogates
papers.abstract: This chapter provides a mathematical introduction to operator surrogates, which are finite-parametric maps approximating complex (typically nonlinear) operators between infinite-dimensional (function) spaces. A typical approach to constructing operator surrogates is the encoder-approximator-decoder paradigm, whereby infinite-dimensional inputs are mapped to a finite-dimensional latent space, processed, and then mapped back to the infinite-dimensional output space. We discuss various methods for creating efficient representation systems, including stable linear frameworks like Banach frames and data-driven techniques such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Active Subspaces, and nonlinear autoencoders. Subsequently, we survey key surrogate architectures, contrasting spectral methods, based on polynomial chaos expansions and related technologies, with more recent neural network approaches. We further discuss architectures that do not rely on representation systems, such as Fourier Neural Operators and transformers. We elaborate on their relationship and how they relate to other neural network operator surrogates, particularly those obtained by so-called "algorithm-unrolling". Additionally, we provide an introduction to the theoretical analysis of approximation and generalization errors. We explain how underlying low-dimensional structures, provided for example by holomorphy, are essential to overcome the so-called "curse of dimensionality": this refers to the fact that the complexity of numerical algorithms tends to increase exponentially in the problem dimensionality. We present convergence rate bounds for holomorphic operators that depend on the number of trainable parameters and the regularity of the input and output data. Throughout, we prioritize intuition over detailed technical proofs and provide precise pointers to the literature for detailed arguments.

papers.title: Unexpected stabilization of a single-$q$ charge density wave in pristine 1T-TiSe$_2$
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, studies revisiting the classical charge-density-wave system 1T-TiSe$_2$, long understood to host the $2 \times 2$ triple-$q$ order with equivalent subcomponents, have suggested that these subcomponents may not be identical, challenging a 50-year-old paradigm. Here, we demonstrate not only that these subcomponents are non-identical but also that they develop sequentially rather than simultaneously. By tracking folded-band features, angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy reveals that a unidirectional $2 \times 1$ single-$q$ order stabilizes first, while the other two components emerge sequentially at lower temperatures, completing the triple-$q$ phase. Our free-energy analysis explains this hierarchy through repulsive coupling among the three subcomponents, as supported by first-principles calculations incorporating phonon anharmonicity. Consequently, the three subcomponents are inequivalent in both phase and amplitude. These results reconcile reported symmetry breaking and differing characteristic temperatures and establish a framework in which ostensibly simple, high-symmetry charge-density order emerges from temperature-dependent competition and cooperation among inequivalent subcomponents.

papers.title: Exact solution of adiabatic time dependent Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov inertia for fission
papers.abstract: An efficient method to exactly compute the adiabatic time-dependent Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov collective vibrational inertias typical of fission is proposed. The method uses the quasiparticle finite amplitude method to invert the stability matrix of linear response. A comparison with other approaches, such as the exact generator coordinate method inertia and the associated cranking non-perturbative approximation, is conducted. It is found that the behaviour as a function of the collective variable (mass quadrupole moment) is essentially the same in the four cases considered, and substantially differs from the commonly used perturbative approach. It is also found that the magnitudes of the inertias are to a good extent related by single factors that seem to be connected with the effective mass of the energy density functional used.

papers.title: Combinatorial bounds for the v-number of binomial edge ideals
papers.abstract: We study the local $\mathrm v$-numbers of binomial edge ideals from a combinatorial perspective. For each minimal prime $P_{\mathcal S}$ of $J_G$, indexed by a cutset $\mathcal S$ of $G$, we consider two combinatorial invariants, $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)$ and $\mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$, defined in terms of transversals of suitable hypergraphs, and show that the local $\mathrm v$-number $\mathrm v_{P_{\mathcal S}}(J_G)$ satisfies $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)\leq \mathrm v_{P_{\mathcal S}}(J_G)\leq \mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$. Under a suitable hypothesis on the connected components, we provide explicit graph-theoretic descriptions of these invariants and analyze when they coincide, giving a combinatorial way to determine the local $\mathrm v$-numbers. As an application, we derive a sufficient condition for this coincidence, which applies to a broad class of graphs. Furthermore, we identify a constant that controls the gap between $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)$ and $\mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$, thereby showing that the local $\mathrm{v}$-number lies within a bounded interval. Applications to cycles and trees illustrate both the equality criterion and the resulting bounds.

papers.title: A certified classical-strip comparison for the de Bruijn-Newman constant
papers.abstract: We give a directed comparison beginning with the classical zero strip \(\lvert\Ima z\rvert\le1\) for the de Bruijn--Newman heat deformation. Under explicitly stated complete model-to-function source, localisation and global contact premises, translated-probe estimates imply \[ Λ\le\frac{148611789321711}{10^{15}} =0.148611789321711<0.148612. \] The construction uses Raymond's finite source data and 57 fixed translated kernels, independently checked by rational Bernstein certificates. An explicit finite Weyl estimate improves the positive first-head tail and its centred logarithmic moment. A centred cone transfer retains the original physical error allowances, exceptional debit and additive cone reserve, and charges the change in existing phase-surplus credits. Directed tail enclosures are regenerated at 192 and 256 bits; a separate exact-rational auditor accepts all 19,023 comparison steps. The controlled decrease from the complete two-source comparison is \(0.000021760452379\). We also prove a compatible matched logarithmic tail transfer and identify the finite requirements for stronger exponent pairs. A supplementary section records Raymond's ceiling below \(0.116398\) under the distinct \(7/8\) zero-free hypothesis.

papers.title: No Truly Sublogarithmic-Round Algorithm for Distributed MIS in the LOCAL Model
papers.abstract: We prove that $o(\frac{\log n}{\log\log n})$-round randomized LOCAL algorithms find a maximal independent set (MIS) with subconstant probability on some input. This shows that the 40-year-old $O(\log n)$-round randomized CONGEST algorithm of Luby and Alon, Babai, and Itai is nearly optimal. Our lower bound improves upon the $Ω(\sqrt{\log n})$-round lower bound of Khoury and Schild and nearly closes the 20+ year-old gap between the $O(\log n)$-round algorithm and the $Ω(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}})$-round lower bound of Kuhn, Moscibroda, and Wattenhofer. To close this gap, one must show a lower bound for a graph that is not locally treelike. We do this by starting with a $D$-regular, $Θ(\log_D n)$-girth graph, with $D = Θ(\log n)$. Crucially, this is not our final graph. We obtain our hard instance by \emph{replacing} each vertex of this treelike graph with a clique on $n^c$ vertices for some constant $c \in (0,1)$. We then replace each edge with a bipartite Erdős--Rényi graph between the corresponding cliques, with each edge present independently with probability $1/2$. We analyze arbitrary LOCAL algorithms on our non-treelike hard instance with a novel round elimination approach. We describe algorithms that output a set of vertices in this graph using two metrics: their \emph{occupancy probability} and their \emph{conflict probability}. Our round elimination framework takes an $r$-round algorithm and produces an $(r-1)$-round algorithm where occupancy and conflict probabilities collectively slightly degrade, but individually can significantly improve or degrade. This round elimination result is obtained by exploiting the lack of large biclique complements in dense bipartite Erdős--Rényi graphs, which in turn allows us to bound the entropy of the output distribution for any independent set algorithm.

papers.title: TextualRL: Textual Reinforcement Learning for Context Management
papers.abstract: LLM agents can adapt to task feedback by revising the textual context that guides their behavior, without changing their model parameters. However, turning execution rewards into reusable context updates is challenging: individual trajectories offer limited comparative evidence about what to change, while task-specific fixes may overgeneralize when incorporated into a shared context. We introduce TextualRL, a gradient-free reinforcement learning framework that treats a group of rollouts from the same task under the same context, rather than an isolated trajectory, as the unit of policy critique. Groupwise Policy Critique contrasts successful and failed rollouts within a task; when outcomes are uniform, it draws on cross-task evidence to identify behaviors worth preserving or formulate repair hypotheses. Cross-Group Policy Update reviews the resulting proposals against evidence pooled across groups, including observations that yield no proposed edit, to refine their content and applicability. Reviewed proposals form a bounded textual patch, with adoption of the candidate context determined by held-out validation rewards. Together, these components establish a reward-driven policy optimization loop in which multiple attempts jointly inform reusable context updates. We evaluate TextualRL with five target agents on six benchmarks. Averaged over the six benchmarks, TextualRL improves test accuracy over the base model by 24.4 and 15.3 percentage points for GPT-5.5 and Qwen3.8-27B, respectively.

papers.title: Fast and Flexible Spiking Network Simulations on Massively Distributed On-Chip Memory Accelerators
papers.abstract: Studying brain function and dysfunction in spiking networks with realistic synaptic densities pushes simulation technology beyond its current limits. It requires simulations substantially faster than biological real-time to cover long model times and enable efficient iterative exploration, particularly when connectivity is plastic. The modelling community aspires to a $100\times$ speedup. Yet on conventional many-core systems this remains elusive, bounded by inter-node communication and memory access. So far, significant speedup has only been shown on a custom-built FPGA system. We demonstrate the potential of commercial systems with large distributed on-chip memory to accelerate brain research. To exploit the local SRAM, we introduce a group-based mapping and communication strategy tackling spike-routing challenges on massively distributed systems. On Graphcore IPUs, the cortical microcircuit runs at a record $22.7\times$ faster than biological real-time with negligible build times and a reusable compiled graph. By design, the algorithm makes no model- or hardware-specific assumptions, providing a general strategy for advancing neuronal simulation technology.

papers.title: Methods for Automated Equivalence Checking of Quantum Error-Correction Codes
papers.abstract: Quantum error-correction code and circuit construction is an active field of research, motivating automated methods for identifying equivalent designs. We develop and evaluate automated strategies for deciding whether two descriptions of quantum error-correction codes are equivalent under specified transformations. We formalize permutation equivalence for stabilizer and CSS codes and local-Clifford equivalence for stabilizer codes within a unified framework that separates physical from representation freedom. We develop three decision strategies (group-action search, isomorphism-based methods, and constraint solving), together with invariants and signatures for preprocessing. The empirical evaluation shows that no paradigm dominates across equivalence notions, code families, and parameter ranges. We therefore combine their complementary strengths in input-dependent hybrid checkers following a staged Refute-Refine-Decide architecture. Mean hybrid runtimes remain below 10 s for most evaluated structured-code cases with $n \leq 37$; for inequivalent code instances with $n=144$, they are about 310 s for permutation and 16 s for local-Clifford equivalence.

papers.title: T^2-invariant Einstein metrics on closed 4-manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct $T^2$-invariant Einstein metrics with positive Ricci curvature on #_m(S^2 x S^2) for every integer $m>1$. These provide infinite family of Einstein metrics on closed $4$-manifolds with $λ>0$, which are in addition not Hermitian. We further establish the uniqueness of the $T^2$-invariant Einstein metrics on $S^4$, CP^2, S^2 x S^2, and CP^2#\bar{CP}^2.

papers.title: MINFF: A Family of Classical Force Fields for Minerals with Tunable Angle Terms
papers.abstract: Atomistic simulations of minerals are limited by the accuracy and transferability of the force field. We introduce MINFF, a force field family for layered and non-layered oxides and hydroxides of M being Si, Al, Fe, Mg, Ca, Ti, Li and F. MINFF has no M-O bond terms. Instead M-O distances follow from electrostatics and dispersion, while a single harmonic angle term on all M-O triplets controls coordination geometry. Metal charges are DDEC6 charges from reference mineral structures, and oxygen charges are assigned by nearest-neighbour charge smearing, covering basal, apical, hydroxyl and edge sites and sites adjacent to isomorphous substitutions. The oxygen Lennard-Jones parameters are based on the OPC3 water model and change by less than 5% when re-optimised per mineral, so compatibility with OPC3 and related ion-pair potentials is measured rather than assumed. Metal Lennard-Jones parameters were fitted to unit-cell metrics, bond distances and angles, both synchronously across more than 30 reference minerals (general, GMINFF) and for individual minerals (tailored, TMINFF), each at four angle force constants (0, 250, 500 and 1500 kJ/mol/rad^2). With angle terms, MINFF reproduces experimental unit-cells metrics to within 0.5% and atom-type distances and angles to within 0.7-1.4% and 0.1-0.4%, with Global Instability Index values as low as 0.11, below those of CLAYFF (0.34) and INTERFACE (0.21). A moderate angle constant reproduces the stiff in-plane and soft shear elastic constants of phyllosilicates and improves the Kaolinite librational bands, and in hydrated Na-Montmorillonite MINFF gives the lowest residual factor against the 2W 00l pattern of the models tested. The general and tailored sets at four angle stiffnesses give direct control over the transferability-fidelity trade-off. Topologies can be generated with the atom (MATLAB) and atomipy (Python) libraries and at www.atomipy.io.

papers.title: Frobenius liftability of isolated complete intersections
papers.abstract: We classify Frobenius liftable normal isolated complete intersection singularities of dimension at least three over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. In dimension three, they are precisely the regular points and the ordinary double points; in higher dimensions, they are regular. We also characterize Frobenius liftability of the complete local hypersurfaces defined by $xy-g(z,t)$ without assuming that the singularity is isolated. Such a hypersurface is Frobenius liftable if and only if, after a formal change of coordinates, $g$ is a unit times $H^pz^at^b$ with $0\le a,b<p$.

papers.title: Isometric dilations and Beurling quotient modules
papers.abstract: In \cite{Dan-Guo}, the authors provided a characterization of all sequences of doubly commuting pure contractions that have the sequence $\textbf{M}_z,$ the sequence of the multiplication by the coordinate functions on the vector-valued Hardy space $H^2_\mathcal E(\mathbb {D}_2^{(\infty)})$ over the Hilbert's multidisk $\mathbb D_2^{(\infty)},$ as their minimal isometric dilation for some Hilbert space $\mathcal E$. In this article, we remove the hypothesis of doubly commutativity and characterize all sequences of commuting contractions that are unitarily equivalent to $(P_{\mathcal Q}M_{z_i}|_{\mathcal Q})_{i\geq 1}$ for some quotient module $\mathcal Q$ of $H^2_\mathcal E(\mathbb D_2^{(\infty)})$. We further characterize those sequences for which $\mathcal Q$ is a Beurling quotient module. This generalizes Theorem 3.2 from \cite{BKD} to a sequence of commuting contractions.

papers.title: Modeling the Microenvironmental Dynamics of Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma in Lacrimal Gland with Treatment Intervention
papers.abstract: Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) of the lacrimal gland is a rare and extremely life threatening malignant tumor with a high risk of recurrence and poor long-term outcomes. On the other hand, due to its complex molecular dynamics and low incidence rate, treatment strategies are very limited. In this study, a mathematical model is developed based on the biological phenomena of the tumor microenvironment using nonlinear ordinary differential equations. It is analyzed both analytically and numerically. According to the findings, the growth of tumor cells is associated with the depletion of oxygen and nutrients, while severe hypoxia promotes the development of abnormal blood vessels and makes tumor control more difficult. Surgery and postoperative radiotherapy have been considered as treatment strategies, and we have observed that surgery alone may not be sufficient to prevent the regrowth of residual tumor cells. In addition, postoperative radiotherapy provides better control of the residual tumor burden, particularly when the remaining tumor cells have higher radiosensitivity. Furthermore, different radiotherapy interruption scenarios have been investigated, and the results indicate that longer gaps between radiotherapy doses can adversely affect the overall treatment response, leading to increased overall toxicity and a higher number of residual tumor cells at the end of the observation period. Consequently, our results suggest that postoperative radiotherapy after surgery, combined with adequate radiosensitivity of the residual tumor cells and adherence to the prescribed treatment schedule without prolonged interruptions, may reduce the risk of tumor recurrence and potentially improve long term survival.

papers.title: Cryogenic characterisation of the FBK NUV-HD-cryo Silicon Photomultipliers for the DarkSide-20k dark matter experiment
papers.abstract: Liquid Argon Time Projection Chambers (TPCs) are highly promising detectors for dark matter searches due to their uniform response, scalability to large target masses, and compatibility with ultra-low background conditions. The DarkSide-20k (DS-20k) experiment, currently under construction at Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare (INFN) Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso (LNGS), aims to achieve unprecedented sensitivity to Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs), approaching the neutrino fog. At the heart of the detector is a dual-phase TPC filled and surrounded by low-radioactivity argon from underground sources (i.e. Underground Argon (UAr)), functioning both as the WIMP target and detection medium. The experiment employs Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) NUV-HD-cryo Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs) as the chosen photon sensors for its optical planes. Key SiPM properties such as dark noise rate, gain and direct crosstalk were measured using specialized test setups at 77 K. The photon detection efficiency (PDE) was measured under vacuum at 77 K over the wavelength range 350-820 nm. Secondary photon emission, which can give rise to external optical crosstalk, was measured under vacuum at 86 K over the wavelength range 550-1020 nm.

papers.title: Zeeman spin quantum geometry and intrinsic gyrotropic spin current
papers.abstract: We uncover an intrinsic gyrotropic spin current (IGSC) driven solely by an oscillating magnetic field, arising from the spin version of Zeeman quantum geometry. Using the density matrix formalism, we derive the IGSC in the low-frequency clean limit, in terms of the Zeeman spin quantum metric and the Zeeman spin Berry curvature. The effect is studied in a minimal Rashba-Dresselhaus model that also supports intrinsic gyrotropic charge currents from the Zeeman Berry curvature. The spin and charge currents exhibit a $π/2$ phase shift and are found to be perpendicular to each other for certain parameter ranges. This not only enables spin current detection but also opens pure spin current channels for energy-efficient spintronics. We further observe that these currents switch directions between longitudinal and transverse relative to the applied field, depending on the relative strength of Rashba and Dresselhaus interactions.

papers.title: PPVM: A Circuit Simulation Framework for Digital Twins of Quantum Processors
papers.abstract: Quantum computers are approaching the early fault-tolerant regime. Verifying the next generation of quantum hardware requires joint emulation of the quantum processor, hardware noise, and classical control and decoding logic. We introduce the Programmable Pauli Virtual Machine (PPVM), an open-source framework for digital twins of quantum processors. PPVM unifies Pauli propagation and generalized tableau simulation under a common abstraction within a single virtual machine. Its bytecode supports arbitrary classical control flow, with measurement-conditioned feed-forward available in the generalized tableau backend. For neutral-atom hardware, we derive independent and correlated atom-loss channels and integrate them into both backends. We demonstrate loss-aware magic state distillation on over a thousand physical qubits and integration with classical decoding through Bloqade QEC Studio.

papers.title: Counting matrices with given characteristic polynomial
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a monic polynomial of degree $n$ with integer coefficients. We use Fourier analysis to prove a new upper bound on the number of $n\times n$ matrices with characteristic polynomial $f$ and integer entries in $[-T,T]$, as $T\to \infty$. The implied constant in our bound only depends on $n$ and is otherwise uniform in $f$. Our bound improves on recent work of Habegger, Ostafe and Shparlinski for $n\geq 4$.

papers.title: A Controlled Evaluation of Curvature Inspired Scalar Feature Scaling for Domain Generalization
papers.abstract: Domain-specific curvature is an appealing idea for domain generalization (DG), but curvature learning can denote substantially different computations. This paper evaluates one deliberately narrow implementation: the code calls it HyperDG, but it rescales Euclidean encoder features during training by learned positive scalars and uses an ordinary linear classifier on unscaled Euclidean features at inference. It does not implement a Lorentz or Poincaré representation, geodesic prediction, or a Sharpness-Aware Minimization inner loop. We audit the executed objective and evaluate six conditions on PACS, VLCS, Office Home, and TerraIncognita. The completed design contains 384 runs: six conditions, four held-out targets, and four run seeds per dataset. Checkpoints are selected using only the three source-validation environments. Inference first averages paired seed differences within each held-out target; targets, rather than 16 seed-by-target observations, are the per-dataset clusters. The full implementation's equal-dataset macro point estimate is 1.61 percentage points below native DomainBed ERM (95% clustered CI [-3.17, -0.04]). All four dataset point estimates favor ERM, but an exact four-dataset sign-flip test gives p = .125 and Holm-adjusted p = .250; we therefore claim no adjusted evidence of a difference. The cleaner domain-specificity contrast, separate learned source scales without their variance penalty versus one shared learned source scale, is -0.13 pp (95% CI [-0.53, 0.27]). Its 90% CI lies within a revision-stage $\pm 1$ pp smallest effect of practical interest (TOST p = .003), supporting equivalence only for the source-selected suite macro, not every dataset, target, or final-step endpoint. The study thus supplies a bounded negative result for this scalar training package; it does not test or refute genuine hyperbolic representation learning.

papers.title: Generic Local Identifiability Does Not Imply Generic Global Identifiability in Linear Networks
papers.abstract: We give a counterexample to the implication from generic local to generic global identifiability for linear networks with a fixed topology, independently unknown edge coefficients, and selected excited and measured nodes. A six-node network with nine unknown coefficients has exactly two compatible parameter vectors generically. Adding six excited and measured nodes preserves this ambiguity while making the added coefficients directly recoverable. The resulting twelve-node structure has forty-two independent unknown coefficients and zero diagonal. For every positive bound on the largest eigenvalue magnitude, a nonempty open set of parameters has two distinct compatible networks satisfying that bound. This holds for both real and complex coefficients. Other open regions have exactly one admissible solution. The proof uses a rational transformation exchanging the two solutions and a common limiting matrix whose fourth power vanishes. Exact rational-number certificates verify an explicit pair. The construction also extends algebraically when the unknown coordinates are whole rational transfer functions. Genericity in prescribed numerator and denominator coefficient families, and the requirement that every transfer function vanish at infinite frequency, remain separate questions.

papers.title: When Does Opponent Modeling Pay Off? Spatial Inference Stabilises Reinforcement Learning under Partial Observability
papers.abstract: Deep reinforcement learning agents in partially observable competitive games must act on beliefs about an unseen opponent's intent. We study a spatial opponent model: a transformer trained with hindsight-relabelled opponent goals that outputs a subgoal heatmap from the opponent's observed trajectory, fused early into a dueling double DQN. In symmetric constant-sum foraging games with partial observability, the module stabilises training. Plain TD(0) DQN suffers degenerate seeds in three of four one-step configurations, whereas the opponent-model agent never collapses and, wherever training succeeds, recovers the majority of the symmetric game value. Transfers zero-shot to a foraging opponent unseen by the learner, with a positive goal advantage over the baseline, and loses this edge exactly where an information argument predicts: against a full-information tracking adversary whose intent is the learner itself, and on resource-dense maps where both agents saturate. A blindfold ablation, zeroing the heatmap at deployment, decomposes the advantage into two mechanisms: training-time stabilisation, which dominates where the credit assignment is hard and survives blinding on the dense map, and deployment-time inference, whose reliance shrinks as fog thins on the sparse map. We conclude that opponent-goal inference is a stability-and-transfer mechanism whose value is governed by measurable boundary conditions: visibility (fog thickness), opponent intent, and resource density.

papers.title: Holding Agents Accountable with Verifiable Agent Insurance
papers.abstract: While AI agents are useful for many tasks, they regularly misbehave in destructive ways, such as deleting important data. While prior work has focused on preventing such misbehavior, we consider how to recover after an agent misbehaves. We propose verifiable agent insurance (VAI), a framework for agent providers to commit financially to promises, a list of programmatically-specified policies that an agent is meant to follow. These promises are embedded in a smart contract on an immutable ledger (e.g., a blockchain) to prevent tampering, along with a monetary escrow. A user who detects a violation of committed promises can prompt a verifier to review agent execution traces, which are logged through the agent harness's shared tool-execution path, without instrumenting each tool separately. Upon verification of the violation, the agent provider's escrow funds are paid to the reporting user. We instantiate VAI as an end-to-end implementation on an Ethereum layer-2 network, and evaluate its coverage on three prominent agent benchmarks, two of which we re-annotated to obtain task-level policy-compliance labels. Currently, many agents do not emit user authorizations and security-relevant information as explicit, structured data objects -- rather, they embed the data needed to verify policy violations in natural language exchanges. Even so, VAI manages to detect violations in 42.2% of runs containing violations across three benchmarks. By augmenting agents to explicitly emit such objects, violation detection rises to 83.0% of traces. Our findings suggest that for improved auditability, agents should be co-designed with their security policies to emit explicit, structured records of user authorization and security-relevant actions.

papers.title: Composite and Stochastic Smoothed Decentralized Bregman Proximal-Gradient Methods
papers.abstract: Smoothed decentralized Bregman proximal-gradient (SDBPG) methods combine relative-smoothness geometry with edge-dual consensus. We extend SDBPG to node-specific convex nonsmooth regularizers and unbiased stochastic local gradients while retaining its Bregman primal-dual smoothing mechanism. The analysis isolates temporal subgradient motion and aggregation mismatch as two defect sequences. For trajectories in a forward-invariant compact subset of the kernel domain and admissible parameters, finite accumulated defects yield an $O(T^{-1})$ bound on the squared best-iterate proximal residual over $T$ iterations. The stochastic bound separates accumulated oracle variance from expected defects and attains the same order when the variance bounds and expected defects are summable. Common active-structure identification, together with local subgradient conditions, gives sufficient finite-defect conditions for $\ell_1$ and group $\ell_{2,1}$ regularization. Experiments with common regularizers and heterogeneous sensing operators relate defect decay to observed support stabilization and compare reconstruction and communication with decentralized proximal and gradient-tracking methods. A separate phase-retrieval study evaluates the effect of a quartic Bregman kernel. Code and experiment scripts are available at https://github.com/shengze-xu/composite-stochastic-sdbpg .

papers.title: Sparse-group Convoluted Smoothed Quantile Regression in High Dimension
papers.abstract: In many applications, covariates are naturally organized into groups, yet conventional group-selection methods often retain all variables within selected groups, failing to achieve within-group sparsity. To address this limitation, we propose an adaptive two-stage sparse-group selection procedure for high-dimensional quantile regression. The proposed method integrates convolution-smoothed quantile loss with $\ell_{2,0}$ and $\ell_0$ penalties to identify important groups and relevant variables within them, achieving sparsity at both levels. We establish theoretical guarantees for sure screening and exact support recovery at both stages, as well as consistent model-size selection using information criteria, with explicit bounds on failure probabilities. The proposed procedure is computationally efficient by restricting optimization to selected groups and active variables. Simulation studies and a breast cancer gene-expression analysis demonstrate its competitive performance in variable selection, estimation accuracy, and computational efficiency, while identifying biologically relevant genes and delivering accurate quantile predictions.

papers.title: Consider, Then Choose: Order-Invariant Decisions in System One Models
papers.abstract: System One models answer typed questions in a single forward pass and promise the same answer for the same input. For choice questions, this promise fails: the answer depends on the order of the options, increasingly so as they grow in number, and averaging over their cyclic shifts reduces this dependence without removing it. Scoring each option alone, which the order cannot affect, shows that the order changes the answer mostly when the model is unsure among its top few options, even though the listwise answer looks confident. We therefore propose $\textbf{Runoff}$, which considers, then chooses: it scores each option alone to keep a few candidates, then compares them in listings where each candidate takes every position. It needs no training and can run in two forward passes, and its answer does not depend on the option order by construction. On two open models and five datasets, it changes no answer under shuffling, against 9.3% for cyclic averaging, and with 20 options it is about as accurate and three to four times faster. Wrapped around eight System One models, it removes the order dependence of the five benchmarks, while cyclic averaging changes up to 15.4%.

papers.title: Signature of GW from the Hidden Sector in light of the Recent LZ Event
papers.abstract: The LZ collaboration has recently reported a single nuclear-recoil event at $E_R=248\pm23_\text{stat}\pm23_\text{sys}$ keV, observed in a 2.84 tonne-year exposure with a local significance of $3.4σ$, pointing towards an inelastic dark matter (DM) interpretation. We explain this event within a gauged $U(1)_X$ hidden-sector model, spontaneously broken by a singlet scalar whose vacuum expectation value (VEV) gives rise to: \textit{(i)} gauge boson mass, \textit{(ii)} a small Majorana mass for the vector-like singlet fermion, the DM candidate, charged under the new symmetry, which splits the fermion into two pseudo-Dirac states (mass splitting proportional to the scalar VEV) thus resulting in a purely off-diagonal vector current, \textit{(iii)} the frequency and the amplitude of the GW signal arising from the hidden sector symmetry breaking via first-order phase transition (FOPT). The symmetry-breaking scale thus provides a multi-messenger probe connecting terrestrial direct-detection kinematics at the LZ and early-universe FOPT thermodynamics while obtaining thermal DM relic abundance. We delineate the viable parameter space compatible with the LZ event, correct relic density, and detectable GW signals in the low frequency regimes at future interferometers like $μ{\rm ARES}$ and THEIA while satisfying existing cosmological, astrophysical, and terrestrial bounds.

papers.title: On Chen's conjecture for the log-concavity of the longest increasing subsequence distribution
papers.abstract: Let $P_{n,k}$ count permutations of $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ whose longest increasing subsequence has length $k$. Chen conjectured that $(P_{n,k})_{k=1}^n$ is log-concave for every positive integer $n$. In this paper, we prove that Chen's conjecture is true when $n\ge 10^{10^{65}}$. The proof combines Gessel's determinantal formula with quantitative coefficient extraction, Tracy--Widom density estimates, and exact inequalities for the extreme lengths.

papers.title: Resource-based reliability of quantum-coherent devices
papers.abstract: Quantum devices can lose the resource needed for a specified function without entering a fixed failure subspace. We propose a resource-based reliability framework for this situation, quantifying the remaining task-relevant resource relative to a stated ideal capacity. The resource measure is selected through its operational connection to the task and the allowed operations. We develop this approach for a trusted quantum random-number generator and a calibrated two-port interferometer. Relative-entropy coherence determines the optimal asymptotic yield of standard coherent qubits under incoherent operations for the former, while logarithmic $l_1$ coherence quantifies the fringe resource of the latter and determines its calibrated correct-port probability. An exactly solvable multi-spin spin-boson model illustrates how environmental records affect these resources at the same isolated-spin dephasing strength. Collective noise preserves coherence within magnetization sectors for product inputs, but enhances the decay of Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger branch coherence. Finite-record simulations connect the resource definitions to measurement counts and show that increasing the sample size reduces statistical fluctuations without eliminating bias from an incorrect many-spin noise model. The resulting framework provides a task-specific route to reliability assessment when a fixed failure projector is insufficient, while keeping retained resource capacity distinct from a classical survival probability.

papers.title: Autonomous optomechanical Maxwell Demon engine
papers.abstract: We present a fully autonomous model of a mechanical Maxwell demon engine that converts heat absorbed by a qubit into population inversion in an attached quantum battery. A damped mechanical oscillator acts as a pointer that incorporates the essential demon function of information acquisition about the qubit state and subsequent feedback into the system dynamics, replacing external measurements and control operations. This is achieved by means of a Holstein-type Hamiltonian, which makes the pointer's equilibrium position depend on the qubit state and thereby induces a state-dependent resonance shift. The mechanism enables a selective energy transfer to an attached spin system that acts as the quantum battery. We derive both local and global Lindblad master equations for the coupled system and identify the parameter regimes in which the engine operates efficiently. The figure of merit is the resulting steady-state population inversion of the battery, quantified in terms of ergotropy. Based on these results, we discuss the necessary conditions for practical implementations of the demon engine on realistic experimental platforms.

papers.title: Heading Hierarchy Reconstruction for Complex and Long Documents with Level-Wise Multimodal Memory
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have been widely adopted for document parsing and optical character recognition (OCR), as they can accurately extract page-level elements. However, downstream applications such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) also require coherent document-level structure. Although these models indicate heading levels using different numbers of preceding ``\#'' symbols, page-by-page prediction often lacks document-level consistency. In practice, input-resolution and context-length constraints make it infeasible for a VLM to jointly process all page images in documents containing tens or hundreds of pages. To address this limitation, we propose a VLM-based framework that incrementally reconstructs heading hierarchies with a \emph{level-wise multimodal memory}. The memory retains a compact subset of all previously processed pages, selected by anchors. Our framework supports flexible anchor selection, and in this work we select the most recent node at each level, allowing the VLM to observe the visual, textual, and layout patterns of headings at every level. For comprehensive evaluation, we also introduce the Complex and Long Document Heading Hierarchy Reconstruction Benchmark (CLDoc-HHRBench), comprising 250 documents and 11,212 pages with expert-verified annotations. Experiments on CLDoc-HHRBench and three existing benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

papers.title: River ribbon tableaux and symmetric group characters
papers.abstract: We introduce river ribbon tableaux, where a river of non-trivial ribbons is placed between two banks of single boxes. Compared to other ribbon peelings, this reduces the geometric differences across diagrams of different shapes, and the maximal number of ribbon configurations. This allows us to prove a uniform character bound for symmetric groups which, specialized to balanced diagrams, proves the conjecture of Moore and Russell. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Dousse and Féray on the number of standard tableaux of skew shapes.

papers.title: Beyond Answer Sharing: TrueMAD for Targeted Peer Engagement in Multi-Agent Debate
papers.abstract: Multi-agent debate (MAD) aims to improve large language model reasoning by exposing agents to alternative solutions and enabling iterative revision. However, standard broadcast-style MAD makes peer answers visible without requiring agents to engage with a particular peer claim. As a result, reliable reasoning may be suppressed by conflicting or majority responses, limiting achievable performance, while erroneous reasoning may persist and degrade final predictions without actionable feedback. We propose TrueMAD, a backbone-agnostic test-time plug-in that introduces one-to-one, free-form peer advice between answer broadcasting and self-revision. Each source agent responds to a target's current reasoning through support, rebuttal, refinement, or further questions, while the target retains control over how to revise. The same mechanism can augment standard MAD and its improved variants without parameter updates. Across AIME, GPQA-Diamond, and TruthfulQA with Qwen3-30B-A3B, TrueMAD improves agent-level and strict-majority accuracy over MAD by 3.62 and 3.52 percentage points on average, while TrueDMAD improves DMAD by 4.72 and 4.06 points, respectively. Analyses at the utterance, agent-transition, and group levels further show more peer-specific deliberation, more correction-oriented revisions, and more favorable consensus dynamics.

papers.title: Adiabatic particle production in a time-dependent accelerated frame
papers.abstract: We study a massive scalar field in flat spacetime written in a time-dependent accelerated frame whose fixed-coordinate observers have maximal proper acceleration at $t=0$ and become asymptotically inertial without forming a horizon. The Klein-Gordon equation separates into a modified Mathieu equation in time and a confining Schrödinger problem in space with a discrete spectrum. We impose an adiabatic vacuum at the instant of maximal acceleration and compute the particle number in the inertial future. For the zeroth-order adiabatic state it falls as the inverse eighth power of the initial mode frequency, and raising the adiabatic order cancels successive terms of the endpoint expansion, in analogy with the switching transients of finite-time detectors. Analytic continuation of the spatial eigenfunctions gives the out modes in closed form and an exact expression for the particle number, which is entirely the mismatch at $t=0$ between the initial state and the out vacuum. The spectrum is algebraic rather than Planckian.

papers.title: One-way pressure-independent valves with hysteresis and chattering
papers.abstract: We propose a model for the one-dimensional isothermal gas flow through a valve in a pipe. The valve aims at keeping the outgoing flow in an assigned interval; moreover, its opening and closing depend on a further parameter. The model is realized by a system of two conservation laws with suitable conditions coupling the ingoing and the outgoing flow. We study the corresponding Riemann problem, where non-classical shocks show up. Although simple, the model allows to study two key oscillatory behaviors of the flow, which are due, respectively, to the chattering of the valve, especially seen in the numerical simulations, and to the stabilizing hysteresis induced by the valve operation. We characterize the states leading to chattering and show how they depend on the parameters of the model. Through several numerical simulations, we study the interplay between the two above phenomena.

papers.title: LiFUSE: Frequency-Spatial Unified Self-Supervised Pretraining for Liver Disease Analysis on Non-contrast CT
papers.abstract: Given the growing global burden of liver tumors and diffuse liver diseases, non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) is increasingly used for opportunistic screening because of its low cost and favorable safety profile. However, downstream tasks such as tumor detection and fine-grained disease diagnosis remain challenging due to NCCT's inherently low tissue contrast, lack of hemodynamic enhancement, and complex anatomical background. These limitations make subtle, heterogeneous, and multifocal hepatic lesions difficult to identify. Although large-scale self-supervised pretraining can learn robust representations from unlabeled NCCT scans, conventional voxel-wise reconstruction does not fully exploit the complementary information available in NCCT. Under weak NCCT contrast, low-level intensity patterns become less informative for pathology recognition, limiting the capture of lesion-specific discriminative features. In this paper, we propose the Liver Frequency-Spatial Unified Self-Supervised Pretraining (LiFUSE). The frequency branch applies random band-stop masking and spectrum reconstruction to encourage the model to capture subtle differences between lesions and surrounding tissues, while the spatial branch performs hybrid-granularity masked volumetric reconstruction to accommodate lesions of diverse sizes and morphologies. Finally, a cross-domain consistency scheme couples the spatial and frequency branches, yielding more discriminative representations for hepatic structures and lesions. Extensive experiments on three clinically relevant tasks across internal cohorts and a public target-domain transfer setting show that LiFUSE consistently outperforms strong baselines. These results suggest that unified frequency-spatial learning can improve liver disease analysis on NCCT, highlighting its potential for large-scale screening.

papers.title: An efficient and flexible generalization of transit compartment models for delayed biological processes
papers.abstract: Transit compartment models are widely used in pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics to represent delayed biological processes such as absorption, maturation, cellular proliferation, and treatment-induced toxicity. This transit compartment formulation imposes an artificial relationship between the mean and variance of the delay distribution, as the number of transit compartment must be integer-valued number of transit compartments. Consequently, estimating the number of compartments from experimental data leads to mixed-integer optimization problems that artificially constrain model dynamics and bias parameter inference. However, these transit compartment models are mathematically equivalent to distributed delay differential equations with Erlang delay kernels. We leverage a hypoexponential generalization of these distributed delay differential equations that preserves the familiar ordinary differential equation structure while allowing the mean and variance of the delay distribution to be estimated directly as real-valued parameters. This approach does not increase the number of inferred parameters and can be immediately implemented as a straightforward modification of existing transit compartment models. We demonstrate the approach using models of viral eclipse phases, lymphocyte proliferation, and chemotherapy-induced neutropenia. Across these examples, the hypoexponential formulation provides comparable or improved fits relative to Erlang transit models and substantially reduces computational cost by avoiding grid search over compartment numbers. This framework provides a practical approach to estimate biologically meaningful delay distributions in quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) models.

papers.title: Experimental Benchmarking of a 256-Qubit Room-Temperature NV-Diamond Quantum Processor with an Optically Programmable Biomolecular Quantum Bus
papers.abstract: We report Zeus-256, a room-temperature nitrogen-vacancy (NV) diamond processor with 256 simultaneously active processor-level logical qubits arranged in a 16 x 16 array. Each logical qubit combines an NV electron-spin ensemble with nuclear-spin memory and ancillary resources. OpenQASM 2.0 circuits are transpiled into RFSoC-controlled microwave, radio-frequency, optical, timing, measurement and bus-configuration sequences. An optically programmable proprietary protein-chromophore layer with an internal metastable-triplet spin mediator provides a reconfigurable biomolecular quantum bus for local and long-range interactions. Benchmarks cover QFT, GHZ entanglement, Grover search, arithmetic, variational, neural-network, graph-state and Shor-family circuits. Factor recovery is reported for 11 integers of 8-84 bits, with 10 attempts per instance; the 84-bit endpoint uses 256 qubits and 40,250,342 reported gates, with a reported execution time of 551.694 ms. Bell-CHSH measurements yield S = 2.8008 +/- 0.0446. Three-qubit Grover search returns the marked state in 958 of 1,024 shots (93.55%), compared with an ideal reference of 94.53%. A separate 30,000-shot population-and-parity protocol yields fixed-phase GHZ+ fidelity of 99.8960%, an estimated standard error of 0.2885 percentage points and a conservative physical 95% interval of [98.2342%, 100%]. Timing metrics are partial and do not establish quantum advantage. Scaling to 9,984 processor-level logical qubits is an engineering target, distinct from the demonstrated register.

papers.title: Integral trace duality and the Witt filtration on Lubin--Tate space
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal O$ be the Lubin--Tate deformation ring of a one-dimensional commutative formal group of finite height $n\geq1$ over a perfect field $k$ of characteristic $p$. We identify Rezk's Witt filtration $\{I_d\}$ with the divisibility filtration of integral trace pairings on subgroup algebras of fixed source lifts. This gives the geometric recursion \[ I_{d+1}=pI_d+J_{d,z}\qquad(d\geq0), \] where $J_{d,z}$ defines the targets of order-$p^d$ quotient isogenies from a $W(k)$-valued lift $z$ of the closed point. The corrected ideal is independent of $z$. We also compute the cokernel of the universal source trace pairing over $\mathcal O$: it is $\bigoplus_{j=1}^d(\mathcal O/p^j)^{r_j-r_{j-1}}$, where $r_j$ counts order-$p^j$ subgroups of $(\mathbf Q_p/\mathbf Z_p)^n$. The same duality extends the generic trace along two-step isogeny flags to an integral surjection, even when the flag-forgetting map is not flat. This computes composition in the subring of weighted trace operations. Applications include sharp projector denominators and congruence fibre products for full-torsion loci.

papers.title: PACT: A Pragmatic Prompting Framework for Expressive and Voice-Preserving Speech-to-Speech Translation
papers.abstract: Speech-to-speech translation should preserve not only what is said, but also who says it and how it is said. Existing end-to-end S2ST, speech MLLM, and cascade systems can preserve content or timbre, but often struggle to realize emotion, tone, rhythm, pauses, and pragmatic attitude in the target language. We propose PACT, a target-space pragmatic prompting framework for expressive and voice-preserving S2ST. PACT extracts source pragmatic cues, projects them into the target-language expression space, calibrates the projected representation to a realizable target subspace, and converts it into continuous prompts for a frozen speech generator. On bidirectional Spanish-English TOPI evaluation, PACT achieves the best overall performance among evaluated systems across content fidelity, voice preservation, and expression preservation metrics.

papers.title: Are We Testing Too Much? A Survey of Benchmark Compression for Efficient Evaluation of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Benchmarks are essential for evaluating and improving large language models (LLMs). Yet many widely used benchmarks are redundant, making evaluation unnecessarily expensive. Benchmark compression lowers this cost by estimating full-benchmark scores and rankings from a partial evaluation. Research in this area has grown rapidly since 2024, but to our knowledge no survey has systematically organized its methods and findings. We review 119 papers to explain how methods choose what to evaluate, recover full-benchmark results, and verify their reliability. From this analysis, we develop a taxonomy covering compression within individual benchmarks, across benchmark suites, and during adaptive evaluation, together with work on redundancy and reliability. We compare their information needs, total costs, reliability checks, and limitations. Methods reduce evaluation costs by selecting representative subsets, using cheaper or reusable information, and testing adaptively, but risk poor coverage, inaccurate estimates, and sequential delays. The resulting taxonomy and practical guide help researchers choose, validate, and deploy methods for more efficient and reliable LLM evaluation.

papers.title: The Complexity of Verifying Strategic Abilities in Succinct Multiagent Systems
papers.abstract: This paper studies the complexity of model checking strategic abilities in multiagent systems under imperfect information, in particular systems represented succinctly. Such a representation can describe systems that are exponentially larger than their input and is particularly relevant to practical implementations of model checkers such as MCMAS. The logics we consider include epistemic strategy logic supporting partial binding $SLK_{P}$, and its syntactic fragments: epistemic strategy logic $SLK$ and variants of Alternating Time Temporal logics. We show that succinct model checking for $SLK_P$ and $SLK$ is $AEXP(poly)$-complete, while objective ATL and ATL$^{*}$ are $P^{NEXP}$-complete. The latter corrects a previous NEXP-completeness result for model checking succinct imperfect-information systems. Under subjective semantics, $P^{NEXP}$-completeness already holds for one-step Coalition Logic, and therefore also for ATL and ATL$^{*}$.

papers.title: Molecular-Dynamics Verification of Effective Gravity under Heat Conduction
papers.abstract: We test the effective-gravity prediction of global thermodynamics using standard molecular dynamics of a two-dimensional Lennard-Jones fluid. Under weak heat conduction with the lower boundary hotter than the upper boundary, the transition between liquid below gas and liquid above gas shifts from zero to finite downward gravity. Using independently measured equilibrium saturation pressures, we calculate the shift predicted by global thermodynamics and find agreement with the observed transition shift. The transition occurs at zero effective gravity, where the hydrostatic pressure difference balances the saturation-pressure difference between the two boundaries. The hysteresis response under heat conduction also agrees with the equilibrium response when plotted against effective gravity. These results establish the predictive power of global thermodynamics for nonequilibrium structure formation.

papers.title: Photoinduced Modulation of Rectification and Charge Transport in Diarylethene-Viologen Molecular Junction
papers.abstract: Large-area molecular junctions combining photochromic and redox-active functionalities provide an attractive platform for controlling charge transport by light. In this work, we study Au/DAEVIO/Ti/Au molecular junctions incorporated with electro-grafted layers of diarylethene-viologen with thicknesses of 12-16 nm. In the initial OFF state, the junctions exhibit low current densities and strong rectification, with a rectification ratio of 300 at 1V. Temperature-dependent measurements reveal a thermally assisted contribution at higher temperatures and a much weaker temperature dependence below 160-180K, consistent with multistep charge transport through molecular and/or interfacial states rather than direct coherent tunneling across the entire molecular layer. Under continuous in situ 385 nm irradiation, the electrical response is strongly and asymmetrically modified. The current density at +1V increases by a factor of 200, while the negative-bias current is only weakly modified, reducing the rectification ratio from 300 to 2. Illumination also produces a nonzero short-circuit current density of + 0.006mA cm-2 and an open-circuit voltage of -0.45V. These results indicate that irradiation simultaneously modifies molecular charge transport and generates a measurable photoelectric response. This behavior is consistent with light-induced changes in electronic coupling associated with DAE photocyclization, combined with photoinduced charge generation and field-dependent charge separation involving the redox-active viologen units and asymmetric electrode interfaces.

papers.title: Interior Hessian estimates for $k$-convex solutions of Hessian quotient equations
papers.abstract: We study interior Hessian estimates for $k$-convex solutions of Hessian quotient equations $\frac{σ_k(D^2u)}{σ_\ell(D^2u)}=1$ with $2\leq k\leq n$, $0 \leq \ell < k$, and $k-\ell \in\{1,2\}$. We first adopt the unified quantitative separation-propagation method of Li--Wu [LW26b] to derive a doubling inequality, and then use the compactness argument of Shankar--Yuan [SY25] to obtain the estimates. This approach also applies to a class of general Hessian equations.

papers.title: Stability and Optimal Design of Adaptive Linear Bus Holding on Open Chains and Loops
papers.abstract: Bus holding can suppress bunching, but its stability and performance depend on the feedback structure and on how the bus sequence is bounded. This paper develops a common analytical framework for adaptive linear holding on finite open chains and loops and relates both to the bi-infinite system studied in the literature. Matrix and Fourier methods yield necessary and sufficient stability conditions for current- and leading-bus kernels on open chains and general cyclic kernels on loops, together with computable covariance bounds on open chains and exact variance formulas on loops. The analysis shows when periodic closure changes stability, when coefficient-sum stability tests in the literature are conservative, and why a stable open chain can still accumulate substantial variance before boundary effects arrive. For loops with same-lap feedback, modal analysis links control coefficients to fleet-wide schedule drift and to relative headway patterns, explaining the behavior of existing rules and yielding closed-form Pareto-optimal designs for schedule-holding and headway-holding tradeoffs. Cross-lap output corrections relate these designs to physical headway and holding performance. Numerical experiments show that the analytical design and a three-tap approximation, both obtained from closed-form coefficients and a one-dimensional search, outperform four established controls at the tested moderate and loose headway-variance budgets, with holding variances within 0.35% and 3.5% of the full cyclic numerical frontier across these budgets and other parameter variations. The framework thus provides a tractable design procedure and an explanation of how feedback structure and boundary conditions shape service reliability and holding effort.

papers.title: Partially-Averaged Navier-Stokes simulation of turbulent annular Poiseulle flow
papers.abstract: Turbulent annular Poiseulle flow is commonly encountered in various engineering applications, such as heat exchangers. The effects of the inner wall transverse curvature on the flowfield, characterised by the ratio of inner and outer radii $η= R_{i}/R_{o}$, have been studied previously using Direct Numerical Simulations (DNS). Scale-resolving simulations based on a Reynolds-Averaged Navier Stokes framework offer a potentially cheaper alternative to traditional Large Eddy Simulations (LES); however it is not clear if such models are able to capture the turbulence anisotropy in the turbulent annular pipe flow. In the present study, turbulent annular Poiseulle flow at $Re_{D_{h}} = 8900$ is performed with the Partially-Averaged Navier Stokes (PANS) model, a variable-resolution turbulence model that is based on the conventional RANS modelling. The ability of the PANS model to capture the effects of the transverse wall curvature is found to be comparable with DNS and other RANS-based scale-resolving approaches despite its relative simplicity and reduced computational cost.

papers.title: Preferential concentration of cloud droplets: Coupled effects of phase change and gravitational settling
papers.abstract: Cloud droplets respond to turbulent motion with finite inertia and settle under gravity, while condensation and evaporation change their sizes. The nonuniform accumulation of cloud droplets in turbulent flows, known as preferential concentration, has attracted sustained interest because it affects droplet collision and coalescence rates. We develop an analytical theory that quantifies the coupled effects of droplet inertia, gravitational settling, and phase change on concentration changes. Applying this theory to simulations of two-dimensional homogeneous thermal convection reveals that phase change markedly enhances preferential concentration in this flow, primarily through spatial differences in settling speed. These differences arise because droplets experience different thermodynamic histories along their trajectories and thus acquire different sizes. Droplet transport further increases this settling contribution by rearranging droplets of different sizes. Fluid deformation partly offsets this enhancement by thinning concentration structures, reducing the preferential concentration measured at a fixed spatial scale.

papers.title: Teach Me After You Learn It: Lookahead Self-Distillation for RLVR
papers.abstract: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) has emerged as a popular training paradigm for LLMs, providing dense, token-level supervision by aligning a model's own distribution with the distribution induced by privileged information. However, existing OPSD methods derive supervision solely from privileged information of the same instance, leaving inter-instance supervision largely unexplored. We propose Lookahead Self-Distillation (LEAD), which introduces inter-instance distillation by allowing the teacher to first learn from other on-policy rollouts before teaching the student. LEAD constructs lookahead teachers through virtual RL updates on disjoint subsets of on-policy rollouts, and uses each teacher to provide cross-group token-level supervision for the other subset. To reconcile the complementary yet potentially conflicting signals from OPSD and RLVR, we introduce harmonious modulation, which adaptively modulates the GRPO advantage based on the agreement between the two signals. Extensive experiments on scientific reasoning and interactive-agent benchmarks show that LEAD achieves the best in-domain average performance across model scales while maintaining out-of-domain generalization comparable to GRPO.

papers.title: Femtoscopic parameters of pion emission sources in EPOS4 Au+Au collisions from 7.7 to 200 GeV
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional femtoscopy probes the space-time structure of particle-emitting sources in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. The collision-energy dependence of Lévy source parameters may reveal the evolution of strongly interacting matter and possible signatures of the QCD phase diagram. We previously studied the excitation function of three-dimensional Lévy source parameters for pion pairs in Au+Au collisions with EPOS4, analyzing the pair-distance distribution \(D(ρ)\) through one-dimensional projections. Here, we analyze the full three-dimensional source distribution and correlation function directly. We construct \(D(ρ_{\rm out},ρ_{\rm side},ρ_{\rm long})\) as a 3D histogram, transform it into \(C(q_{\rm out},q_{\rm side},q_{\rm long})\) using a Fast Fourier Transform, and fit the correlation function with the analytic Lévy formula. This approach can reduce biases arising when one-dimensional projections are used to describe a non-elliptical source. We apply the method across the RHIC Beam Energy Scan range and compare the extracted energy dependence with results from the projection-based method and recent UrQMD calculations. We focus on the out-side observables \(R_{\rm diff}^{2}=R_{\rm out}^{2}-R_{\rm side}^{2}\) and \(R_{\rm out}/R_{\rm side}\), whose different energy dependences in EPOS4 and UrQMD may illuminate the roles of emission duration and source dynamics. This work establishes a direct three-dimensional framework for comparison with future femtoscopic measurements and for exploring possible non-monotonic structures associated with the QCD phase diagram.

papers.title: Optimal Online Regret for Context-Lumpable Bandits
papers.abstract: We study stochastic contextual bandits with an unknown context-lumpable structure. The $S$ contexts are partitioned into $r$ blocks, and every arm has the same mean reward across contexts in the same block. Under arbitrary context distributions and without separation assumptions, we design an algorithm with expected regret $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{r(S+K)T})$, matching the lower bound of Lee et al. (2023) up to logarithmic factors and improving their previous upper bound by a factor of $r$. The algorithm operates over dyadic accuracy levels, using a baseline policy and confidence-based early stopping to control exploration. It then performs cross-context elimination: since rewards are identical within a block, one selected arm eliminates all surviving records from that block, requiring at most $r$ selections at each level. Multi-scale exploration assigns finer accuracies to frequent blocks and coarser accuracies to rare blocks, yielding a near-optimal arm for every block while keeping the weighted policy error small.

papers.title: Square-Root Profiles and Sharp Fourier Decay of Quasiperiodic Spectral Measures
papers.abstract: We study spectral measures of one-dimensional quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators. For subcritical Schrödinger operator with Diophantine frequency, we prove sharp measurable-set bounds, answering a question of Avila and Jitomirskaya \cite{AJ}; we prove optimal Fourier decay and the sharp decay order of the time-averaged quantum return probability, confirming a conjecture of Aloisio, Carvalho, and de Oliveira \cite{ACO} and a prediction of Zhong and Mosseri \cite{ZhongMosseri}. For the subcritical almost Mathieu operator, we establish summable square-root envelopes for the spectral density, with an optimal density-one formulation of the lower bound, thereby answering a question of Avila \cite{Aqi}. These results follow from a general theorem for reflectionless measures under a summable square-root Craig-type condition. We establish an exact residue expansion of the squared Borel transform, which connects local density blow-up with long-time averaged return probabilities: the endpoint residues determine both the square-root edge profiles and the leading coefficient of the time-averaged return probability.

papers.title: FALLNEST: Dual-Domain Dataset Condensation of Imbalanced IMU Data for Wearable Fall Detection
papers.abstract: Wearable fall detection is hampered by rare fall events, scarce labeled IMU data, and the cost of training deep models on large, imbalanced corpora. Existing methods either rely on hand-crafted features with shallow classifiers, which limits learning from raw signals, or train deep networks on full datasets that require re-sampling to counter class skew and demand substantial data and compute. To address this, we propose a novel Fall detection framework via Normalized-gradient and Embedding matched Synthetic Time-frequency condensation, dubbed FALLNEST, a data-centric approach that distills large, imbalanced IMU datasets into tiny, class-balanced synthetic training sets. Building on dual-domain time-series condensation (CondTSC), FALLNEST introduces a fall-specific 7-channel input with accelerometer vector magnitude, class-balanced K-Means initialization, and normalized gradient matching with gradient clipping, combined with MMD-based embedding alignment and multi-view Fourier-domain augmentation, so that class balance arises from the condensed set itself rather than from re-sampling. We evaluate on SisFall, KFall, and MobiFall using strict subject-wise splits and naturally imbalanced test sets, reporting accuracy, Macro-F1, and PR-AUC over five seeds. A 102K-parameter TinyCNN trained on only 32 to 146 synthetic windows (about only 1% of the training windows) reaches 93.5-95.8% mean accuracy and 0.89-0.98 PR-AUC, with standard deviations of 1.0-1.7% in accuracy, demonstrating the efficacy of our approach.

papers.title: The influence of decay in dynamic models of gene regulatory networks
papers.abstract: We investigate the influence of decay rates on the dynamics of three-dimensional gene regulatory networks modeled by nonlinear differential equations with logistic sigmoidal regulatory functions. Particular attention is paid to the existence, location, and stability of equilibrium points in systems involving numerous interacting parameters. An explicit analytical representation of a central equilibrium is obtained under suitable relations between the regulatory weights, thresholds, and decay coefficients, allowing its location to be determined without solving the corresponding nonlinear algebraic system numerically. General formulas for the characteristic polynomial of the linearized system are derived, and spectral conditions for instability are established for several classes of regulatory interactions. We demonstrate how variations in decay rates can change the number and stability of equilibria, transform oscillatory dynamics, and influence the emergence or suppression of complicated attractors. The possibility of chaotic behavior is investigated through eigenvalue configurations, Lyapunov exponents, and the Kaplan-Yorke dimension. Numerical examples illustrate the sensitivity of the dynamics to decay parameters, including the suppression of previously observed chaotic behavior. The results provide an analytical framework for investigating equilibrium configurations, stability transitions, and complex dynamics in parametrized gene regulatory networks.

papers.title: Encrypted Skills Can Become New Security Exploits If AI Agents Know How to Decipher
papers.abstract: Third-party skills can expose LLM agents to malicious instructions hidden by encoding. We introduce Ciphered Skill Injection (CSI), which embeds such instructions in skill files for agents to decode and follow. We evaluate Caesar and layered variants across eight models and 139 injection-task pairs, separating instruction recovery from attack success. In the primary setting with shortened skills, the variants achieve attack success rates of up to 47.5% and 40.3%, respectively. Successful decoding does not guarantee attack success, and layering has model-dependent effects. The tested skill scanners rarely flag injected skills. These findings highlight the risk of promoting decoded, untrusted content into actionable instructions.

papers.title: Massive black holes in the first billion years with JWST
papers.abstract: The James Webb Space Telescope has unlocked uncharted territory for the study of early black holes, enabling the detection of fainter and smaller black holes at larger cosmological distances than previously possible. Compared to nearby massive black holes, they are characterised by several unexpected attributes, such as their multi-wavelength properties or their relation to their host galaxies. These observational findings challenge our understanding of the past evolution of present-day supermassive black holes, and provide novel anchor points to constrain theoretical models of black hole formation and growth. This review summarises our current understanding of the observed properties of newly discovered, active black holes in the early Universe, discusses the status of mass measurements and the relation to their hosts, as well as open questions and future prospects.

papers.title: Data-Driven Surrogate-Model for Real-Time Loads Prediction in Floating Wind Farms
papers.abstract: This work presents a data-driven load-surrogate modelling framework for real-time control of floating offshore wind farms. The proposed methodology uses mid-fidelity simulations performed with OpenFAST and FAST.Farm together with MLife fatigue analysis to generate Damage Equivalent Load (DEL) datasets of floating wind turbines under wake steering conditions. A two-stage surrogate modelling approach is adopted: first, a Feed-Forward Neural Network (FFNN) is trained using data from simulations of a single floating wind turbine, while a second stage corrects the residual error between the FFNN predictions and FAST.Farm simulations using either Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) or an additional FFNN. The results show that the proposed framework can estimate DELs with errors generally below 15% for tower base bending moment, blade root bending moment, yaw bearing moment, and fairlead tension, while maintaining computational times compatible with real-time applications. The study also highlights the challenges related to generalization of the load-surrogate model under varying environmental and control conditions, especially for large floating wind farms. Overall, the proposed methodology demonstrates the potential of surrogate-based DEL estimation for load-aware floating wind farm control applications.

papers.title: Advanced computational methods for simulating the classical hydrogen atom in stochastic electrodynamics
papers.abstract: Stochastic electrodynamics (SED) is a theory of nature seeking to derive key aspects of quantum mechanics and quantum electrodynamics from a purely classical physics perspective. While SED has been successful in many areas, it has had mixed success when addressing the classical hydrogen atom bathed in classical electromagnetic zero-point radiation. Because analytical approaches are largely intractable, advanced numerical simulation methods are required. To address this, we develop a pseudo-wave formulation that integrates the solid angle in k-space utilizing symmetry, resulting in a significantly reduced memory footprint and lower computational overhead for generating the zero-point radiation spectrum. This optimization is paired with a logarithmic frequency grid, a sliding window tracking the instantaneous Keplerian frequency, and a Tukey smoothing function to eliminate discrete force discontinuities. Integrated via an adaptive RK4 algorithm with step-doubling across highly dense grids of up to 100-million bins, these techniques demonstrate the asymptotic convergence of ensemble stability. We show that increasing grid resolution in the high-frequency domain systematically mitigates artificial electron decay, yielding a simulated probability density function that closely aligns with the quantum mechanical ground state P(r). Crucially, the simulations exhibit stable, low-eccentricity orbits without any observed atomic ionization events.

papers.title: Improved Analysis of Adaptive Task Allocation and Non-Stationary Processing Times
papers.abstract: We study the task allocation problem, where our goal is to develop an online algorithm that efficiently distributes tasks among workers based on their computational performance. This task is challenging since computation times are random and non-stationary in practice. Recent works have introduced different online algorithms to address this problem. One of them is Adaptive Task Allocation (ATA), a bandit-style algorithm.
