papers.abstract: Persistent textual memory lets language-model agents reuse lessons from past tasks to improve on future multi-step tasks without retraining. Systems such as ACE and Dynamic Cheatsheet keep it as a playbook: lessons the agent writes after each task and reads in its prompt. A key challenge is to decide which lessons improve later tasks. Current systems leave the decision to the agent itself, which makes performance unstable: the same procedure can write a playbook that helps or one that falls up to 69.6 points below no playbook. These findings motivate valuing lessons by their measured effect on task success rather than by the agent's judgment. We propose Randomized Block Curation (RBC), which measures this effect with a randomized experiment on practice tasks. It groups related lessons into blocks large enough to move success measurably and, on each practice task, includes or leaves out every block at random. Random inclusion makes tasks with and without a block comparable, so the gap in their success estimates the block's effect. RBC keeps the blocks that help and, since the same procedure can write a helpful or a harmful playbook, grows several and serves whichever curated, whole or no playbook scores best on fresh practice episodes. Across two memory systems, three models and three benchmarks, RBC raises average success to 66.9, against 55.5 with the whole playbook, 54.1 with no playbook and 53.8 when the agent's own judgment picks the lessons to keep.

papers.title: Adaptive Variance-Reduced Stochastic Sequential (Quadratic Constrained) Quadratic Programming
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose an adaptive variance-reduced stochastic sequential (quadratic constrained) quadratic programming (AVR-SS(QC)QP) method for nonlinear constrained optimization. The framework integrates SPIDER-based variance reduction, stochastic quasi-Newton curvature information, merit-function globalization, and adaptive switching between stochastic SQP and SQCQP models. The switching mechanism is governed by a relative constraint model curvature indicator that measures the second-order constraint information neglected by the linearized SQP model. A smoothed hysteresis rule ac?tivates the SQCQP model only when the relative constraint curvature is significant. An exact L1 merit function with Armijo backtracking globalizes the resulting directions, while a coupled stochastic Lyapunov analysis controls the interaction between gradient-estimation error and optimization progress. Under standard smoothness, sampling, regularity, and second-order conditions, we establish almost-sure consistency of the variance-reduced gradient estimator and global convergence of the KKT residual. We further show that, near regular KKT points, the curvature indicator vanishes and the method eventually selects the computationally cheaper SQP model. Numerical experiments on a sparse principal component analysis problem illustrate the practical be?havior of the proposed framework.

papers.title: Delving into the depths of NGC 3783 with XRISM VI. Evidence for a failed wind based on Fe xxv absorption line variability
papers.abstract: NGC 3783 exhibits a prominent Fe XXV absorption trough in the time-averaged XRISM/Resolve spectrum. To investigate its short-term variability, we present a time-resolved analysis of the Fe XXV absorption line during the continuous 10-day observation. We divided the resolved absorption profile into five fixed velocity intervals and measured their normalized equivalent widths in 19 time-resolved spectra. Three velocity intervals exhibit significant equivalent-width (EW) variability. Two velocity intervals respond differently to low- and high-flux states with less emission line contamination. The time-dependent photoionisation modelling is unable to reproduce the most significant observed EW variation ($3.5 \, σ$), possibly owing to uncertainties in the assumed initial equilibrium state, which prevent a precise density measurement. Instead, using photoionisation calculations and assuming the high-density limit, we derive approximate constraints on the ionisation parameters of the two relevant components. The low-velocity component (-320 to -680 km/s) shows a delayed inverse response, indicating a high ionisation parameter, while its relatively short lag timescale indicates a relatively high density and a distance upper limit of 0.05 pc. In contrast, the high-velocity component (-680 to -1040 km/s) manifests a positive response with a longer lag to the ionising continuum, implying a relatively low ionisation parameter. This component appears to be less dense, with an inferred distance upper limit of 0.25 pc. The low-velocity component is consistent with a failed wind, as its outflow velocity is below the local escape velocity, whereas the high-velocity component lies near the escape threshold. Together with the lower-ionisation failed wind detected in 2001, this supports a multiphase failed-wind scenario in the unobscured state of NGC~3783 over more than two decades.

papers.title: FedGraph: Defending Federated Large Language Model Fine-Tuning Against Backdoor Attacks via Graph-Based Aggregation
papers.abstract: Federated fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) allows multiple clients to collaboratively adapt models without sharing raw data, offering strong privacy benefits. However, this setting is highly vulnerable to backdoor attacks, in which malicious clients manipulate their updates to induce targeted behaviors while maintaining normal performance on benign inputs. In this work, we make a key observation specific to federated LLM fine-tuning: malicious clients tend to exhibit strong consistency in their model updates, whereas benign clients produce more diverse and dispersed updates. This structural difference is not well captured by existing defense methods, which typically rely on direct anomaly detection in high-dimensional parameter space and therefore struggle in the presence of entangled LLM updates. Motivated by this observation, we propose FedGraph, a graph-based aggregation framework that explicitly models relationships among client updates. By representing clients as nodes in a dynamically constructed graph and extracting structural features that characterize their relative positions and interactions, FedGraph derives compact client representations that effectively separate malicious and benign behaviors. These representations are then used to identify and suppress malicious contributions during aggregation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FedGraph significantly improves backdoor defense. It consistently reduces attack success rates to below 10% while achieving high detection accuracy (95.5% on average) and a low false positive rate (2.33%), substantially outperforming existing federated learning defenses.

papers.title: On Permutations Whose Adjacent-Sum Reciprocals Sum to One
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give a constructive proof that for any integer n>7 (resp. n>6), the numbers 1,2,...,n can be arranged in a circle (resp. in a line) such that the sum of the reciprocals of all adjacent sums equals 1. The above conjecture was originally posed by Zhi-Wei Sun. Partitioning the integers according to n mod 12 into nine residue classes, we prove a recursive proposition and inductively construct new examples. Main lemmas and propositions in introduction are proved in Section 2. The rest of the cases are handled by explicit constructions in appendix.

papers.title: Counterexamples to prescribed scalar curvature in the null case
papers.abstract: We construct smooth functions on the flat torus $\mathbb{T}^{n\ge5}$ that change sign and have negative mean but cannot be realized as the scalar curvature of any metric in the given conformal class.

papers.title: Algebraic Direct Sums and Generalized Drazin Invertibility
papers.abstract: Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex Banach space $X$. We prove that the algebraic decomposition \[ X=\K(T)\oplus \Hq(T) \] forces both summands to be closed and hence characterizes generalized Drazin invertibility. This improves the classical characterizations of Mbekhta~\resultcite{Theorem~1.6}{MbekhtaKato}, Schmoeger~\resultcite{Theorem~4}{Schmoeger}, and Dajić and Koliha~\resultcite{Theorem~6.7}{DajicKoliha}, by removing their closedness assumptions. We also show that $T$ is generalized Drazin invertible if and only if \[ \dim\bigl(\K(T)\cap \Hq(T)\bigr)<\infty \quad\text{and}\quad \codim\bigl(\K(T)+\Hq(T)\bigr)<\infty. \] For ordinary Drazin invertibility, we obtain analogous finite-defect characterizations involving the hyperkernel and the hyperrange. We also give a characterization using pointwise nilpotence on an invariant summand. Finally, we consider arbitrary invariant algebraic decompositions and give a counterexample when the inverse of the restriction to one summand is not assumed bounded.

papers.title: Principled Design of Expected Improvement for Continuous Simulation Optimization
papers.abstract: Expected improvement based on stochastic kriging (SK) surrogate is widely used in continuous simulation optimization, but unknown heteroscedastic noise makes three basic design choices consequential: the incumbent to define improvement, replication allocation, and final recommendation. Existing methods typically either assume the noise levels are known or choose these components separately through heuristic rules or empirical calibration. We instead derive a high-probability upper bound on the simple regret and systematically choose the three components within general rule classes to tighten this bound. We first establish a finite-sample confidence bound for the SK predictor as a foundation for the three design choices. Within general posterior-quantile rule classes, tightening the regret certificate selects a lower-quantile incumbent and an upper-quantile recommendation among sampled designs. The opposing quantiles reflect the different roles of exploratory experiments and the final implemented decision. Under mild conditions satisfied by common kernels, minimizing a tractable kernel-specific bound yields a logarithmic replication order. Based on these design choices, the resulting simple regret matches the existing results under known homoscedastic noise up to logarithmic factors. To our knowledge, this is the first simple-regret guarantee of this form for a continuous-domain EI-type simulation optimization method that learns unknown heteroscedastic variances through replications.

papers.title: How Well Do LLMs Perform in Peer Review? Evidence from Finance and Accounting
papers.abstract: Referees increasingly use large language models (LLMs), while finance and accounting journals disagree about whether to allow it. We ask which part of a referee's job the models can do. GPT-4o, whose training data end before the 2024 conference season, referees the papers presented at the 2024 AFA and NBER finance meetings, and we compare its verdicts with publication in the top-three finance journals over the next two years. Papers the model scores one standard deviation higher are 44\% more likely to be published, net of author reputation. The result is not driven by look-ahead bias, as the model does not recall the outcomes. The information comes from its judgements of correctness and exposition. Its judgements of originality and significance carry none, and a referee guide that stresses importance does not help. The split between correctness and contribution holds for accounting papers and for a newer model, GPT-5. LLMs can check whether research is right, but not whether it matters. The technical check can go to the model, while the judgement of contribution stays with people.

papers.title: Stability of the Markov-Krein Transform Under Classical Convolutions
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every $c>0$, the image of the generalized Markov-Krein transform on probability measures with finite logarithmic moment is closed under classical additive convolution and under the Mellin convolution. This resolves the positivity conjecture for the additive high-temperature convolution, a one-parameter interpolation between classical and free convolution arising in random matrix theory and representation theory in the regime $N\to\infty, Nβ_N/2\to c$. Our proof relies on a convolution theorem for universally prestarlike functions.

papers.title: Connection between MP and DPP for Mean-Field Stochastic Optimal Control Problems
papers.abstract: This paper deals with the optimal control problem for the general mean-field stochastic differential equations, in which the coefficients depend on both the state process as well as on its law. We focus on the connection between the general maximum principle and the dynamic programming principle for such a control problem. We establish the relationship between the value function of the mean-field optimal control problem and the adjoint equations in the maximum principle. We also give a general mean-field stochastic verification theorem. Some examples are solved explicitly to illustrate our results.

papers.title: STAMP as a topology-aware molecular language for fragment-level learning and editing
papers.abstract: Molecular fragments provide chemically meaningful units, but existing molecular languages rarely make their locations and connections explicit for editing. Here we introduce STAMP (Sequential Tree Attachment-based Motif-Preserving representation), a topology-aware molecular language that connects fragment-level representation learning with precise structural editing. STAMP separately encodes motif identity, attachment sites and tree topology, making fragments reusable across contexts and subtrees directly accessible. Learned representations capture motif similarity and recurring transformations, and lower activity-cliff prediction error on 23 of 30 targets versus a matched SMILES encoder. Compatible subtree operations support scaffold-preserving optimization, ranking first among six methods on 15 of 23 benchmark objectives. A deterministic compiler enables frozen language models to act on indexed fragments, improving molecular editing, optimization, transformation transfer and change identification by 9 to 56 percentage points over plain SMILES. Together, these results establish an executable molecular language in which learned chemical units remain directly operable during design.

papers.title: Estimating Surprisal from the Speech Signal
papers.abstract: Although language is predominantly spoken, empirical tests of surprisal theory rely almost entirely on written text. In practice, surprisal is estimated using language models (LMs) trained on text and applied to transcriptions, creating a text bottleneck that limits evaluation of the theory in the spoken modality. We remove this bottleneck by estimating surprisal directly from the speech signal using a speech LM. This raises a key question: should surprisal be defined over realization-specific acoustic inputs or over abstract linguistic units? Since a single unit can have many distinct acoustic realizations, each assigned a different probability by the model, defining surprisal over abstract units is difficult. To address this, we introduce an importance sampling estimator that approximates the probability of an abstract unit by marginalizing over realizations generated by a text-to-speech model. Using pupillometry data from a listening study, we evaluate surprisal theory in this text-free setting at multiple levels of granularity. Obtaining surprisal from several speech LMs, we consistently find that surprisal estimated via importance sampling better predicts pupil dilation than realization-specific surprisal for words. We also find that surprisal values for sub-lexical units are predictive of pupil dilation. While we find that surprisal can be estimated without recourse to text, and that marginalizing over distinct realizations of words is more predictive of lexical processing effort, surprisal as a whole is not a strong predictor of change in pupil size, regardless of its source.

papers.title: A Central Limit Theorem for High-Temperature SYK Model: A case study on mathematical research using AI and Lean
papers.abstract: The Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (SYK) model is a quantum many-body model of Majorana fermions with all-to-all random interactions. It has attracted wide interest in condensed matter and high-energy physics as a solvable model of non-Fermi liquids and holography. Fix an even integer $q\geq4$, and let $Z_N(β)$ be the partition function of the Gaussian $q$-body SYK model. We prove that for all sufficiently small inverse temperatures $β> 0$, there exists $ρ=ρ(β)>0$ such that \[ N^{q/2 -1}(\log Z_N(β)-\mathbb{E}[\log Z_N(β)]) \Longrightarrow \mathcal{N}(0,ρ^2). \] In addition to the mathematical results, we discuss how the proofs were developed and refined through interaction between human researchers and AI, and we describe the subsequent formalization of the main arguments in Lean 4. This work thus serves as a case study of a research workflow that integrates human insight, AI-assisted exploration, iterative proof refinement, and formal verification.

papers.title: Some Bounds on the Lehmer Index
papers.abstract: In this paper, the relationship is studied between the Lehmer index and the reciprocal sum of the prime factors of a Lehmer number. Some upper bounds and a lower bound are proposed for the Lehmer index. Another constraint on Lehmer index is also proposed if a Lehmer number has 3 as its prime factor.

papers.title: A System One Approach to General Protein Evolution
papers.abstract: Protein engineering requires deciding which mutation to test next and when to stop. Existing approaches often require target-family measurements, encode candidates separately, or return scores that are not calibrated to the assay. We introduce Pev, a general mutation policy that explores a System One approach to protein evolution: learning from experiments across families to make decisions in a single parallel query. Given a parent sequence and an assay context, Pev encodes the parent once and returns calibrated probabilities for choosing an edit or stopping, together with each edit's probability of improving the assay outcome. One policy covers peptides, small folded domains, and antibodies across binding and stability objectives, without fitting model weights to the target family. In ten-well screens on held-out families, Pev finds 3.3$\times$ as many beneficial mutations as random selection and 1.8$\times$ as many as zero-shot ESM-2. It also outperforms a ridge surrogate refitted on target measurements in closed-loop search on the held-out GB1 landscape. Post-hoc calibration improves probability reliability without changing decisions, while shared encoding provides over 800$\times$ the throughput of per-mutant encoding at 1,000 candidates per request. These results suggest that a System One approach could support efficient experimental decisions across protein families, with Pev providing an initial demonstration.

papers.title: Altermagnetic Ground States on the Ammann--Beenker Tiling
papers.abstract: We identify exact altermagnetic ground states of a classical Heisenberg model on a quasicrystal. Considering the Ammann--Beenker tiling as an example, we determine the ground states by exploiting the parity structure of its parent four-dimensional hypercubic lattice. The ground state hosts coplanar altermagnetic order characterized by the preserved spin-group symmetry $[C_{2x}\parallel C_{8z}]$. Without translational symmetry, the momentum-space spin splitting that usually identifies altermagnets is not directly accessible. We instead couple the spins to itinerant electrons and show spin-resolved transport with $g$-wave symmetry, confirming the altermagnetic nature in a nonperiodic system. Our results establish a geometric route to altermagnetic order in quasicrystals, connecting exact magnetic ground states to their spin-resolved transport signatures.

papers.title: Copying Is Not Grounding: Training Faithful Long-Form RAG with Authored-Sentence Credit
papers.abstract: In search engines and assistants, long-form RAG answers can mislead readers with claims their sources do not support. Faithfulness rewards, the share of supported sentences, train models toward fewer such claims. We show that these rewards are hacked by copying. A sentence copied from the passages is supported almost by construction, so trained models learn to copy rather than ground what they write. Common defenses only move the hack: a KL or copy penalty leaves copying in place or trades it for shorter, emptier answers and refusals. GRPO, the standard RL algorithm, makes it worse by giving every sentence its answer's advantage, reinforcing copied and grounded sentences alike. We propose Authored-Sentence Credit (ASC) , which fixes both by moving GRPO's reward and advantage from the answer to the sentence level. The reward credits only sentences that are authored rather than copied, say more than the question, and are supported by the passages. The advantage compares each sentence with every sentence sampled for the question, so one that earns no credit ranks last and is never reinforced. Across four models and two in-domain, three held-out corpora, only ASC lowers the error rate of authored sentences and writes more supported ones in every setting, by 38% and 46% at the median under held-out evaluators, giving readers more grounded information. It takes none of these shortcuts, and two LLM judges comparing whole answers prefer no baseline to the base model but rate ASC's answers on par with it. We conclude that a faithfulness reward should credit what a model writes, not what it copies.

papers.title: PACT: Posture-Aligned Co-Design Technique for Hand Configuration and Retargeting in Multi-Finger Imitation Learning
papers.abstract: The fidelity of teleoperated demonstrations used for imitation learning is determined by how faithfully a robot hand can replicate the operator's posture. The posture retargeting law that the robot will execute is typically selected only once the hardware has been finalized, and conventional hand designs often neglect human-like grasping postures. We introduce PACT, an optimization based on human grasping postures that jointly optimizes the mechanical parameters of a 17-servo robot hand (link lengths, joint offsets, mounting angles, and base placements) and its nonlinear posture retargeter (a linear human-to-robot joint map, per-joint posture-IK weights, and damping). The optimization enforces full-finger correspondence (MCP, PIP, DIP, and tip of each finger) to human poses from the DexYCB dataset, and is constrained by servo interference, assembly clearances, and flat-hand protrusion, so the resulting design can be physically assembled. We fabricate the PACT Hand and validate it through teleoperation experiments and an imitation-learning demonstration. The hand reproduces all human hand keypoints with a kinematic RMSE of 3.9 mm, compared to 12.8 mm for the LEAP Hand baseline, and keeps all fingertips within 10 mm on every grasping posture, while the baseline achieves this for only 21.6% of the poses. Under matched per-joint torque limits, it lifts twice the baseline payload, 2 kg against 1 kg, and deforms a held paper cup seven times less, reaching a deformation level comparable to a human hand. It also achieves an 86% grasping success rate on YCB daily objects, compared to 64% for the baseline. Finally, as a demonstration, an imitation-learning policy trained on demonstrations collected with the PACT Hand achieved a 75% success rate at held-out placements in a can pick-and-place task. Project page: https://pact-hand-2027.github.io

papers.title: An Optical KV Cache Network for Disaggregated LLM Serving
papers.abstract: In disaggregated LLM serving, each request's KV cache moves from a prefill GPU to a decode GPU before the response begins, and a coding-agent turn often moves the KV cache of its whole long context. Behind an oversubscribed packet fabric, this transfer adds to the time to first token (TTFT). An optical circuit switch (OCS) can give every transfer a full-rate circuit for less than an oversubscribed packet fabric costs, but a mechanical OCS needs tens of milliseconds to reconfigure. We hide this delay inside the prefill. A reservation scheduler commits each circuit while the prefill is still computing, so the circuit is ready when the KV cache is, and each GPU reaches the OCS through its own wavelength-multiplexed (WDM) optics on one fiber pair. In simulations of GPU clusters on real serving traces with prefill times measured on H100 GPUs, this optical KV cache network matches 400G packet fabrics with adaptive routing at 0.55 to 0.78 times the cost of a 2:1 fabric and tolerates the 50 ms reconfiguration delay of a 384-port mechanical OCS.

papers.title: The Singularity Has a Distribution: Exact Timing Laws and Detection Limits for a Stochastic Intelligence Explosion
papers.abstract: Automating AI research creates a positive feedback loop between software capability and research effort. We study a stochastic realisation of this loop in which independent, positive, multiplicative improvements arrive at a rate proportional to a power of current capability. Within this model, randomness leaves the deterministic explosion threshold unchanged but replaces the blow-up date by an explicit distribution. For equal-sized improvements the explosion time is a geometrically weighted sum of independent exponentials; its $q$-series representation gives its transforms, moments and tail behaviour, including a two-term small-time asymptotic. For Lomax-distributed improvement sizes the explosion time is exactly Gamma distributed. Self-similarity implies that, with parameters known, the relative uncertainty about the remaining time does not vanish as explosion approaches. We formulate a fixed-sample test between constant and geometrically increasing idea-arrival rates. If the baseline rate and the alternative log-rate increment $\ell$ are known, the minimum sample size at error level $α$ is asymptotic to $(12z_α^2)^{1/3}\ell^{-2/3}$, where $z_α$ is the upper-$α$ standard normal quantile. Uncertainty about the growth exponent near its critical value produces a $1/t$ tail with an explicit constant, and hence an infinite conditional mean waiting time, although explosion is certain given a positive exponent. Separate extensions show that a fixed deployment delay prevents explosion in the specified delayed-feedback models, that power-law diversion of effort shifts the growth threshold, and that in a deterministic oversight race a fixed allocation share does not change the asymptotic regime, except at a critical equality of exponents. Numerical illustrations, which are not empirical forecasts, show how timing and detectability depend on the granularity of improvements.

papers.title: CoTL: Compact Token Learning for 3D Scene Representation
papers.abstract: We present CoTL, a framework that learns a compact set of tokens that preserves scene geometry and appearance from unposed multi-view images. Our encoder compresses the input images into small per-view sets of latent tokens that aggregate information across views to form a view-consistent scene representation. Each additional view expands the representation with only a small, resolution-independent set of tokens, allowing its capacity to grow with the available observations. To force this compact bottleneck to retain sufficient scene information, a query-based Gaussian decoder uses scene-independent queries to attend to the learned tokens and recover an explicit, renderable set of 3D Gaussian primitives. Novel-view rendering supervision trains the compact representation end to end through the reconstructed Gaussian scene. Experiments on RealEstate10K and ACID show that the resulting compact, unstructured token set supports competitive novel-view synthesis and can serve as the latent space of a generative model for 3D Gaussian scene generation. Together, these results show that 3D Gaussian reconstruction is an effective objective for compact scene representation learning and the learned token space provides a basis for broader downstream tasks in 3D vision.

papers.title: Thinker-WM: A Unified World Model with Shared Multimodal Representations for Embodied Intelligence
papers.abstract: World models have emerged as a promising paradigm for embodied AI, yet existing systems often remain fragmented in the modalities they model and the functions they support. In particular, visual dynamics, geometric structure, and executable action are commonly coupled through separate interfaces or downstream modules rather than being jointly represented and evolved within a shared dynamics model. In this work, we present Thinker-WM, a unified multimodal world model that jointly models and generates RGB, metric depth, and robot action through a shared intermediate Unified Dynamics Transformer with modality-specific encoders and decoders. The model performs multimodal unification at the representation level: appearance, geometry, and action are transformed into a common dynamic representation and jointly evolved by shared parameters, while their distinct output structures are preserved. The same parameterization supports multiple functions, including joint video-action generation, world prediction, policy inference, action-conditioned generation, video-to-action generation, and inverse dynamics. To examine whether the shared representation captures action-related information, we introduce a lightweight motion probe that shows the frozen visual representation contains recoverable motion information. Thinker-WM is trained on a heterogeneous corpus comprising approximately 20K hours of egocentric video, 10K hours of real-robot data, and 1K hours of simulation data, including approximately 4K hours of real-robot data with aligned depth supervision. Extensive experiments demonstrate strong performance across embodied world-model evaluations. Thinker-WM ranks first on EWMBench, WorldOlympiad and WorldArena, while controlled studies further demonstrate the benefits of action conditioning, geometric interaction, and multi-function training within the shared representation.

papers.title: Substrate-controlled epitaxial-like growth of photochromic yttrium oxyhydride thin films
papers.abstract: Yttrium oxyhydride (YHO) thin films are synthesised by reactive magnetron sputtering of \b{eta}-YHx precursor films onto single-crystalline yttria-stabilised zirconia (YSZ) (111) and (100) substrates at 200 °C, followed by post-deposition oxidation in air. For comparison, reference films are also prepared on amorphous SiO2 and soda-lime glass substrates at both 200 °C and room temperature (RT). The structural (X-ray diffraction and scanning electron microscopy), compositional (elastic recoil detection analysis), and optical properties, including photochromic behaviour, of the films are systematically investigated. The results reveal a strong influence of substrate orientation on the film microstructure and crystallographic texture, leading to epitaxial-like growth with a mosaic spread of ~3-4°. YHO deposited on YSZ(100) exhibits larger crystallite sizes (10-20 nm) than YHO grown on YSZ(111) (~8 nm) and exhibits residual in-plane compressive strain while remaining largely relaxed with respect to the substrate. Compositional analysis revealed that the O/Y and O/H atomic ratios ranged from 0.71 to 0.82 and from 0.33 to 0.44, respectively, for films deposited under optimised conditions. These films exhibit photochromic behaviour under solar simulator illumination, with relative transmittance changes ranging from 7 to 22 % after 10 min of illumination. Despite the pronounced structural differences, the epitaxial-like films show no systematic improvement in photochromic response, indicating that the effect is governed primarily by composition. The study shows that the bleaching time constant increases exponentially with increasing contrast reached during illumination, rather than representing an intrinsic material constant of YHO.

papers.title: Autonomous Science Bench: Evaluating AI Agents for Autonomous Scientific Discovery
papers.abstract: AI agents for autonomous scientific discovery must decide which experiments to run under a limited budget. Most benchmarks for science agents provide fixed datasets, while others that support active experimentation largely rely on simulation. We introduce Autonomous Science Bench, an initial release comprising six budgeted design-build-test-learn campaigns grounded in published experiments across biology, chemistry, and materials science. Agents select batches of designs, receive measurements from a lab service, and use the results to guide subsequent experiments before delivering a predictive model. Success requires passing two calibrated gates: a discovery gate, which evaluates the designs the agent measured, and a learning gate, which evaluates its model's ranking of held-out designs. In a pilot evaluation of eight agent-model configurations and 144 trials, the best configuration succeeds in 67% of trials, while the hardest campaign is solved in only three of 24 attempts. The two gates reveal different weaknesses: some agents build accurate rankings but find too few promising designs, while others find promising designs but fail to predict which unseen designs will perform well. These differences are obscured by overall success rates alone. We release version 0.1 of the campaigns, lab runtime, and public leaderboard at https://yibow.me/autonomous-science-bench.

papers.title: A Three-Axis Rydberg Atomic Receiver Model for Polarization-Based Direction-of-Arrival Sensing
papers.abstract: This paper develops a three-axis Rydberg atomic receiver model for direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation of the radio frequency (RF) signal source. Three nominally orthogonal RF local oscillators (LOs), each assigned a distinct frequency offset, project the weak incident RF field into resolvable complex beat coefficients in the optical readout. A beat-vector observation is obtained by adopting a response calibration mechanism that maps the coefficients onto the three axes of the Cartesian coordinate system. For a known circularly polarised RF signal, this observation induces a direction-dependent Rydberg steering vector, enabling maximum-likelihood DoA estimation. The pro posed procedure translates the Rydberg beat-vector front end into a highly sensitive RF field DoA sensor. Simulation results show that trace-level beat extraction supports the proposed DoA sensing workflow and provides a basis for comparison with a traditional vector antenna (VA) benchmark.

papers.title: FastEEP: Fast Intra-Instance Elastic Scaling for Expert-Parallel MoE Serving
papers.abstract: Large-scale expert parallelism (EP) has become the standard deployment configuration for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models in production. Meanwhile, the highly dynamic nature of LLM workloads requires providers to continuously adjust serving capacity to match fluctuating demand. Scaling MoE serving cannot be efficiently achieved by simply adding or removing serving instances; instead, it often requires resizing the EP group within an existing instance, which we refer to as intra-instance scaling.Existing inference engines primarily rely on instance-level scaling, which destroys and reconstructs entire serving instances, incurring substantial scaling overhead. We present FastEEP (Fast Elastic Expert Parallel), a fast intra-instance scaling system for MoE serving based on the principle of Partial Reuse. FastEEP reuses existing runtime state across worker execution, GPU memory, and communication by separating reusable execution structures from the resources activated by the current EP configuration. This separation enables coordinated resource reclamation and reconfiguration while preserving costly-to-reconstruct state, allowing fast EP scaling without full instance teardown and reconstruction. Our evaluation shows that FastEEP achieves 4.5x--11.7x faster scaling than the existing vLLM-based approach across different models, enabling efficient, fine-grained scaling of MoE serving.

papers.title: Giant Graviton Expansions from Symmetric Functions and Free Fermions
papers.abstract: Giant graviton expansions express finite-rank corrections to supersymmetric indices in terms of indices for wrapped D3-branes. We give detailed algebraic proofs of two previously proposed relations for four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ $U(N)$ super-Yang--Mills theory. The first is the Gaiotto--Lee single-sum expansion of the full superconformal index, proved by Hall--Littlewood orthogonality and an elementary calculation of operator traces. The second is the symmetric double-sum expansion of the flavored Schur index, proved by factorizing its exact free-fermion mode product. We specify the analytic continuation of the brane indices and justify the sums coefficient by coefficient. The two proofs apply to different expansion prescriptions and do not establish the full three-species expansion of Imamura. We discuss the additional physical and mathematical questions raised by that expansion and by the modular properties of the Schur index.

papers.title: The forward-loop-erased ants walk
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a new variant of the ants walk: a model of reinforced random walks for the phenomenon of a colony of ants being able to find the shortest path between their nest and a source of food. In this model, the nest and the source of food are two distinguished nodes in a finite graph. The ants perform successive random walks on this graph, started at the nest and stopped when they first hit the food source; the transition probabilities of each random walk depends on the trajectories of the previous ants, through some edge-weights that represent the amount pheromones deposited on each edge. In our new variant of the model, the ant (1) forgets loops made on the way to the food as soon as they are made, and (2) comes back to the nest following this loop-erased version of its forward trajectory, and deposits pheromone on the edges it crosses by doing so (i.e. adds one to these edges' weights). We say that the ants "find the shortest path" if, almost surely as the number of ants tends to infinity, the proportion of ants that travel along a graph-geodesic path from the nest to the food tends to one and the proportion of ants that travel along the remaining edges tends to zero. We are able to prove that this new variant of the model finds the shortest path when the graph distance between the nest and the source is at most 2. The strength of our result is that there is no other assumption on the shape of the graph. We prove this result using stochastic approximation theory, the electrical network method for random walks on weighted graphs, and the theory of weighted uniform spanning trees (WUSTs). In particular, the link with WUSTs is unique to the model studied in this paper due to the way the ant erases loops on the outward journey.

papers.title: HEPTABench: A framework for portable and controlled agentic evaluations in high energy physics
papers.abstract: Quantifying the capability and reliability of agentic systems in high-energy physics (HEP) requires repeated evaluations under controlled configurations. Establishing whether changes to models, tools, or harnesses improve performance also requires these components to be varied independently. We present the High Energy Physics Tool-and-Agent Benchmarking (HEPTABench) framework for portable and controlled evaluations of agentic systems, with separately configurable tasks, scaffolding, models, providers, harnesses, and domain capabilities. The framework combines HEP benchmark tasks and scientific rubrics with experiment execution and versioned tool interfaces. To support inspection, reproducibility, and post-hoc grading, the framework prioritizes recording and reporting complete experiment specifications, agent trajectories, and experiment artifacts. We demonstrate the framework in two benchmark campaigns. The first campaign evaluates a forward long-lived-particle reach calculation across four frontier coding-agent systems, comparing their built-in coding tools with the same tools supplemented by HEP domain tools. We show that including these HEP domain tools improves numerical accuracy and reduces trial-to-trial dispersion for every tested system. In a complementary campaign covering eight symbolic two-body decay tasks, we show that adding symbolic domain tools increases the fraction of successful trials for Claude Haiku 4.5 from $8\%$ to $79\%$, while GPT-5.5 succeeds in every trial with built-in tools alone. Through systematic evaluation of agentic systems, HEPTABench enables the identification of factors that improve the accuracy and reliability of their scientific work.

papers.title: EmoGenie: Benchmarking and Evaluating Expressed and Evoked Emotion in T2I Generation with MLLMs
papers.abstract: Rapid advances in artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) have significantly promoted using text-to-image (T2I) models to generate images with specific affective intentions. However, the emotional effects conveyed by generated images frequently deviate from target expectations, and it remains unclear whether multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can reliably interpret the emotion of AI-generated visual content. Existing affective benchmarks are predominantly built on natural images, while affective studies of generated images have largely focused on emotions expressed in portraits, lacking a unified benchmark for studying the emotions expressed and evoked by generated images. We therefore introduce EmoGenie, a benchmark of emotion for AI-generated images that evaluates capabilities in T2I generation and MLLM understanding across expressed and evoked emotions. It comprises 6,400 images generated by eight T2I models using 800 emotion-targeted prompts, annotated with question-answer (QA) pairs, termed EmoGenie-QA, and continuous human ratings, termed EmoGenie-Assess. EmoGenie-QA contains 90,000 closed-set questions in single-image and image-pair settings, as well as 1,057 open-ended questions for emotion description. EmoGenie-Assess benchmarks continuous affective and aesthetic prediction using 13,175 mean opinion scores (MOSs) aggregated from human ratings in terms of valence, arousal, dominance, and aesthetic quality. We further develop EmoProbe, which combines emotion question answering with response-aligned, dimension-specific regression heads for continuous score prediction. Experimental results show that EmoProbe achieves superior results on emotion-related QA tasks, while its affective and aesthetic predictions correlate better with human ratings, demonstrating its state-of-the-art capabilities of unified coarse-to-fine affective understanding for AI-generated images.

papers.title: Learning Perturbation-Specific Representations through Conditional Energy Prior for Cellular Response Prediction
papers.abstract: AI-based cellular perturbation prediction is essential to accelerate drug discovery and therapeutic identification. However, perturbation-specific signals are generally obscured by cellular complexity, making it difficult for existing methods to correctly capture perturbation effects. To address this problem, we propose PerturbEnergy, which introduces a conditional energy-based prior over perturbation representations. It assigns lower energy (higher probability) to representations compatible with the given perturbation and higher energy to others, thereby explicitly tilting the latent space toward perturbation-preferred regions. Besides, PerturbEnergy can be integrated into autoencoder architectures as we find its Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO) is equivalent to the ELBO of the complete autoencoder. We further prove that optimizing PerturbEnergy increases the lower bound on the conditional mutual information between representation and perturbation. Extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our PerturbEnergy: it improves perturbation recognition especially in latent space with improvement of up to 83.2\%; It also achieves state-of-the-art performance for predicting top-50/100/200 differentially expressed gene(DEG) response and remaining competitive on highly variable gene(HVG) prediction. The code is provided: https://github.com/BlueWhaleLab/PerturbEnergy

papers.title: Kairos: Transactional Security Enforcement at the System Boundary for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are becoming an integral part of the software development lifecycle, and the capabilities granted to them allow an agent to act with the user's authority on any resource it can access. The reach that gives an agent its utility is equally available to an attacker who can steer it. Anything an agent ingests can carry an injected instruction, and since the model does not reliably distinguish instructions from data, indirect prompt injection should be mitigated by mediating the effects the agent produces. Such mediation faces a structural difficulty. Legitimate work and the first step of an attack often look alike when an individual action is observed, and what separates them lies later in the trace, so a monitor limited to allow and deny is forced to decide before the evidence accumulates. We present Kairos, a reference monitor at the isolation boundary of an unmodified, opaque agent, where a tool call, a shell command, and a script the agent writes all cross the boundary as the same file and network operations, so that confinement holds regardless of the agent's behavior. A declarative policy that states which sources are trusted decides most effects deterministically and defers the rest, which are held while the agent continues speculatively. A decision oracle with bounded authority, such as a language model or a human, releases or refuses each deferred effect on the trace. Across three benchmarks and three agent models, Kairos outperforms existing defenses in the trade-off between attack success and utility. In particular, on AgentDojo, it reduces attack success from 47.0\% to 2.7\% while its benign utility stays at the level of the undefended agent.

papers.title: $\mathrm{S}^3$-PnP: Plug-and-Play Denoising for Scientific Imaging with Self-Supervised Score Priors
papers.abstract: Modern image restoration methods increasingly rely on large-scale supervised training, yet clean targets are often prohibitively difficult to obtain in scientific imaging modalities such as hyperspectral imaging (HSI) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Plug-and-play ADMM (PnP-ADMM) with pretrained diffusion priors offers a promising alternative, but the learned prior distribution can mismatch both the target scientific image distribution and the distribution of ADMM denoiser inputs induced by dual feedback. To mitigate these mismatches, we propose $\mathrm{S}^3$-PnP, a self-supervised plug-and-play restoration framework that learns a score prior directly from observation-derived ADMM intermediate states, without clean training targets or externally pretrained weights. Specifically, the learned score corrects the input to the analytical prior update, combining observation-driven corrections with analytical regularization. We further analyze the convergence and reconstruction error of the corrected ADMM algorithm assuming an ideal score and quadratic data fidelity. Experiments on reference-guided HSI restoration, single-image HSI denoising, and MRI denoising demonstrate consistent improvements over competing methods.

papers.title: Teacher-Guided Tool Learning for Small Language Models via Bidirectional KL Constraints
papers.abstract: External tools can extend the capabilities of small language models (SLMs), enabling their deployment in resource constrained environments. However, their limited capabilities make it difficult for SLMs to discover effective tool use behaviors through reinforcement learning alone, while direct teacher supervision suffers from teacher student behavioral distribution mismatch and may propagate erroneous preferences. To address these challenges, we propose Selective Teacher guided Policy Optimization (SeTPO), which coordinates student exploration with selective teacher guidance and persistent demonstration supervision. Specifically, SeTPO incorporates reverse KL derived token level teacher feedback into policy advantages on low reward trajectories, while auxiliary forward KL supervision preserves teacher demonstrated behaviors throughout training. Under an idealized bidirectional KL objective, we theoretically establish that the optimal policy achieves expected reward no lower than the teacher's while retaining a guaranteed fraction of the teacher's probability mass. Extensive experiments on BFCL v4 and API Bank demonstrate that SeTPO achieves superior overall performance over supervised fine tuning, reinforcement learning, and distillation baselines across all three student scales.

papers.title: Constraints on the cosmic reheating history from PTA data
papers.abstract: The cosmic reheating is an important epoch in the very early Universe, and has significant impacts on the primordial black hole (PBH) abundance and the scalar-induced gravitational wave (SIGW) spectrum. The relevant energy scale and the constituents of cosmic medium are encoded in the reheating frequency $f_{\mathrm{reh}}$ and the equation of state parameter $w$. In this work, we perform a full parameter space Bayesian inference, using the NANOGrav 15-yr dataset to constrain the thermal history of reheating. Treating $f_{\mathrm{reh}}$ and $w$ as free parameters, we systematically investigate the Dirac $δ$, narrow and broad log-normal primordial power spectra. Current pulsar timing array data can effectively constrain the peak frequency of the SIGW spectrum as $f_{\rm p}\sim 10^{-7.6}$--$10^{-7.0}$ Hz, along with $f_{\rm reh}\sim 10^{-9.0}$--$10^{-8.3}$ Hz and $w\sim 0.19$--$0.79$ (the $68\%$ confidence level), when the power spectrum has a relatively narrow width $Δ\lesssim 1$. A broader power spectrum introduces a smoothing effect that obscures the characteristic frequency knee in the SIGW spectrum, leading to the loss of information about cosmic reheating. Furthermore, for the Dirac $δ$ and narrow spectra, the PBH masses associated with the SIGWs are anchored at the planetary mass scale around $10^{-6}$--$10^{-4} M_{\odot}$. This establishes a consistent physical framework that naturally bridges the nanohertz gravitational wave background with the dark matter candidates implied by the Optical Gravitational Lensing Experiment microlensing events.

papers.title: MFVSR: A Multi-Style and Fine-Grained Benchmark for Video Subtitle Removal
papers.abstract: Video subtitle removal (VSR) is an important video restoration task, yet existing evaluation remains limited by low-resolution datasets, fragmented test sets, and generic video-inpainting protocols that fail to adequately capture localized restoration errors, unintended modifications, temporal instability, and incomplete outputs. In this paper, we introduce MFVSR, a large-scale multi-style benchmark for fine-grained and reliability-aware video subtitle removal evaluation. MFVSR distinguishes itself through three key features: (1) Large-scale and diverse data, comprising 3,000 paired videos from Real-HQ, Real-LQ, and AI-Generated sources, with an auxiliary set of 953 in-the-wild real videos for real-world coverage analysis; (2) Controlled subtitle diversity, spanning 16 languages and four factors covering spatial layout, temporal behavior, visual style, and language mode; (3) Fine-grained evaluation, introducing an information-conditioned, spatially decoupled protocol that separates blind from mask-guided removal and measures Restoration Fidelity, Preservation Fidelity, Temporal Fidelity, coverage, and failures. Experiments on six representative methods reveal substantial discrepancies between local restoration, outside-region preservation, temporal consistency, and full-set reliability that are obscured by conventional full-frame metrics. MFVSR therefore provides a more comprehensive and diagnostic foundation for evaluating and advancing video subtitle removal methods.

papers.title: Readout Scaling Shapes Sparse Feature Recovery
papers.abstract: Readout scaling changes what a sparse autoencoder (SAE) learns, but the benefit of removing it depends on the data. We use readout-canonicalized decision-space (RC-DS) coordinates to remove singular-value gains while preserving retained decision information. At a fixed readout condition number, changing the generating distribution reverses which training coordinates recover known factors best. In our controlled coordinate-matching study, recovery is highest when training restores the space in which the factors were generated. When factors are generated before readout scaling, RC-DS increases mean sparse-factor recovery from 0.506 to 0.913 at condition number 100, compared with centered-logit training under the same budget. An exact wrapper reproduces RC-DS training to numerical precision, isolating training geometry rather than additional information. In neural policies, RC-DS improves mean logit reconstruction under the tested budgets. On three fixed language-model checkpoints, RC-DS has higher mean gain-free reconstruction in all 18 tested task-sparsity settings, while centered-logit SAEs reconstruct output logits better in 17. Small-label-head controls show that longer training reduces the reconstruction gap from 0.0198 to 0.0016. Together, these results show how readout scaling, the data distribution, and training shape sparse learning. RC-DS provides an information-preserving method for studying and controlling the readout's contribution. Separate label-detection and steering tests distinguish these reconstruction effects from task-specific feature usefulness.

papers.title: Improved Sidorenko bound for hypergraph Turan densities
papers.abstract: For every fixed integer $r\ge3$, we prove that the Turán density of every $r$-uniform hypergraph $F$ with $m\ge1$ edges satisfies $π(F)\le1-c_rm^{-(r-1)/r}$, where $c_r>0$ depends only on $r$. This improves Sidorenko's general bound, whose gap from $1$ is of order $m^{-1}$. Complete $r$-uniform hypergraphs show that the exponent $(r-1)/r$ is optimal. The proof combines a potential argument for partial embeddings with the Lovász Local Lemma.

papers.title: The group generated by a graph's derangements
papers.abstract: We introduce the leap group of a graph, the subgroup of the symmetric group on the vertex set generated by graph derangements. We summarize historical results on graph derangements, which we call hops, and prove additional existence and complexity results. The leap groups of various canonical graphs are computed, and their behavior under basic graph operations is analyzed. We offer partial results on which groups can appear as leap groups, and study hops and leaps for infinite and directed graphs.

papers.title: Lie groups are countably representable
papers.abstract: We prove that every Lie group can be realized by permutations of a countable set, answering a classical question of Ulam. The key deformation construction originated in an argument produced by OpenAI's GPT 6 Astra during extended mathematical discussions.

papers.title: How Safe Is ChatGPT Health Advice? Evidence from Real User Conversations in Four Global South Countries
papers.abstract: People increasingly bring their health questions to ChatGPT, yet safety evaluations of LLM health advice rest almost entirely on clinician-authored vignettes, synthetic prompts, or simulated user profiles. The gap is widest for the Global South, where concerns about demographic bias and unsafe recommendations are well documented but have never been tested on real usage. We present, to our knowledge, the first demographically grounded safety evaluation of real-world health conversations with ChatGPT. From a consent-based data-donation corpus of 202,590 conversations from 1,252 users in India, Nigeria, Brazil, and Pakistan (December 2022 to February 2026), each linked to self-reported age and gender, we identify 15,555 health conversations, classify their health intent using an LLM classifier adapted from an established taxonomy, and score response safety under both a context-blind and a user-context-aware rubric. Roughly one in five health conversations receives a high-risk rating. Risk concentrates in symptom and condition queries and recurs through identifiable failure modes: unsafe medication or dosage guidance, harmful self-diagnosis, missing safety warnings, encouraging over-reliance on the model, and failure to refer users to professionals. Supplying the user's own accumulated context raises the high-risk share by 13-17 percentage points, and about one in four conversations rated safe in isolation turns out to be unsafe for the specific person asking. Safety evaluations built on synthetic cases are likely to miss these harms.

papers.title: Dynamic viscoelastic membranes
papers.abstract: We rigorously derive a dynamic membrane theory for nonlinear viscoelastic solids with Kelvin-Voigt rheology from the corresponding three-dimensional bulk theory, in the limit of vanishing thickness. The bulk model accounts for inertia, a nonsimple elastic energy depending on the second deformation gradient, and a frame-indifferent dissipation. Orientation preservation is ensured by the energy, while self-interpenetration of the limiting membrane is prevented by a uniform averaged invertibility condition. Our analysis relies on a hyperbolic minimizing movements scheme with two time-scales, which recasts the evolution into a hierarchy of incremental, sequential, and time-delayed problems. For fixed thickness, we prove the existence of solutions to the scheme and their convergence to a weak solution of the continuous-time problem as the time-scales vanish. We then identify the membrane limit at each level of the hierarchy, proving the $Γ$-convergence of the incremental functionals and the convergence of solutions to the sequential and time-delayed problems. Since the constant in the Korn inequality is not uniform in the thickness, these limits rely on estimates for the time derivative of the Cauchy-Green tensor rather than for the velocity gradient. Finally, as the outer time-scale vanishes, the membrane time-delayed solutions converge to a measure-valued solution of the membrane continuous-time problem.

papers.title: Ushering in sub-arcsecond angular resolution observatories in the far-infrared: The case for a double-Fourier interferometer
papers.abstract: A far-infrared (far-IR) interferometer from a space-based platform would bring about a transformational improvement in the spatial detail of astronomical observations that are inaccessible from ground-based observatories. This orders-of-magnitude improvement would significantly advance studies of newly formed and mature exoplanetary systems and their potential for supporting life, the earliest stages of star formation, and the evolution of galaxies up to the peak of the Universe's star formation activity and beyond. In this work, we discuss the potential for such an instrument and the science it enables in complement to current long-term plans of the global astronomical community and in preparation for the next generation of observatories. We also outline notable far-IR mission concepts, pathfinder instruments, and technology development platforms that have been studied and developed throughout the past few decades and briefly discuss key enabling technologies.

papers.title: A pedestrian's approach to Bayesian methods for inverse problems
papers.abstract: In the past two decades, the Bayesian approach to inverse problems in infinite dimensional spaces has seen significant developments in theory, Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods, and in applications. The Bayesian approach in finite dimension produces posterior distributions of finite dimensional random variables. In infinite dimensions, the desired objects are random fields and their laws as measures on Hilbert or Banach spaces. There are many textbooks and tutorials available that explain Bayesian methods and MCMC in finite dimensions. To enter the field of Bayesian inverse problems in infinite dimensions, a newcomer has to engage with a quite diverse and extensive literature. The purpose of this article is to provide a basic path to the subject that is easily accessible to a reader with general knowledge in probability and mathematical analysis. We start with a swift introduction to the finite dimensional case. The infinite dimensional case is introduced for Gaussian priors on Hilbert spaces and Gaussian-type likelihood functions. In this situation, mere continuity of the forward map suffices to prove that the posterior measure is well-defined. We also give some new and simple stability results. Two application examples are elaborated, one finite dimensional, one infinite dimensional.

papers.title: PhonoVoxtLM: Exploring Single-Codebook Phonological Tokens for Speech Understanding and Generation
papers.abstract: We investigate how speech token representations can support both understanding and generation within a unified speech language model. We present PhonoVoxtLM, built on the existing VoxtLM framework using phonological tokens designed to retain linguistic content and prosodic information. The existing tokenizer is jointly trained for speech recognition and resynthesis. Its single-codebook units serve as both speech inputs and generation targets, without additional speech-token prediction modules. Experiments show improvements over HuBERT-based baselines across understanding and generation under different training-data scales. Further comparisons with WavLM-based tokens reveal trade-offs between recognition and synthesis, highlighting the importance of evaluating shared representations across both capabilities. We further extend the framework to spoken question answering through fine-tuning with replay. The adapted model improves answering performance over similarly adapted HuBERT baselines while retaining advantages on the original speech tasks. Our findings support single-codebook representations designed for both content and prosody as a practical choice for unified multitask speech modeling.

papers.title: Continuous-wave 148.4-nm generation in strontium tetraborate for nuclear absorption spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Continuous-wave light near 148.4 nm enables direct absorption spectroscopy of the thorium-229 nuclear transition. We demonstrate single-pass frequency doubling in strontium tetraborate, delivering an estimated 8.1 nW at 920 mW pump power. At this power, oxygen admission leaves a background of 1.22 kHz, corresponding to an estimated signal-to-background ratio of 3.8 x 10^4 after current-integration calibration. Several crystals grown by top-seeded solution growth produce polarization-dependent VUV signals. Temperature scans reveal distinct maxima among specimens cut from one boule and among positions within a specimen. The source sustains operation over 33.3 h. In a separate 3-h record acquired with 1-ms gates, local referencing achieves near-Poisson averaging, reaching a fractional Allan deviation of 3.5 x 10^-5 at 1000 s. These results establish a practical VUV source for stable, long-duration spectroscopy of weak nuclear absorption.

papers.title: Graph Metanetworks for Transformer Based Language Models
papers.abstract: Weight-space learning treats the weights of neural networks as data, processed by other models called metanetworks. A key challenge is that different weights can realize the same function, related by a group of symmetries the metanetwork should respect. While symmetry-aware metanetworks for simple architectures such as MLPs are well developed, a comprehensive treatment of transformers, and in particular transformer-based language models, is still missing. Importantly, their weight space has a richer symmetry group: beyond neuron permutations, attention introduces continuous general-linear symmetries of the attention matrices and permutations of entire heads. Existing methods for transformer weights either capture only part of these symmetries or are restricted to a single, fixed architecture, and none accounts for language-model-specific components such as the token embeddings. Building on graph metanetworks, we propose a graph-based approach that is both symmetry-aware and applicable across depths and widths. We formalize a weight-space symmetry group of complete decoder-only language models and provide a graph construction that is invariant to it. We further introduce two new transformer-population datasets with novel tasks, such as training-corpus prediction and fine-tuning detection, on which our approach notably outperforms existing baselines.

papers.title: Simplifying and Improving On-Policy Distillation for Few-Step Diffusion
papers.abstract: Few-step distillation reduces the sampling cost of diffusion and flow models, but existing approaches often require auxiliary score models or specialized architectures. We show that simple on-policy velocity regression already provides a strong foundation for 4-NFE generation. To represent teacher velocity variation within each coarse transition, we introduce Pivot, a training-only residual proxy that separates local corrections from the student's interval-mean prediction. We further repel the student from weaker teacher predictions, providing a lightweight mechanism for avoiding undesirable modes. The resulting framework, Simplified Matching Distillation (SMD), remains entirely regression-based, requires neither online score estimation nor adversarial training, and leaves the deployed generator unchanged. We evaluate SMD on image generation and editing, 3D generation, video synthesis, and joint audio--video generation, scaling to 33 billion parameters. At 4-NFE, SMD outperforms strong few-step baselines and surpasses multi-step teachers on several benchmarks. It also supports cross-model, multi-teacher, and causal-video distillation.

papers.title: EDGE-INFERNO: The chemical signatures of assembly history in reionization fossils
papers.abstract: In galaxies, stellar populations represent a superposition of both in situ and accreted components, tracing internal chemical evolution as well as the histories of merged satellites. We investigate how assembly history shapes the chemical properties of present-day stellar populations in low-mass dwarf galaxies. We analyze a suite of EDGE-INFERNO star-by-star cosmological zoom-in simulations of galaxies with present-day halo mass $\sim1.4\times10^9\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$. We systematically vary galaxy growth while preserving the present-day halo mass, engineering our simulations to span a continuum of assembly histories. Early-forming systems form most of their stars in a single progenitor, with centrally concentrated star formation and a continuous enrichment history. In contrast, our late-forming systems assemble by accretion of multiple progenitors with their own stellar populations, resulting in fragmented star formation across several halos with independent chemical evolution tracks. These regimes produce qualitatively different chemical signatures: single-progenitor systems exhibit connected, well-defined trends in abundance space, while multi-progenitor systems show multiple, distinct stellar populations with limited overlap. We find that metallicity distribution functions provide initial constraints on assembly history for samples of at least $50$-$100$ member stars. Multi-element abundance analysis significantly improves the recovery of distinct components, although robust reconstruction still requires larger samples. Fully separating in situ and accreted populations likely requires kinematic information. Accreted stars can contribute substantially even at high metallicities in multi-progenitor systems, while external enrichment can cause accreted material to follow similar chemical trends as in situ stars, particularly in the single-progenitor regime.

papers.title: Unequal Coherent Ergotropy at Equal Interferometric Visibility and Energy in Quantum-Controlled Interferometers
papers.abstract: The ergotropy, or unitarily extractable work, of a quantum system naturally splits into incoherent and coherent contributions, respectively set by population inversion and coherences in the energy eigenbasis. We show that this split makes the coherent ergotropy of a Mach--Zehnder qubit sensitive to path predictability that the output interference fringes do not reveal. We send the path qubit, prepared as a thermal quantum battery, through two quantum-controlled interferometers built from the same elements, a fixed beam splitter and a beam splitter coherently controlled to be present or absent, differing only in the order in which these two act. The two arrangements share identical visibility, stored energy, and incoherent ergotropy at every point in the parameter space. Yet, for work extracted from the output battery alone, placing the controlled beam splitter first never yields less coherent ergotropy, and at fixed visibility and interferometric phase the difference is governed by the path predictability that this ordering creates. The same expression reappears as a purity deficit on the beam-splitter controller, so the work advantage comes with a Landauer bound on the cost of locally resetting the controller that is never larger at the same temperature. We further examine the effects of decoherence on the battery and consider a relativistic realization in which a Wigner rotation correlates the particle's spin with its path. Tracing out the spin decoheres the battery and allows the two arrangements to exhibit different coherent ergotropies even in regimes where their non-relativistic counterparts coincide. These results show that interference visibility is not a complete measure of the coherence available as work.

papers.title: Tidal Excitation of Relativistic Stars
papers.abstract: How a relativistic star responds to a time-dependent tide has lacked a first-principles counterpart of the Newtonian normal-mode expansion. In general relativity, the tidal field is gauge sensitive, radiative modes are non-Hermitian and incomplete, and the direct and late-time responses are intrinsically nonmodal. In this work we present, to our knowledge, the first causal relativistic theory that treats all of these components on equal footing. We first develop the spectral decomposition of the retarded Green function of the matched stellar interior--Schwarzschild exterior, which classifies four separate regimes in time domain: acausal region, prompt wave, surface-reflected wave, and mode+tail. The prompt signal is identical to that of a Schwarzschild black hole with the same mass, which is combined with the surface-reflected wave to be referred as the "direct part". With the Green function and a complex bilinear form on the full metric--fluid phase space, we decompose the linear response of a nonrotating perfect-fluid star into direct, quasinormal-mode, and late-time-tail sectors. Crucially, every sector admits an explicit first-order driven evolution equation: discrete bilinear projections determine the dynamically evolving quasinormal-mode amplitudes, while continuum projections of the same tidal source onto branch-cut states determine the direct and tail amplitudes. The result is a complete modal--nonmodal decomposition of the spacetime and fluid perturbations, which is physically described by the dynamics of a discrete and a continuous-frequency set of oscillators. We verify the decomposition numerically under generic time-dependent tidal driving and discuss applications to black hole perturbations.

papers.title: Broadband non-thermal emission predictions based on 3D simulations of supernova explosions within active galactic nuclei jets
papers.abstract: Thermonuclear and core-collapse supernovae are statistically expected to happen within extragalactic jets, as these jets cross the inner regions of their host galaxies, and supernova ejecta-jet interactions can potentially lead to strong non-thermal activity. We model the non-thermal emission from a supernova interacting with a jet on kiloparsec scales, using detailed numerical simulations of the interaction. Using a post-processing method, we applied a non-thermal model of the acceleration and transport of electron and their synchrotron and inverse Compton emissions, simplified and tuned for flexibility and computational speed, to the results of a three-dimensional relativistic hydrodynamics simulation of the ejecta of a supernova interacting with an extragalactic jet. For intermediate jet powers, radio, optical and X-ray fluxes from supernova ejecta-jet interactions may be detectable for distances < 100Mpc. The non-thermal luminosity budget and local conditions associated with these interactions could be enough to explain knots seen in kiloparsec scale jets at different energies. These conditions might also be suitable for the production of heavy ultra high-energy cosmic rays, but photon and neutrino generation from hadronic processes would be minor on kiloparsec scales. The leptonic gamma-ray fluxes are modest but might non-negligibly contribute in TeV for the nearest or more powerful jet sources.

papers.title: Experimental Realization of a C-Shunt Flux-Qubit Coupler for Controlled-Z Gates between Transmons
papers.abstract: Fast entangling gates and low-interaction idling require distinct operating conditions in superconducting quantum processors. We experimentally realize a transmon-C-shunt-transmon (TCT) device in which a flux-tunable, three-junction capacitively shunted flux-qubit coupler connects two transmon data qubits. The C-shunt coupler provides a flux-tunable, positively anharmonic spectrum for tailoring the interactions between the data qubits. Conditional Ramsey and swap measurements identify an idle region with near-zero residual ZZ interaction strength and suppressed transverse exchange. At this bias, simultaneous single-qubit interleaved randomized benchmarking yields X-gate fldelities above 99.7%, consistent with individual operation. A 45 ns nonadiabatic controlled-Z (CZ) gate achieves an interleaved randomized benchmarking fldelity estimate of 99.23(15)%. Numerical simulations identify coupler energy relaxation as an important limitation on CZ-gate fldelity and indicate that extending the coupler lifetime can improve gate performance. These results demonstrate the experimental feasibility of C-shunt flux-qubit couplers for combining low-interaction idling with fast entangling operations between transmon qubits.

papers.title: MemoryVLN: From Ego-Aware Memory Representation to Cross-Context Memory Reuse in Vision-Language Navigation
papers.abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) have shown strong potential for embodied vision-language navigation (VLN), yet their performance degrades on long-horizon trajectories due to context-length limits, redundant historical observations, and unstable spatial alignment across time. These issues make it difficult to both compress long navigation histories and reliably reuse past spatial experience. To address these limitations, we propose \textbf{MemoryVLN}, a unified memory-driven navigation system built around memory construction and management. During memory construction, \emph{Long Sequence Compression} employs forgetting-curve-inspired temporal sampling to preserve dense recent evidence and sparse yet representative distant observations under a limited token budget. \emph{Ego-Aware Memory Representation} further integrates 2D semantic tokens, 3D geometric tokens, and 6D agent poses, allowing each memory to encode both what was observed and where it was observed. During memory management, \emph{Hierarchical Memory Bank} maintains in-episode and context-level memories through cross-context warm-start and confidence-controlled write-back. \emph{Memory Enhancement} then retrieves the Top-$K$ relevant memories according to the current navigation state and fuses them with the current visual tokens. Together, these mechanisms transform raw navigation history into compact, spatially grounded, selectively retrievable, and reusable navigation experience. Extensive experiments on R2R-CE and RxR-CE demonstrate consistent improvements over the state-of-the-art baselines by a substantial margin (i.e., 2\% and 6.5\% in successful rate).

papers.title: RTISSLAM: In-air Imaging Sonar SLAM using a Robust Pose Graph and Occupancy Grid Mapping
papers.abstract: Sonar was one of the first sensors with which mobile robots built maps, and in-air sonar keeps working where cameras and lidar fail, in darkness, smoke, dust and next to glass. Classical sonar SLAM, however, relied on geometric features or occupancy grids built from sparse range readings, and both struggle with the specular reflections that dominate indoor sonar. In this letter, we introduce RTISSLAM, a novel sonar-only SLAM system for an embedded 3D imaging sonar, which combines the robust pose graph of BatSLAM 2.0 as back-end with an occupancy grid as map. Energyscapes from delay-multiply-and-sum beamforming with a range-wise CFAR serve as place descriptors for sequence-verified loop closures, acoustic odometry calibrates the wheel odometry online, recognized revisits are registered metrically, and the grid is stored per keyframe and anchored to the pose-graph nodes, so that it follows every loop closure. In simulated worlds with specular walls, RTISSLAM reduces the trajectory error of the wheel odometry from \SI{8.2}{\meter} to \SI{0.31}{\meter} in an office, while lidar-style grid SLAM on the same sonar data fails.

papers.title: When do lazy and invertible cellular automata generate all cellular automata?
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a group and let $A$ be a set with at least two elements. A lazy cellular automaton over $A^G$ acts as the identity except at the cells where a fixed pattern occurs, where it replaces the central symbol by a fixed different symbol. Let $M(G;A)$ be the submonoid of $\mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ generated by the lazy and the invertible cellular automata. We study when $M(G;A) = \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$. Since no lazy cellular automaton is surjective, every surjective element of $M(G;A)$ is invertible; hence $M(G;A) \neq \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ whenever $A$ is infinite or $G$ has an element of infinite order. More unexpectedly, if $|A| = 2$ and $G$ has a quotient isomorphic to the Klein four-group $C_2 \times C_2$, then $M(G;A) \neq \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$. For locally finite groups, these are the only obstructions: we prove that $M(G;A) = \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ if and only if $3 \leq |A| < \infty$, or $|A| = 2$ and $G$ has no quotient isomorphic to $C_2 \times C_2$.

papers.title: ProTok: Unified Protein Tokenization via Modular Multi-Codebook Quantization
papers.abstract: Protein sequence, structure, and functional annotations each capture complementary aspects of protein biology, yet existing tokenizers encode each modality independently, limiting the expressiveness of discrete protein representations. We present ProTok, a unified protein tokenizer that maps all three modalities into a modular discrete vocabulary via product quantization with per-modality codebook groups and modality dropout. A single ProTok checkpoint supports flexible inference from any modality subset without retraining.
