papers.title: Rethinking electrified transportation: The case for dynamic wireless charging
papers.abstract: Long-term infrastructure investment often requires choosing between an established technology and a capital-intensive alternative that gains value as demand matures. For electric vehicle (EV) charging, this trade-off is between incumbent stationary charging technology and emerging dynamic wireless charging (DWC). DWC could fundamentally alter transportation electrification by enabling high-throughput charging in motion and reducing reliance on large onboard batteries; however, its high upfront cost makes the timing and location of deployment critical. Overcommitting to stationary charging stations (SCS) risks technological lock-in and forgoing the benefits of DWC, whereas premature DWC deployment can strand capital in underutilized corridors. Through a joint investment assessment framework coupling DWC, SCS, and supporting grid infrastructure across nearly 49,000 miles of the US Interstate freight network, we find that higher utilization and longer project lifetimes rapidly shift investment toward DWC, whose share rises sharply from 48% at a project lifetime of 30 years to 100% at 32 years. Contiguous DWC segments can share grid connections, enabling them to provide over six times the rated charging capacity of SCS while requiring 46% less investment in new distribution-grid infrastructure. We also find that a combined DWC and SCS portfolio reaches a maximum lifetime value of USD 60 billion, 63% above the case with only SCS. We further identify specific traffic demand, construction, and grid access conditions that shape where each technology becomes advantageous, yielding actionable thresholds for SCS and DWC deployment that directly inform long-term EV charging infrastructure investment and policy.

papers.title: Structured coordinate systems in $L^p(\mathbb{R})$
papers.abstract: We construct Schauder bases of $L^p(\mathbb{R})$ with significant structural constraints on their elements. First, we construct non-negative Schauder bases of $L^p(\mathbb{R})$ for every $1 \leq p < \infty$. Although such bases cannot be unconditional, their basis constants can be made arbitrarily close to one. By duality, we also obtain bases with positive biorthogonal functionals and the same bounds for all $1\leq p<\infty$. Finally, we prove that $L^p(\mathbb{R})$ admits a Schauder basis consisting of translates of a single function for every $2\le p<\infty$. The generating function $f$ can be chosen to be the restriction to $\mathbb{R}$ of an entire function. For $p>2$, the translation parameters can be chosen from any prescribed unbounded subset of $\mathbb{R}$, a conclusion that fails for $p=2$.

papers.title: Evidence for Distinct One-Off and Repeating Subpopulations in CHIME/FRB Catalog 2
papers.abstract: The Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME) has published its second catalog of 3,641 fast radio bursts (FRBs). While this sample includes 981 bursts from 83 repeating sources, only 2.3% of CHIME FRBs are observed to repeat. This raises the question of whether the FRB population truly consists of a single repeating population or includes a distinct subpopulation of one-off sources. We apply Simulation Based Inference (SBI), a likelihood-free machine learning framework, to model the CHIME/FRB Catalog 2 dataset, testing eight FRB population models, half of which include a subpopulation of truly one-off sources. The current catalog strongly and decisively favors models including such a subpopulation, with the best-fitting model combining a log-normal burst rate distribution, a Poissonian wait-time distribution, and a one-off subpopulation. This preference is corroborated by an independent random forest classifier and by the ability of one-off models to naturally reproduce the hyperactive repeating sources present in the catalog without having been trained on them. We place upper limits on the potentially observable CHIME/FRB population of 36,000 repeating sources and 19 one-off sources per day in the CHIME sky. Models with a one-off subpopulation naturally account for the hyperactive repeating sources present in the catalog without having been trained on them, providing an independent consistency check on our results. We predict the repeater percentage will fall below 2% in the next five years, eventually declining to ~0.5% as the sample saturates with one-off detections.

papers.title: Steertuning Policies from a Few Human Videos
papers.abstract: Current recipes for robot learning require massive amounts of robot demonstrations to obtain robust and adaptive policies. In this work, we introduce Steertuning, a system that enables robots to learn new tasks in new environments from 5 human demonstrations in under 5 Steertuning consists of two parts. (1) We pretrain a 400M-parameter diffusion policy on our egocentric human dataset, which consists of 100 hours of densely annotated random interactions. This pretraining makes Steertuning robust to background differences and enables spatial and object generalization when deployed on new tasks. (2) Given 5 demonstrations of a new task, we finetune our model for only 2 minutes (2000 training updates) and steer the policy's actions during reverse sampling using the demonstration whose observation is closest to that of the deployment environment. Together with a carefully designed data processing pipeline for embodiment transfer, this enables Steertuning to achieve a 71% success rate across 12 tasks in 12 new environments, ranging from lab settings to kitchens in new homes. The entire process, from data collection for a new task to robot policy deployment, takes less than 5 minutes. Our full dataset, model weights, codebase, and robot videos will be made available at our website: https://steertuning.github.io.

papers.title: PULSUS: Direct Frequency-Domain Multidimensional Spectroscopy Beyond the Impulsive Rotating-Wave Approximation
papers.abstract: We introduce PULSUS, a direct frequency-domain framework for multidimensional spectroscopy of open quantum systems beyond the impulsive rotating-wave approximation. Coherence-frequency intervals are represented through Liouvillian resolvents, while finite Gaussian pulses are incorporated through operator-valued functions of the field-free Liouvillian. This enables direct evaluation on Cartesian grids or arbitrary spectral coordinates while retaining molecular evolution during the pulse envelopes and, when required, the complete light--matter interaction. The implementation is validated against analytical and independent time-domain benchmarks and supports targeted spectral sampling that reduces the number of evaluated coordinates when the response is spectrally localized. A controlled hierarchy of finite-pulse, rotating-wave, short-pulse, and impulsive models separates the errors introduced by each approximation. For a coupled electronic dimer, the total impulsive-RWA error is nonmonotonic in pulse duration: an intermediate regime provides the highest accuracy, whereas ultrashort pulses expose coupling-enabled beyond-RWA pathways and longer pulses develop substantial finite-pulse corrections. These results show that the impulsive and rotating-wave approximations cannot be assumed to improve simultaneously and should be tested when quantitatively interpreting multidimensional spectra. PULSUS provides a direct frequency-domain framework for carrying out that comparison.

papers.title: A proof of the rational exponents conjecture
papers.abstract: The rational exponents conjecture of Erdős and Simonovits asserts that for every rational $r\in [1,2]$ there exists a graph $H$ such that $\mathrm{ex}(n,H)=Θ(n^r)$. We present a proof of this conjecture claimed by Epoch AI, explaining how it builds upon ideas and methods developed by many researchers.

papers.title: On Collusion-Free Teaching in Planar Graphs
papers.abstract: Non-clashing teaching minimizes teaching complexity among models satisfying the Goldman--Mathias collusion-avoidance criterion. While the Vapnik--Chervonenkis dimension (VCdim) measures the complexity of learning from samples, non-clashing teaching dimension (NCTD) measures the number of examples required when a teacher can select them. Whether NCTD is always bounded above by VCdim remains a fundamental open question in learning theory. In this paper, we investigate this question for the concept classes of closed neighborhoods in planar graphs. We prove a tight upper bound of two on their NCTD, thereby establishing the conjectured inequality for this family. For the positive variant NCTD+, in which teaching sets contain only positive examples, we obtain a tight upper bound of four. Finally, we show that deciding whether either NCTD+ or NCTD is at most one is NP-complete, even for concept classes of closed neighborhoods in planar graphs. In particular, despite the upper bound of two on NCTD for such classes, distinguishing between NCTD values of one and two remains NP-hard.

papers.title: Carrollian Yang-Mills theories in the homogeneous temporal gauge
papers.abstract: We quantize, in the homogeneous temporal gauge, both the electric and the magnetic Carrollian Yang-Mills theories with SU(N) gauge symmetry in the fundamental representation. We use the BRST method implemented in the path integral. We show that in the first case all the interaction vertices vanish, thus, giving a free theory. In the magnetic case, there are no loop contributions to the Green functions of the elementary fields --i.e., Green functions not involving composite operators-- and the only connected parts of such Green functions with a dependence on the coupling constant are the tree level contributions to the three and four point functions of the field $ξ_i$. We also show that in the magnetic case the Green functions involving only Wilson loops are trivial and not so in the electric case.

papers.title: Imaginary HTEE: Probing Criticality and Coherence
papers.abstract: We study the imaginary part of the holographic timelike entanglement entropy (HTEE) in a charged asymptotically AdS$_5$ black-hole background whose dual field theory exhibits a critical point in the presence of a chemical potential $μ$ and temperature $T$. Identifying the imaginary part of the HTEE with the imaginary part of the pseudoentropy, we derive an analytical expression for this quantity and investigate its behavior on the stable and unstable thermodynamic branches. We find that the imaginary HTEE vanishes in the uncharged limit and is induced entirely by a nonzero chemical potential, signaling the emergence of quantum coherence between the initial and final states. As the dimensionless ratio $μ/T$ approaches its critical value, we obtain an inverse-square-root divergence in the derivative of the imaginary HTEE and extract the critical exponent $θ_I = 1/2$ analytically. We further show that the same exponent governs the temperature response at fixed chemical potential. Our results establish the imaginary part of the HTEE as a non-local quantum-information probe of criticality in strongly coupled systems, and they imply that the initial and final states become maximally coherent at the critical point.

papers.title: Sampling with collective variables: Relative error analysis for umbrella sampling under general conditions
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of estimating the expectation of a function (observable) with respect to a high-dimensional probability distribution, under the assumption that a low-dimensional collective variable map captures all the directions of slow mixing for the distribution. More precisely, under the assumption that the fibers of the collective variable map satisfy a log-Sobolev inequality, we establish non-asymptotic relative-error guarantees for this problem using the eigenvector method for umbrella sampling (EMUS). Our analysis applies to both log-Lipschitz observables and indicator of convex sets, and gives complexity bounds that are polynomial in regularity parameters and inverse relative accuracy, and exponential in the dimension of the collective variable space. As a relative error guarantee, our bounds apply to rare event estimation. We consider Gaussian biasing windows defined on a low-dimensional collective variable space and analyze a modified sparse matrix version of EMUS. The bounds quantify the effect of the map through mixing of the conditional distribution and fluctuation of the observable along the fibers.

papers.title: The Becker-Gottlieb transfer is not functorial: An example using $C_\infty$-algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that the Becker-Gottlieb transfer is not functorial, even on rational cohomology. More precisely, for any even $n \ge 4$, we construct a fibration $f \colon X \to S^{n+1}$ with fiber $S^2 \vee S^n$, and an oriented $S^1$-bundle $g \colon Y \to X$ such that the transfer of $f \circ g$ is non-trivial on rational cohomology. Since the transfer of an oriented $S^1$-bundle vanishes, this implies that the transfer of $f \circ g$ and the composite of the transfers of $f$ and $g$ induce different maps on rational cohomology and are thus not homotopic. The proof that the transfer of $f \circ g$ is non-trivial uses the rational models for the Becker--Gottlieb and THH transfers obtained in previous work of the authors. In the appendix, we provide a second, more involved, proof that relies on constructing explicit $C_\infty$-algebra models for odd spherical fibrations (including circle bundles), which might be of independent interest. Concurrently, another counterexample (of very different flavor) was found by Georg Lehner, Cary Malkiewich, and the first author.

papers.title: Exploring Minimal Blocking Sets for Kernelization Lower Bounds for $\mathcal{F}$-Minor Deletion
papers.abstract: For Vertex Cover, a minimal blocking set of a graph $G$ is an inclusion-wise minimal vertex set contained in no minimum vertex cover of $G$. Bougeret et al. [SIDMA 2022] showed that, for all minor-closed graph classes $\mathcal{G}$, Vertex Cover has a polynomial kernel parameterized by the distance to $\mathcal{G}$ if and only if $\mathcal{G}$ has bounded minimal blocking sets. In this work, we explore how far this connection between minimal blocking sets and kernelization extends to $\mathcal{F}$-Minor Deletion parameterized by the deletion distance to $\mathcal{G}$. A minimal $\mathcal{F}$-blocking set of $G$ is a minimal vertex set not contained in any optimal $\mathcal{F}$-Minor Deletion solution of $G$. For connected families $\mathcal{F}$, we show that if some graph class $\mathcal{G}$ closed under disjoint union has unbounded minimal $\mathcal{F}$-blocking sets, then $\mathcal{F}$-Minor Deletion parameterized by the deletion distance to $\mathcal{G}$ has no polynomial kernel. This generalizes a result of Hols et al. [SIDMA 2022] for Vertex Cover. We then show that this criterion does not capture all kernelization lower bounds for $\mathcal{F}$-Minor Deletion, even for minor-closed graph classes. Motivated by the work of Dekker and Jansen [Discrete Appl. Math. 2024], we study the more general notion of extended $\mathcal{F}$-blocking sets and the kernelization lower bounds they yield. For every fixed integer $η\geq 1$, Pw-$η$ Deletion is the problem of deleting at most $k$ vertices to reduce the pathwidth to at most $η$. We show that it has no polynomial kernel parameterized by the distance to graphs with pathwidth at most $η+1$. Moreover, for connected families $\mathcal{F}$, we show that $\mathcal{F}$-Minor Deletion parameterized by the distance to graphs with pathwidth at most $\max_{F\in\mathcal{F}} pw(F)+1$ has no polynomial kernel.

papers.title: The Becker--Gottlieb transfer is not functorial: An example based on units of group rings
papers.abstract: We show by explicit counterexample that the Becker--Gottlieb transfer cannot be made functorial. A different counterexample using rational homotopy theory was discovered concurrently by the third author and Robin Stoll.

papers.title: Dynamic Attack Surfaces: A Queue of Branching Processes
papers.abstract: Modern attack surfaces are inherently dynamic. Vulnerabilities emerge over time and they remain exposed to exploit until defenders discover and patch them. Artificial intelligence (AI) amplifies these dynamics by accelerating both offensive and defensive processes, making modern cybersecurity increasingly a competition among interacting time scales and resources. We capture this competition using a queue of branching processes that couples vulnerability discovery and resource-constrained patching with the evolving attacker population targeting each vulnerability. Our primary risk metric is the cumulative number of exploits a vulnerability experiences before it is patched. We derive the expected cumulative number of exploits under birth-death-immigration (BDI) and rise-decay (RD) models of attacker activity. Under a BDI model of attacker activity, we identify a phase transition: the expected cumulative number of exploits is finite only when attacker growth remains below both the vulnerability discovery rate and the effective patching rate. Across both attacker models, increasing the exploit rate does not necessarily increase the expected number of exploits because faster attacker departure can sufficiently limit the active attacker population. Finally, we show that equal proportional AI amplification of offensive and defensive capabilities need not preserve security: accelerating both sides can shift the defensive bottleneck and move the system into an unbounded-risk regime.

papers.title: Superexchange coupling between a dilute Gd3+ probe and orphan spins in a valence-bond glass
papers.abstract: The valence-bond-glass state of the 4d^1 double perovskite Ba2YMoO6 combines Mo^5+ singlets with residual paramagnetic "orphan" spins whose coupling is hard to reach with bulk probes. We probe them by electron paramagnetic resonance of a dilute Gd^3+ ion on the Y^3+ site via broadband coplanar-waveguide transmission at 5 K. The isostructural nonmagnetic niobate Ba2YNbO6, doped with the same Gd^3+ probe, is a fixed-lattice control. The Gd^3+ linewidth nearly doubles in the magnetic host. Dipolar coupling to the sparse orphans is nearly an order of magnitude too weak; the excess is instead reproduced by a transferred f-d superexchange of J ~ 0.2 K, so the width is a static measure of orphan-spin coupling. The half-field (Delta m_S = +/-2) satellite collapses in the magnetic host, a dynamical dephasing channel, while the unchanged g-factor marks a zero-mean random internal field. Together the two channels probe the coupling and dynamics of valence-bond-glass orphan spins.

papers.title: Optimal Support Size Testing
papers.abstract: We present an optimal tester for support size that determines whether an unknown probability distribution is supported on $n$ elements or $\varepsilon$-far away (in total variation distance) with sample complexity $Θ(\frac{n}{\varepsilon\log(n)})$, improving the prior best $O(\frac{n}{\varepsilon\log(n)} \log(\min\{\frac{1}{\varepsilon}, n\}))$ due to Ferreira Pinto Jr. and Harms (STOC 2025). As a generalization, we provide a pretty good lower bound on support size.

papers.title: AIRRI: Towards a Human-Readable, Machine-Resistant Reading Interface
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of image-to-text extraction systems and large language models (LLMs) poses new challenges for educational assessment by making assignment materials easy to transcribe and solve with minimal human effort. To address this problem, we present AIRRI (Artificial Intelligence Resilient Reading Interface), a framework for generating machine-resistant educational content, a dataset of higher-education assignments for evaluation, and an initial evaluation of the human readability of AIRRI machine-resistant text designs. AIRRI employs two categories of machine-resistance techniques. First, AIRRI applies image transformations including character spacing, word spacing, line spacing, character opacity variation, stripe overlays, and image noise. Second, AIRRI applies decision-based adversarial attacks: RayS, SurFree, and ADBA. We evaluate AIRRI against three image-to-text systems: Tesseract, EasyOCR, and the transformer-based GOT-OCR2 model. Our results show that AIRRI substantially degrades automated text extraction performance. AIRRI increased character error rates for EasyOCR (6.9% to 55.9%), Tesseract (2.3% to 100.0%), and GOT-OCR2 (30.7% to 48.1%). Word error rates increased for EasyOCR (24.9% to 96.7%) and Tesseract (10.7% to 100.0%). Among the evaluated decision-based attacks, ADBA consistently produced the largest degradation in image-to-text performance, while RayS and SurFree produced more moderate reductions. EasyOCR and Tesseract were generally more susceptible to both image-based and adversarial perturbations than the transformer-based GOT-OCR2 model. Our findings suggest that AIRRI can significantly reduce the reliability of image-to-text-to-LLM workflows, increasing the effort required for AI-assisted assignment completion.

papers.title: Learning Source Structure: Bayesian Prediction with Transformers
papers.abstract: A transformer trained on sequences whose source parameters are drawn afresh each time can learn only what the sequences share: the source family and its prior. The Bayesian predictor that knows both, which we call informed Bayes, is the unique minimizer of the training loss and is computable from the family alone; we use it as a quantitative, falsifiable reference. Where earlier work compared transformers with Bayes on sources whose contexts can be learned independently, we build Markov sources with up to 64 symbols in which observations in one context inform prediction in another: product sources with known or hidden encodings, transition rows sharing an unknown base law and depth, and a mixture of three families. Our main result is that informed Bayes predicts, from the family and prior alone, how a trained transformer behaves in four tests that go beyond the learning curve: the loss that remains under a source outside the training family (predicted 2.237 bits, measured 2.309), the doubling of the extra loss when two independent components change rather than one (0.345 predicted, 0.350 measured), the benefit of other contexts when a token appears for the first time, and the depth at which copying an earlier continuation starts to pay. On the learning curves themselves, small transformers match informed Bayes when the shared structure is visible in the tokens, and hidden structure needs more layers and training, with gaps below 0.01 bits per token for the largest models. We explain why the imitation is possible and where it must fail: informed Bayes decomposes into sufficient statistics that attention selects and accumulates and an estimator, fixed by the prior, that the feed-forward network learns; training pays the complexity of informed Bayes under the architecture's prior, and finite-memory universal prediction bounds how closely a bounded network can reach it.

papers.title: Code-Switching Detection via Language-Selective Dimensions in Speech Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Code-switching (CS), the alternation between languages within an utterance, is common in multilingual speech but underrepresented in pretraining corpora. Increasing CS coverage requires finding relevant utterances in large speech collections so that they can be included in training data. One way to find such utterances is to transcribe the speech and detect language alternation in the text, but this depends on obtaining accurate multilingual transcriptions. We propose a lightweight method that detects CS directly from speech. It uses frame-level language information in pretrained speech encoders to determine whether both languages are present within an utterance. Specifically, we identify language-selective hidden-state dimensions using monolingual recordings and aggregate their frame-level activations into a CS prediction. With a small CS set used to tune a decision rule, we show that the Whisper-small encoder achieves a mean F1 of $0.798$ across 14 language pairs in CS-FLEURS, compared with $0.776$ for a CNN and $0.751$ for a HuBERT linear baseline trained for monolingual language identification. Our findings suggest that pretrained speech encoders already encode the information needed to identify CS utterances, and they provide a lightweight tool for building more representative multilingual corpora.

papers.title: On the Monitorability of Natural Language Autoencoders: Identification vs Discrimination
papers.abstract: Natural Language Autoencoders (NLAs) are proposed as oversight tools for language models: an Activation Verbaliser (AV) writes an English explanation of an activation vector, and an Activation Reconstructor (AR) maps the explanation back to a vector. Their value for oversight depends on a human monitor being able to tell a true account of an activation from a false one, given the AV's explanation. We formalise NLA training and NLA oversight deployment as two different referential games from Emergent Communication: training is a generative referential game, while oversight is a discriminative, multi-modal, partially-observable referential game played over a many-to-many relation between the monitored language model's activations and the accounts that are true of them. The gap between the two games predicts that AV's explanations will identify which activation they describe without discriminating its true account from closely matched false ones, since training never asks explanations to rule anything out. Using the NLA's own AR as a maximally-sympathetic surrogate monitor model, we experimentally confirm this theoretical insight on one released checkpoint: true accounts beat accounts of other activations in all 320 comparisons, but beat fluent rivals differing in a single claim only 60.2% of the time (standard error 6.7%, chance at 50%, $n = 35$). A meaning-preserving rewrite by an uninvolved model costs only 2.1% of the distance to another activation's account, so the failure is not due to the NLA pair having developed private conventions in the AV's explanations. Our rival accounts test only transcript-level truths, which the monitored language model's conversation settles, so these results bound the easiest case and leave claims about the monitored model's own processing untested. We state conjectures that would make both results consequences of the framework.

papers.title: Direct correlation of intravoxel incoherent motion imaging based on implicit neural representations and histopathology in pediatric Wilms tumors: can it differentiate between subtypes?
papers.abstract: Wilms tumor (WT) is a heterogeneous pediatric renal malignancy. Invasive procedures to establish histology prior to pre operative treatment are not recommended by the International Society of Pediatric (SIOP) Oncology Renal Tumor Study Group, yet different tissue components are associated with different responses to therapy (SIOP Umbrella protocol). Intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) may improve subtype differentiation before surgery as a noninvasive radiographic biomarker by capturing both diffusion and perfusion characteristics, as opposed to the conventionally used apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC). The objective of this study is to evaluate the discriminative performance of IVIM MRI in differentiating WT subtypes. IVIM provides quantitative parameters that disentangle the diffusion coefficient (D), incoherent blood flow (pseudodiffusion Dstar) and perfusion fraction (f). This retrospective study included thirthy children with WT. Standardized 1.5T MRI with 10 b value diffusion weighted imaging (DWI) was performed. IVIM parameters were estimated using a selfsupervised implicit neural representations network and were correlated with histopathology via a patient specific 3D printed cutting guide. Statistical analyses included mixed models, receiver operating curve analysis, and logistic regression. Thirty lesions were MRI histopathology correlated on slice level. Significant subtype differences were observed for Dstar stromal versus epithelial (p = 0.024), regressive tumors (p = 0.031) and mixed WT tumors (p = 0.043). ADC showed no significant subtype differences. Direct MRI histopathology correlation enabled differentiation between stromal subtype and epithelial, mixed and regressive subtype on macroscopic slice level using Dstar.
authors: A. F. W. van der Steeg

papers.title: Segment Where You Look: Attention as the Interface Between Language Models and Segmenters
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) that segment from language must pass the location of the referent to a pixel decoder. The dominant interface compresses it into the hidden state of a single [SEG] token, a d-dimensional vector with no spatial index, and leaves the decoder, which never sees the expression, to recover the referent's extent. We show that the VLM already computes a better signal: the [SEG] token's attention over the image tokens, which is defined on the patch grid by construction. Probing a frozen segmentation VLM, we find that this attention yields 18 to 22 more gIoU than the [SEG] hidden state when read by the same probe, that it gains nothing from the image where the hidden state does, and that it is concentrated in the late layers. Building on these findings, we introduce AttnSeg, which replaces the [SEG] embedding with this attention as the decoder's prompt. A learned, signed combination of the attention heads forms a dense spatial prompt, and an attention-guidance objective supervises it directly. A two-stage recipe first trains the VLM to localize without the decoder, then trains the decoder to refine, within the budget of standard fine-tuning. Applied to Sa2VA, AttnSeg improves ReasonSeg by 6.4 gIoU and GS-Eval by 10.2 at 4B (4.2 and 9.6 over the same model fine-tuned on the same data), and by 8.8 and 11.3 at 14B. The gains reach 13 to 18 gIoU on object parts, multiple objects, and single objects, where the referent must be singled out, and are negligible on stuff regions, which the decoder already recovers unaided. Code and models are available at https://eslambakr.github.io/attseg_project_page/

papers.title: Learning When to Transfer: Reinforcement Learning for Carbon-Footprint Modeling in New Manufacturing Domains
papers.abstract: Manufacturers often need to characterize a new material, process, or product before enough operating data are available to train reliable predictive models for this new, target domain. Existing manufacturing operations contain potentially useful knowledge to accelerate this characterization, but indiscriminate reuse of data from existing source domains can cause negative transfer in learning of the new, target domain when the manufacturing domains differ sufficiently. This work proposes a reinforcement-learning method for selective knowledge transfer, where its reward scores each opportunity to transfer against supervised alternatives, so negative transfer is avoided and controlled during forward prediction instead of being diagnosed afterwards. Given limited data from a new target domain, the learned policy chooses among predictors based on individual source operations, subsets of the sources, or the supervised alternatives: fully pooled sources, or target data alone. A validation gate deploys the transferred prediction only when it improves upon the supervised alternatives. The method is designed for learning variables supporting carbon accounting, as well as performance and quality outcomes. We demonstrate the approach by quantifying the embodied greenhouse-gas emissions of parts produced via material-extrusion additive manufacturing, using data from 729 experiments spanning five materials: ABS, PETG, TPU, PLA, and recycled PLA. The response combines measured fabrication electricity with polymer-specific cradle-to-gate production factors, while 22 material, process, and toolpath features characterize each experiment. In leave-one-material-out evaluation, this method achieves a mean test RMSE of 5.2 g CO2e per part, 20.00% lower than target-only training (32.5% lower when only 5-10% of the target training data are available) and 10.30% lower than indiscriminate source-target pooling.

papers.title: Finite-energy two-way assisted capacities: Exact formulas for multimode loss and fading
papers.abstract: We study quantum communication, entanglement distribution, and secret-key generation through multimode bosonic loss and fading channels, assisted by local quantum operations and two-way classical communication. Using sector teleportation, we determine the exact two-way quantum and secret-key capacities of multimode pure-loss channels under a mean photon-number constraint, allowing arbitrary adaptive quantum protocols. We extend these results to continuous frequency-dependent loss under a power constraint and identify the optimal allocation of photons among optical modes. For constant loss over an unlimited bandwidth, we obtain a closed-form capacity proportional to the square root of power. For randomly varying loss, we determine exact finite-energy capacities when the channel realization is publicly revealed, distinguishing knowledge before and after transmission. When fading remains unobserved, we derive capacity bounds and explicit formulas for an on/off channel. We also establish strong-converse bounds, with exact thresholds for the deterministic loss models considered here, observed fading, and unobserved fading with finitely many possible transmissivities. Under mean energy constraints, these thresholds generally exceed the corresponding finite-energy capacities. These results guide energy allocation and provide benchmarks for energy-constrained optical quantum communication with multimode signals and variable loss.

papers.title: From Fourier Amplitudes to Persistence Images for Impact-Echo Defect Detection
papers.abstract: Impact-echo testing is a nondestructive testing method used to detect internal defects in concrete structures. However, boundary reflections, structured interference, and measurement noise can produce complex Fourier amplitude spectra, making defect classification difficult. We constructed a two-dimensional frequency--amplitude persistence image (FA-PI) from the Fourier amplitude spectrum. Using a fixed parameterization of exact multi-parameter persistent homology, each retained Fourier component is represented with frequency-bin location as one coordinate and amplitude as the other, and Gaussian kernels are then applied in this two-dimensional space. This construction has a direct analytical connection to the corresponding one-dimensional Gaussian-smoothed Fourier amplitude spectrum. FA-PI was evaluated on an experimental backfill-void dataset and a public bridge-deck impact-echo dataset, and compared with raw and Gaussian-smoothed Fourier amplitude spectra using a linear classifier with a Softmax output and identical signal-level data splits. The evaluation included original signals and signals corrupted by Gaussian noise, sinusoidal interference, or mixed noise, with matching noise types and signal-to-noise ratios during training, validation, and testing. Performance was assessed using accuracy and macro-averaged precision, recall, and F1-score. Across the two datasets, FA-PI consistently outperformed the raw and Gaussian-smoothed Fourier baselines in the noisy-condition summaries. These findings indicate that representing Fourier spectral components in a two-dimensional frequency--amplitude space can improve impact-echo defect classification beyond frequency-axis smoothing alone.

papers.title: Inverse eigenvalue problem for discrete three-diagonal Schroedinger operator and the continuum limit in Tikhonov regularization approach
papers.abstract: In the present article the self-contained derivation of main formulas of the inverse eigenvalue problem for the Sturm-Liouville operator is given on the base of its discrete approximation and the subsequent transition to the limit of the continuum coordinate. In doing so, we adhere to Tikhonov concept, where the discrete approximation is performed as a regularization of the ill-posed operator problem. While the continuum limit for the three-diagonal matrix Hamiltonian is impossible as such, following the Tikhonov procedure leads not to a limit for the potential matrix itself, but rather for a certain combination of the matrix elements, and this limit is precisely the desired potential in the continuum case.

papers.title: SP$^2$ec: Adaptive Self-Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Speculative Decoding (SD) has demonstrated its efficacy in accelerating large language model inference, but for Vision-Language Models (VLMs), the diverse input modalities make it difficult for a small trained drafter to achieve consistently high throughput. Self-speculative decoding reuses parts of the target model as a drafter which retains the multi-modal capability of the VLMs, yet its efficiency depends on choosing a suitable draft configuration for each prompt. We propose Single-Peak SPeculative decoding (SP$^2$ec), a training-free bandit algorithm that adapts the draft configuration during generation. SP$^2$ec exploits the single-peak throughput pattern observed in existing self-speculative methods, including SWIFT, KnapSpec, SpecVLM, and our simple cosSim. Our algorithmic design explicitly minimizes a novel notion of wall-time regret for each given query, corresponding to the empirical wall-time latency. Theoretical guarantees on the wall-time regret show that SP$^2$ec can exploit the optimal draft configuration, with negligible exploration cost. Extensive experiments on Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral-7B across visual and textual tasks show consistent improvements of up to 11% over the original self-speculative methods, demonstrating the wide applicability of the proposed SP$^2$ec algorithm.

papers.title: Concealed Handgun Detection using WiFi Signals
papers.abstract: While conventional camera-based surveillance systems and metal detectors can provide a sufficient level of security when used appropriately, they have fundamental limitations that reduce their applicability. Camera-based systems are unable to detect occluded or concealed threats and metal detectors require each person to enter through a narrow opening one at a time, leading to congestion issues and limited use in large crowds. A WiFi-based security system has the potential to be a complementary modality that is able to handle occlusions or concealment and is not hindered by strict spatial configurations. In this paper, we propose use Channel State Information estimated from WiFi-signals to detect concealed handguns. To this end we collect a dataset of aligned WiFi signals and RGB images that we call the WiFire dataset. We also propose a deep learning model called WiFireNet tailored to detect concealed handguns in WiFi signals using vision-based supervision signals. Our results show that concealed handgun detection is possible in WiFi and has promise as a complementary modality to surveillance cameras and metal detectors. We release the dataset, model and code to facilitate the further research into WiFi-based handgun detection.

papers.title: Geometric bounds on norms of signed indecomposable integers
papers.abstract: We establish bounds on the norm of signed indecomposable integers in totally real number fields, via a geometric argument. We also improve the bound on the norm of totally positive indecomposable integers in real quadratic fields by Tinková and Voutier.

papers.title: Enabling Token-wise Importance Sampling in Off-Policy RLVR with Proximal KL Regularization
papers.abstract: Off-policy data in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) can arise from asynchronous generation, rollout-training mismatch, and response reuse. Token-wise importance weighting avoids multiplying likelihood ratios across a response but generally biases policy gradients. We prove that, under coverage and local expressiveness conditions, full future KL credit makes the exact proximal optimizer the update's unique stationary policy, even for mixtures of older policies, without full-response weights or a fitted critic. We further establish convergence of continuous-time tabular population updates under persistent coverage and time-varying behavior policies, and a finite-sample reward guarantee for linear logistic models under additional assumptions. These results motivate Proximal KL, a practical off-policy RLVR method that separates the proximal reference from the sampling policy and replaces PPO clipping with bounded future KL credit. Across all seven matched off-policy comparisons on Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B, spanning two learning rates, response reuse, and rollout staleness, Proximal KL outperforms GRPO in micro-averaged accuracy over eight math benchmarks by up to 2.58%. A separate on-policy comparison yields comparable aggregate accuracy. In periodic-refresh experiments, Proximal KL avoids the collapses observed in PG and CISPO, exceeds GRPO's training accuracy, and reaches higher accuracy in fewer policy updates. Ablations show that token-wise correction outperforms sequence-level and unweighted controls. With token-wise correction retained, future KL feedback reduces sensitivity to the tested baseline perturbation relative to PPO clipping. A finite future horizon improves AIME24 mean@16 and pass@16 over the full tail, while fixed-policy measurements show that truncation reduces correction variance over the tested horizons.

papers.title: A Rate Transfer Method: Convergence Rates in Stochastic Gradient Descent via Stochastic Calculus
papers.abstract: We develop a rate-transfer method that converts finite-time Lyapunov estimates for an associated stochastic differential equation (SDE) into finite-time convergence bounds for stochastic gradient algorithms. Under generic moment and smoothness conditions, the convergence analysis of the stochastic gradient method reduces to a calculus argument verifying a Lyapunov generator inequality for the SDE. The method recovers established rates for classical stochastic gradient methods and provides a way to establish convergence rates for new optimization algorithms through calculus arguments applied to their associated SDEs.

papers.title: Selecting the 7th Smallest of 16 Elements Takes Exactly 28 Comparisons
papers.abstract: Let $V_i(n)$ denote the minimum worst-case number of comparisons needed to find the $i$-th smallest of $n$ distinct elements. We construct algorithms showing $V_7(16)\le28$ and $V_8(16)\le29$, improving the previously reported upper bounds of 30 and 31. Together with known lower bounds, these results establish $V_7(16)=28$ and leave $V_8(16)\in\{28,29\}$. For 17 elements, we establish $V_5(17)=27$ and improve the upper bounds for ranks 6 through 9 to 29, 30, 31, and 31, respectively. Every new upper bound has an explicit decision-graph certificate verified by a static checker developed independently of the search. We also derive a lower bound for selection from a partially ordered state by combining the Fussenegger-Gabow weight with its order-reversed counterpart. All new upper bounds and this lower bound are formally verified in Lean 4. For $V_8(16)$, we show that a lower bound based solely on the total number of decision-tree leaves cannot establish $V_8(16)\ge29$. The algorithms were found using fixed-budget search, information-guided comparison ordering, and proof-number search. Proof-number search was decisive in finding the 28-comparison algorithm; in our experiments, refuting a comparison budget remained substantially more expensive than finding an algorithm within it.

papers.title: Context-aware Bayesian Fusion for Multimodal Object Detection
papers.abstract: Reliable detection of pedestrians and road users is essential for the safe operation of autonomous vehicles. However, this task becomes increasingly challenging under adverse environmental conditions, such as poor weather and low lighting, where the performance of state-of-the-art pre-trained object detectors and on-board sensors tends to degrade, which limits their effectiveness and reliability. Moreover, retraining models for each operating context imposes significant constraints due to high data requirements, computational resources, and time. Considering this, we propose a novel context-aware multimodal late fusion approach that integrates a lightweight gating network within our probabilistic calibration framework. The gating network extracts environmental context and dynamically modulates the detection outputs of pre-trained object detectors based on the inferred context, without retraining of the detectors. Our methodology is evaluated on a modified KITTI dataset, in which the camera images and lidar pointclouds are augmented for varying fog levels. Experimental results show that our approach yields an approximately 14% relative improvement over non-adaptive late fusion baselines, achieving a consistent average precision of 56% across different fog levels.

papers.title: Emergent Loop Geometry in Gauge-Equivariant Graph Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Gauge-equivariant graph neural networks generate ordered products of gauge links through local message passing, but the geometry of these internal structures is not captured by the receptive field alone. We investigate the statistical ensemble of closed lattice walks generated by recursive node- and edge-feature operations, independently of network training. Analytical and numerical results reveal a separation between rapid growth of contour length and much slower spatial expansion: deeper compositions generate increasingly long paths through repeated traversal of relatively compact regions. Loop expansions of fermionic observables provide a physical interpretation of this hierarchy, showing how spatial locality remains compatible with high-order dependence on nearby gauge fields. These findings identify complementary roles of network depth in extending spatial reach and enriching the representations constructed within that reach, providing a geometrical perspective on learning lattice gauge observables.

papers.title: Ensuring Complete Consistency between Hops and Wavefunction Propagation in Fewest-Switches Surface Hopping
papers.abstract: Fewest-switches surface hopping (FSSH) is a popular and versatile approach for performing dynamical simulations beyond the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, in which nonadiabatic effects are incorporated through stochastic hops of the active potential energy surface. However, the FSSH algorithm does not ensure that hops are completely consistent with the underlying electronic wavefunction dynamics. This can lead to significant errors as well as requiring small propagation time steps, which can significantly compromise the computational efficiency of the method. These problems are known to be particularly severe at so-called trivial crossings, for which the nonadiabatic coupling is entirely localized at the crossing point. Here, we solve the trivial-crossing problem by developing a fully-consistent hopping-probability formula, which generates attempted hops that match the time-evolution of the wavefunction across any size time step by construction. A state-tracking algorithm is also utilized to ensure that attempted hops are always accepted at trivial crossings. Through application to systems that contain extremely challenging trivial crossings, we demonstrate that this hopping scheme is capable of obtaining highly accurate results, even when large propagation time steps are used.

papers.title: A formula for the free energy of non-convex vector spin glasses
papers.abstract: We consider vector mean-field spin glass models with independent and identically distributed spins without assuming the covariance function is convex. We identify the limit free energy as the minimum of a functional that can be written as the sum of a relative entropy and the solution of a Hamilton--Jacobi equation. The proof of this result relies on the observation that when the spin configurations of the system are constrained to have a given empirical measure, the corresponding free energy approximately satisfies a Hamilton--Jacobi equation with a uniformly bounded error.

papers.title: SolBehave: Evaluating the Behavioural Correctness of LLM-Generated Smart Contracts
papers.abstract: Large language models increasingly generate Solidity smart contracts that, once deployed, can never be patched, making a single latent fault permanent and exploitable. Yet current evaluations mostly ask only whether generated code compiles. We introduce SolBehave, a benchmark for evaluating the correctness of model-generated contracts at scale, moving beyond ad hoc unit tests. Across 250 real, reproducible Ethereum contracts, we apply three complementary tests of behavioural fidelity: differential fuzzing, historical-transaction replay, and, as our core contribution, synthetic-transaction replay guided by a Dynamic Condition Response (DCR) graph that enumerates the space of legitimate function-call sequences. Differential fuzzing compares each generated function with the original on automatically generated inputs; historical replay compares the whole contract on the transactions it actually received on-chain; DCR-guided replay compares it on sequences of calls that follow its intended usage, including orderings that never occurred on-chain. We evaluate seven state-of-the-art open-weight models after one round of automated repair. Compilation success ranges from 26.4% to 92.7%, but under differential fuzzing only 31.4% of all generated function bodies that compile, pooled over models and samples, are equivalent to the original. Divergence at the contract level is the norm rather than the exception: for six of the seven models, between 13% and 31% of the generated contracts that compile diverge from the original under historical replay, and between 13% and 44% under DCR-guided replay; only Gemma-4-31B stays below 3% on both. Compilation is therefore a necessary condition for correctness and far from a sufficient one.

papers.title: Bio-Inspired Electrotactile Feedback: A Framework and Impacts of Multimodal Cues
papers.abstract: Electrotactile stimulation, as a haptic feedback method, often struggles to evoke high-quality natural sensations. Consequently, despite its practical advantages, it is generally less preferred in human-machine systems than mechanical approaches. In this paper, we propose a bio-inspired stimulation framework that generates signals modelled on afferent neural activity derived from a touch model. By producing more biologically plausible spiking patterns, the proposed approach aims to enhance the realism of perceived tactile sensations. To evaluate these stimulation patterns in a realistic task context and to quantify the influence of visual and movement cues, we conducted a series of subjective experiments under three conditions. The results indicate that bio-inspired modulation was effective: in particular, bio-inspired co-modulation of amplitude and frequency achieved a favourable pressure-irritation trade-off, increasing the probability of perceiving pressure while maintaining low irritation (pressure: 0.78; irritation: 0.24) relative to the other patterns. Visual cues and hand movement further improved feedback quality by significantly increasing the probability of reporting pressure (p$<$0.001) without a corresponding increase in irritation, and by increasing mean naturalness ratings. Overall, these findings demonstrate the potential of bio-inspired electrotactile patterns to improve haptic feedback quality, and highlight the importance of evaluating such methods under realistic, multimodal interaction scenarios.

papers.title: Competing delocalisation and localisation induced by the dipolar tail in fragmented lattice gases
papers.abstract: We investigate how the long-range tail of dipole-dipole interactions modifies the dynamics of strongly interacting hard-core bosons in a one-dimensional lattice. In the nearest-neighbour model, large interactions generate an emergent Hilbert-space fragmentation into manifolds labelled by the number of nearest-neighbour bonds \(N_{\mathrm{NN}}\). The dipolar tail has a non-monotonic effect on this fragmented dynamics as the interaction-to-tunnelling ratio \(V/t\) is increased. At intermediate \(V/t\), it enhances delocalisation relative to the nearest-neighbour model by reducing the energetic detuning between neighbouring \(N_{\mathrm{NN}}\) manifolds and sustaining their hybridisation by hopping. At larger \(V/t\), the same tail lifts degeneracies within each manifold, beginning with the splitting associated with the next-nearest-neighbour bond number \(N_{\mathrm{NNN}}\), and promotes intra-manifold localisation and Hilbert-space shattering. The competition between these two effects produces a crossover from a delocalising to a localising role of the dipolar tail, visible in the late-time spatial inhomogeneity. This crossover occurs for nearly all initial states considered and persists at different fillings. Transverse confinement strengthens the short-range part of the dipolar tail and shifts the crossover to lower \(V/t\), bringing it into the regime relevant to current experiments with magnetic atoms and polar molecules.

papers.title: Enabling Polyspectra via Stochastic Realizations of Inverse Decay Curvature Perturbations in Axion Inflation
papers.abstract: Current and upcoming galaxy-redshift surveys offer a promising path for constraining inflationary physics. These constraints are often imposed by relating correlations of the primordial curvature perturbation to the late-time galaxy correlation functions. The primordial correlators can either be computed analytically, or via realizations of the primordial curvature perturbations that are initialized on a grid and evolved numerically according to the classical equations of motion. In this work we take a hybrid approach, initializing the fields in the Bunch-Davies vacuum; and then imposing time evolution through direct numerical integration. Our method efficiently generates realizations of the inverse decay primordial curvature perturbations for axion inflation---an inflationary model in which a pseudoscalar inflaton field couples to a $U(1)$ gauge field via a Chern-Simons interaction. Depending on the choice of parameter $ξ\in\{2, 2.5, 3\}$, which controls gauge field particle production in this model, our method generates realizations with an average runtime of a few hours on 1 CPU core. We compute the power spectrum and bispectrum from these realizations and find a surprisingly large discrepancy between our result and previous work that used an approximation for the gauge field mode functions---up to a factor of $\sim4$ difference for the bispectrum in the case of $ξ=2$. This new method enables not only rapid computation of higher order polyspectra, but also generation of initial conditions for large-scale structure analyses.

papers.title: Virtual photon bremsstrahlung in a magnetized quark-gluon-plasma
papers.abstract: We investigate dilepton production via virtual quark bremsstrahlung in a hot, magnetized quark-gluon plasma (QGP), extending the Landau-Pomeranchuk-Migdal (LPM) framework to account for a background magnetic field and for Fermi-Dirac quark statistics. An external electromagnetic field drives the quark distribution out of equilibrium, and this off-equilibrium correction, obtained from the Boltzmann equation in the relaxation-time approximation, is in principle explicit in the electric and magnetic field strengths. We argue that this correction, being linear in the electric field, vanishes identically upon integration over the full dilepton solid angle and therefore does not contribute to the dilepton production rate (DPR). The leading magnetic-field signature in the rate instead enters entirely through the equilibrium sector: the medium density and Debye screening mass, computed from the Landau-level structure of the magnetized QGP, modifying the LPM suppression parameter. Working in the regime relevant to the hydrodynamic phase of heavy-ion collisions, we present the LPM-induced DPR for quark scatterers and establish, for the first time, a nonzero magnetic-field imprint on this observable through the LPM mechanism.

papers.title: Finite temperature Fredholm determinants for dynamical correlation functions
papers.abstract: We study the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of finite-temperature dynamical Fredholm determinants using effective form factors. The method expresses these asymptotics as a functional of an effective phase shift. We determine its two branches on either side of a quadratic stationary point and the transition profile joining them. The profile is expressed through parabolic-cylinder functions. Its connection to the high-temperature Gaussian $β$ ensemble fixes the finite normalization, in agreement with an independent Riemann--Hilbert analysis. We also show that the leading exponential asymptotics suffice to recover the Euler-scale prediction of generalized hydrodynamics for the dynamical structure factor of hard rods.

papers.title: Methods of Construction of Exponential Bases on Planar Domains Revised
papers.abstract: In [1], we surveyed classical and recent results on the construction of exponential bases on planar domains with explicit control over the associated frame bounds. We also constructed well-conditioned exponential bases on certain planar sets that multi-tile the plane. In this revision, we identify an error in the choice of basis used in the proof of Theorem 3.11 and we provide a new proof using a simpler exponential basis.

papers.title: Noncommutative BTZ Gravastar in Gauss-Bonnet Gravity
papers.abstract: We constructed a (2+1)-dimensional gravastar whose interior region was characterized by a noncommutative geometry with Gauss-Bonnet corrections, while the exterior region was described by a Gauss-Bonnet-modified BTZ solution. The two geometries were joined across a thin shell using the generalized junction formalism, from which we derived the surface equations of state. We investigated the energy conditions at the shell, determining the parameter regimes under which the null, weak, and strong energy conditions were satisfied. We also analyzed the thermodynamic properties of the noncommutative interior region, including the temperature, entropy, and heat capacity.

papers.title: On separable pairs of fields and beautiful pairs of separably closed valued fields
papers.abstract: We continue the study of beautiful pairs of henselian valued fields, initiated in joint work of the second author with Cubides Kovacsics and Ye. As our main result, we show that separably closed non-trivially valued fields of arbitrary imperfection degree admit beautiful pairs which are elementary pairs satisfying certain natural axioms. They satisfy beauty transfer, i.e., saturated models of their theory are again beautiful. The same holds for beautiful pairs associated to natural subclasses of all definable types, most notably for all definable types orthogonal to the value group and for all bounded definable types. This yields strict pro-definability of the space of the definable types from any of these classes, in the theory SCVF of separably closed non-trivially valued fields. We also show a separable analog of a classical result of Keisler's, namely that the first order theory of an infinite separable extension $L/K$ of fields - considered in the pairs language and where the large field $L$ is separably closed, is determined by the theory of the small field $K$ together with the imperfection degree of $L$ over $K$.

papers.title: Generalized Thom Spectra, Conjugate Stacks, and truncated Brown-Peterson Spectra
papers.abstract: We propose a of definition conjugate stack for a class of suitable $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}$-algebras that includes the truncated Brown-Peterson spectra $\mathrm{BP}\langle n \rangle$ for all heights $n$. Then we calculate part of $\mathrm{BP}\langle n \rangle^{\mathrm{conj}}$ as a quotient stack in terms of Witt vectors. To perform this computation we study generalized Thom spectra and their relative Topological Hochschild Homology. We exhibit the Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectrum $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{F}_2$ as a $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}$-Thom spectrum, the $p$-local Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectra $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{Z}/p^n$ (except for $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{Z}/4$) and $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ as $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}_{(p)}$-Thom spectra, and the connective complex K-theory spectrum $ku$ as $\mathbb{E}_1$-$\mathrm{MU}$-Thom spectra. We accompany these ``go" results with ``no-go" results that show these ``go" results do not admit $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-refinements.

papers.title: PreciseCoder: Faithful and Generalizable Debugging Beyond Unit-Test Rewards
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) from unit tests is the common recipe for post-training code models, but a unit test only asks whether the final program passes. We analyze what this unit-test-only reward teaches a model during debugging and find that, while it raises pass rates, it also teaches the model to edit more and to hallucinate bugs in code that is already correct. We introduce PreciseCoder, a training algorithm that augments the unit-test reward with a signal for semantically verified, localized edits, which correlates with smaller edits and higher pass rates. On 4B, 9B, and 27B models, PreciseCoder reduces the average number of edit lines from 7-15to 3 at a pass rate on par with unit-test-only training. Trained only on single-line bugs, PreciseCoder can generalize to repository-level program repair, where it resolves more issues with smaller patches. Its precision also transfers from weaker to stronger models: given the reasoning trace of a 9B PreciseCoder model, frontier models such as GPT-5.6 Sol and Qwen3.8-Max gain 4.6-12.4 points in edit precision with no additional training. Linguistic analysis of the thinking traces shows that our reward encourages the model to reason about individual lines, name the buggy ones, and form consistent bug hypotheses.

papers.title: Optimal transport to non-convex polyhedral domains
papers.abstract: We study optimal transport with a non-convex polyhedral target in $\mathbb{R}^n$. The closure of the singular set is locally a smooth hypersurface outside a relatively closed set of Hausdorff dimension at most $n-2$. For partial transport between domains separated by a hyperplane, the source free boundary has the same regularity.

papers.title: Exact two-loop gravitational tail integrals and their ultraviolet-infrared structure
papers.abstract: Gravitational tail-of-tail corrections arise when radiation scatters twice from the mass-monopole field of its source. In the multipolar effective field theory, one of the two-loop topologies contributing to this process involves genuinely coupled loop momenta, preventing its evaluation through nested one-loop integrations. After tensor reduction, this nonfactorizing structure leads to a particularly challenging family of scalar integrals with unbounded numerator powers as the multipole rank increases. We derive exact closed-form expressions for the entire relevant integer numerator domain, valid in generic dimension and accommodating Feynman, retarded, and advanced prescriptions through consistent analytic continuation. Near $d=3+ε$, we also obtain explicit Laurent expansions through $O(ε)$, retaining the subleading information needed in higher-order radiative calculations. While these expansions determine the dimensional poles, identifying their ultraviolet (UV) or infrared (IR) origin requires a separate analysis of momentum regions. We carry out this analysis throughout the integral domain and apply it directly to the coupled tail-of-tail emission diagram for arbitrary electric and magnetic multipoles. In this way, we independently determine the UV and IR residues, and explicitly verify that the complete infrared pole structure, including both double and simple poles, agrees with the exponentiation of the one-loop gravitational tail. The UV residues, calculated directly from hard-momentum regions, reproduce the established multipole anomalous dimensions when combined with the known contributions of the remaining diagrams.

papers.title: Compositional Sensitivity Analysis for Multiobjective System Co-Design
papers.abstract: Sensitivity analysis of coupled systems typically propagates derivatives of single-valued maps, whereas multiobjective optimization generally treats sensitivity at the system level rather than through interconnected subsystems. We develop a mathematical framework for compositional sensitivity analysis in multiobjective system design, building on monotone co-design. Subsystems are represented as design problems (DPs), interconnected through series, parallel, union, intersection, and feedback composition. We introduce tangential DPs (TDPs) to describe first-order variations around an operating point, show that they preserve the structure of DPs, and characterize their queries through graphical derivatives. To account for multiple internal realizations of a system-level operating point, tangential co-design problems compose families of local TDPs by taking a union over these realizations while retaining the original interconnection structure. We show that these compositions yield families of TDPs and establish conditions under which sensitivity analysis commutes with individual composition operations. Beyond infinitesimal sensitivity, we show that bounded tangential models of convex DPs provide tighter outer approximations of feasible finite changes, which can be propagated through co-design problems without union compositions. We conclude with several convex and nonconvex numerical examples that showcase the framework's accuracy and computational benefits.

papers.title: Engineering Color and Angular Stability in Building-Integrated Photovoltaics Using Metal-Oxide Photonic Glasses
papers.abstract: Coloring building-integrated photovoltaics poses a dilemma: absorptive pigments cost photocurrent, while ordered photonic structures are iridescent. Amorphous photonic glasses, disordered packings of high-index nanospheres, are proposed to avoid both, yet their angle-independent color has rarely been quantified on a realistic module stack. A non-absorbing scatterer needs a high index with visible transparency, which the Moss rule caps near 2.35. Coupling Mie scattering, the Percus-Yevick structure factor, the exact phase function, and two-flux transfer with absorption and refraction at the front glass, we fix four target colors that a crowd-sourced naming survey calls unambiguously blue, green, gold, and terracotta, and map the recipes reaching them across four metal oxides, four encapsulants, two cell technologies, and wide ranges of particle size, packing fraction, and layer number. All four are reached in a laminated three-layer coating, to within DeltaE00 of 0.8 to 2.5, but not from one oxide: transparent TiO2 renders the blue and only pale warm tones; the green, gold, and terracotta require the blue-band absorption of V2O5, and the low-contrast oxides turn grey at the warm end. The encapsulant governs the color, and the cell technology does not. Disorder does not confer angle independence: the colors hold for an observer moving under a fixed sun but drift by DeltaE00 of 5 to 18 over the day, terracotta least, and a facade lit from above and viewed from below shifts every color towards the blue. Oxide, layer number, and facade geometry must therefore be designed together.

papers.title: Beyond the Verdict: Agentic Code Judging with Verifiable Feedback
papers.abstract: Test-time scaling for large language models (LLMs) can involve generating multiple candidate solutions for selection or revising an earlier attempt. To guide selection and revision, we need a verifier that can estimate candidate correctness and provide evidence of failure. In competitive programming, however, official judging systems provide authoritative verdicts under finite submission budgets, without revealing failure explanations or failing inputs. To provide informative feedback without consuming official submissions, we formulate a task in which a model judges and diagnoses a candidate program using only the problem statement and source code, with generated counterexamples serving as checkable evidence. To evaluate this task, we build USACO-JUDGE from the USACO 2026 contests, using accepted and unaccepted programs written by human experts and multiple LLMs. We then train ARBITER, a 35B mixture-of-experts (MoE) agentic verifier, with reinforcement learning in a generic execution sandbox. Training raises counterexample success on incorrect programs from 40.61% to 62.67% and mean binary verdict accuracy on USACO-JUDGE from 71.41% to 87.41%, approaching frontier verification performance. Beyond verification, ARBITER outperforms baselines in both code selection and refinement. In an IOI 2026 case study, ARBITER-guided refinement raises GPT-OSS-120B's expected score above the gold-medal threshold under the official submission limit.

papers.title: Modified support measures and Alexandrov-Fenchel type inequalities for nonsmooth h-convex bodies in hyperbolic space
papers.abstract: We establish the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality and its modified version for arbitrary, possibly nonsmooth, horospherically convex bodies in hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^{n+1}, n\geq 2$, and prove that equality in each inequality holds if and only if the h-convex body is a geodesic ball. A key ingredient is a rigidity theorem characterizing geodesic balls via proportionality between modified support measures of adjacent orders. Its proof combines the $C^{1,α}\cap W^{2,k+1}$ approximation of the outer parallel hypersurfaces by smooth strictly h-convex hypersurfaces with the estimates for the total variation norm of the signed measure associated with the proportionality relation along the shifted curvature flows independent of initial curvature bounds. For $0\leq k\leq n-1$, we construct weak flows preserving the $k$-th modified quermassintegral $\tilde{W}_k$ with arbitrary h-convex initial bodies as Hausdorff limits of the smooth flows. The rigidity theorem above characterizes the limit shape of the flow and gives a positive lower bound on the rate of decrease of $\tilde{W}_{k+1}$ for a short time whenever the initial h-convex body is not a geodesic ball, which characterizes the equality cases in the modified Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality. For the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality, we establish the Hausdorff stability independent of curvature bounds described by the Alexandrov-Fenchel deficits for h-convex bodies, which characterizes the equality cases in the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality.

papers.title: Looking Complete Is Not Being Grounded: Evaluating LLM Sitreps Against Human-Authored Situation Reports
papers.abstract: Evaluation for automatic crisis reporting should measure what practitioners need, not what is convenient to compare. Through LLM-assisted, author-approved content analysis, we derive a 15-slot information schema from professional humanitarian situation reports using qualitative content analysis, then evaluate 121 human and 261 LLM-generated reports across five disasters and three hazard types. Under google/gemini-3.7-flash on Cyclone Idai, the best machine arm is nominally above the empirical human ceiling (0.827 vs. 0.821), but the difference is statistically indistinguishable from zero (95\% bootstrap CI $[-.049,.059]$; permutation $p=.852$), and the ordering does not replicate under openai/gpt-5.6-luna. On a blind 100-item Idai sample, the author agrees with the Gemini judge at 0.910 accuracy and unweighted Cohen's $κ=.799$. All four judges clear the plan's raw-agreement criterion of .7; only Gemini reaches .7 on chance-corrected $κ$. Across the three primary events, machine reports reproduce 5.4-11.0% of same-day official figures. Across those same events, raw exact-number matching links 14.3-19.6% of official figures and 85.4-90.1% of machine figures to the social stream; manual audit confirms 45/50 declared absences, 4/25 official matches, and 24/25 machine matches semantically. The issuing-provenance gap is positive in all 12 observed event-judge cells: report date, organisation, series, and authority were not supplied at professional-report coverage in any cell. On the three primary events, ROUGE-L is uninformative, BERTScore is negatively associated with completeness after multiplicity correction, and a generic LLM judge changes sign.

papers.title: LayerCanvas: Infographic Generation in AI Learning Assistants via Hybrid Layer-Set Diffusion
papers.abstract: Online learning platforms are increasingly deploying AI assistants to provide personalized, on-demand tutoring. These can leverage infographics to communicate complex information and improve the learning experience. However, automating effective infographic generation remains a challenging task, requiring a combination of visual richness with precise typography, structured layouts, and continued editability. Existing representation methods satisfy these goals only in part: Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) representations preserve geometry, hierarchy, and text but provide limited aesthetic flexibility, while raster diffusion models produce richer appearances by flattening content and layout into a single image. Conditioning a diffusion model on a rasterized SVG does not resolve this conflict because the raster preserves approximate placement but discards element ownership, occlusion relationships, and the structure needed to modify and recompose the result. We introduce LayerCanvas, a hybrid approach that retains SVG as the semantic, structural, and typographic program while using diffusion to aestheticize non-text content. Rather than generating one flattened raster, LayerCanvas partitions SVG elements into z-ordered sets of mutually non-overlapping elements and processes them through communicating parallel RGB generation streams. The resulting layers are independently editable and deterministically recomposed, while text is rendered from preserved vector metadata. Our approach combines rich visual synthesis with accurate typography and localized editing. LayerCanvas substantially improves text fidelity over state-of-the-art raster image generators while achieving the highest overall aesthetic quality. We further demonstrate non-destructive content editing, localization, asset reuse, and animation.

papers.title: Ghostline: a six-node Wi-Fi CSI motion tracker with node-to-node Links. System description and a pilot evaluation
papers.abstract: Ghostline is a device-free motion tracking system built on six ESP32-S3 Wi-Fi boards and one consumer router. The boards' Wi-Fi driver reports channel state information (CSI) for every received frame with the sender's address, and a modified open-source firmware forwards both, so every board carries a CSI stream for the router and for each other board: seven radios give up to 36 directed Links over 21 Spans instead of a star of six. Each Link is compared with a self-forming quiet Baseline, disturbed Links vote on a floor grid, and the grid becomes anonymous Tracks. The system was built and run during a three-day hackathon in an ordinary room. We describe it in full and report a pilot evaluation with one walker: spoken cues at seven marked positions, a two-minute free walk and five minutes of empty room, synchronised to video within 0.18 s (median). Walking between marks, the Track lay a median 0.85 m from the straight path and 1.56 m (95% CI 1.29 to 2.83) from a cue-based reference trajectory (constant speed between cues, not measured positions), with 46% of walk updates within 2 m of it; the free walk was tracked in 94% of updates. The limits: a standing person is lost within seconds, a false Track appeared in 15.9% and 2.9% of updates in two empty-room periods, and informal runs that afternoon did not separate two walkers. Two offline replays through the same pipeline show where this comes from: with the node-to-node Links removed and settings unchanged, the tracked share of walk updates falls from 90% to 19% and the free walk from 96% to 60%; a plain radio tomographic image on the same per-Span evidence, at the same false rate, matches the grid and tracker at 2 m (48% against 47%) and is ahead at 1 m (36% against 21%). On this recording the Tracks depend on the Link set, and the imaging stage adds no measurable accuracy. We state what the pilot establishes and what it does not.

papers.title: What Human-AI Interaction Leaves Behind: Residual Human States -- A Trajectory-Based Framework and Multi-Study Analysis
papers.abstract: Human-AI Interaction is commonly evaluated by what an artificial agent enables during use, yet interaction can also alter the human who acts next. We introduce Residual Human States, a trajectory-based framework for representing the potentially multidimensional human state carried forward after interaction with AI, relative to a relevant alternative trajectory. The framework distinguishes assisted output from human-state transition and derives four empirical propositions: multidimensionality, interaction-policy dependence, horizon dissociation, and temporal persistence. Its central claim is that assisted performance does not by itself determine the human state carried forward. We examine these propositions through four empirical cases with different inferential roles. Published medical-training evidence illustrates how one AI interaction history can be associated with both slightly higher observed accuracy on some later unaided cases and transmission of a systematic decision bias on others. A second diagnostic-learning study shows that later unaided behaviour differs across AI-support policies, while also revealing that aggregate accuracy cannot by itself distinguish improved discrimination from a shifted response criterion. In a classroom experiment, generative-AI tutoring substantially improved assisted practice performance without a corresponding detectable gain on a subsequent unaided exam. A longitudinal reanalysis of personalised AI dialogue further shows that residual contrasts can evolve across post-interaction horizons and that such change may arise from the comparison trajectory as well as from the focal intervention. Evaluating interactive AI systems therefore requires attention not only to contemporaneous performance, but also to which human states alternative interaction trajectories produce, relative to which counterfactuals, and how durably.

papers.title: Rubrics from the Task, Verdicts from Evidence: Pointwise Rubric Rewards with Tool-Augmented Judges
papers.abstract: Rubric-based reward models (RMs) evaluate responses against explicit criteria. However, existing methods often derive criteria from observed response candidates, introducing response-induced bias that may limit rubric generalizability. Their judges also struggle with mechanical constraints when relying on reading alone, and commonly used pairwise judges provide only relative preferences, complicating their direct use for policy optimization.
