We propose ReVeR, a pointwise rubric RM that derives hard rules and graded principles by reasoning about the instruction alone and evaluates responses independently through tool-augmented judging. Both components are trained through label-blind distillation, in which preference labels only filter a teacher's outputs, yielding ReVeR-Traces, a large-scale dataset of rubric-reasoning and judging trajectories. Experiments demonstrate that ReVeR outperforms pairwise rubric RMs in average preference accuracy, most clearly on instruction following, as well as in test-time scaling and downstream policy optimization. We further find that generator RL improves preference accuracy while reducing rubric fidelity, and that higher preference accuracy does not necessarily translate into better downstream policies. These findings highlight that rubric fidelity, preference accuracy, and downstream utility are distinct properties, shedding light on future RM research.

papers.title: Two Holes Make a Difference: Deterministic Paging with Delay and Deadlines
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study online paging with delay or deadlines. In online paging with delay, an online algorithm manages a cache of size $k$ and needs to serve incoming requests by adding the requested pages to the cache. In addition, it has the option to delay serving incoming requests at a cost that depends on the delay. We propose a new online algorithm, which combines a threshold rule with first-in, first-out (FIFO) replacement, and show that it is $(2k+2)$-competitive for cache size $k$. This result corrects a previously published claim that the competitive ratio is exactly $2k+1$ regardless of the number of holes (pages outside the cache). However, in the case of one hole, we show that the FIFO rule with a different threshold is indeed $(2k+1)$-competitive, giving a tight result. In the case of deadlines, the same analysis gives a deadline-triggered algorithm that is $(k+1)$-competitive in general and $k$-competitive if there is only one hole. Moreover, we show that the second hole makes paging with deadlines strictly harder than classical paging, where the competitive ratio is independent of the number of holes. For paging with deadlines, we prove a deterministic lower bound of $k+\tfrac12$, already for two holes. We show that, as a consequence, no threshold-triggered algorithm can achieve a competitive ratio less than $2k+\frac32$ in general.

papers.title: Turning Selection Bias into a New Statistic: Asymmetry and Fringes of Lensed Gravitational Waves
papers.abstract: Gravitational waves (GWs) propagating across the Universe can be distorted by intervening lenses, producing characteristic wave-optics signatures. These effects are not incorporated into current matched-filtering searches and can therefore substantially reduce detection efficiency. The underlying mechanism is the signal-consistency test, which measures deviations between the observed and expected signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) distributions. We report a systematic study of the impact of gravitational lensing on signal-consistency tests, using a two-image interference model and representative signal-consistency statistics in both the time and frequency domains. We find that overlapping images produce sharply localized SNR residuals in the time domain, breaking the reflection symmetry of the autocorrelation about the merger time. Although interference fringes produce broadband SNR residuals in the frequency domain, both domains exhibit a minimum for high-mass signals when the fringe structure becomes comparable to the signal bandwidth. This highlights a limitation of current strategies that search for distorted lensed signals only among GW events detected by matched-filtering searches. Exploiting this asymmetry, we develop a statistic that separates selected down-ranked lensed injections from noise-background triggers and paired nonlensed injections, without extending the template bank. Our results establish the first connection between lensing observables and detection, paving the way for the discovery of lensed GWs.

papers.title: MIST: Multi-Scale Spatial Context for Gene Expression Prediction from Histology
papers.abstract: Predicting spatial gene expression from standard H&E images could extend molecular analysis to tissues without spatial transcriptomic measurements. A standard Transformer applies self-attention over spots but ignores where each spot sits in the tissue, whereas a spot's molecular state depends on tissue context at multiple spatial scales. Building on this insight, we introduce MIST, a Multi-context Spatial Transformer that augments the self-attention backbone with two context pathways applied in every layer: a coordinate-invariant local pathway that attends over spatial k-nearest-neighbor spots, and a slide pathway that broadcasts a whole-slide summary to every spot; the model predicts all spots in a single forward pass. Because coordinates enter only through pairwise distances, the local pathway is invariant to translations, rotations, and reflections when image features are fixed. In intra-cohort evaluation across six human organ cohorts from HEST-1k, MIST improves mean Pearson correlation over the strongest evaluated baseline by 9.7%, 11.6%, and 11.4% for 10-, 50-, and 100-gene panels, respectively, with the lowest average MSE and MAE. MIST further improves leave-one-organ-out transfer by 6.0% over the next strongest baseline, attains the best expression-derived domain recovery (highest mean ARI and NMI at every clustering resolution, and higher NMI than the closest baseline on 84% of held-out slides), and reproduces spatial expression patterns of selected cancer-marker genes. Together, these results show that adding local and slide context to a vanilla Transformer backbone is an effective approach to spatial gene expression prediction from histology.

papers.title: On plank coverings of cube annuli
papers.abstract: We study plank coverings of cube annuli $Q\setminusδQ\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, where $Q$ is the $d$-dimensional unit cube and $δQ$ is a homothetic copy lying in its interior. A. Bezdek proved that, in dimension $2$, every plank covering of such an annulus has total width at least~1 whenever $δ\le1-1/\sqrt2$. Smurov, Bogataya, and Bogatyi extended this result to all $d\ge2$ under the condition $δ\le1-1/\sqrt d$. It is conjectured that the same lower bound holds for $δ\le1-1/d$. We provide evidence for this conjecture in dimensions $2$ and $3$ by proving that there exist positive constants $\varepsilon_2$ and $\varepsilon_3$ such that the bound remains valid whenever $δ\le1-1/\sqrt d+\varepsilon_d$.

papers.title: The Federated Tumor Segmentation and Classification (FeTS++) Challenge
papers.abstract: International challenges have become the standard for developing and benchmarking biomedical image analysis methods using centralized multi-institutional data. Federated learning (FL) describes a paradigm-shift on multi-institutional collaborations, where models are trained across institutions while their data are always retained locally. The Federated Tumor Segmentation (FeTS) challenge, first held in 2021, was the first challenge dedicated to FL in medical imaging and editions in 2022 and 2024 pushed the frontiers of real-world method validation. FeTS++ 2027 returns after a two-year gap with a substantially larger and more diverse cohort, and with the two "pluses" that name the challenge: an official classification task alongside segmentation, and a move of the infrastructure to NVIDIA FLARE (NVFlare). Built on the clinically acquired, multi-institutional multi-parametric MRI data of the BraTS 2025 Lighthouse challenge, FeTS++ spans gliomas and meningiomas across patient cohorts from institutions in North America, Europe, Asia, and Africa, and focuses on ranking submitted methodological approaches according to their model utility and an efficiency-aware score. Task 1 asks participants to find the best strategy for aggregating knowledge from per-institution segmentation models, while Task 2 asks them to distinguish glioma from meningioma under the same federated protocol, in which the entity label is heavily confounded with the site of origin.

papers.title: A Distributed Energy Relay Framework for Sustainable Drone Missions
papers.abstract: Limited battery endurance remains a major obstacle to persistent UAV missions. Existing energy-replenishment approaches typically rely on battery-swapping/charging infrastructure or on ground vehicles with accessible road networks - assumptions that may not hold in infrastructure-less regions (ILRs) such as remote wilderness, mountainous terrain, and disaster-stricken areas. We formulate energy resupply in ILRs as a distinct logistics problem, in which energy itself must be projected into a region with no pre-existing infrastructure, and proposes a Distributed Energy Relay Framework that enables cooperative energy delivery using porter drones. The framework introduces a Transportation-by-Relay-and-Cache (TRC) mechanism, in which drones relay battery resources toward a mission location. Additional models are developed to characterize battery transportation capacity, relay amplification, energy-delivery capability, operational cost, and reliability. Based on these models, stations independently evaluate their delivery capability and submit bids to a mission coordinator, which selects an energy-delivery coalition that satisfies mission requirements while minimizing cost. Analytical evaluation illustrates the impact of battery characteristics and drone capabilities on energy projection and demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed framework for sustaining UAV missions in ILRs.

papers.title: Jeva: System One Models from First Principles
papers.abstract: System one models like Jev enable direct, low-latency decision-making. Yet recent open-source practice of predicting an answer from serialized text does not, by itself, respect the structure of a decision problem. We argue that current designs underemphasize four important structural requirements. (i) null-aware: Models should distinguish answer absence from uncertainty among candidates; (ii) permutation-invariant: Reordering alternatives should not change the decision; (iii) option-scalable: Growing candidate sets should not require redefining the output space; (iv) cacheable: Request-independent computation over recurring alternatives should be reusable across requests. We introduce Jeva, a decision-native architecture that addresses these requirements jointly. A shared encoder independently represents the request and each option, while a compact decision stack refines only the request state against immutable option memory. Symmetric aggregation yields permutation-equivariant probabilities; shared scoring accommodates variable-size candidate sets. A separate coverage estimate distinguishes answer absence from candidate competition, enabling explicit null outcomes. Request-independent option representations and layer projections support reuse across newly assembled sets. These mechanisms unify Choice, Noul, and Score outputs. Across evaluations against Jev and open source models, Jeva combines strong typed-decision performance with near-perfect null detection and no decision flips under any tested permutations. It scales to thousands of candidates and substantially reduces latency through cross-request reuse without changing decisions.

papers.title: GreenWAM: A World Foundation Model for Robotics
papers.abstract: A robot needs a world model that predicts how its actions will change the scene and a policy that chooses those actions. Models are usually built and evaluated for only one of these roles, and every robot records its actions in its own format. We ask whether one robot world model can serve both roles across different bodies, and what makes this work. We present GreenWAM, a world foundation model for robotics, together with the recipe that produces it: (1) a shared anatomical action space that describes 20 robot families, from bimanual arms to dexterous humanoids, in common joint coordinates; (2) joint training on these families in visual, action-conditioned and world-action modes; and (3) policies that split an action expert off the generator. As a world model, GreenWAM attains top-tier trajectory, depth and 3D accuracy on WorldArena 1.0, ahead of every world-action model and video generator in our comparison. As a policy, it scores among the top entries of the RoboTwin 2.0 leaderboard, reaches the highest zero-shot LIBERO-plus success among the compared methods and is competitive with dedicated vision-language-action and world-action policies on CALVIN and LIBERO. We further adapt GreenWAM to a real humanoid, where it succeeds more often than policies adapted from $π_{0.5}$ and from Cosmos 3 Edge, and distill it into a single-step policy for real-time control. Controlled experiments yield three findings: robot specialization improves world prediction and control together; an action expert helps when split off at the start of adaptation; and keeping world-model modes during policy adaptation preserves robustness to scene changes.

papers.title: Sharp Global Well-Posedness for the Logarithmically Regularized 2D Euler Equations
papers.abstract: We consider solutions to the two-dimensional Euler equations with a logarithmically regularized velocity given by $u=\nabla^{\perp}(-Δ)^{-1}\ln^{-γ}(|\nabla|+e)ω$ and initial vorticity in $\dot{H}^1 \cap \dot{H}^{-1}(\mathbb{R}^2)$. We show that if $γ>1/2$, then global well-posedness holds.

papers.title: Quantum-enhanced mechanical sensing with machine-learning estimation
papers.abstract: Massive mechanical oscillators couple directly to forces, accelerations and gravity, making them attractive probes of new physics and of quantum mechanics at macroscopic scales. Pushing sensitivities beyond the standard quantum limit for signals of unknown phase requires non-Gaussian quantum states, whose metrological advantage has so far been confined to lighter systems such as trapped ions. Here we operate a microgram-scale acoustic mode of a high-overtone bulk acoustic wave resonator as a phase-insensitive quantum-enhanced sensor. A transmon qubit prepares the mode in Fock states of up to seven phonons by optimal control, and resolves its phonon-number distribution after interaction with a weak resonant signal. Bayesian analysis yields a Fisher information five times the vacuum value, a 7.0 dB gain in signal-amplitude sensitivity over any classical probe state, irrespective of its energy, currently limited by state preparation infidelities. We then train a neural network on the measured sensor response to perform Bayesian estimation without any analytical model of the system, showing the same sensitivity gain with half the systematic bias. Our results establish acoustic resonators prepared in non-Gaussian states as quantum-enhanced probes for high-frequency gravitational waves, dark matter and wave-function collapse.

papers.title: Bipartite Matching with Few Rounds of Demand Queries
papers.abstract: We study the randomised and deterministic demand-query complexity of approximate bipartite matching with few query rounds. The demand-query model, introduced in [Blumrosen and Nisan SICOMP 2009; Nisan SODA 2021], is inspired by combinatorial auctions and welfare maximisation, where an oracle returns the first neighbouring vertex (item) of a vertex u (agent) according to a given permutation pi (preference ordering of the agent over the items). For randomised algorithms, our main result gives a trade-off between the number of rounds k, the per-round query budget q=n^{1+δ}, and the achievable approximation ratio. Let 1 <= k <= log n, and -1 <= delta <= 1/k. Every k-round randomised algorithm using O(q) demand queries per round has a worst-case expected-size approximation factor of Omega(n^{1/2k-delta/2}/k). Conversely, we give a randomised algorithm achieving approximation factor O(n^{(1-k*delta)/(k+1)}/k) in expectation. For deterministic algorithms, for k*q >= n, we show that the optimal deterministic approximation factor is ~Theta(n^2/(q*k^2)), thereby improving the previous lower bound of [Nisan SODA 2021] by a polynomial factor over a wide range of parameters. In particular, for q=Theta(n), we improve the deterministic round-complexity lower bound for constant-factor approximation from ~Omega(n^{1/3}) to ~Omega(sqrt n). Our algorithms produce matching and vertex-cover certificates; the deterministic trade-off also extends to minimum vertex cover and maximum fractional matching. We extend the randomised upper bounds to the weaker Demand-OR model [Nisan 2021]. We prove a non-adaptive simulation of uniform random-neighbour queries using known techniques, avoiding the O(log n)-round penalty of the trivial binary-search simulation. Consequently, our upper bounds yield the same k-round approximation guarantees using O(q * log^2 n) Demand-OR queries per round.

papers.title: Deterministic and programmable generation of mechanical multipartite entangled states
papers.abstract: Multimode mechanical resonators offer a large set of densely packed, long-lived bosonic modes within a single compact device, making them attractive for quantum simulation, quantum information processing, and quantum-enhanced sensing. Many such applications rely on multipartite entanglement, yet deterministic mechanical entanglement has so far been largely limited to pairs of modes. Here we demonstrate the deterministic and programmable preparation of multipartite entangled states among the phonon modes of a high-overtone bulk acoustic wave resonator coupled to a superconducting transmon qubit. By sequentially applying optimal-control-engineered isometries between the qubit and successive modes, we generate matrix product states of bond dimension two, including $W$, Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ), and cluster states. We fully characterize these states via quantum state tomography and certify genuine multipartite entanglement among up to four modes. We further demonstrate correlated-noise sensing by exploiting the complementary decoherence responses of the stored $W$ and GHZ states, isolating inter-mode phase correlations from local decoherence and placing quantitative bounds on collective dephasing. Our results establish a scalable approach to preparing multipartite entangled states in mechanical systems, with promising applications in multiparameter sensing and tests of quantum mechanics with massive objects.

papers.title: GAD: Geometry Attention Distillation for Consistent Video Generation
papers.abstract: Video diffusion models generate visually compelling short-term sequences but often struggle to preserve scene geometry and object structure over time. In this paper, we first demonstrate that current video attention cannot identify reliable correspondences across frames, with responses dispersed across multiple regions even after recognizable scene structure has emerged. We argue that reliable cross-frame associations are essential for information exchange as scene structure forms in video generation. Thus, we introduce Geometry Attention Distillation (GAD), which transfers correspondences from a frozen geometry model's attention to video attention. Extracted from clean videos, these correspondences link the same static surface or moving object across frames. Since structure formation begins in deeper layers at higher noise and shallower layers at lower noise, we apply attention distillation at a student layer selected according to the noise timestep. After training, video attention focuses more consistently on corresponding locations. Experiments across all three video backbones demonstrate improved long-range scene consistency and dynamic temporal consistency, with geometric gains across generation lengths. On Wan2.2 5B, GAD improves cross-frame matching accuracy by at least 30% over the Wan baseline on both long-range benchmarks. Notably, GAD achieves these gains without additional inference modules, offering a promising approach to efficient and consistent video-based world simulation. Project page: https://fantasy-amap.github.io/GAD/.

papers.title: BLADE: Auditing Information Use for Failure Attribution in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Large language model multi-agent systems extend individual agents' capabilities through collaboration across specialized roles, tools, and workflows. Yet collaboration makes failures harder to diagnose: one agent may misinterpret a correct result while others carry the mistake forward. Failure attribution therefore seeks to identify the responsible agent and decisive error step. Recent methods trace dependencies, but knowing where information came from is not the same as knowing where it went wrong. We introduce BLADE (Blame Localization via Audited Dependency Evidence), a training-free framework that moves beyond tracing information to auditing its use. Using Jev for structured probabilistic judgments, BLADE uses dependency probabilities to select relevant source-decision handoffs for auditing. At these handoffs, it examines whether receiving decisions use their sources faithfully and within task requirements, distinguishing error introduction, propagation, and repair. These findings inform a global diagnosis that considers all execution steps. Without reference answers, BLADE achieves the best or tied-best step accuracy among eight strategies under a shared Jev decision interface on 1,228 failed runs across five Who&When and Who&When Pro subsets, outperforming All-at-once by 2.2-11.1 percentage points. Making responsibility evidence explicit offers a path toward more interpretable and reliable agentic systems.

papers.title: Designing for Prediction: Planning Formulas for Expected Out-of-Sample $R^2$ and $r$
papers.abstract: Design calculations let researchers gauge, before data is collected, whether a planned study is likely to detect an effect. In this paper, we develop such calculations for predictive models using ordinary least squares and ridge regression under leave-one-out cross-validation. To do so, we derive closed-form expressions relating the expected out-of-sample $R^2$ and the expected correlation between observed and predicted outcomes to four design-stage quantities: sample size, number of predictors, an assumed population $R^2$ ($ρ^2_{in}$) and a design efficiency factor $D^*$ (which summarizes how leverage is distributed across observations). Unlike the classical shrinkage formulas, which depend only on sample size and dimension, these are sensitive to how covariates are arranged -- to imbalance and skew. A simulation study assesses the accuracy of the formulas against realized values under a variety of data generating mechanisms. We apply the methods to a published study predicting personality from smartphone behavior and show that the design formulas would have indicated, before any analyses were run, that least squares could not be expected to beat the sample mean while ridge could. An R package, predpower, implements the calculations.

papers.title: Late-time electric screening in dS from EAdS loops
papers.abstract: We compute the one-loop gauge-field two-point functions analytically in scalar QED on dS$_{d+1}$ for general dimension and scalar mass, using the EAdS reformulation of the in-in formalism arXiv:2007.09993. The Dirichlet EAdS gauge field acquires a Schwinger-type mass, with its longitudinal mode supplied by a composite of charged scalars obeying opposite boundary conditions, while the Neumann mode remains protected by gauge invariance. In dS, the Dirichlet correction induces an anomalous dimension $γ_J$ for the boundary current and modifies the late-time falloff of the electric field. This bulk calculation reproduces the boundary multiplet-recombination result of arXiv:2509.18888. Summing over the in-in contour branches gives the retarded dS bubble kernel, making direct contact with the Bros-Moschella framework. We establish a spectral Cutkosky rule that expresses the discontinuity of this kernel across the principal-series cut in the Casimir plane in terms of a two-particle cut, with both internal scalar lines placed on shell. Although the full bubble coefficient involves a ${}_7F_6$ hypergeometric function, the cut collapses to a closed product of Gamma functions and determines the complete non-local part of the kernel through a dispersion relation. Analytic continuation of the same cut reproduces the complete one-loop result for $γ_J$. In the complex Casimir plane, the loop-corrected Dirichlet photon appears as a pole on the second sheet and is therefore naturally interpreted as a dS resonance, or quasinormal mode, whose frequency is shifted at one loop.

papers.title: A Künneth theorem for the cyclic homology of A-infinity algebras
papers.abstract: The cyclic homology of a $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-graded, smooth and proper $A_\infty$ category satisfying the Hodge-to-de-Rham degeneration property carries the structure of a polarized semi-infinite Hodge structure or the so-called EP-structure. Given two $A_\infty$ algebras $A$ and $B$ with the above conditions, we construct a Künneth map from the tensor product of their cyclic homologies to the cyclic homology of the $A_\infty$ tensor product $A\otimes_\infty B$ and show that it respects the EP-structures. As an application, we show that if $A$ and $B$ are equipped with weak Calabi-Yau structures, then $A\otimes_\infty B$ also inherits a weak Calabi-Yau structure. Also, we show that the Künneth quasi-isomorphism respects good splittings of the Hodge filtration on $A$ and $B$ compatible with the weak Calabi-Yau structure. Our explicit calculations rely on the combinatorial (tree) description of the tensor product of $A_\infty$ algebras developed in \cite{amorim2016tensor}.

papers.title: Stably exotic knotted surfaces up to equivalence
papers.abstract: In this short note we show the existence of stably exotic knotted surfaces in 4-manifolds in the sense that the embedded surfaces are topologically equivalent but are not smoothly equivalent even after any number of internal and external stabilisations.

papers.title: Pack Light, CarryOn: Building Object-Oriented Context for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.abstract: Long-horizon agents accumulate progress in persistent task state, yet repeatedly process interaction histories describing how that progress was achieved. This raises a natural question: can long-horizon context instead be organized around reusable progress rather than the history that produced it? In this paper, we introduce CarryOn, an object-oriented context runtime that organizes continuation around reusable task objects. Rather than treating compressed histories or reconstructed accounts of progress as the primary basis for continuation, CarryOn builds a context view from continuation carriers, complementary execution context, and a live tail of recent interactions. A core challenge is keeping this reusable basis valid after its surrounding history is retired: how can CarryOn update the basis without reconstructing the full representation at every fold? CarryOn maintains carrier records across folds, revising affected records against bound evidence and applicable environment checks while carrying forward unaffected records and jointly updating execution context. Experiments on OSWorld 2.0 and BrowseComp-Plus show improved gains of 5.8% and 7.0% while reducing total token usage by 51.9% and 22.9%, respectively. Project page: https://ethannju.github.io/carryon

papers.title: Relative-Entropy Geometry and Convergence in Nonconvex Wiretap Optimization
papers.abstract: We develop and analyze an entropic descent method for a nonconvex optimization problem on probability simplices arising in classical and quantum secure communication. The optimization variables describe a randomized encoder, allowing its input distribution and stochastic preprocessing to be optimized jointly. An exact relative-entropy identity yields a channel-independent majorization bound and an explicit mirror-descent iteration with a fixed unit step size. We establish quantitative descent, convergence of objective values, and stationarity of accumulation points on their support faces for arbitrary finite classical channels, without assuming degradedness or less noisiness. For strictly positive transition matrices, a square-root parametrization and a Kurdyka--Łojasiewicz argument establish finite length of the transformed trajectory and convergence of the entire sequence, including limits on the simplex boundary. For less-noisy channels, a restricted convex formulation admits global convergence with an explicit \(O(1/t)\) objective-error bound. We extend the relative-entropy construction to noncommuting quantum outputs and derive monotone alternating updates for covariant encoders, including correlated preprocessing over a fixed block. Numerical experiments compare the method with analytic benchmarks and constrained optimization, reveal multiple attracting values, and demonstrate strict improvements from stochastic preprocessing.

papers.title: Where Do LLM Ensemble Gains Come From? Decomposing Candidate Value, Diversity, and Aggregation
papers.abstract: LLM ensemble gains are often measured against a single baseline, but the value attributed to additional candidates can change with the comparison used. We study an LLM aggregator under four matched conditions: Direct (no candidates), Single-slot (one candidate in a multi-slot interface), Duplicate (one candidate repeated), and Multi-candidate (separately generated candidates). Under either non-diverse control, overall candidate gain (CIV) splits algebraically into an additional-candidate contrast (DSV) and a candidate-context contrast (CCV); the split, but not CIV, depends on the chosen control. On MultiHopRAG model diversity (k=2), the repetition gap Rep=-8.33 pp [-13.25, -3.75] quantifies the difference between gains measured against Duplicate and Single-slot. On a matched FRAMES stronger-panel extension (n=200, k=3, aggregator output limit 4096), paired Delta Rep=+9.67 pp [+6.00, +13.50]; within panels, Rep changes sign (original -6.33; stronger +3.33). In FRAMES evidence aggregation, candidate-context contrasts remain strongly negative under both non-diverse controls. Our results show why ensemble evaluations should state the reference control before attributing gains to additional candidates.

papers.title: OpenMidnight: Closing the Performance Gap Between Open and Proprietary Pathology Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Pathology foundation models offer transferable representations for a range of downstream tasks in computational pathology, but reliance on proprietary data, substantial compute requirements, and limited availability of training code and preprocessing pipelines hinder independent validation and further methodological development. We present OpenMidnight 1.1, an open-source replication and refinement of Midnight trained on approximately 12,000 publicly available whole-slide images from The Cancer Genome Atlas. Using an encoder initialized with pretrained DINOv2 weights, OpenMidnight 1.1 uses approximately 320 H100 GPU-hours for pathology pretraining, a 34-fold reduction relative to the compute reported for Midnight. Across 16 classification and four segmentation datasets in THUNDER, OpenMidnight 1.1 achieves the highest mean segmentation Dice (69.7) and ranks fourth among 14 models, ahead of Midnight, with performance that matches or exceeds models trained on substantially larger datasets in several tasks. Our ablation studies additionally examine how initialization, data volume, model size, and tissue composition affect downstream performance, providing empirical evidence to inform the development of future training recipes. Our release of the training code, preprocessing pipeline, and model weights lowers barriers to reproducible research and further development of competitive pathology foundation models.

papers.title: Bytes to Threats: Byte-Sequence Transformer For Malware Detection
papers.abstract: Existing malware detection approaches heavily rely on handcrafted features derived from static or dynamic analysis of the executable files. These methods require specialized domain expertise, dedicated analysis tools, and time-consuming analysis, which limits their scalability and robustness in the face of the increasing complexity and diversity of modern malware. Consequently, there is a growing interest in approaches that operate directly on raw bytes, which contain rich semantic and structural information. However, capturing long-range dependencies within executable files remains challenging for conventional static and CNN-based methods. This paper presents MalwareFormer, a transformer-based, byte-level malware detection framework that operates directly on raw bytes, without requiring domain knowledge or feature extraction. MalwareFormer achieves an accuracy of 98.35%, a balanced accuracy of 98.32%, a macro-F1 of 98.32%, and a false positive rate of 1.94%, outperforming both baselines across all threshold-dependent classification metrics and demonstrating that transformers provide a powerful and scalable approach for byte-level malware detection.

papers.title: A three-block higher-rank deformed Hermitian--Yang--Mills correspondence on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$
papers.abstract: We study the invariant rank-four deformed Hermitian--Yang--Mills equation associated with the chain $\mathcal{O}(1)\to\mathcal{O}(2)^{\oplus2}\to\mathcal{O}(3)$ over $\mathbb P^1$, with vertical weights $(4,2,0)$ and a fixed product Kähler class and phase. For arbitrary linear arrows $ψ=Bz$ and $φ=(Az)^T$, smooth strictly calibrated reduced solutions exist exactly when $A$ is invertible and $z^TA^TBz$ is not identically zero. The same condition characterizes stability, semistability and polystability in the specified equivariant coherent category. The classification includes all eleven nonempty coefficient strata and both coincident and distinct divisor points on the rank-one lower boundary. The analytic proof retains the ordered, noncommuting middle equation. After constructing positive-parameter solutions, it rules out unbounded metric values by combining the source budgets with moving spectral tests; on the rank-one lower boundary, the divisor mass must also be retained. Global value, gradient and symbol estimates then give a smooth strictly calibrated endpoint on the original chain. No equivalence with full coherent or derived-category stability, uniqueness, or estimate uniform across changing chains is asserted.

papers.title: SituHOI: Scalable Capture of Scene-Situated Full-Body Human-Object Interaction
papers.abstract: Modeling human-object interaction (HOI) in real environments requires jointly representing whole-body motion, manipulated objects, and scene geometry, yet existing datasets trade off scalable capture against structured, scene-aligned supervision. We introduce SituHOI, a large-scale RGB-D dataset containing 18,429 annotated clips across 16 indoor rooms and approximately 86 hours of quality-screened activity. It pairs recordings from a single moving RGB-D camera with static scene scans, object geometry, language descriptions, and estimated human and object trajectories. Using the scans as persistent references, our pipeline combines camera localization and depth-based metric alignment with human mesh recovery, object tracking, and temporal refinement to register all geometric annotations in a shared floor-aligned frame. These data support FlexHOI-Bench, a goal-conditioned joint motion prediction benchmark with variable observation and prediction durations. Given observed histories, scene and object geometry, and a terminal object pose, models predict future human and object motion. We provide SharedHOI as a reference predictor and evaluate world-space accuracy and human-object coordination. On a MoCap subset, our pipeline reduces human G-MPJPE from 195.4 to 68.3 mm and object translation error from 43.0 to 28.7 mm. SharedHOI leads four adapted baselines on all three aggregate FlexHOI-Bench metrics. Data will be released upon acceptance. An anonymized code repository is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/iclr2027-anonymous-code-1DFB.

papers.title: Trust Before Autonomy: Rethinking Agentic Remote Sensing for Crisis Response
papers.abstract: Agentic remote sensing is evaluated on how many questions it can answer, whereas crisis response depends on whether its answers can be relied on and how much of the decision can safely be handed to the agent. This paper argues that \emph{autonomy should be earned, not assumed}: An Earth-Observation (EO) agent should be granted autonomy in proportion to demonstrated reliability, epistemic honesty and verifiability. The position is supported by an evidential meta-analysis of twelve agentic RS/EO/GIS benchmark studies from peer-reviewed venues. Only one repeats runs, three contain unanswerable tasks and none measures calibration. Their own tables show that completed workflows are often not correct (task success exceeds tool-call correctness by up to 54pp on identical queries), that the gap to an expert trajectory widens overall with trajectory length (from 7 to 56pp), and that capability does not predict abstention (Spearman r from -0.25 to 0.50, all n.s.). The paper then contributes three EO-specific trust properties, an autonomy ladder for crisis EO tasks, and a readiness protocol that replays archived emergency activations before any live use. In this context, current evidence justifies assistive roles only.

papers.title: EqC: Equilibrium Energy Control for Introspective Lifelong Robot Learning
papers.abstract: Long-term robot autonomy depends on more than effective action generation: a policy must recognize when its behavior is no longer sufficiently supported and use assistance to improve. We introduce Equilibrium Energy Control (EqC), a framework for introspective lifelong robot learning built around an explicit conditional energy landscape. EqC casts generative action refinement as equilibrium-seeking optimization, while the geometry of the refinement process reveals whether the generated behavior remains consistent with the learned landscape. This competence signal enables Energy-Gated DAgger, where persistent energy-consistency violations trigger expert takeover and the resulting recovery trajectories are aggregated for subsequent policy updates. EqC integrates naturally into both Diffusion Transformer policies and flow-matching-based vision-language-action (VLA) policies. Across simulation and real-world bimanual manipulation, EqC matches or improves control performance and robustness while enabling timely intervention near the policy's competence boundary. A real-world study further shows how these interventions progressively expand the range of situations handled autonomously, providing a practical path from static generative controllers toward self-improving robot systems.

papers.title: Embossing of Tapered, Isometric Micro-Interdigitated Flow Fields for Enhanced Desalination by Faradaic Deionization
papers.abstract: Engineered transport architectures can improve electrolyte distribution and active-material utilization in porous electrodes, yet their implementation remains limited by fabrication methods that compromise precision, throughput, active-material preservation, or scalability. Here, an integrated embossing-calendering method is introduced to pattern Prussian blue analog (PBA) porous electrodes with embedded, micro-interdigitated flow fields (e$μ$-IDFFs) for electrochemical desalination. This non-subtractive, roll-to-roll compatible method forms channels by controlling plastic deformation while simultaneously calendering the electrode, preserving active material and reducing patterning time by 100-fold relative to mechanical milling. Indentation experiments and a closed-form model further show that embossing requires 15-fold less force than stamping, while electrode microstructures show local densification beneath embossed channels. PBA electrodes are embossed with novel e$μ$-IDFFs that use continuous width-tapering with isometric flow paths that promote uniform electrolyte distribution, increase rate capability, and reduce polarization. Compared with e$μ$-IDFFs patterned using less scalable means and non-isometric flow paths, these e$μ$-IDFFs desalinate seawater-salinity feeds near to potable levels with 1.5-fold of its thermodynamic energy efficiency and water recovery. Brackish desalination benefits similarly. Tapered, isometric e$μ$-IDFFs and the embossing method introduced to pattern them are readily translated other electrochemical energy storage and separations systems.

papers.title: SEAR: Self-Evolving Agentic Robotics
papers.abstract: Frontier language-model agents can now improve robots on their own: they write control code, test it, and keep what works as skills and memories for the next task. We introduce SEAR (Self-Evolving Agentic Robotics), a framework and benchmark built around two questions. Is the agent really learning, or just trying more often? And does what it learns still help on new tasks, in a new simulator, and on a real robot? The framework runs an agent in three modes: it writes code that becomes the policy (code-as-policy), acts live in the control loop (agent-as-policy), or works as a researcher that fine-tunes a vision-language-action model (auto-research). The benchmark adds controls that separate retained experience from repeated attempts, familiar tasks, privileged simulator state, larger budgets, and luck. Across seven frontier language models, 330 simulated and five physical tasks, and over four years of agent runtime, we highlight three findings. First, the learning curve of a robotic agent depends both on the overall time budget and the task difficulty relative to model capability. Harder tasks make longer sessions worthwhile; on easier tasks, re-rolling short attempts does just as well. Second, control code and shared routines transfer across tasks and simulators, while task-specific solutions do not. On a real robot, we observe a performance gap between agent-designed practice and novel human-designed scenes. Third, different models evolve more effectively in different ways. Some do best acting live, others writing code first. And a text-only model keeps pace with a comparable multimodal one: perception helps with error assessment, but agentic reasoning and tool use can matter more. We release the benchmark and codebase to support future research.

papers.title: Sharp Yamabe Bounds for Spherical Three-Space Forms via Four-Dimensional Poincaré--Einstein Compactness
papers.abstract: Let $Γ<SO(4)$ be a nontrivial finite group acting freely on $S^3$, and let $M=S^3/Γ$. We prove that every smooth conformal class $C$ on $M$ satisfies \[ Y(M,C)\le |Γ|^{-2/3}Y(S^3), \] with equality for the quotient-round conformal class. Consequently, \[ σ(M)=|Γ|^{-2/3}Y(S^3). \] Our approach uses four-dimensional Poincaré--Einstein fillings of the ball. We first establish compactness for fillings whose conformal infinities range over a compact family of positive-scalar-curvature metrics. Since compactness alone does not guarantee continuation through degenerate Einstein metrics, we use equivariant Fredholm parity to obtain a filling with the prescribed boundary conformal class and group action. A common interior fixed point then makes the Li--Qing--Shi boundary test function invariant, and its descent to $M$ gives the sharp covering factor.

papers.title: Brain Age Gap Progression in Individuals at Risk for Neurodegeneration
papers.abstract: Neuroimaging is a widely used modality for characterizing neurodegeneration in various health conditions. Brain age gap has emerged as a promising biomarker for monitoring brain health from neuroimaging data using machine learning algorithms. Recent studies have leveraged coVariance neural networks (VNN)-driven pipelines based on the advancements in graph signal processing for relatively transparent construction of brain age gap from neuroimaging data. In this paper, we focus on a longitudinal study of VNN-based brain age gap in conjunction with Alzheimer's Progression Score (APS) in individuals that are at a higher risk of neurodegeneration due to family history of Alzheimer's disease. APS is a multimodal marker of disease progression. The longitudinal analysis of APS and VNN-derived brain age gap metrics revealed that a higher risk of disease progression at baseline predicted a larger rate of increase in brain age gap in follow-up visits. Thus, our findings revealed potential stratification in the brain age gap modulated by clinical/biological risks of AD in the at-risk population.

papers.title: Discrete-Time Survival Modelling with Dynamic Industrial Graphs for Mortgage Credit Risk
papers.abstract: Mortgage credit risk may exhibit dependence across economically connected areas, even when they are geographically distant. However, current models typically represent cross-area dependence through fixed geographical neighbourhoods, potentially overlooking economic connections that extend beyond physical proximity and evolve over time. These models may fail to capture shared risks among geographically distant but economically similar areas, and cannot describe a changing dependence of risk; it therefore risks retaining economically obsolete connections while omitting newly emerging ones. This paper uses similarities of industrial composition as a measure of economic proximity and develops a discrete-time survival model with dynamic industrial graphs to capture evolving cross-area dependence in mortgage default risk. The resulting graphs are reconstructed annually, allowing both their topology and edge weights to change as regional industrial compositions evolve. Jointly combining a proper conditional autoregressive process with a first-order autoregressive process governs the temporal cross-area dependence and the temporal persistence in latent risk simultaneously. The model is estimated using Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation and evaluated on U.S. mortgage loan-level data against the static industrial graph specifications. The results show that the proposed dynamic model achieves better in-sample fit and out-of-sample discrimination, while its estimated parameters indicate substantial graph-induced cross-area dependence and temporal persistence. These findings demonstrate the value of allowing economically defined neighbourhoods to evolve when modelling mortgage default risk.

papers.title: Information-theoretic measures of electron correlation in a double quantum dot
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigated how variations in spatial confinement affect the electron correlation between two electrons in a symmetric double quantum dot. In strong confinement regime, the ground-state energy can be obtained using the Hartree-Fock method neglecting the electron-electron repulsion term. Under a weaker confinement, the FCI method provides a more accurate description. Using the mutual information as a measure of correlation, we determine the confinement regions where electronic motion is uncorrelated. We conjecture that the Shannon entropy can serve as a qualitative guide to to study the electron correlation. We identified an approximately linear relationship between mutual information and relative correlation energy.

papers.title: $λ_0$: Scaling Open-World Egocentric Human Data for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
papers.abstract: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires coordinated whole-body interaction with the physical world, yet collecting robot demonstrations at scale remains costly. Human demonstrations offer a scalable alternative, but existing egocentric human supervision often omits locomotion and posture, while embodiment differences and controller dynamics hinder accurate end-effector execution. We introduce HumanVerse, a 500-hour dataset of open-world human loco-manipulation pairing egocentric video with synchronized body and hand motion. Our human-to-humanoid pipeline aligns camera viewpoints and arm appearance, and refines motion references and controller inputs offline to reduce end-effector errors while preserving whole-body coordination. We validate the pipeline through zero-shot transfer to Unitree G1 on representative whole-body manipulation and long-range loco-manipulation tasks, without target-task robot demonstrations. Building on this pipeline, we develop $λ_0$, a humanoid foundation model for whole-body loco-manipulation, with robot-aligned human demonstrations providing supervision for mid-training. Increasing whole-body human data consistently improves downstream task progress. $λ_0$ achieves 90.0% success on SIMPLE and 62.5% across real-world loco-manipulation tasks. We expect this study to guide scalable whole-body human data collection toward humanoid foundation models for richer interaction with the physical world. Homepage: https://lambdahumanoid.github.io/

papers.title: Global existence of smooth solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations for initial data with infinite energy
papers.abstract: We prove the global existence of solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations for any divergence-free distributional initial data. The solutions are smooth in both time and space at positive times. When the initial data belong to the Sobolev spaces $W^{-1,p}$ for $1<p<\infty$, our constructed solutions are weak in the classical sense. We also characterize the distributional initial data admitting weak solutions and obtain the sharp ranges in Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces.

papers.title: Non-Wellfounded and Cyclic Proofs for LTL: A Syntactic Correspondence with Linear Nested Sequents
papers.abstract: We introduce the formalism of non-wellfounded and cyclic linear nested sequent calculi, developing concrete systems for linear temporal logic (LTL). The paper addresses two central problems, which we call "cycle recognition" and "unraveling." Cycle recognition concerns identifying cycles in non-wellfounded proofs in order to extract corresponding cyclic proofs, while unraveling studies the converse transformation, from cyclic proofs to non-wellfounded ones. Although these processes are well understood for Gentzen sequents, they have received little attention for more expressive sequent formalisms and become more challenging in the linear nested sequent setting. To address cycle recognition, we show the completeness of non-wellfounded proofs relative to a particular normal form exhibiting a property we call "saturation recurrence," which enables the systematic extraction of cyclic proofs. To address unraveling, we introduce a specialized procedure that shifts rule applications forward along linear nested sequents, allowing non-wellfounded proofs to be reconstructed from cyclic ones. Overall, our work provides new proof-theoretic techniques for cycle recognition and unraveling in expressive multisequent formalisms.

papers.title: $\mathsf{EFI}\Leftrightarrow\mathsf{1PRS}$
papers.abstract: A series of recent works has established EFI pairs as the "minimal" assumption for quantum cryptography. Recently, Cavalar et al. [CCC+26] showed that EFI pairs are equivalent to non-uniform expanding single-copy pseudorandom state generators (1PRS), and obtained a non-uniform meta-complexity characterization of EFI pairs. We remove the non-uniformity in their construction and prove that EFI pairs are equivalent to expanding 1PRS. As a corollary, we obtain the first uniform meta-complexity characterization of EFI pairs. Together with the equivalence of statistically verifiable one-way state generators and commitments proved by Batra and Jain [BJ24], this gives a quantum analogue of the classical equivalence between one-way functions, commitments, and pseudorandom generators.

papers.title: Spin textures at the Fermi surface of ferromagnets and associated torque
papers.abstract: We establish theoretically that transverse spin textures are generically induced by the spin-orbit interaction at the Fermi surface of centrosymmetric ferromagnetic metals. We confirm this prediction with {\em ab initio} computations for Fe, Co and Ni. By symmetry, this cannot be associated with spin-orbit torques under a uniform current. However, a new {\em current-gradient-induced} torque emerges in nanoscale geometries. For a series of Ni-based bilayers, the computed Ni thickness dependence of the current-gradient-induced torque is in quantitative agreement with measurements previously attributed to orbital torques. We discuss how this opens a new avenue for the electrical control of magnetic orders, possibly also including the Néel vector of metallic altermagnets.

papers.title: Cellular Algebra of $A_2$ webs
papers.abstract: We introduce a diagram algebra $\mathcal{K}_L$ based on Kuperberg's $A_2$-webs and prove a Schur--Weyl duality $\mathcal{K}_L \cong \operatorname{End}_{U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)}((V^+ \oplus V^-)^{\otimes L})$, where $V^\pm$ are the fundamental representations of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$. Thus, $\mathcal{K}_L$ is a natural $A_2$ analogue of the Temperley--Lieb algebra. We construct an explicit cellular structure for $\mathcal{K}_L$, with the web basis as its cellular basis and cell modules indexed by dominant $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$-weights. The bases of these modules are parametrized by dominant lattice paths via a recursive growth algorithm. Using this structure, we determine local generators of $\mathcal{K}_L$ and establish web formulations of the first and second fundamental theorems of invariant theory. In particular, we show that the braid-group image, augmented by local idempotents, does not generate $\mathcal{K}_L$, and identify an additional local generator. Finally, we derive a bimodule decomposition of $(V^+ \oplus V^-)^{\otimes L}$, yielding a complete set of irreducible $\mathcal{K}_L$-modules for formal or generic $q$.

papers.title: Branching explosion of Brownian Fleming-Viot systems
papers.abstract: We resolve the long-standing non-extinction problem for Brownian Fleming-Viot systems in bounded domains. For every fixed N >= 3, we construct a bounded connected domain in R3 in which branching explosion occurs with positive probability before every prescribed positive time, from every interior initial configuration. On this event all particles converge to one boundary point. Together with two-particle non-extinction, this gives the sharp population threshold for bounded-domain Brownian explosion. The mechanism is directed transport generated by uniform copying in a periodic absorbing environment. We compute a positive cubic current for the same two-harmonic killing profile at every N >= 3, with an explicit population coefficient and a controlled fourth-order remainder. To realize this transport by spherical absorption, we develop a marked genealogical transfer theorem that retains the Euclidean displacement inherited at each copy. Common ancestry makes the integer winding reconstructible from phase records and yields convergence of the stationary signed current. A boundary restart law with P'olya weights supplies the continuity needed to turn that current into stable escape. Diffusion coefficients adapted to a common Kelvin clock preserve the joint Brownian law and uniform donor marks while compressing escape into finite lifetime. Disjoint spherical holes in a ball accumulate only at the explosion point. The boundary is smooth elsewhere, with finite area and perimeter. Boundary area within distance r of the singularity is of order r. For three particles, the transfer theorem covers every smooth positive periodic killing rate.

papers.title: The Links--Gould polynomial of an alternating link is alternating
papers.abstract: Building on work of Kauffman--Saleur and earlier work of the second author, we derive a determinant formula for the Links--Gould polynomial of links. As an application, we prove a 20-year-old conjecture of Ishii: for any alternating link, the Links--Gould invariant is an alternating polynomial.

papers.title: Registration is a Representation Problem: Solving Whole-Body PET/CT Registration
papers.abstract: Raw image intensities are a poor surrogate for similarity across images in correspondence problems. Further, while auxiliary segmentation labels can provide semantic identification and improve matching, they can assign only coarse identities to fine-grained anatomy and often cover only a subset of structures, particularly in whole-body settings. We present an approach that instead establishes correspondence using complementary representations of anatomy and demonstrate its utility for longitudinal whole-body PET/CT registration in the Learn2Reg 2026 PSMAReg Challenge. We use our 3D foundation model, anatomix, to derive fine-grained, per-voxel semantic representations that are consistent across volumes and further employ off-the-shelf segmentation models to obtain coarse anatomical identities. Together, these representations drive a GPU-accelerated iterative registration solver (FireANTs) in a hybrid multistage framework: the first stage estimates alignment from dense multi-channel features, after which a second refines the deformation using both anatomix- and segmentation-based losses. Lastly, because registration should not introduce non-biological tumor volume changes across time, we develop lesion-specific, component-wise volume preservation schemes. Without any task-specific training, our system placed first on the PSMAReg Challenge leaderboard. Code and interactive visualizations are available at https://www.neeldey.com/reps-for-reg.

papers.title: Minimal presentations of finite-dimensional representations of pseudocompact algebras
papers.abstract: We give a general formula for minimal projective presentations and for minimal discrete-injective presentations of finite-dimensional modules over basic pseudocompact algebras. We also show that the representation-theoretic g-vector of a module coincides with its DWZ-g-vector. These results generalize the description that Derksen, Weyman and Zelevinsky gave of minimal projective presentations for modules over certain finite-dimensional Jacobian algebras. In particular, we can drop their finiteness assumption, and we may work over fields of arbitrary characteristic.

papers.title: A Spatial Map of the Atmospheric Limb of a Hot Jupiter
papers.abstract: Planets are inherently three-dimensional objects shaped by their thermal structure and dynamics. Observations of transiting exoplanets have begun to uncover this three-dimensional nature, with JWST measuring their dayside atmosphere structure with eclipse mapping, and exploring spectroscopic asymmetries in the limbs of planets during transit. We apply the novel mapping method of transmission strings to the hot Jupiter WASP-17b. With this method, we are not only able to extract hemispheric limb asymmetries from east-to-west, but can map equator-to-pole variations around the transmitting atmosphere as a function of angle, spanning 0.6-12$μ$m. We find a clear transition in the thermal scale height around the limb of the atmosphere, with a $\sim$650K temperature difference between the morning (T=858$^{+434}_{-233}$K) and evening (T=1522$^{+116}_{-114}$K). These results are consistent with both nightside emission and dayside eclipse mapping measurements, and represent a fully comprehensive set of observations for a transiting exoplanet. We are also able to constrain the abundances of H$_2$O and CO$_2$ to constant values around the limb, providing observational constraints to results from global circulation models. The transmission string technique combined with the outstanding observability of WASP-17b pushes the study of exoplanet atmospheres further into a three-dimensional understanding of hot Jupiter dynamics and chemistry

papers.title: SkillScaffold: Scaffolding Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Policy-Adaptive Skill Credit Assignment and Selective Injection
papers.abstract: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) enables large language models (LLMs) to learn from multi-turn interactions with verifiable outcomes. Textual skills can improve exploration by distilling prior interactions into reusable guidance. However, existing skill-based RL approaches often either assume skill injection is beneficial or rely on indirect feedback or rollout-intensive evaluation to assess its utility. Our pilot studies show that rollout-based utility estimation for skill credit assignment is costly and unstable under limited sampling, while skill benefits vary across candidates and depend on the current policy's competence on each query. To address these challenges, we introduce SkillScaffold, a policy-adaptive training scaffold that combines low-cost skill-utility estimation with selective skill injection. By reusing outcome-verified training trajectories, SkillScaffold generates candidate skills and estimates their utility through outcome-aware likelihood comparisons, without candidate-specific environment rollouts. The resulting utility guides whether and which skill to inject, retaining skill-free execution when no candidate is estimated to help. Joint training enables the Generator to produce skills tailored to the evolving Executor. Scaffolded RL encourages skill internalization for skill-free inference. Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, ScienceWorld, and $τ^2$-Bench demonstrate gains over strong agentic-RL and skill-based RL baselines across both short- and long-horizon tasks. Ablations and further analyses support the importance of utility-based selection and abstention. Our code is available at https://github.com/Vaidurya00/SkillScaffold.

papers.title: Optimizing Team Behavior via Extremum-seeking Control in Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: In cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), agents must learn to coordinate their actions to achieve shared objectives. A key indicator of effective coordination is behavioral diversity, i.e., the agents' potential to enact distinct yet complementary control policies given the same set of observations. Although behavioral diversity can enable role specialization and richer joint behaviors, its appropriate level is highly context- and task-dependent and often costly to tune. We propose Adaptive Diversity Control (ADiCo), a two-timescale framework that adapts behavioral diversity online during training. On a fast timescale, Diversity Control (DiCo) regulates system diversity toward a target value. On a slower timescale, an Extremum Seeking Controller (ESC) adjusts this target using only mean episodic returns, without requiring an explicit model or analytical gradient of the diversity-performance landscape. We evaluate ADiCo on six configurations across two cooperative MARL tasks, where it maintains task-appropriate diversity levels: low diversity when homogeneous policies are beneficial and higher diversity when heterogeneous policies are required. Through this adaptation, ADiCo matches or exceeds the mean performance of DiCo (best grid-searched diversity target) and Unconstrained DiCo (diversity allowed to emerge without target regulation). These results demonstrate that incorporating classical feedback control into MARL training enables effective coordination by providing a systematic alternative to task-specific manual selection of the diversity target.

papers.title: Depth Memory
papers.abstract: Residual connections propagate information through a network by additively accumulating layer outputs. Recently proposed alternatives, such as Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) and Attention Residuals (AttnRes), instead use more expressive depth aggregation mechanisms that improve language modeling performance at scale. In this work, we consider the mixing of representations over depth as a problem of storing and retrieving information across layers. Formalizing this perspective, we introduce Depth Memory (DM), a unified framework that describes the standard pre-layer-norm (PreLN) transformer, mHC, and AttnRes in terms of streams that carry representations through the network. One such stream, for example, could be an explicit memory stream that is queried to enrich the input to every layer, and whose output is subsequently written back into the memory for use by later layers. For AttnRes, this memory stream is a growing cache of explicit layer representations. For mHC, it is an expanded residual stream. Building on this view, we propose Linear Depth Memory (LDM), which formulates information retrieval across depth as a regression problem solved using recursive least squares. The resulting architecture propagates three streams across depth: the standard residual stream, a linear associative memory stream, and an inverse covariance stream. For high-throughput training and inference, we propose a hardware-aware implementation of LDM that reduces peak activation memory and memory traffic. LDM consistently achieves the lowest perplexities among PreLN, mHC and AttnRes baselines at the 400M and 1.5B parameter scales, alongside competitive zero-shot accuracy.

papers.title: Differential Luminosity Response of Balmer-Line Profiles in Galactic B/A Luminous Stars
papers.abstract: We investigate the differential luminosity response of the optical Balmer series from H8 to H-alpha in Galactic B5-A5 luminous stars using homogeneous measurements of central depth, FWHM, and equivalent width at a resolving power of approximately 12,000. Direct line-to-line comparisons show a systematic change in the central-depth response toward the lower-order transitions. For the primary 72-star luminosity sample, the fitted luminosity coefficients show an overall positive trend with upper-level quantum number, with a point-estimate gradient of dq/dn = 0.0419. A joint Monte Carlo analysis with 10,000 realisations gives a median dq/dn = 0.0387 and a 95 percent interval from 0.0253 to 0.0532, with no non-positive gradients obtained. The higher-order H8-H-delta coefficients form a statistically unresolved plateau, followed by a well-supported increase in response magnitude from H-delta toward H-alpha. The result is robust to the adopted effective-temperature scale. The FWHM coefficients show no comparable Balmer-order progression, and the directly fitted profile-shape response is consistent with zero from H8 through H-beta. For H-alpha, the full logarithmic sample is not formally significant, whereas removal of the three remaining strongly filled-core profiles yields a significantly negative shape response. The observed behaviour is qualitatively compatible with the systematic variation of pressure broadening across the Balmer series, while the enhanced H-alpha response may additionally reflect non-LTE and wind-related effects.

papers.title: Statistical Vignettes on the Grokking Phenomenon
papers.abstract: In this work, we study grokking in a simple, analytically tractable setting whose rich phenomenology allows us to disentangle the effects of initialization, signal strength, weight decay, sample size, and input dimension. These factors can produce superficially similar learning curves through distinct mechanisms, complicating their interpretation. Our analysis distinguishes early fitting through nuisance features, core feature learning, and delayed generalization. We identify sharp conditions under which grokking provably occurs and derive analytic asymptotic expressions for the lengths of the generalization plateaus. Our results also characterize regimes of early generalization and failure to reach a prescribed test accuracy target. We show that the interpolation edge constitutes a distinct dynamical regime, where vanishing spectral gaps separate core learning from generalization, helping clarify the role of proximity to interpolation in existing accounts of grokking. The resulting picture is analogous to fast and slow phases in chemical kinetics and suggests that the lazy-to-rich transition discussed in the literature may reflect a similar separation of dynamical time scales. Our theoretical results are faithfully supported by extensive experiments.

papers.title: The Geography of (Concurrent) Block Proposing
papers.abstract: The resilience and censorship resistance of a blockchain depend on where the validators and proposers of that blockchain physically operate. We study the economic incentives behind this location choice, both with a single proposer and with multiple concurrent proposers. Formally, we study a game where proposers first choose locations and then compete in a first-price auction for an opportunity whose common value is driven by information from geographically dispersed sources. A single proposer minimizes variance-weighted delay, locating at a weighted median of the sources and co-locating with any dominant one. By contrast, with two proposers, information both observe equally early earns no rent, and each proposer's expected profit is proportional to the standard deviation of the information it receives before its rival. We show that the location game admits the jointly unobserved variance as an ordinal potential, so global solutions of a weighted two-median problem are equilibria. With two sources, one proposer locates at each, however weak one is. With more proposers and at least as many sources, equilibrium locations are distinct under regular bidding. Multiple concurrent proposers thus do more than limit any single proposer's control over inclusion: by rewarding exclusive rather than shared information, they create an economic force toward geographic decentralization.

papers.title: Self-Evolving Agent Harness
papers.abstract: Harness self-evolution revises an agent's software scaffolding, including prompts, memory, workflows, and executable components, while keeping model weights fixed. We formalize a feedback-driven process in which accepted revisions persist across runs. The framework separates update targets from proposal and admission mechanisms. It distinguishes changes to interpreted state from revisions to tools and code, repository-level control logic, and plugin composition. We characterize search through evolutionary optimization and examine its reliability through continual PAC-learning. Under explicit assumptions, the analysis yields an expected generalization bound, a retention bound conditional on historical regression budgets, and a high-probability admission rule using fresh, independent validation data. We examine how persistent harness revisions affect knowledge sharing and organizational workflows, with implications for scientific reliability, physical safety, and institutional accountability. Cases from prior work illustrate model--harness co-design, distributed execution, and plugin reuse. Reliable deployment requires continual validation as task distributions and evaluators change, with independent safeguards for learning, runtime privileges, and consequential actions. We provide a comprehensive 66-page discussion of related work, theory, algorithms, evaluation, applications, and the broader impact of Harness RSI, together with continuously updated code and supplementary materials, at https://github.com/zgcagi/Harness-RSI.

papers.title: Towards synergy between theory and experiments: First-passage processes under resetting with stochastic return protocols
papers.abstract: Stochastic resetting with stochastic return (SR) has recently emerged as an effective and practically relevant strategy for controlling first-passage phenomena and optimizing search processes by significantly reducing completion times in a wide class of stochastic systems. While most theoretical studies assume instantaneous return (IR), in realistic systems the return to the resetting position typically occurs over a finite time. We consider a 1-d diffusing particle in a harmonic trap with stiffnesses $k_1$ and $k_2$ during search and return, respectively. The particle searches for the target and, upon resetting at rate $r$, enters the return phase, continuing until it reaches either the origin or the absorbing target at $L>0$. Notably, the model permits target detection throughout the return phase, distinguishing it from IR scenarios. We analytically derive the MFPT for our model and determine parameter regions where SR enhances or suppresses search efficiency over the underlying dynamics, constructing the corresponding phase diagram using the coefficient of variation criterion. We further identify regimes in which SR is more efficient than IR using the SR criterion. This behavior is tested across different parameter sets taken from experimental studies by Goerlich et al., Biroli et al., and Besga et al. We map the parameter values reported in existing experimental studies onto our theoretical phase diagram, thereby identifying the regimes in which SR outperforms IR. In particular, we find that the most relevant region of the phase space, where SR is most beneficial corresponds to larger values of the potential strength in the search phase and lower values of potential in the return phase. Our results provide experimentally testable predictions and bridge the gap between theoretical resetting models and optical trap mediated finite-time return dynamics.

papers.title: Counting quaternion extensions by multi-heights
papers.abstract: We prove a case of a conjecture of Gundlach on the number of Galois extensions over $\QQ$ with bounded multi-invariants for the group $G=Q_8$. We also obtain results when imposing local conditions at the wildly ramified place. As an application, we prove asymptotics for the number of $Q_8$-extensions with bounded product of ramified primes.

papers.title: On the coincidence of discrete and continuous definitions of Entanglement of Formation
papers.abstract: It is proved that every Borel ensemble of pure states on a separable bipartite Hilbert space with finite average entanglement admits a countable ensemble with the same barycenter and arbitrarily small additional average entanglement. Consequently, the discrete and continuous versions of the Entanglement of Formation coincide on the whole space of states of infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum system (with infinite values allowed). The main idea of the proof (realized with the AI-assistance) is the lifting a Borel ensemble of pure bipartite states to a Borel probability measure on the unit sphere in the space of Hilbert--Schmidt operators followed by dividing the support of this measure into appropriate cells and replacing each cell by its conditional barycenter. The resulting countable ensemble is obtained by a recursive construction.

papers.title: Single anyons and anyon binding in a quantum Hall dot
papers.abstract: Anyons are particles with quantized fractional statistics. In theory, a single anyon can be stabilized as a localized fractional charge within the bulk of a topologically ordered two-dimensional insulator. However, experiments to date have focused on probing anyons in structures in which many anyonic excitations coexist and interact. Here, we demonstrate the trapping of a single anyon in a device consisting of a graphene-based quantum point contact with an embedded tunable quantum Hall dot. Benchmarking our device at v = 1, we demonstrate backscattering between Fermi liquid edge states mediated by the whole-electron Coulomb blockade of the dot. The cleanliness and control available in our device allow depletion of the dot to the last quasihole, and we observe spin blockade for transitions to the opposite-spin Landau level. At v = 1/3 and 2/3, we observe backscattering resonances with three times the frequency, consistent with resonant transmission of e/3 charges via a single anyon transistor. We demonstrate controlled depletion to the last quasiparticle to form a single anyon quantum dot. Tracing the charge addition spectrum for quasiparticle number Nqp = 1-5, we observe highly irregular addition energies, consistent with DMRG modeling showing a complex orbital shell-filling behavior. At higher Nqp = 10-20, the addition energies show a striking pattern: quasiholes at 1/3 (and quasiparticles at 2/3) show a regular addition spectrum while quasiparticles at 1/3 (and quasiholes at 2/3) do not. We trace the origin of this irregularity to an attractive component of the inter-anyon interaction: by experimentally tuning the confining energy, we observe complete suppression of alternating charge sectors, after which the dot charges in increments of twice the fundamental charge. This observation indicates the emergence of an anyon binding energy as large as the charging energy.

papers.title: Back-Translation Still Matters: Leveraging Monolingual Data for Low-Resource Machine Translation with LLMs
papers.abstract: Pre-trained Large Language Model (LLMs) are effective on many tasks in zero-shot and few-shot settings. For machine translation of low-resource languages, the obvious options are few-shot prompting and fine-tuning on a small parallel set. We ask: what if moderate amounts of low-resource monolingual data are also available? We argue that, rather than continued pretraining, a more effective use of this data is the pre-LLM era technique of back-translation (BT). The current fine-tuned LLM translates monolingual sentences in each language, and the resulting pairs train it in the reverse direction. Updates on the parallel set are interleaved for stable learning. With 1K parallel pairs on Odia and Swahili, BT beats continued pretraining into the low-resource language by 7.7 to 16.4 XCOMET-XXL points in domain. With beam-decoded intermediate translations, it also beats a model with 10 time more parallel data. In-context examples retrieved from the parallel data further improve BT. We also analyze the source, quality and amount of monolingual text. Across five low-resource languages, with Hindi as a high-resource control, and two 3B backbones, BT improves translation into the low-resource language by 16 to 173% XCOMET-XXL over parallel-only fine-tuning. Blind human evaluation on Odia and Sanskrit agrees with the automatic metrics.

papers.title: DuplexBridge: Coordinating Understanding and Generation for Unified Image Editing
papers.abstract: Complex image editing requires faithful task interpretation and accurate execution, but a failed edit does not reveal which responsibility failed. We present DuplexBridge, which uses a unified model's own understanding capability to enhance prompts for its own generation capability, without an external understanding module. A source-grounded bridge specifies targets, final-state changes, and preservation constraints. Understanding is supervised on fidelity to the original request without observing the generated image; generation is supervised on execution of the condition it actually receives. Reciprocal trust checks selectively admit global task feedback to each role while retaining independently valid local supervision. We introduce CE-Bench, a 1,200-task benchmark measuring joint satisfaction of task-derived change and preservation requirements. Across three model configurations, the full system improves complete compliance over direct editors by 21.75-25.75 percentage points, with gains also observed on KRIS-Bench, RISEBench, ImgEdit, and GEdit-Bench. From a common supervised Wan-Image initialization, gated joint training reaches 77.08% complete compliance, compared with 70.92% without gates and 75.00% when generation-local supervision instead checks the original task with both gates retained.
