We formulate agentic self-awareness (ASA) as the alignment of task-grounded feasibility judgments (know), warranted behavior (act), and responses to reconsideration (hold), distinguishing what a task permits from what an agent can solve. We build paired feasible and blocked tasks in Terminal-Bench 2.1 and retail $τ^2$-bench and introduce an authorship-aware M0-M3 rubric that separates recognizing a blocker from taking the certified deferral action for the correct reason. Separate probes assess stated feasibility beliefs and responses to a single challenge. In a Terminal-Bench protocol baseline, blocker recognition reaches 84.4%, but strict self-awareness (SA) reaches only 40.6%. Harness search without model-weight updates increases strict SA from 45.3% to 93.8% on reused Terminal-Bench search tasks; selection for abstention alone, however, can reduce success on feasible tasks. Independently initialized joint-objective searches improve both blocked-task SA and feasible-task solve on their own search sets. Retail held-out gains remain limited, and Terminal-Bench blocked-task transfer is not measured. This evaluation pipeline makes the recognition-action gap measurable and sets a two-sided target for improving agent decisions under changing task evidence.

papers.title: Memento: Communicating Sensor Observations Through Shared Memory
papers.abstract: Wireless sensing systems often transmit highly redundant observations, making communication a bottleneck for low-power devices. We present Memento, a communication system that exploits recurring content by transmitting observations by reference. The sender embeds each observation and searches a shared vector table stored in persistent memory. When it finds a sufficiently similar prior observation, it sends a compact reference; otherwise, it sends the observation itself and adds it to the table. This design shifts work from wireless communication to local computation and storage, without requiring a fixed task-specific model. We implement Memento on a microcontroller with an SD card and evaluate it on three image datasets and one radar dataset. Memento provides favorable accuracy-communication and accuracy-energy tradeoffs against compression-based and task-oriented baselines. At high-accuracy operating points, it matches cloud classification accuracy on three workloads while using 5.5 to 27.1 times less energy, and comes within 0.14 percentage points on a fourth while using 14.7 times less energy. These results show that retrieval over persistent local memory can reduce communication costs in recurrent sensing workloads.

papers.title: Chandra-JWST Probing the Effects of Moderate X-Ray Superflares on Protoplanetary Disks
papers.abstract: Powerful X-ray flares from young stars may rapidly alter the physical and chemical conditions of their planet-forming disks, but direct observational tests remain scarce. We present a Chandra-JWST/NIRSpec study of infrared spectral variability associated with pre-main-sequence (PMS) X-ray flares in the Orion Nebula. Combining six Chandra/ACIS-I observations with three NIRSpec-MOS visits, we analyze two-epoch spectra of 10 X-ray Flare stars and 12 matched non-flaring Controls among 84 observed disk-bearing PMS stars. We investigate three diagnostics: narrow 2.8-4.3 micron features, HI Br-alpha, and the CO fundamental band. Flare stars show tentative evidence for relatively fewer variable narrow features at longer wavelengths than Controls, while feature incidence decreases strongly with projected distance from the dominant ionizing O star Theta1 Ori C. Most classifiable features appear in absorption. These properties suggest that at least some features may arise in externally irradiated disk atmospheres and/or associated photoevaporative flows, with their apparent epoch-to-epoch variability potentially reflecting spatial sampling of such locally structured material rather than intrinsic temporal changes. Br-alpha behaves differently: flare stars show systematically stronger variability and uniquely exhibit absorption-core profiles, suggesting control by magnetospheric accretion and stellar magnetic processes rather than disk irradiation. The CO fundamental band shows no significant flare-associated variability, consistent with thermochemical models predicting weak responses to moderate X-ray superflares. This pilot study demonstrates the potential of coordinated Chandra-JWST observations to probe how young stellar magnetic activity affects planet-forming environments, motivating future monitoring to build larger superflare samples and extend them into the rare X-ray mega-flare regime.

papers.title: Per-Bundle, Pre-Reconstruction Inversion for Temporal CT: Flux-Compensation Design and Training-Free Empirical-Bayes Estimation
papers.abstract: In Temporal computed tomography (TCT) each detector reading sums the photons of up to three rays. Earlier work set the resulting per-bundle limits and tested a learned prior on one patient at one incident count $N_0$; this paper lifts both. N$_0$FC ($N_0$ flux compensation), a bow-tie and tube-current-modulation co-design, equalizes each bundle's detected flux. SNN2 is a per-bundle Poisson maximum-likelihood estimator. V8c is a neural-network corrector trained on 19 patients stratified by water-equivalent diameter (WED). T2bp, a training-free empirical-Bayes post-processor, combines per-bundle Poisson likelihoods with a prior built from the patient's own bundles. Results use that work's Dose Inflation Factor (DIF), charging bias as error. On 23 non-test volumes, N$_0$FC lowers the per-volume median middle-path Cramer-Rao floor, as a DIF, from 23-48 under a flat-fluence (no bow-tie) baseline to 3.3-6.3 at 35-62% of its incident photons, near the equal-attenuation value 13/3 and 1.4-1.7 times below conventional bow-ties; the bow-tie alone achieves this median, and tube-current modulation trims the tail. For bundles with $X_2<6$ (83%), SNN2 attains this floor (median mean-squared-error ratio 1.02); training-free T2bp$\circ$SNN2 lowers the ratio to 0.89 (0.74-1.26). It is best or tied on three of four N$_0$FC test cells (WED 207-342 mm) and trails T2bp$\circ$V8c by 3% on the fourth. V8c beats SNN2 in distribution under baseline acquisition, gains at most 9% under N$_0$FC (losing 14% on the largest in-distribution test patient), and fails on a patient acquired below its training count level. Acquisition co-design removes most of the attenuation-contrast penalty, and training-free estimation attains the resulting limit. The remaining three- to six-fold gap to single-source CT at equal fluence, and the high-attenuation tail, are targets for inter-bundle priors.

papers.title: Generalized Fibonacci gates are Frobenius algebras: a proof of Liu's conjecture
papers.abstract: Liu introduced generalized Fibonacci gates on domains of size 3 and 4, proved that Holant problems built from them are tractable by a cut-and-merge algorithm, and conjectured that Fibonacci gates with matching polynomial-time algorithms exist on all higher domains. We extend the definition uniformly to every domain size $k$ and show that a family of domain-$k$ generalized Fibonacci gates is the same thing as a $k$-dimensional commutative Frobenius (equivalently, Artinian Gorenstein) algebra $A$ equipped with an orthonormal basis containing $1$. Under this dictionary Liu's parameter constraints are exactly associativity of $A$, a gate is an element $w\in A$, merging two gates is multiplication in $A$, and the Holant value of a connected graph $G$ is $τ\bigl(h^{\,|E|-|V|+1}\prod_v w_v\bigr)$ for a fixed ``handle'' element $h\in A$. This proves Liu's conjecture for every $k$, with an algorithm whose cost is polynomial in $k$ as well as in the graph. We also give a closure criterion for linear recurrences of any depth (a balance condition implies closure, and is necessary when the unit is a combination of the colours), and we map the landscape: semisimple algebras are exactly Liu's orthogonal frames, smoothable algebras with nilpotents are collided frames, and families whose algebra is not smoothable (``frameless'' families) exist exactly when $k\ge 14$. Finally we show that every non-semisimple part of a family is invisible to the Holant on connected graphs with two or more independent cycles. This note states the results and sketches the proofs; the proofs of the main theorems are short and are given essentially in full.

papers.title: Do Syntax Heads Influence Model Behavior?
papers.abstract: Transformer language models develop attention heads that specialize in syntactic relations, for example, attending from verbs to their subjects. Do these heads play a causal role in the model's syntactic predictions? Evidence for such a role is mixed to negative: even when we force these heads to attend to a distractor noun other than the subject, the model's syntactic predictions are still more consistent with the subject than with the distractor. Interventions on specialized syntax heads had a significantly stronger effect on syntactic predictions than interventions on random heads, but only in one of the two measures we propose.

papers.title: Spectral-MoE: Heterogeneous Per-Layer Expert Utilization in Dense-to-MoE Conversion
papers.abstract: Large language models impose substantial memory demands and arithmetic costs during inference. Dense-to-mixture-of-experts (MoE) conversion is a model optimization technique that aims to reduce these arithmetic costs. Dense-to-MoE conversion partitions pretrained feed-forward network (FFN) neurons into experts and selects a subset for each token. Leading methods fall into two categories: analytic methods produce a converted model quickly using heuristics, while learning methods produce a model much more slowly by optimizing via gradients. Both approaches, however, fix the same active expert count, or "utilization," at every layer. We introduce Spectral-MoE, which learns to allocate a utilization budget heterogeneously across layers. Its name draws a metaphor between separating a dense FFN into experts and separating a light beam into its spectrum. Spectral-MoE consists of two distinct approaches: a static approach that uses a single per-layer scalar which is shared across tokens, and a dynamic approach which emits a per-token schedule. We demonstrate that both allocators improve performance over uniform on both the analytic-based and learning-based SOTA dense-to-MoE methods. At 25% FFN utilization, dynamic allocation reduces WikiText-2 perplexity relative to uniform by 1.04, 2.96, and 2.71 points on the learned base for Llama-2-7B, Llama-3-8B, and Qwen2.5-7B, respectively. The corresponding reductions on the analytic base are 2.45, 6.26, and 2.17 points. On the learned base, dynamic allocation improves six-task mean accuracy over uniform by an average of 1.5, 4.2, and 3.6 percentage points across the three models at FFN utilizations of 12.5%, 25%, and 50%, respectively. These results establish per-layer expert utilization as a novel optimization axis in dense-to-MoE conversion.

papers.title: Moment-optimal Gamma approximation of Bessel Process exit times
papers.abstract: We construct finite Gamma convolutions approximating the first hitting time of $1$ by a Bessel process of index $ν>-1$ started at the origin. The scale measure in the classical exponential representation of this law is obtained by squaring the positive half of a dilated modified Lommel polynomial orthogonality measure. Its Jacobi recurrence yields an $N$-factor Gamma convolution that uniquely matches the first $2N$ cumulants, the maximal number attainable in this class. From an exact Gaussian quadrature remainder we derive supergeometric convergence of the Laplace transforms on compact subsets of a common slit plane and geometric convergence of the distribution functions uniformly on the real line. The approximants have total Gamma shape $N(N+ν+1)$, and their Laplace transforms and negative moments decrease to those of the exit law.

papers.title: Write Once, Plan Many: Building Reusable Visual Planning Systems from One Scene
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can reason about visual planning tasks, but querying them for every instance incurs repeated inference cost and latency. Generating reusable planning programs offers an alternative, but constructing reliable planning systems for new problem domains without extensive supervision remains challenging. We present a training-free framework that constructs reusable perception and planning programs from a domain specification and a single practice scene without a paired solution. The central challenge is obtaining useful feedback from the limited input. Our framework addresses it by leveraging VLM's ability to provide a renderer and a dynamic model based on its scene understanding. Rendering detected states enables comparison with the practice scene, while checking simulated action outcomes against the domain specification helps expose errors in rule implementation. Together, these checks guide refinement of the grounding program and planner without requiring solution labels. After refinement and component selection, the programs are frozen and solve new instances without further VLM calls. The same framework constructs systems across domains without manual pipeline redesign. Across fifteen domain variants spanning 2D and 3D scenes with discrete and continuous state, our systems achieve 99.3% average planning success, compared with 80.9% for the strongest domain-level program-generation baseline and 90.7% for the strongest instance-level baseline. Cost analyses show a favorable success-cost trade-off, and ablations confirm the contributions of the executable domain model, execution feedback, and component selection.

papers.title: From Detection To Anticipation: Continuous Onset Forecasting For Stuttered Speech
papers.abstract: Automatic stuttering systems primarily detect dysfluencies after they have occurred, limiting their use for anticipatory intervention. We address this gap by formulating stuttering prediction as continuous causal time-to-event forecasting, where a model estimates the risk of an upcoming stuttering onset every 100 ms using only preceding speech. To support this task, we augment FluencyBank Timestamped for 36 speakers with manually reviewed repetitions, prolongations, and blocks, yielding 2,872 forecasting events. We then model the temporal evolution of frozen Whisper-large-v3 speech representations using a compact causal Conformer with 3.67M trainable parameters. The proposed approach achieves an AUROC of 0.63. Temporal analysis further shows that explicitly modeling preceding speech states outperforms simply increasing the static acoustic window, while a discrete-time survival formulation provides coherent forecasts from 300 ms to 1.5 s using a single model. These results provide initial evidence that stuttering onset is preceded by measurable temporal information in speech and establish a framework for future anticipatory stuttering systems.

papers.title: An oral history of FPSAC
papers.abstract: As its 40th anniversary nears, we present a history of the International Conference on Formal Power Series and Algebraic Combinatorics (FPSAC), through interviews with figures from its past, present, and future.

papers.title: An Open-Source Web-Based Viewer for Disseminating Image-Derived Models
papers.abstract: Patient-specific 3-dimensional (3D) models are increasingly central to planning surgery and catheter-based intervention in children with congenital heart disease (CHD), whose anatomy is often atypical and variable. These models inform care only when the surgeons and interventional cardiologists who make treatment decisions can rotate, crop, and measure them directly. Desktop modeling applications require local installation, capable hardware, and training. Commercial web-based viewers are portable but closed, and, in our experience, cannot display volume rendering, time-resolved (e.g., 4-dimensional) data, or the custom workflows centers build for CHD. Because CHD populations are small and heterogeneous, such workflows are unlikely to be prioritized commercially, and end users have no means to add them. To address these limitations, we developed the SlicerHeart Viewer, an open-source module that presents a simplified interface to a complete 3D Slicer/SlicerHeart session running on a server. Clinicians access models created by clinical modeling services from any device through a web browser. Because 3D Slicer runs underneath, volume rendering, time-resolved data, and any SlicerHeart workflow, including those developed for CHD, are available without modification. The module is independent of the hosting environment; we chose internal servers behind institutional single sign-on, and a cloud-hosted option is in development. Over one year at a single pediatric center, nearly all of 82 modeled cases were shared through the Viewer with clinicians from five specialties, with cases loading in 5 to 10 seconds. The approach is not specific to CHD and is deployable at other centers.

papers.title: LLMs program using Reusable and Composable Abstract Representations
papers.abstract: When writing code, the same computation can be expressed in different programming languages and through different implementation strategies. We show that the activations of LLMs capture this shared structure in reusable and composable abstract representations when they generate code. These representations emerge in the middle layers, are reusable across programming languages, and afford the model an impressive amount of generalization ability when generating code under various interventions. Using activation steering, we show that function, programming language, and implementation strategy can be independently manipulated. The independent interventions on language and function can be flexibly composed to control code generation, even in cases when the prompt contains no information about language and function. We additionally find that finetuning on examples of arbitrarily defined functions in one programming language transfers to other languages, consistent with the models reusing abstract features of code generation that are shared across different examples. Finally, to study how such abstract representations come to be, we implement a minimal model of shared, reusable, and composable structure in a synthetic setting, and show that transformers trained on such data learn representations that reuse these parts flexibly across contexts.

papers.title: With Leverage, the Gambler is Not the One Who Gets Ruined
papers.abstract: In this note we explore the following simple question: How does the classic \emph{gambler's ruin} phenomenon change if we allow the gambler \emph{financial leverage}? We show that, with a moderate amount of leverage, it is possible for an (idealized) gambler to sustain seemingly improbable profits over a remarkably long time horizon without ever going bankrupt, \emph{even} if the gambler makes only fair bets. With a leverage ratio of $L = 10$ (less than what Lehman Brothers Holdings had from 1995--2008), the probability of multiplying one's money by $1000\times$ without going bankrupt is roughly $50\%$. More generally, given $L$-fold leverage, and given the goal of multiplying one's money by a factor of $r > 1$, the optimal gambling strategy has probability roughly $r^{-1/L}$ of success. The results in this note are designed as part of the course development for the CMU randomized algorithms course.

papers.title: FinGREAT: Evaluating LLMs on Financial Graph-guided Retrieval And Typing
papers.abstract: Financial disclosures express the underlying relationships of double-entry accounting through unstructured text. While financial LLM benchmarks predominantly emphasize question answering and classification, schema-guided evidence discovery remains relatively under-explored. We investigate whether open-weight LLMs can extract and classify evidence corresponding to predefined double-entry accounting relationships underlying the text. Using a financial accounting graph comprising 11 nodes (accounts) and 11 edges (transaction types), we evaluate mid-sized models from 5 open-weight families across 1,300 SEC 10-K Item 7 filings spanning 26 years, comparing their extraction performance against three proprietary models. Results reveal substantial differences in extraction volume, edge distributions, and cross-model agreement. Building on this study, we introduce a human-annotated relation classification benchmark comprising 483 passages across three financial accounting categories, evaluating 34 open-weight and 10 proprietary models. The strongest open-weight and proprietary models achieve 84.1\% and 92.8\% accuracy, respectively, with considerable variation across accounting categories. Our findings highlight the importance of evaluating evidence discovery and relation understanding separately, while investigating locally deployable models for scalable, privacy-sensitive financial analysis.

papers.title: Existence of exhaustions with controlled sign of mean curvature in noncompact manifolds
papers.abstract: Given a complete and non-compact Riemannian manifold of dimension $3\le n\le 7$, we find conditions for the existence of compact exhaustions $\{U_i\}_{i=1}^\infty$ such that all boundaries $\partial U_i$ have the same sign of mean curvature. In particular, we show that in these dimensions, a manifold with one end satisfying a no tentacle condition always has a weakly mean convex, weakly mean concave, or minimal exhaustion, according to the behaviour of the area profile of separating hypersurfaces. This is a version of a result sketched by Gromov, under a condition which is weaker than his thickness at infinity. In more general situations, we study the existence of exhaustions which are weakly mean concave or weakly mean convex apart from an arbitrarily small $L^1$ error. That is, we find sufficient conditions for the existence of exhaustions $\{U_i\}_{i=1}^\infty$ which satisfy $\int_{\partial U_i}H^+\to0$, $\int_{\partial U_i}H^-\to0$, or $\int_{\partial U_i}|H|\to0$, where $H^-$, $H^+$, and $|H|$ are the negative part, positive part, and the absolute value of the mean curvature respectively. As an application of our methods, we study the existence of almost $c$-convex exhaustions, that is, exhaustions whose boundaries satisfy $\int_{\partial U_i}(H-c)^-\to0$ for some $c>0$.

papers.title: Paleo-heat flux estimates across Enceladus derived from flexural response of the ice shell
papers.abstract: Saturn's moon Enceladus has active plumes suggestive of locally high heat fluxes at present, and the present-day heating is reasonably well characterized. However, the moon's thermal history is not well understood. In this study, we model flexural deformation of chasmata and dorsae in various regions of Enceladus to find the effective elastic thickness of the ice shell and constrain temporal and spatial variations in heat flux. We find paleo-heat fluxes of 60-$\geq$350 mWm$^{-2}$, with most clustered around 125-200 mWm$^{-2}$. Present day measured heat fluxes at the South Polar Terrain (SPT) are comparable to our estimated paleo-heat fluxes in non-SPT regions. Our paleo-heat fluxes, however, are significantly higher than the corresponding present day heat fluxes for the same locations inferred from shell thickness maps. This suggests that regions outside the SPT experienced a past episode of heating (heat fluxes in excess of 100mWm$^{-2}$) followed by a cooling and thickening ice shell. A relatively constant paleo-heat flux for terrains of different ages (determined from crater densities) supports the "resonance locking" hypothesis of dissipation in Saturn and might imply a long-lived resonance between Enceladus and Dione. Our results suggest that Enceladus's tidal heating appears to have been consistent over time. Consistent peak heating at Enceladus could support a long-lived subsurface ocean, which has important consequences for astrobiology and the habitability of the outer solar system.

papers.title: Eremenko's conjecture on higher-order Briot--Bouquet equations
papers.abstract: The Briot--Bouquet theorem describes the meromorphic solutions of autonomous first-order algebraic differential equations. We prove Eremenko's conjecture extending it to all orders: if $f$ is meromorphic in $\mathbb{C}$ and $P(f,f^{(n)})=0$ for a nonzero polynomial $P$, then $f$ is rational, elliptic, a rational function of $e^{cz}$ with $c\neq 0$, or satisfies $f^{(n)}=af+b$. In particular, every meromorphic solution with $P$ irreducible of degree at least two belongs to the Weierstrass class. Solutions with poles were classified by Eremenko, Liao and Ng. We settle the remaining entire case with a rigidity theorem for polynomial compositions: if $h$ is nonconstant entire and $D^nR(h)=S(h)$, where $D=d/dz$ and $°R=°S\ge 2$, then $h(z)=Ae^{bz}+Be^{-bz}+C$. No growth assumption is needed. The proof turns the cancellation of leading terms into a contraction of indicator diagrams and obtains incompatible zero counts near an exposed edge. As an arithmetic application, an algebraic Laurent expansion at one algebraic point and an algebraic value at another force a solution to lie in $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}(z)$. Hence any two distinct derivatives of a function in Mahler's class (transcendental meromorphic functions with algebraic Laurent coefficients at every algebraic point) are algebraically independent over $\mathbb{C}$.

papers.title: Tracing Accretion and Inner-Disk Gas Evolution in the Orion Nebula via Br-alpha and CO
papers.abstract: We present a systematic spectroscopic study of hydrogen Brackett-alpha (Br-alpha) and carbon monoxide (CO) fundamental-band (4.3-5.2 micron) emission from a homogeneous sample of 0.2-1.5 Msun pre-main-sequence (PMS) stars in the Orion Nebula observed with JWST/NIRSpec-MOS as part of our Chandra-JWST project. Using 73 Br-alpha and 46 CO spectra, we investigate correlations between warm-gas emission, stellar properties, accretion, and environment with censored correlation and regression analyses accounting for multiple testing. Br-alpha luminosity correlates strongly with accretion luminosity (Lacc), even after excluding sources within 2' of Theta1 Ori C, the nebula's main ionizing O-type star, whose radiation may bias proplyd Lacc estimates. This supports Br-alpha as a robust empirical tracer of accretion in PMS stars. Br-alpha also correlates with visual extinction (Av) and more weakly with stellar bolometric luminosity and mass. CO fundamental-band luminosities likewise correlate positively with Lacc and Av, relationships that persist in a larger combined JWST/NIRSpec+MIRI sample spanning multiple star-forming regions. In contrast to Br-alpha, CO luminosity shows no significant dependence on basic stellar properties, suggesting that warm molecular gas is governed primarily by accretion and local disk conditions. The weaker correlations of the Spitzer/IRAC spectral slope with Lacc and Av suggest that warm inner-disk gas may evolve or disperse faster than optically thick dust. Overall, the CO results tentatively indicate declining warm-gas emission as disks evolve, modulated by accretion-powered thermal and ultraviolet excitation, although variations in emitting area inherited from natal core conditions may also contribute.

papers.title: High-resolution retinal matrix imaging via computational motion and aberration correction
papers.abstract: High-resolution optical imaging of the human retina is essential for diagnosing ophthalmic and neurodegenerative diseases. While adaptive optics combined with coherence gating can resolve retinal structures at the cellular scale, it requires complex, costly, and cumbersome hardware to physically correct for ocular aberrations and motion. Matrix imaging offers a powerful digital alternative by leveraging wave linearity to undo aberrations and multiple scattering; however, its in vivo deployment has been hindered by continuous, involuntary eye movements that destroy phase coherence during acquisition. Here, we overcome this fundamental barrier and demonstrate the first in vivo reflection matrix imaging of the human retina using an ultra-simplified optical setup without physical correctors. We introduce a fully computational framework that tracks and compensates for multi-axial ocular motion directly from raw interferometric data, thereby restoring the phase coherence of a multi-spectral distortion matrix. This enables local, high-order aberration correction to achieve diffraction-limited, volumetric imaging of retinal tissues. By shifting the hardware burden to physics-guided numerical computation, this paradigm opens the way for accessible, non-invasive, and high-resolution digital ophthalmology.

papers.title: Refined Topology-Pass Scheduling: Damped Trust-Region Compensation for Dynamic k-NN Graphs in SE(3)-Equivariant Structure Prediction
papers.abstract: Equivariant structure-prediction pipelines alternate coordinate updates with the construction of a k-nearest-neighbour (kNN) graph whose membership is a discrete, piecewise-constant function of the coordinates. Rebuilding that graph at every block boundary (PB) is the expensive part of an epoch, whereas reusing one frozen graph (F) is fast but leaves a topology gap. We study a two-pass design in which the cheap pass records a small amount of state (margins, kNN radii, measured per-boundary displacements) and a second pass compensates conservatively. We formulate the choice of the graph-construction basis as a damped fixed-point iteration whose unique fixed point is exactly PB, and derive (i) exact non-flip certificates with the two-sided constant $m_i/4$ and one-sided constant $m_i/2$, (ii) the minimum-variance (BLUE) replay gain $γ^*$ and the resulting feasibility crossover, (iii) an $\ell_\infty$ trust-region projection that preserves convergence, and (iv) an analytic near-tie spacing law $E[m] \approx r_k/(3k)$ that matches measurements to 1\%. Three compensation levels are implemented in C++ (L1: frozen set with live geometry; L2: margin-gated local repair; L3: damped, projected basis) and validated under a matched-conditions protocol (identical seed, MSA depth and trajectory family, only the topology mode differs). L2 reproduces the PB edge set exactly ($D = 0.0000$ at every boundary), L1 stays within 0.6% and L3 interpolates monotonically: L2 reproduces the PB edge set exactly when the trust region is removed, and L3 interpolates between the frozen and the PB topology. The recorded trajectory itself yields a measured $1.5\times$ Pass-1 and $1.76\times$ epoch speed-up with no measurable loss gap. An open-source implementation of the runtime and of all the experiments reported here is available at https://github.com/AlbertHuang96/ProteinPredictMachineLearning.

papers.title: Copy-Paste Language Models
papers.abstract: Transformers are intuitively considered to be efficient at copying from their inputs. We actually show that the ability of LLMs to copy in context can be improved through explicit modeling. We propose Copy-Paste Language Models (CPLMs), which add a lightweight Copy-Paste head to the conventional language modeling (LM) head. CPLMs improve training efficiency, downstream performance, and offer new operating points in long-context and retrieval setups. We validate our approach by pretraining models from 135M to 1.7B parameters, showing improvements across all scales and backbones with negligible training and inference overheads. We explain the success of CPLMs by showing that they partially mitigate the LM head gradient bottleneck through an alternative gradient path.

papers.title: PACER: Process-Aware VLA Policy Learning from Human Corrections for Robotic Disassembly
papers.abstract: Robotic disassembly of end-of-life (EoL) products requires robots to accommodate product variation, follow prerequisite sequences, and approach components precisely for contact-rich manipulation. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) provides a practical path for adaptation, but limited and costly disassembly data cannot capture the distribution shifts arising from changing environments and product uncertainties. The policy's own rollouts record its approach attempts, and human corrections demonstrate recovery from its errors, but turning these experiences into better policy performance remains challenging. We introduce PACER, a Process-Aware Correction and Evidence Reweighting framework that learns from these experiences through SFT, using progress toward the target and each trace's source and outcome to weight valid action chunks in the native supervised action loss. PACER trains one policy per weighting setting and selects one of the resulting policies through held-out validation. We evaluate PACER on UR5e motherboard disassembly across five component classes, where it achieves 87/100 successful approach-and-handoff trials on the held-out benchmark, compared with 54/100 for vanilla post-SFT.

papers.title: Graph binomial coefficients and a positivity conjecture of Guo and Krattenthaler
papers.abstract: We investigate Conjecture 7.4 of Guo and Krattenthaler \cite{GK}, which predicts that for every positive integer $n$, the polynomial \[ P_n(q) = \frac{(1-q)^2}{(1-q^{10n-1})(1-q^{15n-1})}\qbin{30n}{5n} \] has non-negative coefficients, except for $q^1$ and $q^{125n^2-25n+3}$, which equal $-1$. We study this problem through three main perspectives: First, by linking the boundary coefficients to the second differences of the partition function, we settle the first and last $25n+1$ coefficients via a novel partition injection. Second, by introducing a ``defect'' generalization of Andrews' classical lemma, we reduce the conjecture to an almost-unimodality property and employ a uniform saddle-point analysis to prove it analytically for all large $n \ge 2\cdot 10^{29}$. Finally, we connect these quotients to graph binomial coefficients, providing a natural orbit-counting interpretation via Burnside's lemma on directed cycles and paths.

papers.title: Full-Order Safety for Nonlinear Reduced-Order MPC
papers.abstract: Reduced-order models (ROMs) make model predictive control (MPC) of high-dimensional nonlinear systems tractable, but the resulting modeling error can lead to constraint violations on the real system. We introduce CoRE-MPC, a robust MPC formulation that plans with a nonlinear ROM and guarantees recursive feasibility and constraint satisfaction for the full-order system. It can be applied with a broad class of nonlinear model reduction techniques and the resulting MPC does not require evaluating the full-order model online, thus ensuring computational efficiency. The key insight is in how the ROM affects the dynamics of the prediction error. We account for this with two error radii that are propagated alongside the ROM and provide a guaranteed bound on the prediction error. The approach is validated in simulation on an 80-state oscillator chain, a Burgers equation, and a 9,768-state finite-element soft robot, where a two-state ROM with data-driven bounds keeps all 1,628 nodes clear of a wall at a median solve time below 1 ms for a 20 ms control period. Across these examples, CoRE-MPC is 13 to 61 times faster than full-order robust MPC at only 27 to 35% higher closed-loop cost, whereas existing certified schemes are either infeasible or at least twice as conservative. Code: [released upon publication].

papers.title: An analog of Quillen-Venkov for eventually negligible classes and radicality for finite irreducible Coxeter groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group, $M$ a $G$-module, and $F$ a field. A continuous group homomorphism $i : Γ_L=\text{Gal}(L_{\text{sep}}/L) \rightarrow G$ yields a homomorphism $i^* : H^d(G,M) \rightarrow H^d(L,M)$ for every $d\in \mathbb{N}$. An element $u \in H^d(G,M)$ is negligible over $F$ if $u\in\ker(i^*)$ for every $i$ and every field extension $L/F$. If $M=\mathbb{F}_p$ for a prime $p$ with a trivial $G$-action, an element $u$ is eventually negligible over $F$ if $u^k$ is negligible over $F$ for some $k\geq1$. The (eventually) negligible elements over $F$ form an ideal of the cohomology ring $H^*(G,\mathbb{F}_p)$, called the (eventually) negligible ideal. We prove an analog of Quillen-Venkov for eventually negligible elements. An element $u\in H^*(G,\mathbb{F}_p)$ is eventually negligible over $F$ if and only if the restriction of $u$ to the cohomology of each elementary abelian $p$-subgroup of $G$ is eventually negligible over $F$. Paired with applications of a Gysin-type long exact sequence, we identify generators of the negligible ideal over $\mathbb{Q}$ of the mod-2 cohomology of dihedral groups, cyclic $2$-groups, and generalized quaternion groups. We prove that the negligible ideal over $\mathbb{Q}$ of the mod-2 cohomology of every finite irreducible Coxeter group is radical. The result was previously known for Weyl groups; we prove it for the remaining non-Weyl types $I_2(m)$, $H_3$, and $H_4$.

papers.title: Multi-Sensitive Distributional Fairness: Joint Wasserstein Audits and Shapley Allocation
papers.abstract: Fairness audits with several sensitive attributes are often performed one coordinate at a time. This can miss purely intersectional disparities: a score may be independent of each sensitive coordinate while depending on their joint profile. We study distributional demographic parity for a real-valued score using one-dimensional Wasserstein geometry. We distinguish two complementary constructions. Conditional and sequential audits characterize joint parity through their zero sets, but their positive values do not generally decompose a fixed joint Wasserstein disparity. By contrast, full-cell conditional quantile functions define a Hilbert-valued random variable whose variance is the joint disparity. Conditional expectations of this quantile process induce a monotone information game: every reveal order yields an exact martingale decomposition of the same joint disparity, while Shapley values provide an order-free attribution across sensitive attributes. Under independent sensitive attributes, the game reduces to a Hoeffding-ANOVA decomposition and Shapley splits each interaction energy equally among its members; under dependence, orthogonality is lost and explicit formulas reveal suppression and redundancy effects that marginal audits can hide. We give fixed-grid estimators and permutation calibration, and illustrate the framework on synthetic examples and ACSIncome. The resulting framework separates three questions that are often conflated: whether joint distributional parity holds, how a fixed joint disparity decomposes along an information path, and how that disparity can be attributed across sensitive coordinates without privileging an ordering.

papers.title: Natural Geometry Based on the Rectilinear Plane
papers.abstract: The aim of this note is to introduce natural geometry, in which the rectilinear plane is a primitive. This plane is admitted together with its rectitude, and its rectitude states that a Lambert quadrilateral has its fourth angle right. The fourth angle of a Lambert quadrilateral may be right, acute or obtuse, and this trichotomy distinguishes three planes. Starting from the rectitude, we prove the uniqueness of the parallel by a chain of neutral steps: the rectangle, the triangle whose angles sum to $π$, and Legendre's theorem \cite{legendre}, all borrowed from the classical literature. That uniqueness is equivalent to the fifth postulate, which we thus reach in Euclid's own wording: the equivalence is read in the natural direction, and it is not a derivation of the fifth postulate from the other four, since the independence of that postulate is not in question. In the rectilinear plane the parallels are characterised as exactly the images of a line under a point-reflection, and equivalently as the pairs of equidistant lines. The other two planes are then placed beside the rectilinear one, and the same definitions serve for all three.

papers.title: Beyond Time Induction: Structured Conditional Neural Solvers for Parametric Stochastic-Volatility Pricing
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks provide a flexible framework for learning parametric PDE solution families without labeled data, yet preserving accurate derivatives across heterogeneous regimes remains challenging. Structured neural solvers offer compact representations, but restrictive conditional parameterizations can limit adaptation across the solution family. We introduce BeTINN, a structured conditional architecture extending time-induced modulation through multi-directional time-parameter conditioning and a joint residual pathway. We evaluate BeTINN on the Heston stochastic-volatility PDE, a demanding parametric problem with mixed derivatives and economically relevant first- and second-order sensitivities. BeTINN improves joint accuracy across normalized option value and key sensitivity metrics relative to our baselines. Controlled ablations characterize the roles of its architectural components. We further find that validation physics loss is informative but does not fully determine differential fidelity, and that accurate solution values can coexist with localized derivative errors. These results support structured conditional adaptation and motivate derivative-aware evaluation when sensitivities are downstream quantities of interest.

papers.title: Quantum-classical algorithm interpolation for spatial search
papers.abstract: Quantum-walk algorithms can quadratically reduce the dependence of spatial search on the classical hitting time $\mathrm{HT}$. Realising this speedup using standard quantum-walk algorithms, however, requires deep coherent circuits, limiting their applicability on near-term and early fault-tolerant quantum devices. We derive a parameterised family of hybrid quantum-classical spatial search algorithms that continuously interpolates between the classical and fully coherent quantum regimes, trading off circuit depth for total query complexity. For any $γ\in[0,1]$, our algorithms use circuits of depth $\widetilde{O}(\mathrm{HT}^{γ/2})$ and find a marked vertex with constant success probability at total cost $\widetilde{O}(\mathrm{HT}^{1-γ}\mathsf{S} + \mathrm{HT}^{1-γ/2}(\mathsf{U} + \mathsf{C}))$, where $\mathsf{S}$, $\mathsf{U}$, and $\mathsf{C}$ denote the setup, update, and checking costs, respectively. We also derive an optimal continuous depth-query trade-off for fixed-point amplitude amplification, providing a potential building block for other hybrid designs.

papers.title: Bottom-Charm $[bc]$ Diquark Masses from QCD Laplace Sum-Rules
papers.abstract: Constituent mass predictions for bottom-charm $[bc]$ color-antitriplet diquarks are generated using QCD Laplace sum rules. We calculate the diquark correlator within the operator product expansion to next-to-leading-order (NLO), including terms proportional to the four- and six-dimensional gluon and six-dimensional quark condensates. Existing analytic expressions for the resulting multi-scale master integrals are insufficient for these calculations, so we utilize numerical $D$-dimensional loop integration techniques. The sum rule analyses stabilize in all four channels yielding constituent masses in GeV of: scalar ($0^+$) $(5.60\pm0.56)$, pseudoscalar ($0^-$) $(6.04\pm0.60)$, axial vector ($1^+$) $(5.60\pm0.56)$ and vector ($1^-$) $(5.99\pm0.60)$. These constituent mass results are discussed in comparison with values used in diquark models of tetraquark hadronic states. We also summarize QCD sum rule predictions for diquark masses for all possible quark-flavor combinations, providing QCD-based criteria for assessing the diquark mass parameters used in constituent diquark models of hadrons.

papers.title: Long-horizon Video Generation with Slot Memory Addressed By Region Tokens
papers.abstract: Memory for long-horizon video generation must satisfy two competing requirements: it must remain bounded so generation can continue indefinitely, while still recovering what was observed at a place when the camera returns, regardless of how long ago it was seen. Reconstruction-based memories provide spatial recall by caching and reprojecting explicit geometry, but require growing storage and depend on estimated 3D structure. Recurrent memories keep a constant-size state, but retention is governed by temporal recurrence, causing old observations to fade with time. We introduce SMART, a slot memory addressed by region tokens, which combines bounded storage with spatially addressed recall. SMART stores content in a constant-size slot recurrence whose writes are addressed by the observing camera and whose reads are queried by the rendering camera, without constructing an explicit 3D representation or maintaining a growing cache. Consequently, recall is conditioned on inter-view geometry rather than on recency. Each read additionally provides a confidence estimate that conditions a chunk-causal diffusion transformer, allowing it to selectively trust retrieved content while relying on its generative prior elsewhere. On long trajectories in Memory Maze and Minecraft, SMART maintains high-fidelity recall far beyond its training horizon while using constant memory and per-step cost.

papers.title: Quantum Residues and the Geometry of Perturbative/Non-perturbative Relations
papers.abstract: We develop a systematic, Whitham-based construction of perturbative/non-perturbative (P/NP) relations for one-dimensional quantum mechanical systems admitting a genus-one WKB period description, and derive a higher-genus formulation under explicit regularity assumptions. We select external deformations that preserve the independent quantum residues and lift them by varying the internal moduli so that the independent perturbative quantum periods remain fixed. The Riemann bilinear identity then determines the induced evolution of the non-perturbative periods through local residue pairings and the inverse period Jacobian. At genus one, this reduces to a relation between the flow of the non-perturbative quantum period and the energy derivative with respect to the perturbative action, providing a constructive connection between the Rayleigh-Schrödinger expansion and fluctuations around non-perturbative saddles. We recover known P/NP relations and derive extensions for explicitly coupling-dependent potentials, which we verify at the computed orders through independent perturbative and non-perturbative period calculations for quantum-corrected quartic and Jacobi elliptic examples.

papers.title: Topologically Protected Surface Acoustic Wave Edge States in Phononic Integrated Circuits
papers.abstract: Phononic integrated circuits enable the development of compact systems to manipulate radio frequency signals through interconnected networks of acoustic waveguides. Introducing topologically protected robustness in these circuits to counter fabrication imperfections and local perturbations, remains a challenge. This work presents a validated modeling framework for topologically protected edge states using surface acoustic waves in etch-defined waveguides consisting of scandium aluminum nitride on silicon carbide, directly comparing analytical, full-wave numerical simulation, and laser Doppler vibrometer measured experimental approaches and their agreement. This work represents the first experimental demonstration of topological edge states on a ScAlN on SiC platform, validated through direct quantitative comparison with analytical and numerical analyses, with future implications for topological protection in phononic and optomechanical integrated circuit platforms.

papers.title: Conformal dimension and self-similar groups
papers.abstract: We study the Ahlfors-regular conformal dimension of spaces with locally expanding self-covering maps and, more generally, limit spaces of contracting self-similar groups. We show that the conformal dimension is characterized by combinatorial moduli associated with the Schreier graphs of these groups. We compare these moduli with contraction coefficients of self-similar group actions and with algebras of functions on the limit spaces satisfying asymptotic $p$-energy conditions. We also give conditions on the group when the conformal dimension is equal to the infimum of visual metrics on the self-similarity complex.

papers.title: Beyond the lemon: Spectra of random Lindblad operators with a Hamiltonian component
papers.abstract: Generators of continuous-time quantum Markovian evolution, known as Lindblad operators, play a key role in the theory of open quantum systems. The question of how to define and characterize random Lindblad operators has attracted considerable attention in recent years. Purely dissipative random Lindbladians have been extensively studied using toolboxes of free probability and non-Hermitian random matrix theories, which helped to uncover a characteristic lemon-like spectral support. In this work, we focus on random Lindbladians with a Hamiltonian component. We analyze three ensembles of increasing complexity, designed to illustrate the joint effects of dissipative and Hamiltonian dynamics. While the first two allow for an exact analytic treatment with standard probabilistic and scalar-valued free-probability methods, the most general case requires the more general framework of operator-valued free probability. We explain how the spectral support changes with the relative Hamiltonian strength and the rank of the dissipative component and characterize the effect of Hamiltonian-induced spectral squeezing.

papers.title: MIND: Instruction-Conditioned Incremental Grounding for Robots
papers.abstract: Robots following persistent language instructions must decide which cached room judgments remain valid as their environment changes. We present MIND (Maintenance via INstruction-conditioned Dependencies), a framework for maintaining target-room decisions without re-evaluating every room after each event. A language model compiles each instruction into dependencies for semantic qualification and target selection. The controller intersects semantic dependencies with event footprints, refreshes affected judgments, and updates reachability and selection separately. For fixed deterministic evaluation, planning, and selection, conservative dependency and footprint coverage preserves the decisions of full recomputation. On 240 five-event ProcTHOR sequences with an exact benchmark predicate, MIND reduces mean semantic evaluations from 30.6 to 11.2 while preserving all 1,200 post-event decisions. Frozen-evaluator experiments with Phi-4 and Qwen3-14B also preserve all 1,200 decisions, without improving the evaluators' underlying task accuracy. In 32 closed-loop AI2-THOR episodes using exact-predicate qualification and metadata-derived footprints, MIND matches the final target decision of full recomputation in every episode. Unitree G1 experiments demonstrate target reuse and reselection across room transitions without additional semantic evaluations under MIND, and abstention after a barrier and an object removal at 4 evaluations against 15 to 18. Additional materials are available at https://mind-icra27.github.io/.

papers.title: Exotic $\mathbb{R}^4$'s as unions of two thickened circles
papers.abstract: We give an infinite family of non-diffeomorphic exotic $\mathbb{R}^4$'s, each of which is the union of two copies of a standard open tubular neighborhood of the circle, which intersect in a standard open tubular neighborhood of the wedge of two circles. This gives the simplest known decomposition of an exotic $\mathbb{R}^4$ into two open sets, making progress on Question 4.43 (A) of Kirby's 1995 problem list. The decompositions are obtained by studying fibered slice disk complements in certain Casson-Gordon homotopy 4-balls, for which we provide similar decompositions. We distinguish the $\mathbb{R}^4$'s using end Floer homology.

papers.title: Beyond Maliciousness: Static and Runtime Attack-Surface Profiling of Agent Skills
papers.abstract: Agent skills are Markdown documents that a tool-using agent reads as instructions and then acts on with the privileges of the session that loaded them. Installing one grants authority (the standing to direct the agent, not new privilege), and the size of that grant is what we measure. We present a two-phase attack-surface profiling methodology that combines whole-bundle static analysis and dependency provenance checking with instrumented sandbox execution and separate model-based assessment of the resulting traces. We apply the methodology to 6,309 listings from two marketplaces, selecting listings for execution without conditioning that decision on a prior threat or risk signal. Half the corpus carries evidence of shell-execution capability; the corresponding shares are 35% for filesystem read, 31% each for filesystem write and network egress, and 13% for credential access; seven listings in ten carry at least one elevated capability. That is the surface a user accepts at install time, and almost none of it is visible then. A permission model exists but is close to inert. Authors may list the tools a skill pre-approves in its own frontmatter, which removes confirmation prompts rather than restricting what the skill can reach; of the 6,061 listings whose frontmatter parses, 770 declare anything at all, the vocabulary cannot express credential or environment access, and nothing checks what it does express against the bundle. Declaring is also not declaring accurately: 59% of declaring listings understate what their bundle can do. ClawHub declares roughly twice as often as skillsmp, yet under-declares on 88% of its declarations against 31%. Triage at the marketplace boundary therefore cannot rest on what a listing declares. It must rest on what the bundle can do. These results position capability-oriented attack-surface profiling as a necessary complement to maliciousness detection.

papers.title: FFDT: Sim-to-Real Domain Transfer Method for Far-Field Ground Penetrating Radar
papers.abstract: The scarcity of real-world ground penetrating radar (RealGPR) data is a major barrier to the development of deep learning (DL) methods for GPR data processing. Although simulated GPR (SimGPR) datasets can be used to train DL models, differences in hardware configuration and system parameters between SimGPR and RealGPR create a sim-to-real domain gap that leads to poor generalization of DL models to RealGPR measurements. To address this gap, we present a physics-based far-field GPR domain transfer (FFDT) method to transfer far-field SimGPR data to the corresponding RealGPR-domain data in the same scenario. In FFDT, SimGPR and RealGPR are modeled using angle-dependent transfer functions that capture three-dimensional antenna radiation characteristics. These transfer functions are then combined with ray tracing to enable the sim-to-real data transfer. Extensive studies across diverse objects and soil conditions demonstrate that FFDT-transferred data closely match RealGPR ground truth. To further demonstrate its value for RealGPR-domain dataset generation, FFDT is implemented to build a RealGPR-domain dataset for training a DL model for clutter removal. The model achieves robust performance on RealGPR measurements. With one-time SimGPR and RealGPR system calibration, FFDT enables RealGPR-domain dataset generation without requiring task-specific RealGPR field measurements for DL model training or fine-tuning, thereby addressing the RealGPR data scarcity bottleneck and supporting reliable development and deployment of DL methods for real-world GPR applications.

papers.title: LAMP: 3D Source-Aware Lighting Estimation at Multiple Points
papers.abstract: Existing illumination estimation methods primarily recover lighting distributions for rendering, but typically leave the contributions of individual physical light sources at specific scene locations implicit. We address this gap by leveraging the scene understanding capabilities of vision-language models (VLMs) to connect local illumination with its physical sources. We introduce LAMP, a framework for point-conditioned, source-aware illumination reasoning from a single RGB image with marked query points. LAMP constructs a shared inventory of active light sources, ranks contributing sources for each query, and predicts their 3D query-to-source directions. We supervise these relationships using procedurally controlled indoor scenes, reusing independently rendered source responses to derive contribution targets across lighting configurations and obtaining exact directions from source and query positions. On the Infinigen test set, fine-tuning Qwen3-VL-8B increases dominant-source 3D PCK@0.5m from 0% to 70.6%, with 94.5% of directions within 12.5 degrees of ground truth among correctly localized sources. Combined with a lightweight network predicting dense RGB irradiance, LAMP achieves probe-rendering quality comparable to prior lighting-estimation methods while additionally localizing individual physical sources in 3D and explicitly attributing local illumination to them.

papers.title: MemeTrace: A Multimodal LLM-Based Agent for Safety-Aware Meme Provenance Analysis
papers.abstract: Online memes are often carriers of unsafe content such as disinformation and propaganda. Their rapid evolution in response to news events and strong dependence on contextual information make it difficult for platforms and moderators to detect and moderate them effectively. Moreover, existing moderation studies typically classify memes as safe or unsafe based on individual images, lacking the ability to perform broader provenance analysis, i.e., where a meme originates, how it spreads, what cultural symbolism it represents, whether it poses potential risks to society, etc. To bridge this gap, we introduce MemeTrace, a multimodal LLM-based agent that automatically traces the provenance and potential risks of emerging memes. We evaluate MemeTrace on Meme100, a dataset of 100 real-world memes, using both human annotation and automatic metrics. The results demonstrate that MemeTrace substantially outperforms the VLM baseline. More importantly, MemeTrace achieves higher accuracy in detecting unsafe memes, especially those involving disinformation and sensitive content, and remains robust under visual perturbations.

papers.title: Whose Data, Whose Benchmark? A User-Centric Framework for Auditing Evaluation Resources
papers.abstract: Benchmarks shape how model capabilities are measured and interpreted, yet their scores can obscure whose conventions, contexts, and judgments define successful performance. We introduce a user-centric audit framework that distinguishes users who contribute benchmark content from those whose needs evaluation results are intended to represent. The framework operationalizes seven dimensions across benchmark content, metadata, documentation, and scoring procedures. Across 16 resources, we find that American-centered conventions account for 62.4-94.4% of matched signals in 11 text benchmarks, while geographic visibility in five image-text resources is concentrated and strongly associated with national GDP share (mean Pearson r = 0.780; Spearman p = 0.778). Documentation reveals a systematic source-target gap: all 16 resources operationalize source-user context, but none operationalize target-user context. Paired scoring experiments further show that meaning-preserving answer variants reduce DROP exact-match accuracy from 100.0% to 33.3%, while TruthfulQA exhibits metric-dependent reductions in reference similarity. Our framework and documentation checklist make user assumptions auditable, clarifying what benchmark scores represent and where evaluation claims are supported.

papers.title: Spectral signatures of spin textures and the emergence of a pseudogap
papers.abstract: Strongly correlated solids exhibit phenomena -- from Mott localization to high-temperature superconductivity -- that escape conventional band theory. Efforts to address this unconventional physics have been typically cast in the language of Green's function theories, with the associated self-energies capturing strong correlations beyond the reach of mean-field theories. Here, we underscore that frequency- and momentum-dependent self-energies emerge also from mean-field solutions that break translational symmetry, and that these self-energies can display the characteristic fingerprints of strong correlations for certain, physically meaningful, spatial patterns. In the paradigmatic case of the 2D Hubbard model, we find that already at the mean-field level the doped antiferromagnet develops, in addition to long-range ordered stripes, many quasi-degenerate self-consistent solutions with antiferromagnetic textures organized into antiphase domains separated by hole-rich interfaces of convoluted shape, reminiscent of the phase-separation scenario. Remarkably, these solutions map into spectral functions that display very distinctively the phenomenology of the pseudogap, including the nodal-antinodal dichotomy, Fermi arcs, and a complementary Luttinger surface. The result is a conceptually simple description of such a complex phenomenon, where a pseudogap emerges as the momentum-space spectral portrait of the real-space interplay between antiferromagnetic domains and their metallic interfaces.

papers.title: Exploring Interpretability in Deep Learning-Based Forest Classification - Separating Similar Forest Classes using Sentinel-2 Time Series
papers.abstract: The ecological insurance theory posits that diverse forests are more resilient and better able to adapt to changing environmental conditions. Increasing drought and heat stress in Central Europe promotes mixed forests for maintaining ecosystem services. However, a diverse species distribution complicates remote sensing-based species mapping, as distinguishing pure from mixed species compositions at the pixel level remains challenging. We evaluated the potential of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for tree-species classification from Sentinel-2 time series and investigated the spectral-temporal features underlying class discrimination, with particular emphasis on separating pure from mixed Norway spruce pixels. We compared RNN classification models with Random Forest (RF) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and used Integrated Gradients (IG) to quantify feature attributions across spectral bands and time. The best-performing RNN achieved a Macro-F1 score of 0.851 on the test data, outperforming XGBoost by 0.012 and Random Forest by 0.103. Beyond classification performance, the attribution analysis revealed distinct spectral-temporal patterns associated with the separation of pure and mixed Norway spruce pixels. Attribution values increased particularly after approximately day of year (DOY) 125, while B11 showed the strongest contribution during periods of increasing spectral divergence between the two classes. These findings show that recurrent models can provide competitive classification performance while also revealing the phenological periods and spectral regions that are most relevant for distinguishing closely related forest compositions. Combining time-series classification with explainability therefore provides additional insight into the spectral-temporal mechanisms underlying tree-species discrimination and may support more detailed mapping of mixed forest structures.

papers.title: Outcome-Routed Distillation and Reinforcement Learning for Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation provides dense supervision on the student's own samples, but its targets still come from the teacher. Verifier reinforcement learning (RL) instead uses an outcome signal, but it provides no direct constraint on capabilities outside the verifier. Combining the two is difficult for diffusion language models (dLLMs), because bidirectional denoising makes the policy likelihoods required by ratio-based RL unreliable. We develop a likelihood-free pipeline for a mixture-of-experts dLLM. Each rollout group is routed by verifier outcome. Mixed groups use ratio-free, group-centred REINFORCE. If every student rollout fails but a teacher succeeds, the model receives dense KL supervision on the student's denoising canvases. All other groups are skipped. A KL term anchored to the distilled checkpoint limits changes outside the verifier reward. The tool-calling teacher succeeds on only 18.6% of the training prompts. At 24 denoising steps, distillation exceeds the teacher by 6.77 percentage points, and routing improves the distilled checkpoint by a further 18.31 points. Routing lowers reasoning-trace accuracy by 0.71 points but raises direct-answer accuracy on the same items by 13.21 points. The anchored arm restores trace accuracy. Its tool-calling score differs by -0.16 points, with a confidence interval that includes zero, although this comparison also removes a small fallback distillation route. A domain-conditional recipe retains a 16.37-point tool-calling gain; a second seed gives 18.23 points and reproduces both preservation results, but the math result is seed-dependent. We pre-registered every arm and evaluated each comparison on paired items in a single sweep on one machine.

papers.title: Quantum Reservoir Computing for Attention-like Selective Reproduction
papers.abstract: Choosing which information to use as the context changes is a basic cognitive operation. We introduce a new task of this kind for quantum reservoir computing (QRC): a binary cue indicates which of two simultaneous input streams the reservoir must reproduce. In simulated spin reservoirs with a trained linear readout, infinitely many measurements (exact expectation values) let the reservoir reproduce the cued stream accurately. At a finite number of measurements \(N_M\), the score exceeds that of a linear readout of the raw inputs only at large \(N_M\) because of sampling noise. Performance increases with both entanglement and coherence in the computational basis, and then saturates. These results show that QRC can select and reproduce a cued stream, and they are a starting point for harder cognitive tasks.

papers.title: Long-Time Behavior of the $α$-Ricci Flow on the 2-Torus
papers.abstract: We study the $α$-Ricci flow $(g(t),α(t))$, which is a Ricci flow coupled with a harmonic 1-form heat flow, on the 2-torus $M$. We prove global existence for this flow as well as a Type III curvature estimate. The long-time behavior of the $α$-Ricci flow depends on the cohomology class $[α] \in H^1(M,\mathbb{R})$, which is invariant under the flow. If $[α]$ is rational, then as $t\to\infty$, $(M,t^{-1}g(t))$ Gromov--Hausdorff converges to $S^1$ with length $\ell([α])/\sqrt 2$ where $\ell([α])$ is the primitive length of $[α]$. On the universal cover, the rescaled flow $(s^{-1}\tilde g(st),\tildeα(st))$ smoothly converges to an expander $(g^*(t),α^*(t))$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$ as $s\to \infty$ where $α^*(t)$ is nonzero and constant in spacetime and $g^*(t)$ is flat and expanding in the $α^*$ direction. If $[α]$ is irrational, then there is a sequence $s_i\to\infty$ such that $(M,s_i^{-1}g(s_it))$ Gromov--Hausdorff converges to a point. Moreover, on the universal cover, $(s_i^{-1}\tilde g(s_it),\tildeα(s_it))$ smoothly converges to $(g^*(t),α^*(t))$.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Atmospheric Turbulence Mitigation: A Comparison Between GANs and Transformers
papers.abstract: Atmospheric turbulence creates complex spatial and temporal distortions that significantly reduce image quality. This work compares two deep learning methods for turbulence reduction: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Transformer-based models. Both methods are trained and tested on the SOTIS dataset, which includes multi-frame sequences under different turbulence conditions with ground truth references. Our results show an important finding: GAN-based models perform better in severely degraded, low-quality situations, while Transformer-based models achieve better results in moderate to high-quality settings, especially in correcting geometric distortions. We also enhance the Turbulence Mitigation Transformer (TMT) by introducing a refined training strategy, an augmented input design that includes a temporally averaged frame as prior structural information, and a modified loss function that incorporates the Structural Similarity Index (SSIM). These improvements lead to consistent performance gains across various turbulence conditions. Overall, this study provides an in-depth evaluation of deep learning methods for turbulence reduction and offers practical guidance for selecting models in different imaging environments.

papers.title: Atomic ironing for conformal interfaces in freestanding oxide nanomembranes
papers.abstract: Atomically well-defined interfaces are essential for realizing functional interlayer coupling in stacked and twisted oxide heterostructures, yet transferred freestanding oxides can develop structural inhomogeneities, including local curvatures, interfacial voids, and incomplete contacts with substrates. Here, we demonstrate that these transfer-induced structural disorders and imperfections evolve substantially and can be suppressed by post-transfer thermal treatments, yielding bulk-like crystalline freestanding oxide nanomembranes. Using freestanding SrTiO3 membranes as a model system, we report a systematic understanding of the role of "atomic ironing" and the associated evolution of lattice mosaicity, interfacial roughness, and optical bandgap. We further demonstrate atomically bonded conformal interfaces in twisted SrTiO3 heterostructures, highlighting the importance of post-transfer thermal processes. These results establish a synthetic strategy to restore the structural integrity and intrinsic bulk-like functionality of freestanding oxide nanomembranes, enabling stacked, twisted, and heterogeneously integrated oxide architectures with atomically well-defined interfaces for emerging quantum functionalities.

papers.title: Signatures of symmetry-stabilized Dirac fermions in correlated oxide CaNbO3 thin films
papers.abstract: Symmetry-protected electronic states in correlated oxides offer a route to combining topology, lattice tunability, and many-body interactions, but creating such topological electronic states in complex oxides remains challenging. Here, we show that oxygen octahedral rotations provide a symmetry-control parameter for stabilizing Dirac-related electronic states in epitaxial CaNbO3 films. By comparing compressively strained tetragonal films and relaxed orthorhombic films, we demonstrate that distinct octahedral rotation patterns preserve nonsymmorphic symmetry and lead to distinct transport signatures consistent with Dirac-like electronic states. The films exhibit metallic transport with high mobility of 138,000 cm2 V-1 s-1, multichannel conduction, and Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations from small high-mobility Fermi pockets. Landau-fan diagram analysis indicates finite Berry-phase contributions, while first-principles calculations reveal a strain-driven evolution from nodal-line band crossings in the orthorhombic phase to Dirac-electron band features in the tetragonal phase. These results establish oxygen octahedral symmetry as a design knob for engineering topological electronic states in correlated perovskite oxides.

papers.title: TALU: A Reconfigurable Tiled-ALU Grid for RISC-V
papers.abstract: Lane-based RISC-V vector processors exploit data parallelism well but pay a recurring cost for two common patterns: reductions, which require a separate tree pass, and deep dependent expression chains, which cannot be fused and are issued as serial vector instructions. We present TALU, a 5-stage RISC-V core whose execute stage is an NxN grid of registered ALU tiles instead of a single ALU. The grid is a reconfigurable, feed-forward spatial fabric: tiles route operands only from non-backward neighbours, and added diagonal forwarding lets a reduction collapse spatially. A minimal custom extension configures the per-tile operation, routing, and per-tile constants, and streams operands through the array. On a single fabric, TALU runs ordinary scalar code, single deep-path expressions, and multi-lane vector kernels. On the benchmark suite of the RISC-V2 vector processor, TALU is 1.8-5.5x faster than RISC-V2 and 4.5-15.5x faster than Vicuna at equal lane count, with a reduction cost (dot÷add) of 1.05x versus 1.96x and 1.26x for the vector cores. A retimed implementation places and routes at 1.03 GHz in 45 nm in 0.30 mm2, half the area of RISC-V2.

papers.title: TrackShield: An Efficient Runtime Defense Against Availability Attacks on High-Performance Real-Time Multi-Object Tracking
papers.abstract: High-performance camera-based perception pipelines must sustain per-frame real-time budgets on resource-constrained embedded GPU platforms. Availability attacks such as SlowTrack inflate the persistent state of multi-object trackers: data-association workload accumulates across frames, so per-frame latency increases and drives the pipeline past its deadline. Detector- and NMS-layer defenses do not directly control this persistent tracker-side resource. We present TrackShield, a lightweight runtime resource-management layer that protects the tracker at the point where attack-induced workload accumulates. TrackShield combines low-overhead anomaly monitoring with staged birth capping, pruning of young or weakly matched tracks, and per-stage association-input admission control. Its hard admission guard provides a deterministic bound on admitted association workload, independently of the heuristic monitor. On a Jetson AGX Orin, TrackShield reduces attacked tracking-stage latency from $139.90$ to $6.27$\,ms and whole-pipeline P99 latency from $190.9$ to $48.8$\,ms, at a benign MOTA cost of $1.06$ points. As an availability defense, TrackShield focuses on keeping the tracker responsive under attack instead of recovering the full tracking accuracy degraded by adversarial detections.

papers.title: Dimension-Free Scaling Laws for Size Generalization: An Exponential Separation
papers.abstract: Modern machine learning models increasingly operate on variable-size structured data, such as sets and graphs. A central requirement is \emph{size generalization}: the ability of a model trained on inputs of one size to generalize to inputs of a different, potentially much larger, size. Classical statistical learning theory, however, primarily considers fixed input domains, and its guarantees often deteriorate with input dimension. Although extensive work has established when models on sets and graphs can be transferred across input sizes, such results do not characterize the statistical cost of doing so: the sample complexity of size generalization, and its relationship to classical in-domain learning, remain largely unknown. We develop a statistical learning theory of size generalization and establish a sharp exponential separation in sample complexity. Letting $n$ denote the number of training samples, we show that polynomial source decay is insufficient for efficient size generalization: while it yields error $n^{-Θ(1)}$ and hence polynomial sample complexity for in-domain learning, size-generalization error decays only as $(\log n)^{-Θ(1)}$, yielding an exponential separation. Thus, polynomial in-domain sample complexity can become exponential across sizes. We then identify an exponential source condition under which size generalization achieves error $n^{-Θ(1)}$, recovering polynomial sample complexity. These guarantees are independent of input dimension and depend only on the number of training samples, yielding dimension-free scaling laws. We also provide matching minimax lower bounds, establishing optimality. To our knowledge, this work provides the first dimension-free minimax theory of size generalization and a rigorous characterization of when, and at what statistical cost, learning can transfer across input sizes.

papers.title: The Limits of Tidal Circularization and Atmospheric Escape for Mini-Neptunes and Super-Earths: The Case of TOI-2257 b
papers.abstract: With a 35-day orbital period and $\sim$0.5 eccentricity, TOI-2257 b occupies a sparsely populated corner of transiting mini-Neptune parameter space and may lie near the orbital distance at which tidal and atmospheric escape process become negligible. To test this hypothesis, we performed simulations of the combined stellar, tidal, and atmospheric evolution and confirmed that TOI-2257 b does lie near this boundary, regardless of whether it formed with or without a primordial hydrogen envelope. In the mini-Neptune scenario, we find that all cases retain an envelope of at least 0.02 M$_\oplus$ for 8 Gyr, but that the envelope mass can be halved if it was initially larger than 0.2 M$_\oplus$. We find that tidal evolution only occurs for cases with initial envelope masses larger than 0.02 M$_\oplus$ because their radii are large enough to generate significant torques. In the super-Earth scenario, the planet could lose $\sim$10 Earth ocean masses of surface water during the $\sim$75 Myr pre-main sequence and therefore could be habitable if it formed with $\gtrsim$2x Earth's surface water mass. The predicted tidal heating surface flux tends to be similar to Io, with no cases approaching the flux required to drive a runaway greenhouse. We find that if the planet is rocky, then eccentricities larger than 0.62 today are strongly disfavored, implying that larger eccentricities could confirm the gaseous nature of the planet. These results suggest that TOI-2257 b could provide valuable constraints on mini-Neptune properties and new insight into the radius valley shape as a function of eccentricity.

papers.title: Exact Scaling Laws for a Random-Features Bigram Model
papers.abstract: Understanding neural scaling laws is increasingly important for theory and practice, yet first-principles explanations remain limited even in simple settings. In this work, we study capacity-limited scaling in a bottlenecked bigram model with power-law (Zipf) token statistics, viewed as an analytically tractable toy model of a large language model. Fixed random embeddings serve as a proxy for representational capacity and induce an explicit bottleneck of width, allowing us to derive scaling laws for prediction regret as a function of model width, vocabulary size, and the Zipf exponent. Our results complement recent theoretical accounts based on optimization dynamics by isolating scaling due purely to representational constraints. In the appropriate regime, the theory recovers the functional form of classical neural scaling laws and suggests that heavy-tailed language statistics may underlie both optimization- and capacity-driven scaling. Experiments natural language datasets (WikiText2, OpenWebText) closely match the predicted curves.

papers.title: Effects of cortisol time-scales in a model of emotion regulation
papers.abstract: Stress reshapes cortico-limbic dynamics across multiple timescales, with important consequences for healthy and pathological arousal responses. We develop and analyze a Wilson-Cowan model of prefrontal-amygdala circuitry, incorporating excitatory and inhibitory populations involved in emotional regulation. The effects of stress cortisol are represented as history-dependent modulations of two stress-sensitive interactions: recurrent prefrontal excitation and inhibition of basolateral amygdala principal cells.
